PREFACE

If one reflects carefully with a keen intellect, one finds that there is no instrument for attaining the four aims of life (dharma, artha, kama, and moksha — righteousness, wealth, desire, and liberation) other than the body itself; the body alone is that instrument. But it fulfills its functions properly only when it is free from mental and physical afflictions. Therefore it is proper to protect it in every possible way. For this very reason it is stated even in the texts on statecraft: "One should always protect the self, even at the cost of one's home, even at the cost of one's wealth." And the Lord Dhanvantari himself took incarnation for the protection of the body alone, and revealed Ayurveda — that Ayurveda whose Charaka Samhita was composed by the sage Charaka, through which he considered himself to have fulfilled his soul's purpose before the great sages. However, because it was composed by a great sage and is consequently difficult, the physicians of the present time have been unable to derive benefit from it. Therefore, having had a vernacular commentary prepared under the guidance of the learned Pandit Mihirachandra ji, we have carefully printed and published this universally useful work at our own "Shri Venkateswara" press. In its various sections, various subjects are described such that a physician who reads them has no need of other texts. And indeed, without Charaka, can a physician become proficient even by studying a hundred other works? It has also been said: "He who has not read Charaka — what kind of physician is he? He is but a servant of Yama (the god of death)." There is nothing more to say — can the water of the ocean fit inside a pot? That will be understood only by seeing for oneself. Thus it is enough.

Seeking the grace of the learned —
Khemraj Shri Krishnadas,
Director, "Shri Venkateswara" Press — Mumbai.

Charaka Samhita

An illustrative diagram of the intestines (bowels), showing the full form of the alimentary canal (Alimentary Canal) from the throat to the rectum.

[DIAGRAM WITH NUMBERED LABELS 1 through 22]

In this diagram, the mark numbered 1 through 2 indicates the alimentary canal, the Oesophagus. 4 is the Stomach. From 5 to 8 is the upper portion of the tract. 7 is the Jejunum and 8 is the Ileum — these three together are called the small intestines (Small Intestines). 9 is the lower portion of the large intestine — the Caecum; and 10 is the Ascending Colon, 11 is the Transverse Colon, and 12 is the Descending Colon. These are collectively called the large intestines (Large Intestines). 13 is called the Rectum. 14 and 15 are the two Kidneys. 16 is the urinary Bladder. 17 is the Liver. 18 is the Gall-bladder. 19 is the Spleen. And where the number 2 appears, that is the Trachea, the second airway of the throat. 20 and 21 are the two Lungs, and 22 is the Heart. "Ka" and "Ga" mark the two main [illegible] passages. And "Ga" indicates the anus and the excretory opening.

Charaka Samhita.

Eye Ball (Netra Mandala)

Eyelid (Palak)

In this diagram:
"Nya" — the first layer of the eye, that is, the white membrane (sclera).
"Ka" — the transparent portion.
"Rva" — the second layer of the eye wall, that is, the dark membrane (choroid).
"Ga" — the transparent portion beneath it.
"Gha" — the space that is always filled with fluid (aqueous humor).
"Nga" — the third layer, that is, the membrane bearing the pupil (iris).
"Cha" — the pupil, that is, the dark portion.
"Chha" — the crystalline lens, the fourth layer, that is, the glassy substance.
"Ja" — the fluid matter within the eye, that is, the place of the colored lens-like substance (vitreous humor).
"Jha" — the optic nerve, that is, the vein of sight.

Physicians versed in Ayurveda consider there to be four layers (membranes) in the eye, while Unani hakims count up to seven, and modern doctors recognize only three membranes.

अस्थिप्रदर्शक पार्श्व चित्र.

शरीरका मुख्य आधार अस्थिपंजरपर है. इसहीसे शरीरका आकार, दृढता, गमनशक्ति, उत्पन्न होती है. इसहीपर सम्पूर्ण कार्यका व्यवहार निर्भर है. शरीरमें संपूर्ण अस्थिसंरव्या डाक्टरी मतसे इस प्रकार है. खोपडीमें ८, चहरामें १४, गर्दनके उपर ९, करवटमें २६, उरमें ९, पांसूमें २१, सम्पूर्ण हाथमें ६४, सब पांवमें ६२, इसतरह सब मिलकर २००हैं. दांत ३२ और अलेक कानमें तीन तीन छोटी अस्थि हैं सब मिलकर २३८ होती हैं. और ८ अनुमंडलास्थि ये मिलकर २४६ हैं.

22
Charaka Samhita.

Lateral View of the Skeleton

Lateral Diagram of the Bones.
( Bones. )

The principal support of the body rests upon the skeleton. From it alone arise the body's shape, firmness, and power of movement. Upon it depends the conduct of all bodily functions. The total count of bones in the body, according to medical opinion, is as follows: in the skull 8, in the face 14, above the neck 9, in the sides 26, in the chest 9, in the ribs 21, in the complete arms 64, in all the feet 62 — thus altogether these make 200. The teeth number 32, and in each ear there are three small bones, making altogether 238. Adding 8 cranial bones, the total comes to 246.

And according to Ayurvedic medical opinion:
In all four limbs (arms and legs) there are 120 bones, in the trunk 117, and above the neck 63 bones. All these together make 300. See the chapter on Bodily Locations, Chapter 5, the fifth.

Description of Pataladi medicines in diseases such as Vadavata and others.
Description of the five purificatory procedures (Panchakarma) including Snehadi for persons afflicted with doshas.
Description of twenty-eight types of Yavagu (gruel), their preparations, and their uses and indications in various diseases.          19
Thus ends the second chapter of the Meshanchatushka, named Apamargatanduliya. ║ 2 ║

THIRD CHAPTER

Explanation of the Aragvadhiya Chapter.          21

Description of Amalatasadi and other external applications (pradeha) that quickly destroy diseases such as kushtha (skin diseases) and others.
Description of the application of Kutadi and other pastes (ubtan) for itching and other bodily ailments.          22
Description of Iridadi and other liquid pastes for the relief of certain diseases.          23
Again, description of Chaturguladi and other medicines for kushtha (skin disease).
Description of Koladi paste for vata diseases.
Tagaradi paste for head pain.          24
Raysanadi paste for side pain.
Shevaladi paste for cooling applications.
Chandranadi paste for destroying cold.          25
Shirasadi paste for body odor.
Thus ends the third chapter named Aragvadhiya. ║ 3 ║

FOURTH CHAPTER

Explanation of the Shadvirecanashatashritiya Chapter.

Brief description of formulations for each of the six hundred purgatives and their basis in six types of Drisha and other purgatives.          26
Description of the sources of the five sweet (Madhuradis) decoctions, and the preparation of decoctions of five types including Svarasa and others.
Description of the fifty Mahakashayas (major decoctions) and their individual classifications.          27
Again, description of the marks of the fifty Mahakashayas, and by dividing each into ten sub-varieties, description of the properties of five hundred (500) decoctions.          28
For the completion of the five hundred decoctions, the opinion of the great sage Punarvasu-ji, the exchange between Agnivesha-ji and him, and Punarvasu-ji's reply to them is described.          26
Thus ends the Meshanchatushka. ║ 4 ║

विषयानुक्रमणिका । ( ३ )

विषय: पृष्ठांक. | विषय. पृष्ठांक.

पंचमोऽध्यायः । | षष्ठोऽध्यायः ।

मात्राश्रितीय अध्यायका व्याख्यान. ३७ | तस्याशितीय अध्यायका व्याख्यान. ५१

गुरुद्रव्यों तथा लघुद्रव्योंके गुणागुणका
व्याख्यान और तिनको मात्रासे उपयोगमें लेनेकी पृथकु २ क्रिया. ३८

नेत्रोंके दर्दमें चंद्नादि अंजन लगानेकी क्रिया
तथा काल. ३९

पुनः नेत्रोंके दर्दमें हरेण्वादि अंजन. ४०

पुनः नेत्ररोगपर वार्तिक्या. ,,

ऊर्ध्विरेचनादि रोगोंपर श्वेतादि औषधियोंका धूम्रपान. ४१

स्नानादि आठकालोंमें वारसिहित धूम्रपानका प्रयोग और लक्षण. ४२

बिना समय धूम्रपान करनेके अवगुण और तिसकी शान्ति तथा जिनको न पीना चाहिये उनके पीनेसे दारुण रोगोंकी उत्पत्तिका वर्णन. ,,

पृथकु २ रोगोंमें धूम्रपान करनेकी विधि तथा अत्यंत धूम्रपानके अवगुण. ४३

नेत्रादिकोंके रक्षाके अर्थ नस्य क्रिया और तिसके गुणागुण. ४४

विदोषादि रोगों पर चंद्नादि तैलकी नस्यक्रिया. ४५

दतोंन करनेकी क्रिया और तिसके गुणागुण. ४६

सुवर्णादिनिलेखन ( जिम्मी ) करनेकी क्रिया और लक्षण. ,,

करंजादि दतोंन करनेके गुणागुण. ,,

प्रतिदिन शिरमें तेल लगानेके गुण और कान में तेलडालनेके गुणागुण. ४७

अभ्यंग करनेके गुणागुण. ४८

स्नान करनेके गुणागुण. ४९

निर्मल वक्ष और सुगंधित पुष्प व रत्नादिकोंके धारण करनेके गुणागुण. ,,

केशादिकोंको साधन करनेके गुणागुण. ,,

पादत्राण धारण करनेके गुणागुण. ,,

छत्र धारण करनेके गुणागुण. ५०

दंडधारण करनेके गुणागुण. ,,

इति मात्राश्रितीनाम पंचमोऽध्यायः ॥ ५ ॥

षष्ठोऽध्यायः ।

तस्याशितीय अध्यायका व्याख्यान. ५१

वर्षके छः ऋतुभों के विभागसे अंगोंका वर्णन और तिनअंगोंमें रवि उत्तरायण व दक्षिणायनके गुणागुण. ,,

शीतादि छः ऋतुओंमें पृथकु २ कर्चव्यता. ५२

इति तस्याश्रितीयोऽध्यायः ॥ ६ ॥

सप्तमोऽध्यायः ।

नवेगान्धारणीय अध्यायका व्याख्यान. ५८

मूत्रादिवेगोंको रोकनेके अवगुण तथा तिनकी पृथकु २ चिकित्सा. ,,

उभय लोकाभिलाषी मनुष्यको साहसादि वेगोंके धारण करनेके गुण. ६०

व्यायाम करनेके गुण तथा अधिक व्यायाम करनेके अवगुण. ६१

हरमकारके कर्मोंको मात्रासे अधिक सेवन करनेवालोंके अवगुण. ,,

बुद्धिके अपराधसे ईष्यादिकोंकी उत्पत्ति. ६२

पापाचारी मनुष्योंके सेवनमें अवगुण और बुद्धिमानोंके सेवनका गुण. ६४

दव्यादिक पदार्थोंको अन्यके संयोगसे सेवन करनेके गुणागुण तथा काल. ,,

विधिको त्यागकर दिघ मक्षणकरनेके अवगुण. ६५

इति न वेगान्धारणीयोऽध्यायः ॥ ७ ॥

अष्टमोऽध्यायः ।

इंद्रियोपक्रमणीय अध्यायका व्याख्यान. ६६

इंद्रियाधिकारका कथन. ,,

चक्षादि पांच इंद्रियें और पांच इंद्रियोंके द्रव्यादिकोंका कथन. ६७

मनादि अध्यात्म द्रव्योंके लक्षण तथा क्रियाका वर्णन. ,,

चरकसंहितायाः ।
( सूत्रस्थानम् )

अथातो दीर्घजीवितमध्यायंव्याख्यास्यामः ।
इसके अनंतर दीर्घ जीवित अध्यायका व्याख्यान करतेहैं–

दीर्घजीवितमन्विच्छन्भरद्वाजउपागमत् । इन्द्रमुशतपाबुद्धाशरण्यममरेश्वरम् ॥ १ ॥

कि दीर्घजीवनके अभिलाषी महातपस्वी भरद्वाज ऋषि, देवताओंके ईश्वर शरणागतके रक्षक समझकर इंद्रके समीप गये ॥ १ ॥

ब्रह्मणाहियथाप्रोक्तमायुर्वेदंप्रजापतिः । जग्राहनिखिलेनादाविश्वनौतुपुनस्ततः ॥ २ ॥

ब्रह्माने जैसा आयुर्वेद कहाहै वह संपूर्ण प्रजापतिने अश्विनीकुमारोंको ग्रहणकराया फिर उन ॥ २ ॥

अश्विभ्यांभगवाञ्छकःप्रतिपेदेहि केवलम् । ऋषिभ्योकोभरद्वाजः तस्माच्छकमुपागमत् ॥ ३ ॥

अश्विनीकुमारोंसे केवल भगवान् शक्रकोही आयुर्वेद प्राप्तभया तिससे ऋषियोंके कहनेसे भरद्वाज इंद्रके समीपगये ॥ ३ ॥

विघ्नीभूतायदारोगाःप्रादुर्भूताःशरीरिणाम् । उपवासतपःपाठब्रह्मचर्यव्रतायुषाम् ॥ ४ ॥

जब तप उपवास अध्ययन ब्रह्मचर्यव्रत इनसे युक्त अवस्यावार् देहधारियोंमेंभी विघ्नकारक रोगोंकी अकटता हुई ४

तदाभूतेष्वनुकोशंपुरस्कृत्य महर्षयः । समेताःपुण्यकर्माणः पार्श्वे हिमवतःशुभे ॥ ५ ॥

तब भूतोंपर दया करके संपूर्ण पुण्यकर्मी महर्षि हिमाचलके शोभनपार्श्वमें इकठे होते भये कि ॥ ५ ॥

Salutation to the Auspicious.
Now begins
The Charaka Samhita.
(Sutrasthana — The Section on Fundamental Principles)

Now we shall expound the chapter on long life.
What follows is the commentary on the chapter regarding long life:

Verse 1: Desiring long life, the sage Bharadvaja approached Indra — the lord of the immortals, the protector of those who seek his refuge, he who is revered and worshipped.

Commentary: That is, Bharadvaja, the great ascetic who longed for long life, regarding Indra — the lord of the gods and the protector of those who surrender to him — went to his presence. ॥ 1 ॥

Verse 2: Prajapati received the Ayurveda in its entirety exactly as it was proclaimed by Brahma, and thereafter transmitted it onward.

Commentary: Just as Brahma had declared the Ayurveda, Prajapati caused the Ashvini Kumaras to receive it in full, and then from them... ॥ 2 ॥

Verse 3: From the Ashvini Kumaras, the lord Shakra (Indra) alone received the Ayurveda, and therefore Bharadvaja, at the request of the sages, went to Shakra.

Commentary: The Ayurveda was received solely by the lord Shakra from the Ashvini Kumaras; hence, at the urging of the sages, Bharadvaja went to Indra's presence. ॥ 3 ॥

Verse 4: Diseases appeared as obstacles in the lives of embodied beings who were engaged in fasting, austerity, study, and the vow of celibacy.

Commentary: When diseases became obstacles even for those engaged in austerity, fasting, study, and the vow of celibacy, causing obstruction to their lives... ॥ 4 ॥

Verse 5: Then, taking compassion on all living beings, the great sages of holy deeds assembled on the auspicious slopes of the Himalayas.

Commentary: Then, taking pity on all beings, the great sages of wholly meritorious conduct gathered together on the beautiful slopes of the Himalayas, thinking... ॥ 5 ॥

From the Charaka Samhita.

[Verse 24]
By that [teaching], Bharadvaja obtained unlimited lifespan with great joy, and without holding anything back, he taught that entire Ayurveda to the other sages. (24)

[Commentary 24]
Through the glory of that Ayurveda, Bharadvaja, filled with joy, attained unlimited life and, keeping nothing back, taught that complete Ayurveda to the sages. (24)

[Verse 25]
The sages received it from Bharadvaja — that [knowledge] which is beneficial to all people — desiring long life, just as one would approach a cow for nourishment. (25)

[Commentary 25]
Those sages, desiring long life for themselves and the welfare of all people, received that Ayurveda from Bharadvaja. (25)

[Verse 26]
The great sages perceived with the eye of knowledge the general and specific qualities, substances, and actions [of things]. (26)

[Commentary 26]
Those great sages, using the eye of knowledge, properly perceived the general, specific, qualities, substances, and actions [described in Ayurveda]. (26)

[Verse 27]
Having known that coordination [of factors], they followed the methods prescribed in the treatise and thereby obtained supreme happiness and a life free of disease. (27)

[Commentary 27]
Having understood that coordination, and firmly following the methods prescribed in the treatise, they attained supreme joy and a life free from disease. (27)

[Verse 28 — continued from previous page]
— Punarvasu, devoted to benevolence and compassion for all living beings, taught the sacred Ayurveda again to his six disciples. (28)

[Commentary 28]
After that, Punarvasu, ever devoted to friendship and having compassion for all creatures, gave the sacred Ayurveda to six disciples. (28)

[Verse 29]
Agnivesha, Bhela, Jatukarna, Parashara, Harita, and Ksharapani — these six received the words of that sage. (29)

[Commentary 29]
Agnivesha (1), Bhela (2), Jatukarna (3), Parashara (4), Harita (5), and Ksharapani (6) — these six sages received the teaching of that sage. (29)

[Verse 30]
Among them there was a distinction of intellect, though the teaching of the sage was the same for all — and it is for this reason that Agnivesha became the first to compose a treatise. (30)

[Commentary 30]
Because Agnivesha was the first to compose the treatise (shastra), it was solely on account of a difference in intellectual sharpness; there was no difference in the teaching of the sage (Punarvasu). (30)

[Verse 31]
Thereafter, Bhela and the others also composed their own separate treatises, and recited them to the assembly of sages along with the wise Atreya (Punarvasu). (31)

[Commentary 31]
After that, Bhela and the others also composed their own respective treatises and recited those treatises before the assembly of sages along with the wise Atreya (Punarvasu), who listened to them. (31)

...of the sages. Having heard that composition (sutra) which was perfectly well-formed, they were delighted and acknowledged that it had been composed correctly. (32)

All beings, wishing welfare for all creatures, praised them, and with one loud voice said: "Compassion has been shown to all beings!" (33)

The gods and divine sages dwelling in heaven heard that auspicious sound, and upon hearing the words of the great sages, they were filled with the highest joy. (34)

"Excellent! Well done!" — this exclamation resounded through all three worlds and through the sky; uttered by the beings with joy, it spread as a sound rich, deep, and affectionate. (35)

An auspicious wind blew, all directions shone with radiance, and from heaven there fell a rain of flowers mixed with water. (36)

Thereafter, the divine beings of knowledge — Intelligence, Attainment, Memory, Wisdom, Steadfastness, Fame, Forbearance, and Compassion — entered into the bodies of Agnivesha and the others. (37)

Those treatises, approved by the great sages for the welfare of the multitudes of living beings, were established upon this earth. (38)

That in which beneficial and harmful things, happiness and suffering, the lifespan and what is wholesome and unwholesome for it, and its measure are discussed — that is called Ayurveda. (39)

The conjunction of body, senses, mind, and soul that sustains life — that is called ayus (life); it is described by various synonyms, both as that which is constant and that which is contingent. (40)

( ६ )
Digitized By [stamp] Gyayan Kosha

शरीर इंद्रिय सत्व, सत्व आत्मा इनके संयोगका धारक जीवित और नित्यग और अनुबंध इन पर्यायोंसे आयु कहीहै अथात् ये आयुके नामहैं ॥ ४० ॥

तस्यायुषःपुण्यतमोवेदोवेदविदां
मतः । वक्ष्यतेयन्मनुष्याणांलोक
योरुभयोहितः ॥ ४१ ॥

उस आयुका अत्यंत पवित्र वेद वेदके ज्ञाताओंने जो माना है उसको कहतेहैं जो मनुष्योंके दोनों लोकोंको हितहै ॥४१॥

सर्वेदासर्वेभावानांसामान्यंवृद्धि
कारणम् । हासहेतुर्विशेषश्च
वृत्तिरुभयस्यतु ॥ ४२ ॥

सब कालोंमें संपूर्ण भावोंका जो सामान्य वृद्धि कारण है और हास हेतुका विशेष और हास वृद्धि इन दोनोंकी प्रवृति ॥ ४२ ॥

सामान्यमेकत्वकरंविशेषस्तुपृथ
क्तकरत् । तुल्यार्थतासामा
न्यंविशेषस्तुविपर्ययः ॥४३॥

सामान्य एकताको करताहै और विशेष पृथक्ताको करता है तुल्य अर्थकी सामान्य और उससे विपरीतको विशेष कहतेहैं॥४३

सत्वमात्माशरीरञ्चत्रयमेतञ्चिद
ण्डवत् । लोकस्तिष्ठितसंयोगात्
त्रसर्वंप्रतिष्ठतम् ॥ ४४ ॥

सत्व आत्मा शरीर ये तीनों त्रिदंडके समान हैं और इनके संयोगसे लोक टिकता है उसमें सब टिकेहुये हैं॥४४॥

सपुमांश्वेतनंतच्चताधिकरणंस्मृ
तम् । वेदस्यास्यतदर्थेहिवेदोऽ
यंसम्प्रकाशितः ।। ४५ ।।

वही पुमान् है वही चेतन है वही अधिकरण इस वेदका कहा है उसके लिये इस आयुर्वेदका भलीप्रकार प्रकाश किया ४५

खादीन्यात्मामनःकालोदिशश्चद्र
व्यसंग्रहः । सेन्द्रियंचेतनंद्रव्यं
निरिन्द्रियमचेतनम् ॥ ४६ ॥

आकाश आदि आत्मा मन काल दिशा द्रव्यका संग्रह यह चेतन द्रव्य इंद्रियों सहित है और अचेतन इंद्रियोंसे रहित है ॥ ४६ ॥

साथांगुवादयोबुद्धिःप्रयत्नान्ताः
परादयः ।गुणाःप्रोक्ताःप्रयत्नादि
कर्मेतेंषिवदमुच्यते ।। ४७ ।।

अर्थ सहित गुरु आदि और बुद्धि और परसे लेकर प्रयत्न पर्यंत गुण कहे हैं और प्रयत्न आदि चेष्टित कहाताहै॥४७

सशरीरःपृथगभावोद्रव्यादीनांगु
णैमेतः । सनित्योयत्रिहद्रव्यंनत
त्रानियतागुणाः ॥ ४८ ॥

द्रव्योंका जो गुणोंसे अपृथक् भाव वह समवाय माना है जिसमें द्रव्य रहता है वह नित्य है, उसमें गुण अनियत हैं अथात् सदा नहींरहते हैं ॥ ४८ ॥

translation:
(6)

The body, sense-organs, and mind — and the union of mind with the self (atma) — its bearer is called living (jivita); and by the terms "eternal continuity" (nityaga) and "continuance" (anubandha), life (ayus) is designated. These are the names of ayus. (40)

Of that ayus, the most sacred teaching comes from this Veda, as recognized by those who know the Veda — it will be declared here for the benefit of human beings in both worlds. (41)

Similarity (samanya) is the cause of increase in all things at all times; particularity (vishesha) is the cause of decrease; the activity of both operates in these two ways. (42)

Similarity brings about unity; particularity brings about distinction. Sameness of meaning is samanya; its opposite is vishesha. (43)

Mind, self, and body — these three are like a tripod (tridanda). The world stands through their union, and everything rests in it. (44)

That very being is the conscious subject, that is the conscious one, that is the locus (adhikarana) spoken of in this Veda — for its sake this Ayurveda has been well illuminated. (45)

Space (akasha) and the rest, the self, mind, time, and direction — this is the collection of substances (dravyas). The substance that possesses sense-organs is sentient (chetana); that which lacks sense-organs is insentient (acetana). (46)

Heaviness and the other qualities, intellect (buddhi), and those beginning with effort (prayatna), such as para (priority) and the rest — these are the qualities (gunas) declared; and actions beginning with effort (prayatna) are called cheshta (activity). (47)

The inseparability of qualities from substances is called samavaya (inherence). That substance in which they inhere is eternal; the qualities therein are not fixed — that is, they do not remain always. (48)

Digitized By Siddh सूत्रस्थानम् tri Byaan Kosha ( ७ )

वायियत् । तद्द्रव्यंसमवायीतु
निश्चेष्टःकारणगुणः ॥ ४९ ॥

जिसमें कर्मके गुण आश्रित हैं और
जो समवायि कारण है वह द्रव्य है और
द्रव्यमें समवायी होकर चेष्टासे रहित
हुआ कारण है वह गुण होताहै ॥४९॥

संयोगेचवियोगेचकारणंद्रव्यमा
श्रितम् । कर्तव्यस्यकियाकर्म
कर्मनान्यदपेक्षते ॥ ५० ॥

वह संयोग और वियोगमें कारण
द्रव्यके आश्रित है करने योग्यकी जो
क्रिया उसको कर्म कहते हैं वह कर्म
अन्यकी अपेक्षा नहीं करता है ॥ ५० ॥

इत्युक्तंकारणकार्येधातुसाम्यमि
होच्यते । धातुसाम्यिकयाचो
क्कातन्त्रस्यास्यप्रयोजनम् ॥ ५१ ॥

ये कारण और कार्य कहे, अब धातु-
ओंकी समताको कहतें हैं इस तंत्रका प्रयो-
जन धातुओंकी समता करना है ॥५१॥

कालबुद्धीन्द्रियार्थानांयोगोमि
थ्यानचातिच।त्रयाश्रयाणांव्या
धीनांत्रिविधोहेतुसंग्रहः॥ ५२॥

काल बुद्धि इंद्रिय अर्थ इनका योग है
और मिथ्या योग नहीं है और जो व्याधि-
दोंके आश्रय (द्वंद्वज) उनके तीन
प्रकारके हेतुका संग्रह है ॥ ५२ ॥

शरीरंतत्वसंज्ञंचव्याधीनामाश्रयो

मतः । तथासुखानांयोगस्तुसुखा
नांकारणंशमः ॥ ५३ ॥

सत्व संज्ञक जो शरीर है वह व्याधि-
योंका आश्रय मानाहै तिसी प्रकार सुखोंका
योग सुखोंका कारण शम(शांति)है॥५३॥

निर्विकारःपरस्त्वात्मासत्वभूत
गुणेन्द्रियै । चेतनेकारणंनित्यो
द्रष्टापश्यतिहिक्रियाः ॥ ५४ ॥

परम आत्मा निर्विकार है सत्व भूत
गुण इंद्रियोंसे चैतन्यमें कारण है नित्य
द्रष्टा है क्योंकि वह क्रियाओंको देखता
है ॥ ५४ ॥

वायुःपित्तंकफश्चोक्तःशारीरोदोष
संग्रहः । मानसःपुनरुदिष्टोरजश्च
तमएवच ॥ ५५ ॥

वात पित्त कफ यह शरीरके दोषोंका
संग्रह है और मनके दोषोंका संग्रह रज
और तम है ॥ ५५ ॥

प्रशाम्यत्यौषधैःपूर्वोद्रव्ययुक्तिव्य
पाश्रयैः । मानसोज्ञानविज्ञानधैर्य
स्मृतिसमाधिभिः ॥ ५६ ॥

उनमें पहिला द्रव्य युक्तिके आश्रित
जो औषधि उनसे शांत होता है और
मानस रोग–ज्ञान विज्ञान धैर्य स्मृति समा-
धियोंसे शांत होता है ॥ ५६ ॥

रूक्षःशीतोलघुःसूक्ष्मश्चलोऽथिव
पदःखरः । विपरीतगुणैःद्रव्यैर्मा

Page 7 — Sutrasthana (Chapter on Foundational Principles)

[Verse 49]
That in which the qualities of action inhere, and which is the inherent cause — that is substance (dravya). And that which, residing inherently in substance, becomes the cause devoid of independent activity — that is quality (guna). ॥49॥

[Verse 50]
In both conjunction and disjunction, the cause resides in substance. That action which is to be performed is called karma (action); action does not depend upon anything else. ॥50॥

Having thus stated cause and effect, dhatu-samya (equilibrium of bodily constituents) is now described. The purpose of this treatise is the maintenance of equilibrium among the dhatus (bodily constituents). ॥51॥

[Verse 51 commentary]
Cause and effect have been explained; now the equilibrium of the dhatus is described. The purpose of this system is to establish equilibrium among the dhatus. ॥51॥

[Verse 52]
The conjunction of time, intellect, sense organs, and their objects — and similarly their improper or excessive use — constitutes the threefold collection of causes of diseases, which rest upon the three substrates. ॥52॥

The body, known as the seat of diseases, is their abode. In the same way, the conjunction of pleasures is the cause of well-being, and that cause is tranquility (shama). ॥53॥

[Verse 54]
The supreme Self (Atman) is free from modification. The sattva, the five elemental qualities, and the sense organs are the cause of consciousness. The Self is the eternal witness, for it observes all actions. ॥54॥

[Verse 55]
Vata, pitta, and kapha are declared the collection of bodily doshas (humors). Rajas and tamas are declared the doshas of the mind. ॥55॥

[Verse 56]
The first — bodily disorders — are pacified by medicines grounded in substance and proper use. Mental disorders are pacified by knowledge, discriminative wisdom, courage, memory, and meditative absorption (samadhi). ॥56॥

रतःसंप्रशाम्यति ।। ५७ ।।
रूक्ष शीत लघु सूक्ष्म चल विषद् खर
जो वायुहै वह विपरीत गुणवान् द्रव्योंसे
शांत होताहै ।। ५७ ।।

सस्नेहमुष्णंतीक्ष्णंचद्रवमम्लंसरं
कटु । विपरीतगुणैःपित्तंद्रव्यैः
राशुप्रशाम्यति ।। ५८ ।।

स्नेहसे युक्त उष्ण तीक्ष्ण द्रव अम्ल
सर कटु जो पित्तहै वह विपरीत गुणवान्
द्रव्योंसे शीघ्र शांत होताहै ।। ५८ ।।

गुरुशीतमृदुस्निग्ध मधुरिस्थरिप
िच्छलाः । श्लेष्मणःप्रशमंयान्ति
विपरीतगुणैगुणाः ।। ५९ ।।

गुरु शीत मृदु स्निग्ध मधुर स्थिर
पिच्छल जो श्लेष्माके गुणहैं वे विपरीत
गुणवान् द्रव्योंसे शांत होतेहैं ।। ५९ ।।

विपरीतगुणैर्देशमात्राकालोपपा
दितैःभेषजैर्विनिवर्तन्तेविकाराः
साधुसंमताः ।। ६० ।।

देश मात्रा काल इनसे उत्पन्न किये
विपरीत गुणवान् भेषजोंसे साध्य संमत
( माने हुए ) विकार विशेषकर नष्ट
होतेहैं ।। ६० ।।

साधनंनत्वसाध्यानांव्याधीनामुप
दिश्यते । भूयश्चातोयथाद्रव्यंगु
णकर्मप्रवक्ष्यते ।। ६१ ।।

और असाध्य व्याधियोंका साधन-

नहीं कहाहै–इसके अनंतर फिरभी द्रव्य२
के गुण और कर्मको कहतेहैं कि।। ६१ ।।

रसनार्थीरसस्तस्यद्रव्यमापःक्षि
तिस्तथा । निवृत्तौचविशेषेचप्र
त्ययाःखादयःस्मृयः ।। ६२ ।।

रसनाईंद्रियका विषय रसहै उसके
द्रव्य जल और पृथ्वीहैं और आकाश
आदि तीनों निवृत्ति और विशेषमें प्रती
तिके उत्पादकहैं ।। ६२ ।।

स्वादुरम्लोऽथलवणोकटुंकसित
कएवच । कषायश्चेतिषट्कोऽ
यंरसानांसंग्रहःस्मृतः ।। ६३ ।।

स्वादु अम्ल लवण कटु तिक्त कषाय
यह छः प्रकारका रसोंका संग्रह कहाहै६ ३

स्वाद्रम्ललवणावायुंकषायस्वादु
तिक्तकाःजयन्तिपित्तंश्लेष्माणं
कषायकटुतिक्तकाः ।। ६४ ।।

स्वादु अम्ल लवण ये वायुको कषाय
स्वादु तिक्तक ये पित्तको कषाय कटु
तिक्त ये श्लेष्माको पैदा करतेहैं ।। ६४।।

किंचिद्दोषप्रशनंकिंचिद्धातुमदूष
णम् । स्वस्थवृत्तौहितंकिंचि
द्व्यंत्रिविधमुच्यते ।। ६५ ।।

कोई दोषका प्रशमनहै कोई धातुको
दूषित करताहै कोई स्वस्थ वृत्तिमें हितहै
इसप्रकार द्रव्य तीन प्रकारका कहाहै६५
तत्पुनस्त्रिविधंज्ञेयंजाङ्गमौद्भिद्

From the Charaka Samhita

[Verse 57]
It is pacified thereby. Vata (wind), which has the qualities of roughness, coldness, lightness, subtlety, mobility, clarity, and sharpness, is calmed by substances that have the opposite qualities. [57]

[Verse 58]
That which is unctuous, hot, sharp, fluid, sour, and pungent — Pitta is swiftly pacified by substances possessing opposite qualities. [58]
Pitta, which is characterized by unctuousness, heat, sharpness, fluidity, sourness, and pungency, is quickly calmed by substances with the opposite qualities. [58]

[Verse 59]
Heavy, cold, soft, unctuous, sweet, stable, and slimy — these are the qualities of Kapha; they are pacified by substances of opposite qualities. [59]
Heavy, cold, soft, unctuous, sweet, stable, and slimy are the qualities of Kapha; they are calmed by substances of opposite qualities. [59]

[Verse 60]
Diseases that are considered curable are certainly destroyed by medicines generated with opposite qualities, applied with due consideration of place, dose, and time. [60]
Diseases that are curable, as determined by place, dose, and time through properly prepared medicines of opposite qualities, are especially eradicated. [60]

[Verse 61]
Treatment is not prescribed for incurable diseases. Furthermore, the properties and actions of substances will now be described in greater detail. [61]
The treatment of incurable diseases is not described here. After this, the qualities and actions of substances will again be explained. [61]

[Verse 62]
Taste is the object of the faculty of taste; its substances are water and earth; space and the remaining elements are known as the causes of perception in both the absence and special manifestation of taste. [62]
The object of the sense organ of taste is rasa (taste); its substances are water and earth; and the other three — space, etc. — are the generators of perception in the cessation and particularization of taste. [62]

[Verse 63]
Sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, and astringent — these six constitute the complete enumeration of tastes. [63]
Sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, and astringent — this is said to be the sixfold collection of tastes. [63]

[Verse 64]
Sweet, sour, and salty conquer Vata; astringent, sweet, and bitter conquer Pitta; astringent, pungent, and bitter conquer Kapha. [64]
Sweet, sour, and salty increase Vata; astringent, sweet, and bitter aggravate Pitta; and astringent, pungent, and bitter produce Kapha. [64]

Some substances pacify the doshas, some vitiate the dhatus (bodily tissues), and some are beneficial for maintaining the health of a healthy person — thus substances are described as being of three kinds. [65]
Some are for pacifying a dosha, some are for corrupting a dhatu, some are beneficial for the regimen of a healthy person — in this way, substances are said to be of three kinds. [65]

Digitized By Siddha Gyaan Kosha (९)

सूत्रस्थानम् १

पार्थिवम् । मधुनिगोरसाःपित्तं
सामञ्जामृगामिषम् ॥ ६६ ॥

वह फिर जांगल औद्भिद पार्थिव
भेदसे तीन प्रकारकाहै. मधु गोरस पित्त
वसा मज्जा मृगोंका मांस ॥ ६६ ॥

विण्मूत्रचर्मरेतोऽस्थिस्नायुरङ्खु
रानखाः । जङ्गमेष्यःप्रयुज्यन्ते
केशालोमानिरोचनाः ॥ ६७ ॥

विष्ठा मूत्र चर्म रेत अस्थि स्नायु शृंग
खुर नख केश लोम रोचन ये जंगमोंके
प्रयोगोंमें आतेहैं ॥ ६७ ॥

सुवर्णसमलाःपञ्चलोहाःसिसक
तासुधा । मनःशिलालेमणयोल
वणगैरिकाञ्जने ॥६८॥

सुवर्ण मल और सिकता सहित पांचों
लोह सुधा मनशिल मणि लवण गेरू
अंजन ॥ ६८ ॥

भौममौषधमुदिष्टमौद्भिदन्तुचतु
र्विधम् । वनस्पतिर्विरुधश्चवान
स्पत्यस्तथौषिधः ॥ ६९ ॥

ये भूमिकी औषध कहीहैं औद्भिदतो
चारं प्रकारका वनस्पति वीरुध वानस्पत्य
औषध इनके भेदसे है ॥ ६९ ॥

फलैर्वनस्पतिःपुष्पैर्वानस्पत्यःफलैः
रपि । औषधयःफलपाकान्ताः
प्रतानैर्विरुधःस्मृताः ॥ ७० ॥

जिनके फल आवे वे वनस्पति जिनके
पुष्पफलदोनोंहों वे वानस्पत्य—जो फलको

पाक पर्यंत रहैंवे औषध–जिनका प्रतान
( फैलाव ) हो वे वीरुध कहेहैं ॥ ७०॥

मूलत्वकसारिनियासनाडस्वरसप
ञ्जवाः । क्षाराःक्षीरंफलंपुष्पंभस्म
तैलानिकण्टकाः ॥ ७१ ॥

मूल त्वचा सार गोंद नाड स्वरस पते
क्षार दूध फल पुष्प भस्म तैल कांटे७१

पत्राणिशुङ्गाःकन्दाश्चप्ररोहाश्चौ
द्भिदोगुणः । मूलिन्यःषोडशैकोना
ःफलिन्योविपरीतकाः ॥७२॥

पत्र शुंग कंद प्ररोह ये औद्भिदोंका
गण ( समूह ) होताहै और सोलह मूलिनी
और उनीस फलिनी कहीहैं ॥ ७२ ॥

महास्नेहाश्चचत्वारःपंचैवलवणा
नि च । अष्टौमूत्राणिसंख्यातान्य
ष्टावेवपयांसिच ॥ ७३ ॥

चार महा ( बड़े ) स्नेह और पांच
लवण आठ मूत्र और आठही दूध
कहेहैं ॥ ७३ ॥

शोधनार्थाश्चषड्वृक्षाःपुनर्वसुनिद
शिताः । यएतान्वेत्तिसंयोगकुं
विकारेषुसवेदिवत् ॥ ७४ ॥

और शोधनके लिये छः ६ वृक्ष
पुनर्वसुने दिखायेहैं जो विकारोंमें इनके
संयोगको जानताहै वह आयुर्वेदका
ज्ञाताहै ॥ ७४ ॥

१ विंशतिःस्मृताः इत्यपिपाठः ।

translation:
Sutra-sthana, Chapter 1 (Page 9)

[Verse 66]
That which is of the earth (parthiva). Honey, cow-products, bile — these are the products of forest-dwelling (jangala) animals. [Commentary: The jangala, audbhida, and parthiva are three categories. Honey, cow-products, bile, fat, marrow, and the flesh of deer are included here.] (66)

[Verse 67]
Feces, urine, hide, semen, bone, sinew, horn, hoof, nail, hair, body-hair, and the bile-stone (rochana) — these are the animal-derived (jangama) substances used in treatment. (67)

[Verse 68]
Gold along with its ore-impurities, the five metals, lead, chalk (sudha), realgar (manashila), gem, salt, red ochre (gairika), and collyrium (anjana) — [Commentary: Gold, its dross, sand together with the five metals, chalk, realgar, gem, salt, red ochre, and collyrium.] (68)

[Verse 69]
The medicines of the earth are called bhauma; those of the plant world (audbhida) are of four kinds: vanaspati, virudha, vanaspatya, and aushadhi. [Commentary: These are the plant-derived medicines; audbhida has four sub-types: vanaspati, virudha, vanaspatya, and aushadhi.] (69)

[Verse 70]
Those that bear fruit (without flower) are vanaspati; those that bear both flower and fruit are vanaspatya; those that die after their fruit ripens are aushadhi; those that spread by creeping are called virudha. (70)

[Verse 71]
Root, bark, heartwood, resin (gum), pith, expressed juice, alkali (kshara), milk, fruit, flower, ash, oil, and thorns — these are the parts used. (71)

[Verse 72]
Leaves, buds, bulbs (kanda), and sprouts (praroha) — these constitute the group of audbhida plants. Of these, sixteen are root-bearing (mulini) and nineteen are fruit-bearing (phalini). (72)

[Verse 73]
The great fats (snehas) are four in number; the salts are five; the urines counted are eight; and the milks are likewise eight. (73)

[Verse 74]
For the purpose of purification, six trees have been indicated by Punarvasu (Atreya). One who knows how to combine these in the treatment of diseases is truly a knower of Ayurveda. (74)

Footnote: 1. In some readings it is "vinshati" (twenty) instead.

text:
( १० )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangoth Gyaan Kosha

हस्तिदन्तीहैमवतीश्यामात्रिवृद्धो
गुडा । सप्तलाश्वेतनामाचप्रत्य
क्श्रेणिगवाक्षिपि ॥ ७५ ॥

गज पीपल लज्जालु श्यामा( हरड़े )
निसोथ अघोगुडा ( मुनक्का ) वा ईख
सप्तला श्वेतनामा प्रत्यक्श्रेणी और
गवाक्षी ॥ ७५ ॥

ज्योतिष्मतीचबिम्बीचशणपुष्पी
विषाणिका। अजगन्धाद्रवन्तीच
क्षीरिणीचात्रषोडशी ॥ ७६ ॥

ज्योतिष्मती बिम्बी शणपुष्पी विषा-
णिका अजगंधा द्रवंती और इनमें सोल-
हवीं क्षीरिणी ॥ ७६ ॥

शणपुष्पिचबिम्बीचछर्दनेहैमव
त्यपि । श्वेताज्योतिष्मतीचैवयो
ज्याशीर्षविरेचने ॥ ७७ ॥

इनमें शणपुष्पी बिम्बी हैमवती ये
छर्दनमें और श्वेता और ज्योतिष्मती ये
शिरके विरेचनमें युक्त करने योग्यहैं॥७७॥

एकादशावशिष्टायाःप्रयोज्यास्ता
विरेचने । इत्युक्तानामकर्मभ्यां
मूलिन्यःफलिनीःश्रृणु ॥ ७८ ॥

एकादश जो शेषहैं वे विरेचनमें प्रयोग
करने योग्यहैं ये नाम और कर्मोंसे
मूलिनी कही अब फलिनियोंको श्रवण
कर ॥ ७८ ॥

शंखिन्यथिवडङ्गानितरुषंमदना

निच । आनूपं स्थलजंचैवक्ली
तकंद्विविधंस्मृतम् ॥ ७९ ॥

शंखिनी वायिवडंग तरुष मैनफल
जल और स्थलमें पैदाहुआ दो प्रकारका
क्लीतक कहाहै ॥ ७९ ॥

प्रकीर्य्याचोदकीर्य्याचप्रत्यकृपु
ष्पीतथाभया। अन्तःकोटरपुष्पी
चहस्तिपण्याश्शारदम् ॥ ८० ॥

प्रकीर्यां उदकीर्यां प्रत्यकृपुष्पी
और अभया ( हरड़े ) अंतःकोटरपुष्पी
हस्तिपणिका शारद ॥ ८० ॥

कम्पिल्वकारग्वधयोःफलंयतकुट
जस्यच । धामार्गवमथेक्ष्वाकुजी
मूतंकृतवेधनम् ॥ ८१ ॥

कंपिछुक और अमलतासका फल
और कुटजका फल ये मूलिनी हैं धामार्गव
और इक्ष्वाकु जीमूत कृतवेधन ॥ ८१ ॥

मदनकुटजश्चैवत्रपुषंहस्तिपणिनी।
एतानिवमनेचैवयोज्यान्यास्थाप
नेषु च ॥ ८२ ॥

मदन कुटज तरुष हस्तिपणिनी ये
वमन और आस्थापनमें युक्तकरने
योग्यहैं ॥ ८२ ॥

दशयान्यवशिष्टानितान्युक्तानिवि
रेचने। नामकर्मेभिरुक्तानिफला
न्येकोनविंशतिः ॥ ८३ ॥

नासिकासे छर्दनमें प्रत्यकृपुष्पी कहीहै
दश जो शेषहैं वे विरेचनमें कहीहैं ये नाम
कर्मसे उन्नीस फल कहेहैं ॥ ८३ ॥

translation:
( 10 )
From the Charaka Samhita.

[Verse 75]
Hastidanti, Haimavati, Shyama, Trivrit, Ghuda, Saptala, Shvetanama, Pratyakshrenika, and Gavakshi — these are [the herbs enumerated].

Commentary: Elephant-tooth plant (Hastidanti), Haimavati (a Himalayan herb), Shyama (identified here as Haritaki/Harade), Nisoth, Adhoghuda (raisin/Munakka), or sugarcane, Saptala, Shvetanama, Pratyakshrenika, and Gavakshi — these are the nine. ||75||

[Verse 76]
Jyotishmati, Bimbi, Shanapushpi, Vishanika, Ajagandhaa, Dravanti, and Kshirini — these make the sixteenth group.

Commentary: Jyotishmati, Bimbi, Shanapushpi, Vishanika, Ajagandhaa, Dravanti, and among these the sixteenth is Kshirini. ||76||

[Verse 77]
Among these, Shanapushpi, Bimbi, and Haimavati are suitable for inducing vomiting (emesis), while Shveta and Jyotishmati are to be used for head-purification (shirovirechana). ||77||

[Verse 78]
The remaining eleven are suitable for use as purgatives. Thus, having described their names and actions, now hear about the Phalinyas (fruit-bearing herbs), after having described the Mulinyas (root-bearing herbs). ||78||

[Verse 79]
Shankhini, Vidanga, Tarusha, Madana — and also the two varieties of Klitaka, one growing in marshy land and one on dry ground, are to be known as two types.

Commentary: Shankhini, Vidanga (embelia), Tarusha, Mainphala — born in water and on land, Klitaka is said to be of two kinds. ||79||

[Verse 80]
Prakirya, Udakirya, Pratyakpushpi, and Abhaya (Haritaki/Harade), Antahkotarapushpi, and Hastipani — these belong to the autumnal group.

Commentary: Prakirya, Udakirya, Pratyakpushpi, and Abhaya (Harade), Antahkotarapushpi, and Hastipani — these are the autumnal ones. ||80||

[Verse 81]
The fruits of Kampillaka and Aragvadha, and also the fruit of Kutaja — these are the Mulinyas. Dhamargava, Ikshvaku, Jimuta, and Kritavedhana likewise.

Commentary: Kampiluka and Amaltas (Cassia fistula) fruits, and the fruit of Kutaja — these are Mulinyas. Dhamargava, Ikshvaku, Jimuta, and Kritavedhana. ||81||

[Verse 82]
Madana, Kutaja, Tarusha, and Hastipanini — these are to be employed both for emesis (vamana) and for enema (asthapana).

Commentary: Madana, Kutaja, Tarusha, and Hastipanini — these are suitable for use in emesis and in asthapana (enema). ||82||

[Verse 83]
The remaining ten of these have been described as purgatives. Named and described by their actions, the fruit-bearing herbs (Phalinyas) number nineteen.

Commentary: Pratyakpushpi has been mentioned for nasal emesis; the ten that remain are described as purgatives. Together, by name and action, nineteen fruits have been enumerated. ||83||

text:
सूत्रस्थानम् ।
( ११ )
Digitized By Siddhantas Gangesh Gyaan Kosha

सर्पिस्तैलंवसामज्ञास्नेहोदद्धःचतु
विध्ः । पानाभ्यञ्जनवस्त्यर्थं
नस्यार्थेचैवयोगतः ॥ ८४ ॥

घी तेल वसा मज्जा यह चार प्रकारका
स्नेह कहौहैं पान अभ्यंग बस्तिके और
नस्यके लिये योगसे ॥ ८४ ॥

स्नेहनाजीवनाबल्यावर्णोपचयव
धर्नाः । स्नेहाह्येतेषुविहितावात
पित्तकफापहाः ॥ ८५ ॥

ये चारों स्नेहन जीवन बलकारी और
वर्णकी वृद्धिकारकहैं वात पित्त कफके
नाशक स्नेह इनमें कहे हैं ॥ ८५ ॥

सौवर्चलंसैन्धवञ्चविडमौद्भिदमेव
च । सामुद्रेणसहेतानिपञ्चसुलव
णानिनच ॥ ८६ ॥

सौवर्चल सैंधव विड औद्भिद और
समुद्रका ये पांच लवण होतेहैं ॥ ८६ ॥

स्निग्धान्युष्णानितीक्ष्णानिदीपनी
यतमानिच ।आलेपनार्थेयुज्यन्ते
स्नेहस्वेदविधौतथा ॥ ८७ ॥

ये स्निग्ध उष्ण तीक्ष्ण दीपनीयोंमें
उत्तम होते हैंये आलेपनके लिये और
स्नेह स्वेदिविधिमें युक्त होतेहैं ॥ ८७ ॥

अधोभागोद्र्ध्वभागेषुनिरुहेष्वनुवा
सने । अभ्यञ्जनेभोजनार्थेशिरस
श्विरेचने ॥ ८८ ॥

अधोभाग ऊर्ध्व भागके निरुहोंमें अनु-

वासनमें अभ्यंगमें भोजनमें शिरके
विरेचनमें ॥ ८८ ॥

शस्त्रकर्मणिबस्त्यर्थमअनोच्छा
दनेषुच । अजीर्णनाहयोर्वातगु
ल्मेशूलतथोदरे ॥ ८९ ॥

शस्त्रकर्ममें बस्तिमें अंजन और
उत्सादनमें अजीर्ण और आनाहमें वात
गुल्म शूल और उदरमें ॥ ८९ ॥

उक्तानिलवणान्युद्धृंमूत्राण्यष्टौनि
बोधमे । मुख्यानियानिच्यहस्थानि
सर्वाण्यात्रेयशासने ॥ ९० ॥

ये लवण कहे इसके अनंतर मूत्रोंको
मेरेसे श्रवणकर जो सब आत्रेयके शास्त्रमें
मुख्य और इष्टहैं ॥ ९० ॥

अविमूत्रमजामूत्रंगोमूत्रंमाहिषंतथा
हस्तिमूत्रमथोष्ट्रस्यह्यस्यचखर
स्यच ॥ ९१ ॥

भेडका मूत्र अजाकामूत्र गोमूत्र भैंस-
कामूत्र हस्तिमूत्र ऊंटकामूत्र अश्वका
मूत्र खरकामूत्र ॥ ९१ ॥

उष्णतीक्ष्णमथोस्निग्धंकटुकंलव
णान्वितम् । मूत्रमुच्छादनेयुक्तं
युक्तमालेपनेषुच ॥ ९२ ॥

उष्ण तीक्षण रुक्ष कटु लवण से तयु
मूत्र होताहै वह उत्सादन और आले-
पनोंमें युक्त होताहै ॥ ९२ ॥

translation:
Sutrasthana (Chapter on Fundamental Principles)
Page 11

Verse 84:
Ghee, oil, fat (vasa), and marrow (majja) — these are the four kinds of sneha (oleaginous substances). They are used for drinking (pana), unction (abhyanga), enema (basti), and nasal administration (nasya).

Commentary 84: Ghee, oil, fat, and marrow are the four types of sneha. They are prescribed for drinking, unction, enema, and nasal treatment.

Verse 85:
These four oleaginous substances nourish, invigorate, strengthen, improve complexion, and build up the tissues. They are prescribed for these purposes and destroy the vitiation of vata, pitta, and kapha.

Commentary 85: These four snehas nourish, give life, strengthen, and enhance complexion. They are described as destroyers of vata, pitta, and kapha.

Verse 86:
Sauvarchala, saindhava, vida, audbhida, and samudra — along with samudra these are the five salts.

Commentary 86: Sauvarchala, saindhava, vida, audbhida, and samudra — these are the five salts.

Verse 87:
These (salts) are unctuous, hot, sharp, and most stimulating to digestion. They are used for external application (alepa) as well as for oleation and sudation (sveda) procedures.

Commentary 87: These are unctuous, hot, sharp, and most stimulating to digestion. They are used for external application and also in oleation and sudation therapies.

Verse 88:
(Sneha is used) in lower-purgative enemas (niruha), upper-cleansing procedures, unctuous enemas (anuvasana), unction (abhyanga), food preparation, and cephalic purgation (shirovirechana).

Commentary 88: In lower and upper cleansing enemas, in unctuous enemas, in unction, in food, and in cephalic purgation.

Verse 89:
Also in surgical procedures, for basti (enema), for anjana (collyrium), for massage (utsadana), in indigestion, in bloating (anaha), in vata disorders, gulma (abdominal tumors), colic (shula), and abdominal diseases (udara).

Commentary 89: In surgery, enema, collyrium, and massage; in indigestion, bloating, vata disorders, gulma, colic, and abdominal diseases.

Verse 90:
Having described the salts, now hear of the eight urines that are chief and desirable, as taught in the treatise of Atreya.

Commentary 90: After describing the salts, hear of the urines — listen to those that are chief and esteemed in the teaching of Atreya.

Verse 91:
The urine of sheep, goat, cow, buffalo, elephant, camel, horse, and donkey.

Commentary 91: Sheep's urine, goat's urine, cow's urine, buffalo's urine, elephant's urine, camel's urine, horse's urine, and donkey's urine.

Verse 92:
Urine is hot, sharp, non-unctuous, pungent, and saline in nature. It is suitable for utsadana (cleansing massage) and also for external application (alepa).

Commentary 92: Urine, being hot, sharp, dry, pungent, and saline, is suitable for cleansing massage and external applications.

text:
( १२ )
चरकसंहितायाम्
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

युक्मास्थापनेयुक्तंमूत्रञापिविरेचने । स्वेदेष्वपिचतयुक्तमानाहेषुगदेषुच ॥ ९३ ॥

आस्थापन और विरेचनमेंभी मूत्र युक्त है स्वेदोंमें वह युक्त है आनाहोंमें ३ उदरेष्वथचार्शस्सुगुल्मकुष्ठिकलासिषु । तदुक्तमुपनाहेषुपारिषेकेतथैवच ॥ ९४ ॥

उदरके रेगोंमें अर्श गुल्म कुष्ठ किलासियोंमें युक्त होताहै वह उपनाहोंमें और परिषेकमें युक्त है ॥ ९४ ॥

दीपनीयंविषघ्नंचिकिमिघ्नंचोपिदश्यते । पाण्डुरोगोपमृषानामुत्तमंशर्मचोच्यते ॥ ९५ ॥

और दीपनीय विषनाशक और क्रिम नाशक कहाहै और पांडुरोगियोंको तो सर्वथा उत्तम कहा है ॥ ९५ ॥

श्लेष्माणशमयेत्पीतंमारुतश्चानुलोमयेत् । कर्षेत्पित्तमधोभागिमत्यस्मिन्गुणसंग्रहः ॥ ९६ ॥

पीनेसे श्लेष्माको शांत करता है और वातको अनुलोम करता है और पित्तको अधेभागमें खींचताहै ये इसमें गुणहैं ९६

सामान्येनमयोक्तंतुपृथक्त्वेनमवक्ष्यते । अविमूत्रंसितिकस्यात् त्निग्धंपित्ताविरोधिचन ॥ ९७ ॥

यह मैं सामान्यसे कहा अब पृथक्

मूत्रोंके गुणको कहताहूं भेडका मूत्र तिक्तस्निग्ध पित्तका अविरोध होता है ॥ ९७॥

आजंकषायमधुरंपथ्यंदोषानिहन्तिच । गव्यंसमधुरंकिञ्चिद्दोषघ्नंक्रिमिकुष्ठनुत् ॥ ९८ ॥

अजाका मूत्र कसेला मधुर पथ्य दोषोंका नाशक होताहै गौका मूत्र मधुर किंचित् दोषोंका नाशक क्रिमिकुष्ठ ९८

कण्डूलशमयेत्पीतंसम्यग्दोषोदरेहितम् । अर्शःशोफोदरघ्नंतुसक्षारंमाहिषंसरम् ॥ ९९ ॥

कंडू इनको पीनेसे नष्टकरता है और उदरके दोषोंमें अत्यंतहितहै भैंसका मूत्र अर्श शोफ उदर इनकानाशक और क्षार और सर ( दस्तावर ) होता है ॥ ९९ ॥

हस्तिकंलवणंमूत्रंहितन्तुक्रिमिकुष्ठिनाम् । प्रशस्तंबद्धविण्मूत्रविषश्लेष्मामयार्शसाम् ॥ १०० ॥

हस्तिकामूत्र लवण है और क्रिम कुष्ठियोंको हित है और बद्ध विण्मूत्र विष कफ अर्श इन रोगोंमें उत्तम है ॥१००॥

सितिकंश्वासकासघ्नमर्शोघ्नंचैष्ट्रमुच्यते । वाजिनांतित्तककटुकंकुष्ठव्रणविषापहम् ॥ १०१ ॥

और ऊंटकामूत्र श्वास कास अर्शका नाशक और तिक्त कहा है घोडोकामूत्र तित्त कटु होता है और कुष्ठ व्रण विष इनका नाशक है ॥ १०१ ॥

Charaka Samhita
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

Urine is also suitable for asthapana (enema) and virechana (purgation). It is appropriate in fomentation therapies and in conditions of abdominal distension and disease. [93]

Urine is suitable in asthapana and virechana therapies; it is suitable in fomentation, in abdominal distension — and in udara (abdominal diseases), arsha (piles), gulma (abdominal tumors), kushtha (skin diseases), and kilasa (a type of skin discoloration); it is appropriate in upanaha (poulticing) and parisheka (affusion/sprinkling) as well. [94]

It is seen to be dipaniya (digestive stimulant), vishaghna (anti-toxic), and krimighna (anti-parasitic). For those suffering from pandu-roga (anemia/jaundice), it is said to be in every way excellent. [95]

When drunk, it pacifies kapha (phlegm) and promotes the proper downward movement of vata (wind). It draws pitta downward — these are its qualities. [96]

I have described this in general; now I shall describe each urine individually. The urine of a sheep is bitter and unctuous, and does not aggravate pitta. [97]

The urine of a goat is astringent, sweet, wholesome, and destroys the doshas. The urine of a cow is somewhat sweet, destroys the doshas to a degree, and alleviates krimi (parasites) and kushtha (skin disease). [98]

When drunk properly, it destroys itching (kandu) and is very beneficial in abdominal disorders. Buffalo urine destroys arsha (piles), shopha (swelling), and udara (abdominal disease); it is alkaline and laxative. [99]

The urine of an elephant is saline and beneficial for those suffering from krimi (parasitic infestation) and kushtha (skin disease). It is excellent for conditions of constipation of stool and urine, poisoning, kapha disorders, and arsha (piles). [100]

The urine of a camel is said to destroy shvasa (dyspnea), kasa (cough), and arsha (piles), and is bitter. The urine of a horse is bitter and pungent, and removes kushtha (skin disease), vrana (wounds), and visha (poison). [101]

सूत्रस्थानम्
( १३ )

खरमूत्रमपस्मारोन्मादग्रहिविनाश
नम् । इतीहोक्तानिमूत्राणियथा
सामर्थ्ययोगत: ॥ १०२ ॥

गधेकासूत्र अपस्मार उन्माद ग्रह
इनका विनाशक होता है ये सब मूत्र
अपनीशुद्धिके सामर्थ्यनुसार कहे१०२॥

अतःक्षीराणिवक्ष्यन्तेकर्मचैषांगु
णाश्रये । अविक्षीरमजाक्षीरंगो
क्षीरंमाहिषंचयत् ॥ १०३ ॥

इसके अनंतर दुधोंको कहते हैं और
इनके जो कर्म और गुण हैं उनको
कहते हैं भेड बकरी गौ भैंस ॥ १०३ ॥

उष्ट्णामथनागीनांवडवायाःस्त्रि
यास्तथा । प्रायशोमधुरंस्निग्धंशी
तंस्तन्यंपयःस्मृतम् ॥ १०४ ॥

ऊंटनी हथिनी घोडी और स्त्री इनका
दूध प्रायः मधुर स्निग्ध शीतल है और
स्त्रिके स्तनोंका दूध ॥ १०४ ॥

प्रीणनंवृंहणंवृष्यंमेध्यंबल्यंमनस्क
रम् । जीवनीयंश्रमहरंश्वासकास
निबर्हणम् ॥ १०५ ॥

प्रीणन बृंहण वृष्य मेध्य बल्य और
मनकी प्रसन्नता कारक है जीवनीय है
श्रमहरहै श्वास कासका नाशक॥१०५॥

हन्तिशोणितपित्तश्वसन्धानंविह
तस्यच । सर्वप्राणभृतांसात्म्यंश
मनंशोधनंतथा ॥ १०६ ॥

और शोणित पित्तको हतेहैं विहत
( घाव ) का संधान करता है सब
प्राण धारियोंका सात्म्य शमन और
शोधन है ॥ १०६ ॥

तृष्णाग्नंदीपनीयंचश्रेष्ठंक्षीणक्षते
षुच । पाण्डुरोगेऽम्लपित्तेचशोषे
गुल्मेतथोदरे ॥ १०७ ॥

तृष्णाका नाशक अग्नि दीपन और
क्षीण और क्षतमें श्रेष्ठ कहा है पांडुरोग
अम्लपित्त शोष गुल्म उदर ॥ १०७ ॥

अतीसारज्वरेदाहेश्वयथौचविषी
यते । योनिशुक्रदोषेषुमूत्रेष्वम
सरेषुच ॥ १०८ ॥

अतीसार ज्वरदाह सूजन इनमें श्रेष्ठ
कहा है योनि शुक्रके दोषोंमें मूत्र और
प्रदरके दोषोंमें ॥ १०८ ॥

पुरीषेऽथितेपथ्यंवातपित्तविका
रिणाम् । नस्यालेपावगाहेषुवम
नास्थापनेषुच ॥ १०९ ॥

पुरीषमें मथितमें और वात पित्तके
विकारोंमें पथ्यकहाहै नस्य लेप अवगाह
( स्नान ) वमन आस्थापन ॥ १०९ ॥

विरेचनेस्नेहनेचपयःसर्वत्रयुज्यते ।
यथाकमंक्षीरगुणानिकैकस्यपृथ
ज्पृथक् ॥ ११० ॥

विरेचन स्नेहन इन सबमें दूध युक्त

[Verse 102]
The urine of the donkey destroys epilepsy, insanity, and demonic afflictions. Thus the urines have been described here according to their respective capacities and uses.

[Commentary on 102]
The urine of the donkey destroys epilepsy, insanity, and demonic possession. All these urines have been described according to their purificatory potencies.

[Verse 103]
Next, the milks will be described along with their actions and qualities. These are: the milk of the sheep, the goat, the cow, and the buffalo.

[Commentary on 103]
After this, the milks are described, and their actions and qualities are enumerated — those of the ewe, goat, cow, and buffalo.

[Verse 104]
The milk of the she-camel, the she-elephant, the mare, and the woman — all these milks are by nature sweet, unctuous, and cooling. Such is the milk from the breast of a woman.

[Commentary on 104]
The milk of the she-camel, she-elephant, mare, and woman is generally sweet, unctuous, and cool; and so is a woman's breast milk.

[Verse 105]
It nourishes, builds bulk, promotes virility, enhances intellect, gives strength, gladdens the mind, sustains life, relieves fatigue, and destroys cough and asthma.

[Commentary on 105]
It nourishes, builds the body, promotes virility, sharpens the intellect, gives strength, gladdens the mind, is life-sustaining, removes fatigue, and destroys cough and asthma.

[Verse 106]
It destroys hemorrhage and disorders of bile-blood, heals wounds, is wholesome for all living beings, and brings pacification and purification.

[Commentary on 106]
It checks hemorrhage and disorders of pitta-blood, heals wounds, is wholesome for all creatures, and both pacifies and purifies.

[Verse 107]
It is excellent for quenching thirst and kindling the digestive fire; it is especially commended in conditions of wasting, injury, anemia, hyperacidity, consumption, abdominal tumors, and abdominal disorders.

[Commentary on 107]
It destroys thirst and stimulates digestion; it is best for those who are emaciated or wounded — for anemia, hyperacidity, consumption, abdominal tumors, and distension of the abdomen.

[Verse 108]
It is recommended in diarrhea, fever, burning sensation, edema, and in cases of poisoning; also for disorders of the female generative organ, disorders of semen, disorders of urine, and conditions of prolapse.

[Commentary on 108]
It is excellent in diarrhea, fever, burning sensation, and swelling; and in disorders of the female organs, of semen, of urine, and in conditions of prolapse.

[Verse 109]
In the feces and in churned preparations, it is wholesome for disorders of vata and pitta; and it is used in nasal therapy, application, immersion baths, emesis, and enemas.

In fecal conditions and in churned preparations, and in disorders of vata and pitta, milk is said to be wholesome; it is used in nasal therapy, as a topical application, in immersion baths, in emesis, and in enemas.

Milk is used universally in purgation and oleation therapies. The individual qualities of each milk will now be described separately.

[Commentary on 110]

text:
( १२ )

कहाँहै और यथा क्रमसे एक २ दूधके
पृथक् २ गुणोंको ॥ ११० ॥
अन्नपानादिकेऽध्यायेभूयोवक्ष्या
म्यशेषतः । अथापरेत्नयोवृक्षाः
पृथग्येफलमूलिभिः ॥ १११ ॥
अन्नपानादिक अध्यायमें संपूर्ण रूपसे
कहूंगा इसके अनंतर फल मूलवानोंसे
अन्य तीन वृक्ष ये भिन्नहैं ॥ १११ ॥
रूह्यकाश्मन्तकास्तेषामिदंकर्म
पृथकपृथक् ॥ वमनेऽश्मन्तकंविव
धात्स्तुहीक्षीरिविरेचने ॥ ११२ ॥
कि थूहर आक बहेड़ा उनका पृथक् २
कर्म यह है वमनमें बहेड़ेको जाने और
थूहरके दूधको विरेचनमें ॥ ११२ ॥
क्षीरमर्कस्यविज्ञेयंवमनेसिवंरेचने ।
इमांस्त्रीनपरान्वृक्षानाहुर्येषांहिता
स्तचः ॥ ११३ ॥
और आकका दूध वमन और विरेचन
दोनोंमें जानना इन तीन अन्य वृक्षोंको
कहतेहैं जिनकीत्वचा हितहै ॥ ११३ ॥
पुितकःकृष्णगन्धाचितिछकश्वत
थातरुः । विरेचनेप्रयोक्तव्यः पूित
कःस्तिछकस्तथा ॥ ११४ ॥
पूितक कृष्णगंधा और तिछक वृक्ष
पूितक और तिछक ये दोनों विरेचनमें
प्रयोग करनेयोग्य हैं ॥ ११४ ॥

कृष्णगन्धापरीसर्पेशोथेष्वर्शस्सु
चोच्यते । दद्रुविद्रिधिगण्डेषुकुष्ठे
ष्वप्यलजीषुच ॥ ११५ ॥
और कृष्ण गंधा परीसर्प शोथ और
अर्शं रोगोंमेंकहा है दद्रु विद्रिध गंड कुष्ठ
और अलजी इनमेंभी ॥ ११५ ॥
षड्वृक्षाञ्शोधनानेतानिपिवया
द्विचक्षणः । इत्युक्ताःफलमूलि
न्यःक्षेहाश्वलवणानिनच ॥ ११६ ॥
इन छः पूर्वोक्त शोधनके वृक्षोंका
बुद्धिमान् मनुष्यजाने ये फलिनी मूलिनी
स्नेह और लवण ॥ ११६ ॥
मूत्रंक्षीराणिवृक्षाश्चषड्येदृष्टाःपय
स्तवचः । औषधीर्नमरूपाभ्यां
जानतेह्यजपावने ॥ ११७ ॥
मूत्र और दूध और त्वचाके छः वृक्ष
जो देखे वे कहें नामरूपसे औषधोंको
वनमें अजाके पालक ॥ ११७ ॥
अविपाश्चेवगोपाश्चयेचान्येवनवा
सिनः । ननामज्ञानमात्रेणरूप
ज्ञानेनवापुनः ॥ ११८ ॥
और भेड़के पालक गोप और जो
अन्य वनवासी हैं वे जानते हैं नामके
ज्ञानमात्रसे वा रूपके ज्ञानसे ॥ ११८ ॥
औषधीनांपरांप्राप्तिंकश्चिद्वेदितुम
हंति । योगज्ञस्तस्यरूपज्ञस्तासां
तत्विदुच्यते ॥ ११९ ॥
translation:
(Page 12)

He says: and thus, in order, the separate qualities of each kind of milk are described. (110)

The topic of food and drink will be discussed more fully in the relevant chapter. Beyond that, three other trees differ from those that bear fruit and roots. (111)

The rohitaka, aśhmantaka, and others — each has its own distinct action. Know that the aśhmantaka is used in emesis (vamana), and the latex of the thūhar (snuhi/euphorbia) in purgation (virechana). (112)

The milk of the arka (calotropis) is to be known as useful in both emesis and purgation. These three additional trees are spoken of as those whose bark is beneficial. (113)

The pūtika, kṛṣhṇagandhā, and tichchhaka trees — the pūtika and tichchhaka are both to be employed in purgation. (114)

The kṛṣhṇagandhā is indicated in erysipelas (parisarpa), edema (śhotha), hemorrhoids (arśhas), and is also mentioned in ringworm (dadru), abscess (vidradhi), goiter (gaṇḍa), leprosy-type skin disorders (kuṣhṭha), and boils (alaji). (115)

The wise person should drink these six purificatory trees. Thus have been described those that bear fruit, those that are root-plants, fats, and salts. (116)

Urine, milk, and the bark of the six trees that are seen — those who tend goats in the forest know the medicines by name and form. (117)

The shepherds of sheep and the cowherds, and others who dwell in the forest, know through mere knowledge of names or through knowledge of forms. (118)

Hardly anyone is able to attain the full knowledge of medicinal plants. One who knows both their practical application (yoga) and their form (rūpa) is truly called a knower of their essence. (119)

Digitized By Siddha Gyaan Kosha
सूत्रस्थानम् १
( १५ )

औषधियोंकी उत्तम प्राप्तिको कोई नहीं जानसकता है जो उनके योगका ज्ञाता और रूपका ज्ञाता है वही तत्ववित् ( ज्ञाता ) कहाता है ॥ ११९ ॥

किंपुनर्योविजानीयादोषधीःसर्वदाभिषक् । रूपन्तासान्तुयोविद्यादेशकालोपापादितम् ॥१२०॥

और जो वैद्य औषधियोंको सर्वथा जाने तो क्या कहना है देशकालके विभागके ज्ञानसे जो ॥ १२० ॥

पुरुषंपुरुषंविक्ष्यसिविज्ञेयोभिषक्तम: । यथाविषंयथाशस्त्रंयथाग्निरशिनिर्यथा ॥ १२१ ॥

पुरुष २ को देखकर उन औषधियोंके रूप जो जाने वह अत्यंत श्रेष्ठ भिषक् जानना जैसा विष जैसा शस्त्र जैसा अग्नि जैसा वज्र है ॥ १२१ ॥

तथौषधमविज्ञातंविज्ञातमसृतंयथा । औषधंह्यनभिज्ञातंनामरूप गुणैश्चिभिः ॥ १२२ ॥

तैसीही बिनाजानी औषध है और जानी हुई अमृतके समान है नामरूप गुण इनतीनोंसे नहीं जाना हुआ औषध १२२

विज्ञातंवापिदुर्युक्तंयुक्तिबाह्येनभेषजम् । योगादिपिविषंतीक्ष्णमुत्तमंभेषजंभवेत् ॥ १२३ ॥

और जाना हुआभी दुष्टयोगसे वा

युक्तिके बिना युक्त भेषज अधम जानना योगसेतीक्ष्ण विषभी उत्तम औषध होता है ॥ १२३ ॥

भेषजंवापिदुर्युक्तंतीक्ष्णसंपद्यते विषम् । तस्मान्निभिषजायुक्तंयुक्तिबाह्येनभेषजम् ॥ १२४ ॥

और दुर्युक्त होनेसे भेषजभी तीक्ष्ण विष होजाता तिससे है बुद्धिमान् वैद्यको युक्तिसे अन्यथायुक्त जो कोई भेषजहै १२४

धीमताकिञ्चिदोदयंजीविताroग्यकांक्षिणा । कुर्यान्निपतितोमूर्ध्निसशेषंवासवाशिनः ॥ १२५ ॥

वह यदि जीवितके आरोग्यको चाहै तो ग्रहण न करनी इंद्रकावञ्च मस्तकपर पडै तो शेषको छोड देता है अर्थात् मारतानहीं ॥ १२५ ॥

सशेषमातुरंकुर्यान्नित्वञ्चमतमौषधम् । दुःखितायशयानायशद्धानायरोगिणे ॥ १२६ ॥

और मूर्खकी संमत ( दी ) औषध रोगीको शेषनहीं रखती जो माञ्का अभिमानी दुःखित सोते हुये श्रद्धावान् रोगीको ॥ १२६ ॥

योभेषजमविज्ञायप्राज्ञमानीप्रयच्छति । तस्याचमृत्युदूतस्यदुर्मतेस्त्यक्तधर्मणः ॥ १२७ ॥

बिनाजाने औषध देता है मृत्युके दूत

Sutrasthana 1
(15)

No one can know the highest quality of medicines unless one is knowledgeable about their combinations and their forms — only such a person is called a true knower (of medicines). || 119 ||

What then of the physician who knows all medicinal herbs at all times? One who knows their forms as they arise according to place and time. || 120 ||

Examining each person individually, the physician must be known as the most excellent — just as poison, just as a weapon, just as fire, just as the thunderbolt. || 121 ||

Thus, a medicine that is unknown is like poison; but one that is known is like nectar. A medicine that has not been known by its name, form, and qualities (these three) — || 122 ||

Even a well-known medicine, if used improperly or applied without proper reasoning, is to be considered inferior. But even a sharp poison, when used with proper combination, becomes an excellent medicine. || 123 ||

A medicine improperly used becomes a sharp poison. Therefore, the intelligent physician must never use medicine without proper reasoning and method. || 124 ||

A wise person desiring life and health should not accept something that, falling upon the head like the stroke of Indra's thunderbolt, destroys everything — that is, it does not leave the patient alive. || 125 ||

The medicine approved by a fool does not leave the patient alive — especially one who is proud, suffering, lying down, and lacking faith. || 126 ||

One who administers medicine without knowing it, thinking himself learned — such a person of corrupt conduct and abandoned duty is the messenger of death. || 127 ||

Without knowing, one who gives medicine is a messenger of death —

translation:
( 16 )
From the Charaka Samhita.

127. One who abandons righteous conduct is said to be of corrupt mind.

128. Even conversing with such a person leads a man to hell. The venom of a serpent is dangerous, yet drinking copper prepared by fire is equally so.

129. Being burned in the most intense fire, or eating lumps of iron heated to extreme heat, is preferable — but do not approach for refuge a physician who merely wears the garb of a learned man without truly possessing the knowledge.

130. A physician who desires to advance in the virtues of his profession should not accept food, drink, or wealth from a patient afflicted with disease. Thus a wise and modest physician preserves the wealth of his qualities.

131. He should make every effort as though he were the giver of life to human beings. That medicine alone is truly appropriate which brings about recovery from disease.

132. And that physician is foremost among physicians who liberates patients from their diseases — for success is declared to come from the correct application of all procedures.

133. Success, fame, and all good qualities are declared to belong to the most excellent physician endowed with all virtues. Thus ends this section.

Here follow the summary verses:

134. The reason for the origin of Ayurveda, the exposition of that origin, the authorization of its teaching, and the final determination of Ayurveda — these are the topics of the following verses.

135. The complete knowledge of all causes constitutes the purpose of Ayurveda. The causative factors, the dosas (humors), and the collection of medicines — these are to be known in full.

136. The rasas (tastes), substances with their properties, the collection of drugs of various kinds, plants with roots, plants bearing fruit, fats and oils, and the various salts —

पाटलाश्वाग्निमन्थाश्विबिल्वश्योनाकमेवच । काश्मर्यंशालपर्णींचपृश्निपर्णींनिदिग्धिकाम्।।९।।

पाटल अरणी बिलसयोनाक केशरशाल पणी पृश्निपणीं निदिग्धका, ( कटेहली ) बलांश्वदंष्ट्रंबृहतीमेरण्डंसगुनंनवम् यवान्कुलुत्थान्कोलानिगुडूचींमदनानिच ॥ १० ॥

वला, गोखरू, कटेहरी, अरंड सांठ जौ कुलथी कोल बैर-मिरचांगिलोह मैनफल ॥ १० ॥

पलाशड्कृतृणंचैवस्नेहांश्वलवणानिच । उदावर्तेविबन्धेषुयुंज्यादास्थापनेसदा ॥ ११ ॥

पलाश कतृण स्नेह और लवण इनको उदावर्ते विबंध आस्थापनोंमें सदा युक्त करै ॥ ११ ॥

अतएवौषधगतात्संकल्प्यमनुवासनम्।मारुतघ्निमितिप्रोक्तःसंग्रहःपाञ्चकिर्मिकः ॥ १२ ॥

इनहीं औषधोंके समूहसे अनुवासनकी कल्पना करै यह मारुतका नाशक पांच-कर्मिक संग्रह कहा है ॥ १२ ॥

तान्यपिस्थितदोषाणांस्नेहस्वेदोपादनैः। पञ्चकर्माणिकुर्वीतमात्राकालौविचारयन् ॥ १३ ॥

प्राप्त है दोष जिनको ऐसे मनुष्योंको स्नेह स्वेद उपादनोंसे पांच कमोंको मात्रा कालको विचारकर करै ॥ १३ ॥

मात्राकालाश्रयायुक्तिःसिद्धिंकौशतिष्ठता । तिष्टयुपारियुक्तिज्ञोद्रव्यज्ञानवतांसदा ॥ १४ ॥

मात्रा और कालके आधीन युक्तिमें सिद्धि स्थित है और द्रव्यके ज्ञानवानोंके ऊपर सदैव युक्तिका ज्ञाता टिकताहै १४

अतऊर्ध्वंप्रवक्ष्यामियवागुर्विविधौषधाः । विविधानांविकाराणांत
translation:
(18)

Verse 6: In cases of excess phlegm (kapha) and bile (pitta), the physician should administer emesis (vamana) without causing harm to the body of the patient. (6)

Verse 7: Trivrita, triphala, danti, nilini, samalavaca, kampillaka, gavakshi, akshirini, and mudakitika — these are the herbs to be used. (7)
That is: Nisoth, triphala, danti, nilini, satala, vacha, kampillaka, gavakshi, kshirini, and udakiya. (7)

Verse 8: Pilu, aragvadha, raksha, dravanti, and nichula — these should be used for purging (virechana) in disorders of the digestive system. (8)
That is: Pilu, amaltas, munakka, dravanti, nichula — administer these for cleansing disorders of the digestive tract through purgation. (8)

Verse 9: Patala, shyonaका, agnimantha, bilva, shyonaka, kashmarya, shalparni, prishniparni, and kantakari — these too should be included. (9)
That is: Patala, arani, bilva, shyonaka, keshar, shalparni, prishniparni, kantakari (katehli); also bala, gokshura, brihati, eranda, shatavari, yava (barley), kulattha, kola, guduchi, and madana fruit. (10)

Verse 11: Palasha, kutrina grass, fats (sneha), and salts — these should always be employed in cases of udavarta (upward movement of wind) and constipation (vibandha) in asthapana enema preparations. (11)

Verse 12: From these very medicinal substances, the anuvasana (oil-based enema) should also be formulated. This collection, known as the Panchakarmika group, is proclaimed as the destroyer of vata disorders. (12)

Verse 13: For those patients in whom the doshas have become established, the five therapeutic procedures (panchakarma) should be performed after proper oleation (sneha) and fomentation (sveda), carefully considering the appropriate dose and timing. (13)

Verse 14: Success depends on correct dose, proper timing, and sound judgment (yukti); and among those who possess knowledge of substances, the one who truly knows the art of application (yukti) always stands supreme. (14)

Now I shall describe in detail the various gruels (yavagu) and medicinal preparations for the treatment of various disorders — [text continues]

सूत्रस्थानम् ।
( १९ )

त्साध्यानांनिवृत्तये ॥ १५ ॥
इसके अनन्तर अनेक प्रकारके औषधोंकी यवागुओंको अनेक प्रकारके विकार और उनके साध्योंकी निवृत्तिके लिये कहताहूं॥ १५ ॥

पिप्पलीपिप्पलीमूलचव्यचित्रक नागरैः । यवागूदीपनीयास्याच्छुलघ्नीचोपसादिता ॥ १६ ॥
पीपल, पीपलामूल, चव्य, चीता, सोंठ इनकी बनाई यवागू दीपनी और शूलनाशक होतीहै ॥ १६ ॥

दधिथिविल्वचाङ्गेरीतकदाडिमसाधिता । पाचनीग्राहणिपेयासवातेपाञ्चमूलिकौ॥ १७ ॥
दधिथ(कैथ) बेल चांगेरी तक अनार इनकी बनाई यवागू पाचनी और ग्राहिणी होतीहै और वात सहित रोग होयतो पंचमूलकी यवागू हित होतीहै ॥१७ ॥

शालपर्णीबलाबिल्वैःपृश्निपर्ण्यिचसाधिता । दाडिमाम्लाहितापेयापित्तश्लेष्मातिसारिणाम् । १८।
शालपणीं बला बेल पृश्निपणीं इनसे बनाई यवागू अनारकी खटाई मिलाकर पित्त कफके अतिसार विकारियोंको पीने योगथैं ॥ १८ ॥

पयस्यर्द्धोदकेच्छागेहीवेरोत्पलनागरैः । पेयारक्तातिसारग्निपृश्नीपण्यिचसाधिता ॥ १९ ॥
आधे जलके बकरीके दूधमें हाइवेर कमल सोंठ पृश्निपणीं इनकी बनी यवागू पीनेसे रक्तातिसारका नाश करती है ॥ १९ ॥

दध्यात्सातिविषापेयांसामेसाम्लां सनागराम् । श्वदंष्ट्राकण्टकारीभ्यांमूत्रकृच्छेसफाणिताम्॥ २०।
आम सहित रोग होयतो अतीस और अम्ल सहित और सोंठकी और गोखरू कटेढली फाणित सहित इनकी मूत्रकृच्छ्रमें यवागूको दे ॥ २० ॥

विडङ्गपिप्पलीमूलशिग्रुभिर्मिरचेनच । तक्रसिद्धायवागूःस्यात्क्रिमिघ्नीसमुवर्चिका॥ २१॥
वायविडंग पीपलामूल सहिंजना मिरच सुवर्चिका इनकी तक्रमें सिद्ध यवागू किमि नाशक होती है ॥ २१ ॥

मृद्वीकाशारिवालाजपिप्पलीमधुनागरैः । पिपासाग्नीविषग्नीचसोमराजीिवपाचिता ॥ २२ ॥
मुनक्का शारिवा खील पीपल सहत नागर इनकी सोमराजीमें पकाई यवागू विष नाशक होतीहै ॥ २२ ॥

सिद्धावराहिनियूहेयवागूबृंहणीमता । गवेधुकानांमृष्टानांकर्षणीयासमाक्षिका ॥ २३ ॥
वराहके निगृहमें बनाई भुने गेहूंकी यवागू बृंहणी कही है और सहत मिली कर्षणीया कही है ॥ २३ ॥

Sutrasthana (Chapter on Fundamental Principles)
(Page 19)

For the alleviation of those ailments — Verse 15
After this, I shall describe the various types of medicinal yavagus (medicinal gruels/porridges) prepared from numerous kinds of medicines, for the cure of various disorders and their treatable conditions. 15.

Verse 16: A yavagu prepared with long pepper (pippali), long pepper root, chavya, chitraka, and dry ginger (nagara) is digestive-stimulating and pain-relieving. That is, the gruel made from pippali, pippali root, chavya, chitraka (chita), and dry ginger is digestive and destroys colic pain. 16.

Verse 17: A yavagu prepared with kapittha (kaitha/wood apple), bilva (bael), changeri (wood sorrel), buttermilk, and pomegranate is digestive and binding (grahani). And when disease is accompanied by vata disorders, the yavagu made from the five-root formula (panchamula) is beneficial. 17.

Verse 18: A yavagu prepared with shalparni, bala, bilva, and prishniparni, mixed with pomegranate sourness (amla), is suitable for drinking by those suffering from diarrhea due to pitta and kapha disorders. 18.

Verse 19: A yavagu prepared with goat's milk in half water, along with hrivera, lotus, dry ginger, and prishniparni — drinking this destroys bloody diarrhea (raktatisar). 19.

Verse 20: When disease is present with ama (undigested matter), give a yavagu made with ativisha and sour substances along with dry ginger, and with gokhru (gokshura), kataeli, and phanita (molasses concentrate), for urinary obstruction (mutrakriccha). 20.

Verse 21: A yavagu prepared in buttermilk with vidanga, pippali root, shigru (drumstick), black pepper, and suvarchika is a destroyer of intestinal worms. 21.

Verse 22: A yavagu cooked in somaraji with munakka (dried grapes), sariva, laja (roasted grain), pippali, and dry ginger is a destroyer of poison. 22.

Verse 23: A yavagu prepared in the broth of wild boar, made from roasted wheat grains, is said to be nourishing (brinhani), and when mixed with honey it is said to be reducing/scraping (karshani). 23.

चरकसंहितायाम् ।

सर्पिष्मतीवहुतिलाऌहनीलवणा
न्विता । कुशामलकिनर्यूहेश्या
माकानांविरूक्षणी ॥ २४ ॥

अधिक तिल और घी जिसमें हो
ऐसी लवण मिली यवागू स्नेहिनी होती
है–कुशा और आंवलोंके निर्यूहमें साम-
ककी बनी यवागू विरूक्षणी कही है २४

दशमूलीश्ठाकासिहकाश्वासक
फापहा । यमकेमदिरासिद्धापका
शयरुजापहा ॥ २५ ॥

दश मूलमें पकाई कास श्वास हिका
कफ इनकी नाशक होती है यमकमें
मदिराकी बनी यवागू पकाशयके रोगको
दूर करती है ॥ २५ ॥

शाकैमांसैस्तिलैमाषैःसिद्धावर्चो
निरस्यित । जम्बूआ्रास्तिदधि
थाम्लबिल्वैःसांग्राहिकीमता २६

शाक मांस तिल उडद इनकी यवागू
मलको निकासती है जामुन आम इनकी
गुठली दाधित्य अम्ल बेल इनकी यवागू
संग्राहिणी मानी है ॥ २६ ॥

क्षारिचित्रकहिङ्गवम्लवेतसैर्भेदनी
मता । अभयापिप्पलीमूलविश्वै
वातानुलोमनी ॥ २७ ॥

क्षार चीता हींग अमलवेत इनकी
यवागू भेदिनी कही है–हरड पीपलामूल
सोंठ इनकी यबागू वातके अनुलोम
करती है ॥ २७ ॥

तकसिद्धायवागूःस्याद्घृतव्याप
तिनाशिनी । तैलव्यापिदशस्ता
तुतक्रिपण्याकसाधिता ॥२८॥

मठेमें बनाई यवागू घृतसे पैदाहुये रोग
को नष्ट करती है और मठेके पिण्याकमें
बनाई यवागू तैलसे पैदाहुये रोगमें
श्रेष्ठ है ॥ २८ ॥

गव्यमांसरसैःसाम्लाविषमञ्वर
नाशिनी । कण्ठ्यायवानांयमके
पिप्पल्यामलकैःश्रिता ॥ २९ ॥

गोमांसके रसमें बनी जो अम्लसहित
यवागू है वह विषमज्वरकी नष्टकरती
है जौके यमकमें पीपल और आमलोंकी
बनाई यवागूकंठको हितहोती है ॥२९॥

ताम्रचूड़रसेसिद्धारेतोमार्गरुजा
पहा। समाषविदलावृष्याघृतक्षी
रोप साधिता ॥ ३० ॥

ताम्रचूड ( मुर्गा ) के रसमें सिद्धतो
वीर्यके मार्गकाजो रोग उसकी नाशक
है और उडदकी दालसाहित होय और
दूधमें बनाई होयतो वीर्य वर्द्धक होती है ३०

उपोदिकादिघिष्यान्तुसिद्धामदवि
नाशिनी ॥ क्षुधंहन्यादपामार्ग
क्षीरगोधारसेश्रिता ॥ ३१ ॥

पोई और दही से सिद्ध तो मदको
नष्ट करती है और ओंगा दूध गोधा-
कारस इनमें पकाई यवागू क्षुधाको नष्ट
करती है ॥ ३१ ॥

translation:
( 20 )
Charaka Samhita

[Verse 24]
A yavagu (thin gruel) prepared with an abundance of sesame and ghee, combined with salt, is unctuous (snehinī); and that prepared with the expressed decoction of kusha grass and āmalakī (Indian gooseberry) is drying (virūkshaṇī). (24)

When sesame and ghee are present in abundance along with salt, such yavagu is unctuous; that prepared in the decoction of kusha and āmalakā is called drying. (24)

[Verse 25]
The yavagu prepared with the ten roots (daśamūla) destroys cough, dyspnea, hiccup, and kapha; and that prepared in the manner of yamaka with wine alleviates diseases of the stomach and digestive tract. (25)

A yavagu cooked with the ten roots destroys cough, dyspnea, hiccup, and kapha; and a yavagu prepared with wine in the yamaka manner removes diseases of the stomach. (25)

[Verse 26]
A yavagu prepared with leafy vegetables, meat, sesame, and black gram expels feces. That prepared with jambū (rose apple), mango kernels, dādhittha (wood apple), sour substances, and bilva (bael) is considered astringent (saṃgrāhiṇī). (26)

A yavagu made with greens, meat, sesame, and black gram removes waste matter; one made with jamun, mango kernels, dadhittha, sour things, and bael is regarded as astringent. (26)

[Verse 27]
A yavagu prepared with alkalis (kṣāra), chitraka, asafoetida, and āmlavetasa is regarded as purgative (bhedinī). That prepared with harītakī, long pepper root, and dry ginger promotes downward movement of vāta (vātānulomanī). (27)

A yavagu with alkalis, chitraka, asafoetida, and āmlavetasa is purgative; one with harītakī, long pepper root, and dry ginger brings vāta into proper downward motion. (27)

[Verse 28]
A yavagu prepared with buttermilk destroys disorders caused by ghee; and that prepared with buttermilk and pinyāka (oil-cake residue) is best for disorders caused by oil. (28)

A yavagu cooked in buttermilk removes diseases arising from ghee; one cooked with the oil-cake in buttermilk is best for diseases arising from oil. (28)

[Verse 29]
A yavagu prepared with the sour meat-broth of cow's flesh destroys irregular fever (viṣamajvara); and that prepared in barley yamaka with long pepper and āmalakī is beneficial for the throat. (29)

A yavagu made with cow's meat broth combined with sour things destroys irregular fever; one prepared in barley yamaka with long pepper and āmalakā is beneficial for the throat. (29)

[Verse 30]
A yavagu cooked in the broth of a rooster (tāmracūḍa) removes diseases of the urinary and seminal passages; when prepared with split black gram and ghee and milk, it promotes virility and enhances semen. (30)

A yavagu cooked in rooster broth removes disorders of the seminal passages; prepared with split black gram, ghee, and milk, it becomes an enhancer of virility. (30)

[Verse 31]
A yavagu prepared with upodiká (a leafy plant) and curd destroys intoxication; and that prepared with āpāmārga, milk, and the flesh of the monitor lizard (godhā) destroys hunger and weakness. (31)

A yavagu prepared with poi herb and curd removes intoxication; one cooked with āpāmārga, milk, and godhā flesh removes excessive hunger. (31)

Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha
सूत्रस्थानम् । ( २१ )

तत्रश्लोकाः ॥अष्टाविंशतिरित्ये तायवाग्वःपरिकीर्तिताः । पञ्च कर्माणिचाश्रित्यश्लोकोनैषज्य संग्रहः ॥ ॥ ३२ ॥

उसमें ये श्लोकहैं कि, ये अट्ठाईस २८ यवागू कही हैं और पाँचकमों के आश्रयसे भैषज्यका संग्रह कहाहै ॥ ३२॥

पूर्वंमलफलज्ञानहेतोरुक्तंयदौषध म् । पञ्चकर्माश्रयज्ञानहेतोस्तत् कीर्तितंपुनः ॥ ३३ ॥

पहिले मूल फलके ज्ञानार्थे जो औषध कहीथी वही औषध पांच कर्मोंके आश्रित ज्ञानके लिये पुनः कही है ॥ ३३ ॥

स्मृतिमान्युक्तिकेहेतुज्ञोजितात्मा न्तिपत्तिमान् । भिषगौषधसंयोगैः चिकित्सां कर्तुमर्हति ॥ ३४ ॥

इतिभेषजचतुष्केऽपामार्गतण्डुलीयो नामद्वितीयोऽध्यायः ॥ २॥

स्मृतिमान् युक्ति के हेतुओंका ज्ञाता जितात्मा प्रतिपत्तिमान् ( ज्ञानी ) जो वैद्य है औषधोंके संयोगोंसे चिकित्सा करने को योग्यहै ॥ ३४ ॥

इति भेषज चतुष्के अपामार्ग तंडुलीयो नाम द्वितीयोऽध्यायः ॥ २ ॥

तृतीयोऽध्यायः ।

अथातआरग्वधीयमध्यायंवक्ष्यामः ।

इसके अनंतर आरग्वधीय अध्याय का वर्णन करतेहैं–

इति हस्माह भगवानात्रेयः ।

यह भगवान् आत्रेयकहतेहैं।

आरग्वधःसैंडगजःकरञ्जोवासागु डूचीमदनंहरिद्रे । श्याढ़ःसुराढ़ः खदिरोधवश्निम्बोविडङ्गंकरवीरकत्वक् ॥ १ ॥

अमलतास ऐंडगज करंज वासागिलोह मेनफल दोनों हल्दी श्रीसुरा खदिर धमासा नींव वायिबिडंग कनेरकी त्वचा ॥ १॥

यन्थिश्वमौजेलशुनःशिरीषःसलो मशोगुग्गुलुरुक्ष्णगन्धे । फिणिञ्झकोवत्सकसत्पर्णैपीछुनिकुठंसुमनःप्रवालाः ॥ २ ॥

मंथ भोजपत्र लहसन शिरस छोमश गूगल कृष्णगंधा फिणिञ्जक वत्सक सत्पर्ण पीछु कूट सुमन के पत्ते ॥ २ ॥

वचाहरेणुनिःवृतानिकुम्भोभद्रात कंगैरिकमअनञ्च । मनःशिलालेग्रहधूमएलाकासीसमुस्तार्जुनरोधसजाः ॥ ३ ॥

वच मोथा निशोथ निकुंभ भिलावा गेरू अंजन मनशिल गृहधूम इलायची कसीस मोथा अर्जुन लोध सज्जी॥ ३ ॥

इत्यर्द्धैरूपैविहिताःषंडेते गोपित्पीताःपुनरेविपिष्टाः । सिद्धाःपरंसर्षपतैलयुक्ताःचूर्णप्रदेहाभिषजामयोज्याः ॥ ४ ॥

ये आधे २ श्लोकमें कही जो औषधहैं

कुष्ठानिकच्छाणिनवं किलासंसुरेन्द्रलुमंकिटिमंसदडु । भगन्दराशांस्यपचींसपामांह्न्युःअयुकास्तव चिराचराणम् ॥ ५ ॥

ये कुष्ठकुच्छू नवीन किलास सुरेन्द्रलुत किटिम दाद भगंदर अर्श अपची खुजली इनमनुष्योंके रोगोंको प्रयोग करनेसे शीघ्रही नष्ट करतेहैं ॥ ५ ॥

कुष्ठहरिद्रेसुरसंपटोलंनिम्बाश्वगन्धेसुरदारुशिशु । सर्षपंतुम्बुरुधान्यवन्यंचण्डांशचूर्णानिसमानिकुयात् ॥ ६ ॥

कूट दोनों हलदी सरस पटोल नींब आसगंध देवदारू सोहंजना सरसों वनकातुंबरुधान्य चंडा इनको समभाग लेकर चूर्णकरें ॥ ६ ॥

तैस्तकयुकैःप्रथमंशरीरीरतैलाकमुद्र्निय तुंनुयतेत।तथास्यकण्डूःपिडकाःसकोठाःकुष्ठानिशोफाश्वशमं व्रजन्ति ॥ ७ ॥

तैलाकगात्रस्यक्तानिचूर्णान्येतानिदद्यादवचूर्णनार्थम् । दद्रुःसकण्डुः किटिमानिपामांविचचिकाचीवतथैतिशान्तिम् ॥ ९ ॥

सूत्रस्थानम् । ( २३ )

रसोत प्रपुञ्राड (पुँवाड) के बीज इनको कैथके रसमें मिलाकर लेप करना युक्तहै करंजके बीज एडगज (पुँवाड) कूट इनको गोमूत्रमें पीसकर प्रदेह करना श्रेष्ठ है ११॥

उभेहिर्द्रेकुटजस्यबीजंकरञबीजं सुमनःप्रवालान् । त्वचंसच व्यांहयमारकञलेपंतिलक्षारयुतं विदध्यात् ॥ १२ ॥

दोनों हलदी कुटजकाबीज करंजकाबीज सुमना के प्रवाल हयमारक (कनेर) की त्वचा और गुहा इनका तिलके क्षारमें मिलाकर लेपकरैं ॥ १२ ॥

मनःशिलात्वकुटजात्सकुष्ठःसलोमशःसैंडगजःकरञः । ग्रन्थिश्च भौर्जःकरवीरमूलंचूर्णिनिसाध्यानितुषोदकेन ॥ १३ ॥

मनसिल कुटजकी बकली कूट लोमश एडगज करंज ग्रंथि भोजपत्र कनेर की जड़ इनके चूणोँ को तुषके जलमें पकावैं ॥ १३ ॥

पलाशिनिदाहरसेनचापिकर्षोंड्वतान्याढकसम्मितेन । दर्वीप्रलेपंप्रवदन्तिलेपमेतत्परंकुष्ठिनिषूदनाय १४॥

पलाशकी भस्मके रसमें पकावैं आढ़कभर जलमें पकाकर कर्षभर निकासें इसलेपको दवीं प्रलेपकहतेहैं यह कुछके नाशके लिये अतिश्रेष्ठहै ॥ १४ ॥

पणिनिपिष्ठाचतुरंगुलस्यतकेण

पण्णन्यथकाकमाच्याः । तैलाकगाञरस्यनरस्यकुष्ठान्युद्र्वर्तयेद्श्वहनच्छदैश्व ॥ १५ ॥

चतुरंगु लके पत्तोंको और काकमाची (मकोह) के पत्तोंको मद्दूमें पीसकर और ऐसेही अश्वमारके (कनेर) के पत्तों को पीसकर तैलमें गात्रको भिगोकर उद्र्तन (मलना) करैं तो मनुष्यका कुछ दूर होताहै ॥ १५ ॥

कोलंकुलत्थाःसुरदारुराश्नामाषातसीतैलफलानिकुष्ठम् । वचाशताह्वायवचूर्णमम्लमुष्णानिवातामयिनांप्रदेहः ॥ १६ ॥

कोल कुलथी देवदारु रायसन उड्ड अलसीका तेल और फल कूट वच सौंफ जौकाचूर्ण अम्ल यह प्रदेह वातरोगोंको दूरकरताहै ॥ १६ ॥

आनूपमत्स्यामिषवेशवारैरुष्णैःप्रदेहःपवनापहःस्यात् । श्रेहैश्च तुभिंर्देशमूलमिश्रैर्गन्धौषधैर्विनिलजित्प्रदेहः ॥ १७ ॥

जलके मत्स्योंका मांस वेशवार इनको उष्णकरके जो प्रदेहहै वह वातनाशकहै चारों श्रेहोंमें दशमूल वा गंधौषध मिलाकर जो प्रदेहहै वहभी वातको जीतेहै ॥ १७॥

text:
( २४ )
नाकसंहितायाम्

सवचांयवानांचूर्णसतैलाम्लमुषन्ति वाते ॥ १८ ॥

तकमें मिला जौका चूर्ण क्षार मिला और उष्णहोय तो मलनेसे उदरकी पीड़ाको शांतकरताहै कूट सौंफ वच जौंका चूर्ण तैलमें अम्ल मिलाहुआ बातमें कहाहै १८

उभेशताह्वमधुकंमधूकंबलांपियालुञ्चकशेरुकञ्च । घृतंविदारींञ्च सितोपलाञ्चकुर्यात्प्रदेहंपवनेस रक्ते ॥ १९ ॥

दोनों शताह्व ( सौंफ शतावर ) महुआ शहद खरैंडी वला चिरौंजी कसेरू घृत विदारीकंद मिश्री इनका प्रदेह रक्त वातमें करना ॥ १९ ॥

राञ्चांगुडूचींमधुकंबलेंद्रेसजीवकं सर्षभकम्पयश्च । घृतंञ्चसिद्धंमुधुशेषयुक्तंरक्तानिलाजिर्णमणुदेत्म देहः ॥ २० ॥

रायसन गिलोह महुआ दोनों वला जीवक ऋषभक दूध इनकासिद्ध घृतमोम मिलाकर मलाजाय तो रक्तवातकी पीडा को शांतकरताहै ॥ २० ॥

वातेसरकेसघृतःप्रदेहोगोधूमचूर्णं छगलीपयश्च । नंतोत्पलंञ्च न्दनकुष्ठयुक्तंशिरोरुजायांसघृतः प्रदेहः ॥ २१ ॥

और रक्त सहित वातमें गेहूंका चूर्ण बकरीका दूध इनका घृत सहित प्रदेह रक्त बातमें और नत ( तगर ) उत्पल चंदन कूट इनका घृत सहित प्रदेह शिरकी पीडामें उत्तमहै ॥ २१ ॥

प्रपौण्डरींकंसुरदारुकुष्ठंयष्ट्याह्वमेलाकमलोत्पलेञ्च । शिरोरुजायांसघृतःप्रदेहोलोहैरकापञ्च कचोरकैश्च ॥ २२ ॥

बड़ाकमल देवदारु कूट मुलहटी इलायची कमल उत्पल लोहेकी एरका पञ्चाह्व चोरक इनका घृत सहित प्रदेह शिरकी पीडामें उत्तम है ॥ २२ ॥

राञ्चाहिर्दे्रनलदंशताह्वेंद्रेदेवदारूणिसितोपलाञ्च । जीविन्तमूलंस घृतंसतैलमालेपनंपाश्र्वरुजासुकोष्णमू ॥ २३ ॥

रायसन दोनों हलदी नलद सौंफ सतावर देवदारु मिसरी जीवंतिका मूल इनको घी तेल मिलाकर कुछ उष्णलेप पाश्वॉंकी पीडामें श्रेष्ठहै ॥ २३ ॥

शैवालपञ्चोत्पलवेत्रतुङ्गंप्रपौण्डरी काण्यमृणाललोध्रम् । प्रियंगु कालीयकचन्दनानिनिर्वापणःश्यात्सघृतःप्रदेहः ॥ २४ ॥

शेवाल पञ्च उत्पल वेतकी तुंग बड़ा कमल मृणालं ( बिष ) लोध प्रियंगु कालीयक चंदन इनका घृत सहित प्रदेह निर्वापण करताहै ॥ २४ ॥
translation:
(24)
[From the] Charaka Samhita

[Verse 18] The powders of all the samavedic herbs, mixed with oil and sour substances, are used as a paste in vata disorders.

Commentary 18: Mix barley flour with alkali (kshara), heat it, and apply by rubbing to relieve abdominal pain. Kuta, fennel, vacha, barley flour mixed with oil and sour substances is described for vata conditions.

[Verse 19] Both shatahva (dill and shatavari), mahua, honey, kharaindi, bala, chironji, kaseru, ghee, vidarikanda, and sugar — these should be made into a poultice (pradeha) for conditions of rakta (blood) and vata.

Commentary 19: Both shatahvas (fennel and shatavari), mahua, honey, kharenti, bala, chironji, kaseru, ghee, vidarikanda, and sugar — apply as a poultice in blood-vata disorders.

[Verse 20] Giloy (guduchi), licorice (madhuka), bala, indra herbs, jivaka, sarshapa (mustard), and camphor — ghee prepared with these, mixed with milk, when rubbed on the body, alleviates pain of blood-vata disorders.

Commentary 20: Giloy, mahua, both balas, jivaka, rishabha, milk — ghee prepared and siddha with these, mixed and rubbed, alleviates blood-vata pain.

[Verse 21] A poultice of ghee with sesame paste for vata with rakta (blood): wheat flour, goat's milk with ghee as a poultice; and nata (tagara/valerian), utpala (blue lotus), chandana (sandalwood), kushtha — with ghee as a poultice, excellent for headache.

Commentary 21: For blood-vata conditions, wheat flour and goat's milk with ghee as a poultice; and nata (tagara), utpala, chandana, and kuta — with ghee as a poultice, excellent for head pain.

[Verse 22] Prapaundarika (white lotus), suradaru (devadaru), kushtha, yashtimadhu (licorice), ela (cardamom), kamala (lotus), utpala (blue lotus) — with ghee as a poultice for headache; together with loha (iron compounds), kachora.

Commentary 22: Large lotus, devadaru, kuta, mulethi (licorice), cardamom, lotus, blue lotus, iron compounds, arka, panchahva, choraka — with ghee as a poultice, excellent for head pain.

[Verse 23] Rasna, both turmerics, nalada (nardostachys), shatahva, shatavari, devadaru, misri (sugar), and the root of jivanti — mixed with ghee and oil, a moderately warm poultice applied to the sides (parsva) is excellent for flank pain.

Commentary 23: Rasna, both turmerics, nalada, fennel, shatavari, devadaru, mishri, jivanti root — mixed with ghee and oil, a slightly warm poultice is the best remedy for pain in the flanks.

[Verse 24] Shevala (algae), the five utpalas (lotuses), vetra (rattan), tunga, prapaundarika, mrinala (lotus stalk), lodhra, priyanghu, kaliyaka, and chandana — with ghee as a poultice, this cools and pacifies (nirvapana) the affected area.

Commentary 24: Shevala, the five utpalas, cane (veta), tunga, large lotus, mrinala (vishha variety), lodha, priyanghu, kaliyaka, and sandal — a poultice made with ghee from these ingredients provides cooling relief.
