सूत्रस्थानम् । (२५)

सिताऽलतावेतसपञ्चकानियष्ट्याह्
मैन्द्रीनिलिनानिदूर्वा। यवासमूलं
कुशकाशयोश्चनिर्वापणःस्यात्
जलमेरकाच ॥ २५ ॥

मिश्री छता वेंत पञ्च मुलेहटी इंद्रायण
कमल दूर्वा जवासेका मूल कुशा काशकी
जड जलका पटेरा इनका प्रदेहभी निवा
पण करता है ॥ २५ ॥

शैलेयमेलागुरुणीसकुष्ठेचण्डानतं
त्वक्सुरदारुराक्षा । शीतंनिह
न्यादिचिरात्मदेहोविषंशिरीषस्तु
सिसिन्धुवारः ॥ २६ ॥

चंदन इलायची अगर कूट चंडा वेंत
दालचीनी देवदारु रायसन विष झिरस
सिंधुवार इनका प्रदेह शीघ्रही शीतको
नष्ट करता है ॥ २६ ॥

शिरीषलामञ्चकहेमलोध्रैस्त्वग्दो
षसंस्केदहरःप्रघर्षः । पत्राम्बुलो
ध्राभयचन्दनानिशारीरदौर्गन्ध्यह
रःप्रदेहः ॥ २७ ॥

शिरस लामञ्चक हेम लोध इनका
प्रघर्ष त्वचाके दोषका नाशक है पत्रोंका
(ओस) जल लोध हरडे चंदन इनका
प्रदेह शरीरकी दुर्गंधको हरता है॥ २७॥

तत्र श्लोकः ।

इहात्रिजःसिद्धतमानुवाचद्वात्रिंश
तंसिद्धमहर्षिपूज्यः । चूर्णप्रदेहां

न्विविधामयघ्नानारग्वधीयेजगतो
हितार्थम् ॥ २८ ॥

इति भेषजचतुष्केआरग्वधीयो नाम
तृतीयोऽध्यायः ॥ ३ ॥

उसमें यह श्लोक है कि इस आरग्व
धीय अध्यायमें सिद्ध महर्षियोंके पूज्य
आत्रेयने अनेक प्रकारके रोगोंके नाशक
बत्तीस चूर्णोंके प्रदेह जगतके हितके लिये
कहे हैं ॥ २८ ॥

इति आरग्वधीयोनाम तृतीयोऽध्यायः ॥ ३ ॥

चतुर्थोऽध्यायः ।

अथातःषड्विरेचनशताश्रिती
यमध्यायंव्याख्यास्यामः ।

इसके अनंतर षड्विरेचन शताश्रितीय
अध्यायका व्याख्यान करते हैं—

इति ह्स्माह्भगवानात्रेयः ।

यह भगवान् आत्रेय कहते हैं.

इहखलुषड्विरेचनशतानिभव
न्ति । षड्विरेचनाश्रयाः। पञ्च
कषायशतानि । पञ्चकषाययो
नयः। पञ्चविधंकषायकल्पनम्।
पञ्चाशन्महाकषायाइतिसंग्रहः ३
किं यहां निश्रयसे छः सौ विरेचन होते
हैं छः विरेचनोंके आश्रय, पांचसौ कषाय
पांच कषायोंकी योनि पांच प्रकारके
कषायों की कल्पना पचास महाकषाय हैं
इतना संग्रह इस अध्यायमें है ॥ १ ॥

translation:
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha
Sutrasthana (Chapter on Fundamental Principles), Page 25

[Verse 25]
Sharkara (sugar candy), lata, vetasa, the five roots, yashtimadhu (licorice), maindri, nilini, durva — these along with the root of yavasa, kusha, kasha, and water from the erika plant should be used as a cooling paste application.

[Commentary on verse 25:] Mishri (sugar candy), cane, the five roots, mulethi (licorice), indrayan, lotus, durva grass, yavasa root, kusha, kasha root — their application as a paste also provides a cooling, soothing effect.

[Verse 26]
Shaileyaka, mace, aguru, kushtha, chandana, tvak (cinnamon), suradaru (devadaru/cedar), raksha (lac), shirisha — and sindhuvara: a paste of these quickly destroys heat in the body and removes poison.

[Commentary on verse 26:] Sandal, cardamom, agaru, kuta, chanda, cane, cinnamon, devadaru, raisins, shirisha, sindhuvara — a paste of these very quickly destroys heat.

[Verse 27]
Shirisha, lamanjaka, gold, lodhra — rubbed together as a scrub, they remove skin blemishes. A paste made of patra (leaves), water, lodhra, haritaki, and sandal removes bodily foul odor.

[Commentary on verse 27:] Shirisha, lamanjaka, gold, lodhra — their rubbing destroys skin disorders. Dew water from leaves, lodhra, harade, sandal — their paste removes foul smell from the body.

[Concluding verse of the chapter — Verse 28]
Here the great sage Atri, venerated by the siddha maharshis, taught thirty-two powder-pastes of various kinds that destroy diseases, for the benefit of the world, in this Aragvadhiya chapter.

End of the Aragvadhiya, the Third Chapter of the Bheshaja Chatushka. Chapter 3.

[Commentary:] In this Aragvadhiya chapter, the revered Atreya, honored among the siddha maharshis, has described thirty-two medicinal pastes (churna-pradeha) that destroy diseases of many kinds, for the welfare of the world.

End of the Aragvadhiya, Third Chapter. 3.

FOURTH CHAPTER

Now we shall explain the chapter called Shadvirechana-shataashritiya (Relating to the Six Hundred Purgatives).

Thus spoke Bhagavan Atreya:

Here indeed there are six hundred purgatives. The six bases of purgatives; five hundred decoctions (kashaya); the five sources of decoctions; the five types of decoction preparations; and fifty great decoction groups — this is the summary of this chapter.

[Commentary:] That is to say, there are six hundred purgatives by firm reckoning; six supports (ashraya) of purgatives; five hundred kashaya (decoctions); five origins of kashaya; five types of kashaya preparations; fifty mahakashaya (great decoctions) — this is the total content of this chapter. 1.

text:
( २६ )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।
Digitized By Srudhama Soangsri Gyaan Kosha

षड्विरेचनशतानीतियदुक्तंतद
हसंग्रहेणोदाहृत्यविस्तरेणकल्पो
पनिषदिव्याख्यास्यामः ॥ २ ॥
छःसौ विरेचन जो कहे हैं उनको यहां
संग्रहसे कहकर विस्तारसे कल्पोपनिष-
द्में व्याख्यान करेंगे ॥ २ ॥

त्रयत्रिंशत्योगशतंत्रणीतंफलेष्वे
कोनचत्वारिंशज्जीमूतकेषुयोगाः।
पञ्चचत्वारिंशदिक्ष्वाकुषुधामार्गवः
षष्टिधाभवतियोगयुक्तः ॥ ३ ॥
तेतीस योगोंका शतफलोंमें १३३
एकोनचत्वारिंशत् ३९ जीमूतक
( जल ) के योग पैंतालीस इक्ष्वाकुओंके
योग धामार्गव साठ प्रकारके योगसे युक्त
होताहै ॥ ३ ॥

कुटजस्तवष्टादशधायोगमेतिकत
वेधनंषष्टिधाभवतियोगयुक्तम् ।
श्यामात्रिवृयोगशतंत्रणीतंदशाप
रेचात्रभवन्तियोगाः ॥ ४ ॥
कुटजके अठारह योगहैं कुतवेधनके
साठि योगहैं श्याम निशोथके सौ योगहैं
और दश अन्य योग यहां होते हैं ॥४॥

चतुरंगुलोद्दादशधायोगमेतिलो
ध्रिवधैषोडशयोगयुक्तम् । महा
वृक्षोभवतिविंशतियोगयुक्तःएकोन
चत्वारिंशत्सप्तलाशिखिन्योयों
गाः ॥ ५ ॥

चतुरंगुलके बारह योग होते हैं लोध
विधिसे सोलह योगसे युक्त है महावृक्ष
वीस योगोंसे युक्त है सप्तला शिखिनीको
योग उनतालीस हैं ॥ ५ ॥

अष्टचत्वारिंशद्न्तीद्रवन्त्योरि
तिषड्विरेचनशतानि । षड्विरेच
नाश्रयाइति ॥ ६ ॥
दंती द्रवंतीके योग अडतालीस ये
छःसौ विरेचन हैं ॥ ६ ॥

क्षिरमूलत्वकुपत्रपुष्पफलानीति ।
पञ्चकषाययोनयइति ॥ ७ ॥
छः विरेचनके आश्रय ये हैं कि दूध
जड त्वचा पत्ते पुष्प फल इति ॥ ७ ॥

मधुरकषायोऽम्लकषायःकटुक
षायस्तिक्तकषायःकषायकषाय
श्चेतितन्त्रेसंज्ञा ॥ ८ ॥
पांच कषायकी योनि मधुर कषाय
अम्ल कषाय कटु कषाय तिक्त कषाय
कसेला कषाय ये तंत्रमें संज्ञाहै ॥ ८ ॥

पञ्चविधंकषायकल्पनमिति । त
थ्यथा। स्वरसःकल्कःश्रुतःशीतः
फाण्टःकषायइति ॥ ९ ॥
पांच प्रकारके कषायकी कल्पना जो
है वह ऐसे है कि स्वरस कल्क शृत शीत
फांटः कषाय यह कही है ॥ ९ ॥

" यन्त्रप्रपीडनाद्रव्यादुसःस्व
रसउच्यते । यत्पिण्डंरसिपष्टानां
तत्कल्कंपरिकीर्तितम् ॥ १० ॥

translation:
( 26 )
In the Charaka Samhita

[Verse 2]
The six hundred purgatives (virechanas) that have been mentioned — those will now be summarized briefly and then explained in full detail in the Kalpopanishad chapter. (Commentary: The six hundred purgatives that have been spoken of will be summarized here and then expounded at length in the Kalpopanishad.) ॥2॥

[Verse 3]
One hundred and thirty-three formulations are counted among the fruit-based groups; thirty-nine formulations belong to the Jimutaka (water plant) group; forty-five belong to the Ikshvaku group; the Dhamargava group yields sixty kinds of formulations in all. (Commentary: Thirty-three sets in the hundred — that is 133 in the fruit group, 39 in the Jimutaka [water] group, 45 in the Ikshvaku group, and the Dhamargava comes to sixty types of formulations.) ॥3॥

[Verse 4]
Kutaja yields eighteen kinds of formulations; Kutavedha yields sixty kinds; Shyama and Trivrit together yield one hundred formulations; and ten more formulations arise from others. (Commentary: Kutaja has eighteen formulations, Kutavedha has sixty, Shyama-Nishoth has one hundred formulations, and ten other formulations occur here.) ॥4॥

[Verse 5]
Chaturangula yields twelve kinds of formulations; Lodhra, following its method, yields sixteen; Mahavriksha yields twenty formulations; and Saptala and Shikhini together yield thirty-nine formulations. (Commentary: Chaturangula has twelve formulations, Lodhra by its method is joined with sixteen, Mahavriksha is joined with twenty, and Saptala-Shikhini have thirty-nine formulations.) ॥5॥

[Verse 6]
Danti and Dravanti together have forty-eight formulations — thus the six hundred purgatives are complete. These are the six bases of purgation. (Commentary: Danti and Dravanti have forty-eight formulations; these are the six hundred purgatives.) ॥6॥

[Verse 7]
The six bases of purgation are: milk (kshira), root (mula), bark (tvak), leaf (patra), flower (pushpa), and fruit (phala) — these are the five sources of decoction (kashaya). (Commentary: The six supports of purgation are milk, root, bark, leaf, flower, and fruit.) ॥7॥

[Verse 8]
Sweet decoction (madhura kashaya), sour decoction (amla kashaya), pungent decoction (katu kashaya), bitter decoction (tikta kashaya), and astringent decoction (kashaya kashaya) — these are the five designations recognized in this treatise. (Commentary: The five sources of kashaya are sweet, sour, pungent, bitter, and astringent — these are the classifications in the treatise.) ॥8॥

[Verse 9]
The preparation of decoction is of five kinds, as follows: fresh juice (svarasa), paste (kalka), decoction by boiling (shrita), cold infusion (shita), and hot infusion (phanta). (Commentary: The five types of kashaya preparation are: fresh juice, paste, boiled decoction, cold infusion, and hot infusion — this is what is said.) ॥9॥

[Verse 10]
"That which is obtained by pressing a substance through a device is called svarasa (fresh juice). That which is the solid residue of ground substances is called kalka (paste)..." ॥10॥

text:
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha
सूत्रस्थानम् । ( २७ )

द्रव्यको यंत्रमें पीडकर जो रसनिकसै वह स्वरस कहा है रसमें पीसे हुयोंका जो पिंड वह कल्क कहा है ॥ १० ॥

वह्नौतुकथितंद्रव्यंश्रतमाहुशिकत्सकाः । द्रव्यादापोतिथताचो येतत्पुनिनिशसंस्थितात् ॥११॥

अग्निमें पकाया जो द्रव्य उसको वैद्य लोग श्रृत कहते हैं पीसे हुये द्रव्यको रात्रिमें जलमें स्थित रखनेसे ॥ ११ ॥

कषायोयोऽभिनयोितससशीतःसमुदाहृतः । क्षिप्नवोष्णेतोयेमृदितं तत्फाण्टंपरिकीर्त्तितम् ॥ १२ ॥

जो कषाय निकसै वह शीत कहाताहै और उष्ण जलमें डालकर मलनेसे जो कषाय निकसै उसको फांट कहतेहैं॥ १२॥

तेषांयथापूर्वेंबलाधिक्यम् ।अतः कषायकल्पनाव्याध्यातुरवलापेक्षिणीनत्वेवंखलुसर्वाणिसर्वत्रोपयोगीनिभवन्ति । पञ्चाशन्महाकषायाइतियदुक्तंतदनुव्याख्यास्यामः ॥ १३ ॥

उसमें पिहले २ का क्रमसे अधिक बल होता है इससे कषायकी कल्पना व्याधि और आतुरके बलकी अपेक्षासे होती है इससे इसप्रकार सबका सर्वत्र उपयोग नहीं होता है–पचास जो महाकषाय कहे हैं उनका व्याख्यान करते हैं ॥ १३ ॥

तथथा । जीवनीयोबृंहणीयोलेखनीयोभेदनीयःसन्धानीयोदीपनीयइितिषट्कःकषायवर्गः॥११४॥

वह ऐसे हैं कि जीवनीय बृंहणीय लेखनीय भेदनीय संधानीय दीपनीय ये छः कषायोंका वर्ग हैं ॥ १४ ॥

बल्योवर्ण्यःकण्ठ्योहृद्यःइतिचतुष्कःकषायवर्गः ॥ १५॥

बलकारी वर्णकारी कंठको हित हृदयको प्रिय यह चार कषायोंका वर्ग है१५

तृिित्घ्नोऽशोण्घ्नःकुष्ठघ्नःकण्डूघ्नःकिमिघ्नोिवषघ्नइतिषट्कःकषायवर्गः १६

तृितिनाशक अर्शनाशक कुष्ठनाशक कंडूनाशक क्रिमिनाशक विषनाशक ये छः कषायोंके वर्ग हैं ॥ १६ ॥

स्तन्यजननःस्तन्यशोधनःशुकजननःशुकशोधनइतिचतुष्कःकषायवर्गः ॥ १७ ॥

स्तन्यजनन स्तन्यशोधन शुक्रजनन शुक्रशोधन यह चार कषायोंके वर्ग हैं१७

स्नेहोपगःस्वेदोपगोवमनोपगोविरेचनोपगआस्थापनोपगोऽनुवासनोपगःशिरोिवरेचनोपगइतिसप्तकःकषायवर्गः ॥ १८ ॥

स्नेहोपयोगी स्वेदोपयोगी वमनोपयोगी आस्थापनोपयोगी अनुवासनोपयोगी शिरोविरेचनोपयोगी यह सात कषायोंका वर्ग हैं ॥ १८ ॥

Sutrasthana, Chapter 1 (Page 27)

The juice extracted by pressing a substance in a press is called svarasa (fresh juice); the paste made from ground substances is called kalka (paste). [Verse 10]

A substance boiled in water over fire is called shrita (decoction) by physicians; a substance ground and kept immersed in water overnight [is another preparation]. [Verse 11]

The cold decoction obtained [by soaking] is called kashaya; that which is obtained by macerating the substance in hot water and pressing it out is called phanta (hot infusion). [Verse 12]

Each of these preparations is progressively stronger than the one before it. Therefore, the selection of the form of preparation depends upon the strength of the disease and the patient — hence not all preparations are used universally everywhere. We shall now explain the fifty mahakashayas (great groups of decoctions) that have been mentioned. [Verse 13]

And they are as follows: Jivaniya (life-promoting), Brinhania (nourishing), Lekhaniya (scraping/reducing), Bhedaniya (purgative), Sandhaniya (healing/uniting), and Dipaniya (digestive-stimulating) — these constitute the group of six kashayas. [Verse 14]

Balya (strength-giving), Varnya (complexion-enhancing), Kanthya (beneficial to the throat), and Hridya (pleasing to the heart) — these constitute the group of four kashayas. [Verse 15]

Trishnaghna (thirst-relieving), Arshoghna (hemorrhoid-destroying), Kushthagnha (skin-disease-destroying), Kandughna (itch-relieving), Krimighna (worm-destroying), and Vishaghna (poison-neutralizing) — these constitute the group of six kashayas. [Verse 16]

Stanyajanana (milk-producing), Stanyashodhana (milk-purifying), Shukrajanana (semen-producing), and Shukrashodhana (semen-purifying) — these constitute the group of four kashayas. [Verse 17]

Snehopaga (conducive to oleation therapy), Svedopaga (conducive to sudation/sweating therapy), Vamanopaga (conducive to emesis), Virechanopaga (conducive to purgation), Asthapanopaga (conducive to decoction enema), Anuvasanopaga (conducive to oil enema), and Shirovirechanopaga (conducive to head-purging/nasal therapy) — these constitute the group of seven kashayas. [Verse 18]

text:
( २८ )

छदिनिग्रहणस्तृष्णानिग्रहणोहिका
निग्रहणइतितिकःकषायवर्गः १९
छदींकानिग्रहण तृषाकानिग्रहण
हिचकीकानिग्रहण यह तीनकषायोंका
वर्ग है ॥ १९ ॥

पुरीषसंग्रहणीयःपुरीषिवरजनी
योमूत्रसंग्रहणीयोमूत्रविरेजनीयो
मूत्रविरेचनीय इतिपञ्चकःकषा
यवर्गः ।। २० ।।

मलसंग्रहणीय पुरीष विरजनीय मूत्र
संग्रहणीय मूत्रविरजनीय मूत्रविरेचनीय
यह पांचकषायोंका वर्ग है ॥ २० ॥

कासहरःश्वासहरःशोथहरोज्वरहरः
श्रमहरइतिपञ्चकःकषायवर्गः २१
कासहर श्वासहर शोथहर ज्वरहर
श्रमहर यह पांच कषायोंका वर्ग है॥२१॥

दाहप्रशमनःशीतप्रशमनउदर्दंप्र
शमनोऽङ्गमर्दंप्रशमनःशूलप्रशमन
इतिपञ्चकःकषायवर्गः ।। २२ ।।

दाहप्रशमन शीतिप्रशमन उदर्दंप्रशमन
अंगमर्दंप्रशमन शूलप्रशमन यह पांच
कषायोंका वर्ग है ॥ २२ ॥

शोणितास्थापनोवेदनास्थापनः
संज्ञास्थापनःप्रजास्थापनोवयः
स्थापनइतिपञ्चकःकषायवर्गः ।
इतिपञ्चाशन्महाकषायाः।।२३।।
शोणितास्थापन वेदनास्थापन संज्ञा

स्थापन प्रजास्थापन वयःस्थापन यह पांच
कषायोंका वर्गहैं ये पचासमहाकषायहैं२ ३

महताञ्चकषायाणांलक्षणोदाहर
णार्थेव्याख्याताभवन्ति । तेषा
मेकैकस्मन्महाकषायेदशदशा
वयविकान्कषायानुव्याख्या
स्यामः । तान्येवपञ्चकषायश
तानिभवन्ति ।। २४ ।।

महान् कषायोंके लक्षण और उदाहरणके लिये कहेहैं उनके मध्यमें एक २
महाकषायमें अंगोंके दश २ कषायोंका
व्याख्यान करते हैं वेही पंचशत ५०० कषाय होते हैं ॥ २४ ॥

तद्यथा । जीवकर्षभकौमेदामहा
मेदाकाकोलीक्षीरकाकोलीमुद्गमा
षपर्णिजीवन्तीमधुकिमितदशेमा
निजीवनीयानिभवन्ति ।।२५।।

वे ऐसे हैं कि जीवक ऋषभक मेदा
महामेदा काकोली क्षीरकाकोली मुद्रपर्णी
माषपर्णी जीवंती महुआ ये दश कषाय
जीवनीय होते हैं ॥ २५ ॥

क्षीरिणीराजक्षवकबलाकाकोली
क्षीरकाकोलीवाट्यायनीभद्रौदनी

मानिबृंहणीयानिभवन्ति ।।२६।।

translation:
(28)

The group of decoctions (kashaya-varga) for suppressing vomiting, suppressing thirst, and suppressing hiccup — this is the nineteenth group of five decoctions. The group called: suppressors of vomiting, suppressors of thirst, suppressors of hiccup — this is the group of three decoctions. ॥19॥

The group consisting of: feces-consolidating, feces-expelling, urine-consolidating, urine-expelling, and urine-purging — this is the twentieth group of five decoctions. Feces-consolidating, feces-expelling, urine-consolidating, urine-expelling, urine-purging — this is the group of five decoctions. ॥20॥

The group consisting of: cough-relieving, dyspnea-relieving, edema-relieving, fever-relieving, and fatigue-relieving — this is the twenty-first group of five decoctions. Cough-relieving, dyspnea-relieving, edema-relieving, fever-relieving, fatigue-relieving — this is the group of five decoctions. ॥21॥

The group consisting of: burning-sensation-pacifying, cold-pacifying, skin-rash-pacifying, body-ache-pacifying, and colic-pacifying — this is the twenty-second group of five decoctions. Burning-pacifying, cold-pacifying, skin-rash-pacifying, body-ache-pacifying, colic-pacifying — this is the group of five decoctions. ॥22॥

The group consisting of: blood-stabilizing, pain-stabilizing, consciousness-restoring, progeny-promoting, and age-sustaining — this is the twenty-third group of five decoctions. Thus these are the fifty great decoction-groups (mahakashaya). Blood-stabilizing, pain-stabilizing, consciousness-restoring, progeny-promoting, age-sustaining — this is the group of five decoctions. These are the fifty great decoctions. ॥23॥

The characteristics and examples of the great decoctions are being explained. From each of the great decoctions, ten constituent decoctions will be described; those together form five hundred decoctions. ॥24॥

They are as follows: Jivaka, Rishabha, Meda, Mahameda, Kakoli, Kshirakakoli, Mudgaparni, Mashaparni, Jivanti, and Madhuka — these ten constitute the life-promoting (jivaniya) decoctions. ॥25॥

Kshirini, Rajashvaka, Bala, Kakoli, Kshirakakoli, Vatyayani, Bhadraudani, Bharadvaji, Payasya, and Arshyagandha — these ten constitute the nourishing (brimhaniya) decoctions. ॥26॥

सूत्रस्थानम्

द्राजी पयस्या ऋष्यगंधा ये दश कषाय
बृंहणीय होते हैं ॥ २६ ॥

मुस्तकुठहरिद्रादारुहरिद्रावचा
तिविषाकटुरोहिणीचित्रकिंचिर
बिल्वहैममत्यइतिदशेमानिलेख
नीयानिभवन्ति ॥ २७ ॥

मोथा कूट हलदी दारुहलदी बच अतीस
कटुरोहिणी चित्रक करंजुवा हैमवती
ये दश कषाय लेखनीय होतेहैं ॥ २७ ॥

सुवहाकोरुवृकाग्निमुखीचित्राचि
त्रकिंचिरबिल्वशंखिनीशकुलाद
नीस्वर्णक्षीरिण्यइतिदशेमानिभेद
नीयानिभवन्ति ॥ २८ ॥

सुवहा अर्क रुवृका अग्निमुखी चित्रा
चीता पुराणवेल शंखिनी शकुलादनी
स्वर्णक्षीरिणी ( सोनामक्खी ) ये दश
कषाय भेदनीय होते हैं ॥ २८॥

मधुकमधुपर्णीपृश्निपर्ण्यंबष्ठकी
समङ्गामोचरसधातकीलोध्राभिय
गुकट्फलानीतिदशेमानिसंधानी
यानि भवन्ति ॥ २९ ॥

महुआ मधुकपणीं पृश्निपणीं अंबष्ठकी
समंगा मोचरस धातकी लोध प्रियंगु
कायफल येदश कषाय संधानीय होतेहैं२९

पिप्पलीपिप्पलीमूलचव्यिचित्रक
शृङ्गवेराम्लवेतसमिरिचाजमोदा
भञ्जातकास्थिहिंगुनियर्यासाइतिद

शेमानिदीपनीयानिभवन्ति ॥ ३०
पीपल पीपलामूल चव्य चित्रक गुंगवेर
अम लंवेत मिरच अजमोद भिलाये हींग
ये दश दीपनीय होते हैं ॥ ३० ॥

इतिषट्ककषायवर्गः । ऐन्द्रीऋष
ष्यितरसभ्यमोक्तापयस्यश्वगंधा
स्थिरारोहिणीबलातिबलाइतिद
शेमानिबल्यानिभवन्ति ॥ ३१॥

ये छः कषायोंके वर्ग हैं इंद्रायण ऋषभ
अतिरस ऋष्यमोक्ता पयस्या आसगंध
स्थिरा रोहिणी बला अतिबला ( खरैंटी)
ये दश कषाय बलकारक होते हैं ॥ ३१॥

चन्दनतुङ्गपद्मकोशीरमधुकमञि
ष्ठाशारिवापयस्यासितालताइति
दशेमानिवण्र्यानिभवन्ति। ३२॥

चंदन तुंग, पद्माख खस महुआ मजीठ
सारिवा पयस्या सितालता ये दश कषाय
वर्णशोधक होते हैं ॥ ३२ ॥

सारिवेक्षुमलमधुकिपिप्पलीद्राक्षा
विदारीकैटर्यंहंसपदीबृहतीकण्ट
कारिकइतिदशेमानिकण्ठ्यानि
भवन्ति ॥ ३३ ॥

सारिवा इखुमल महुआ पीपल
मुनका विदारीकंद कैटर्य हंसपदी बडी
कटेहली ये दश कषाय कंठके हितकारी
होतेहैं ॥ ३३ ॥

आम्राम्रातकिनिकुचकरमर्दवृक्षा
म्लाम्लवेतसकुबलबदरदाडिममा

translation:
(Page 29 — Sutrasthana, Charaka Samhita)

[Verse 26]
Draji, Payasya, and Rishyagandha — these ten decoctions (kashaya) are considered nourishing (brimhaniya).

[Verse 27]
Musta, Kutha, Haridra, Daruharidra, Vacha, Tivisha, Katurohi­ni, Chitraka, Chitraka (variety), Bilva, and Haimamati — these ten are the ones known as lekhaniya (scraping/reducing). That is: Motha, Kut, Turmeric, Daruharidra, Bach, Atees, Katurohi­ni, Chitraka, Karanju, and Haimavati — these ten decoctions are lekhaniya (fat-reducing).

[Verse 28]
Suvaha, Koruvrika, Agnimukhi, Chitra, Chitraka, Bilva, Shankhini, Shakuladani, Svarnaksirini — these ten are the ones known as bhedaniya (purgative/breaking). That is: Suvaha, Arka, Ruvrika, Agnimukhi, Chitra, Chitta (Puranavel), Shankhini, Shakuladani, Svarnaksirini (Sonamakkhi) — these ten decoctions are bhedaniya.

[Verse 29]
Madhuka, Madhuparni, Prishniparni, Ambasthaki, Samanga, Mocharasa, Dhataki, Lodhra, Abhiyagu, and Katphala — these ten are the ones known as sandhaniya (healing/binding). That is: Mahua, Madhukaparni, Prishniparni, Ambasthaki, Samanga, Mocharasa, Dhataki, Lodh, Priyangu, and Kayaphal — these ten decoctions are sandhaniya.

[Verse 30]
Pippali, Pippali-mula, Chavya, Chitraka, Shringavera, Amlavetasa, Maricha, Ajamoda, Bhanjataka, Hingu, and Niyaryas — these ten are dipaniya (digestive stimulants). That is: Peepal, Peepala-mula, Chavya, Chitraka, Gingiver (ginger), Amlavetasa, Mirch (pepper), Ajamoda, Bhilawa, and Hing (asafoetida) — these ten are dipaniya.

[Verse 31 — End of the group of six kashaya sets]
Aindri, Rishyaprokta, Payasya, Ashvagandha, Sthira, Rohini, Bala, and Atibala — these ten are balya (strength-promoting). That is: the six groups of decoctions are concluded. Indrayana, Rishabha, Atirasa, Rishyamokta, Payasya, Ashvagandha, Sthira, Rohini, Bala, and Atibala (Kharainti) — these ten decoctions are strength-promoting (balakarak).

[Verse 32]
Chandana, Tunga, Padma, Koshira, Madhuka, Manjishtha, Shariva, Payasya, and Sitalata — these ten are varnya (complexion-improving). That is: Chandan, Tunga, Padmakh, Khas, Mahua, Majith, Sariva, Payasya, and Sitalata — these ten decoctions are varnasodhak (purifying the complexion).

[Verse 33]
Sariva, Ikshumala, Madhuka, Pippali, Draksha, Vidari, Kaitarya, Hamsapadi, Brhati, and Kantakari — these ten are known as kanthya (beneficial for the throat). That is: Sariva, Ikhumala, Mahua, Peepal, Munakka, Vidari-kanda, Kaitarya, Hamsapadi, and Badi-Katehli — these ten decoctions are beneficial for the throat.

text:
( ३० )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।

तुलुङ्गानीतिदशेमानिहृद्यानिभवन्ति ॥ ३४ ॥

आम्र आम्रातक निकुच करमर्द वृक्षाम्ल अमलवेत कुवलय बेर अनार मातुलुंग ( विजोरा ) ये दशकषाय हृद्यकोहितकारी होते हैं—यह चार कषायोंका वर्ग है ॥ ३४ ॥

इतिचतुष्कःकषायवर्गः । नागर चित्रकचव्यविडङ्गमूर्वागुडूचीवचामुस्तिपिप्पलीपटोलानीतिदशेमानितृघ्नानिभवन्ति ॥ ३५ ॥

सूंठ चीता चव्य वायिविडंग मूर्वांगिलोय बच मोथा पीपल पटोल ये दश कषाय तृसिके नाशक हैं ॥ ३५ ॥

कुटजबिल्वचित्रकनागरातिविषाभयाधन्वयशकदारुहरिद्रावचाचव्यानीतिदशेमानिअशोर्घ्नानिभवन्ति ॥ ३६ ॥

कुटज वेल चीता सूंठ अतीस हरडे धमासा दारुहलदी बच चव्य ये दश कषाय अर्शके नाशकहैं ॥ ३६ ॥

खदिराभयामलकहरिद्रारुष्करसतपणार्गवधकरवीराविडङ्गजातिप्रवालाइतिदशेमानिकुष्ठघ्नानिभवन्ति ॥ ३७ ॥

खदिर हरडे आमले हलदी अरुष्कर सतपण अमलतास कनेर वायिविडंग जातिके पत्ते ये दश कषाय कुष्ठनाशक होतेहैं ॥ ३७ ॥

चन्दननलदकुतभालनकमालिनम्बकुटजसर्षपमधुकदारुहरिद्रामुस्तानीतिदशेमानिकण्डुघ्नानिभवन्ति ॥ ३८ ॥

चंदन नलद कुतमाल नक्तमाल निंब कुटज सरसों महुआ दारुहलदी मोथा ये दश कषाय कंडूनाशक होतेहैं ॥ ३८ ॥

अक्षीवमारिचगण्डिरकेवूकविडङ्गनिर्गुण्डीकिणहीश्वदंष्ट्रावृषपणिकाआखुपणिकाइतिदशेमानिक्रिमिघ्नानिभवन्ति ॥ ३९ ॥

अक्षीव मिरच गंडीर केबुक वायिविडंग निर्गुंडी किणही गोखरू वृषपणीं आखुपणीं ये दश कषाय क्रिमि नाशक होतेहैं ॥ ३९ ॥

हरिद्रामञिष्ठासुवहासूक्ष्मैलापालिन्दीचन्दनकनकशिरीषसिन्धुवारश्लेष्मातकाइतिदशेमानिविषघ्नानिभवन्ति ॥ ४० ॥

हलदी मंजीठ सुहागा छोटी इलायची पालिन्दी चंदन कतक शिरस सिंधुवार बहेडा ये दश कषाय विषनाशक होतेहैं ४०

इतिषट्कःकषायवर्गः । वीरण शालीषिठिकेशुवालिकादर्भकुमूकाशगुन्द्रेतकटकतृणमूलानीतिदशेमानिस्तन्यजननानिभवन्ति ४१
translation:
(30)
From the Charaka Samhita.

These ten are known as the heart-benefiting group — verse 34.

Amra (mango), Amrataka (hog plum), Nikucha, Karamarda, Vrikshamla, Amalaveta, Kuvalaya, Bera (jujube), Anar (pomegranate), Matulunga (citron/bijora) — these ten decoctions are beneficial to the heart. This is the fourth group of decoctions. ॥34॥

Thus ends the Chatushka (fourth) group of decoctions. Nagara (dry ginger), Chitraka, Chavya, Vidanga, Murva, Guduchi, Chamustha, Pippali, Patola — these ten are known as destroyers of thirst. ॥35॥

Dry ginger, Chitraka, Chavya, Vidanga, Murva, Giloy, Bach (sweet flag), Motha, Pippali (long pepper), Patola — these ten decoctions destroy thirst. ॥35॥

Kutaja, Bilva, Chitraka, Nagara, Ativisha, Abhaya, Dhanvayasa, Daruharidra, Vacha, Chavya — these ten are known as destroyers of hemorrhoids (arsha). ॥36॥

Kutaja, Bel, Chitraka, dry ginger, Atees, Harada, Dhamasa, Daruhaladi, Bach, Chavya — these ten decoctions destroy hemorrhoids. ॥36॥

Khadira, Abhaya, Amalaka, Haridra, Rushkara, Shataparna, Aragvadha, Karavira, Vidanga, Jati-pravala — these ten are known as destroyers of skin diseases (kushtha). ॥37॥

Khadira, Harada, Amla, turmeric, Arushkara, Shataparna, Amaltas, Kaner, Vidanga, leaves of Jati — these ten decoctions destroy skin diseases. ॥37॥

Chandana, Nalada, Kutabhala, Naktamala, Nimba, Kutaja, Sarshapa, Madhuka, Daruharidra, Musta — these ten are known as destroyers of itching (kandu). ॥38॥

Sandalwood, Nalad, Kutamal, Naktamal, Neem, Kutaj, mustard, Mahua, Daruhaladi, Motha — these ten decoctions destroy itching. ॥38॥

Akshiva, Maricha (pepper), Gandira, Kevuka, Vidanga, Nirgundi, Kinahi, Shvadanshtra, Vrishaparna, Akhuparnaka — these ten are known as destroyers of worms (krimi). ॥39॥

Akshiva, black pepper, Gandir, Kebuk, Vidanga, Nirgundi, Kinahi, Gokharu, Vrishaparni, Akhuparni — these ten decoctions destroy worms. ॥39॥

Haridra, Manjishtha, Suvaha, Sukshmaila (small cardamom), Palindi, Chandana, Kanaka, Shirisha, Sindhuvara, Shleshmantaka — these ten are known as destroyers of poison (visha). ॥40॥

Turmeric, Manjith, Suhaga (borax), small cardamom, Palindi, sandalwood, Katak, Shiras, Sindhuvara, Baheda — these ten decoctions destroy poison. ॥40॥

Thus ends the sixth group of decoctions. Virana, Shali, Ishtika, Ikshuvala, Darbha, Kumuka, Ashagundra, Itakata, and the roots of grasses — these ten are known as promoters of breast milk (stanya-janana). ॥41॥

text:
सूत्रस्थानम् १ ( ३२ )

यह छःकषायोंका वर्गहै–वीरणशाली सांठीचावल इक्षुवालिका दर्भ कुशकाश गुंद्र उत्कट कटुणकी जड ये दश कषाय स्तन्यजनन होतेहैं ॥ ४१ ॥

पाठामहौषधसुरदारुमुस्तमूवागुडूचीवत्सकफलिकरातितक्त कटुरोहिणीशारिवाइतिदशेमानी स्तन्यशोधानानिभवन्ति ॥ ४२ ॥

पाठा सूंठ देवदारु मोथा मूवाँ गिलोय वांसाका फल किरात तित्त कटुरोहिणी शारिवा ये दश कषाय स्तन्य शोधन होतेहैं ॥ ४२ ॥

जीवकर्षभककाकोलीक्षीरकाकोलीमुद्रपणींमाषपणींमेदावृक्षरुहाजिटलाकुलिङ्गाइतिदशेमानिशुकजननानिभवन्ति ॥ ४३ ॥

जीवक ऋषभक काकोली क्षीरकाकोली मुद्रपणीं माषपणीं मेदा वृक्षरुहाजिटला कुलिंगा ये दशकषाय शुक्रजनन होतेहैं ॥ ४३ ॥

कुष्ठैलवालुककट्फलसमुद्रफेणकदम्बिनयासेक्षुकाण्डेक्षुरकवमुकोशीराणीतिदशेमानिशुकशोधनानिभवन्ति ॥ ४४ ॥

इति चतुष्कः कषायवर्गः ।

कूट, एलवालुककायफल समुद्रझाग कदंबका गोंद इक्षु, कांडेक्षु इक्षुरकवसुक खस ये दश शुक्रशोधन होतेहैं ॥४४॥

यह चार कषायोंका वर्ग है–

मृद्वीकामधुकमधुपणींमेदाविदारीक कोलीक्षीरकाकोलीजीवकजीवन्तीशालपण्यईतिदशेमानि स्नेहोपयोगानिभवन्ति ॥ ४५ ॥

मुनका मधुआ मधुपणीं मेदा विदारीकंद का कोली क्षीरकाकोली जीवत जीवंती शालपणीं ये दशकषाय स्नेहके उपयोगी होतेहैं ॥ ४५ ॥

शोभाअरनैकेरण्डाकेवृश्चीरपुनर्नवायवितलकुलत्थमाषबदराणितिदशेमानिस्वेदोपगानिभवन्ति॥४६

सहिंजना एरंड आख वृश्चीर पुनर्नवा ( सांटवा विषखपरा ) जों तिलककुलथी उड्द बेर ये दश कषाय स्वेदोपग ( पसीनाकारक ) होतेहैं ॥ ४६ ॥

मधुमधुककोविदारकर्बुदारणोपविदुलबिम्बीशाणपुष्पीसदापुष्पीप्रत्यकृपुष्पयिति दशेमानिवमनोपगानिभवन्ति ॥ ४७ ॥

सहत मधुआ कचनार वा कनेर कर्बुदा अरणी अरल उपविदुल बिंबी वा कडबी तुंबी शणपुष्पी सदापुष्पी प्रत्यकपुष्पी ये दश कषाय वमनकारी होतेहैं ॥ ४७ ॥

द्राक्षाकाश्मर्यपरूषकाभ्यामलकिविभीतककुवलबदरककेन्दुपीलूनीतिदशेमानिविरेचनोपगानिभवन्ति ॥ ४८ ॥
translation:
Sutra-sthana, Chapter 1 (Page 32)

This is the group of six decoction-categories — Virana-shali (fragrant grass), Santhi-rice, Ikshu-valika, Darbha, Kusha, Kasha, Gundra, Utkata, Katunaki root — these ten decoctions promote breast-milk production. (41)

Patha, Mahaushadi, Suradaru, Musta, Muva, Guduchi, Vatsaka-fruit, Kirata-tikta, Katu-rohini, Shariva — these ten promote purification of breast milk. (42)

Patha, dry ginger, Devadaru, Motha, Muva, Giloya, bamboo fruit, Kirata-tikta, Katu-rohini, Shariva — these ten decoctions purify breast milk. (42)

Jivaka, Rishabha, Kakoli, Kshira-kakoli, Mudra-parni, Masha-parni, Meda, Vriksha-ruha, Jitala, Kulinga — these ten promote the production of semen. (43)

Jivaka, Rishabha, Kakoli, Kshira-kakoli, Mudra-parni, Masha-parni, Meda, Vriksha-ruha, Jitala, Kulinga — these ten decoctions generate semen. (43)

Kushtha, Ela-valuka, Katphala, Samudra-phena, Dambini, Ikshu-kanda, Ikshu-raka, Vasuka, Koshire — these ten purify semen. (44)

Here ends the group of four decoction-categories.

Kuta, Ela-valuka, Samudra-phena (sea foam), the resin of Kadamba, sugarcane, Kandeiksu, Ikshu-raka, Vasuka, Khasa — these ten purify semen. (44)

This is the group of four decoction-categories —

Mridvika, Madhuka, Madhu-parni, Meda, Vidarikanda, Koli, Kshira-kakoli, Jivaka, Jivanti, Shala-parni — these ten are useful for oleation therapy. (45)

Munakka, Madhua, Madhu-parni, Meda, Vidarikanda, Koli, Kshira-kakoli, Jivaka, Jivanti, Shala-parni — these ten decoctions are useful for oleation (snehana) therapy. (45)

Shobhanjana, Eranda, Akh, Vrischira, Punarnava (Santva or Vishakha-para), barley, sesame, Kulattha, Urad, Ber — these ten decoctions are sudorific (sweat-inducing). (46)

Madhu, Madhuka, Kovidara, Karbuda, Vidula, Bimbi, Shana-pushpi, Sada-pushpi, Pratyak-pushpi — these ten promote emesis (vomiting therapy). (47)

Sahta, Madhua, Kachnar, Kaner, Karbuda, Arani, Aral, Upvidula, Bimbi or Kadabi, Tumbi, Shana-pushpi, Sada-pushpi, Pratyak-pushpi — these ten decoctions cause vomiting. (47)

Draksha, Kashmari, Parusha, Amalaki, Vibhitaka, Kuvala, Badara, Kekenda, Pilu — these ten are useful for purgation (virechana) therapy. (48)

चरकसंहितायाम् ।
Digitized By Slodhanka Sangum Gyaan Kosha

मुनक्का केशर काश्मरी अपरूषक(फाल
सा )हरडे आंवले वहेडा कमलवेर हाऊवेर
पीलु ये दश कषाय दस्तावर होतेहैं॥ ४८॥
त्रिवृद्धिल्विपिप्पलीकुष्ठसर्षपवचा
वत्सकफलशतपुष्पामधुकमदन
फलानीतिदशेमान्यास्थापनीयो
पगानिभवन्ति ।। ४९ ।।
हरडे बेल पीपल कूट सरसो वच वांसे-
काफल सौंफ महुआ मेनफल ये दश
कषाय मलबंधक होतेहैं ॥ ४९ ॥
राश्नासुरदारुबिल्वमदनशतपुष्पा
वृश्चीरपुनर्नवाश्वदंष्ट्राघ्रिमन्थश्यो
णाकाइतिदशेमानिअनुवासनोप
गानिभवन्ति ।। ५० ।।
रायसन देवदारु बेल मेनफल सौंफ
विच्छू घास सांटि अश्वदंष्ट्रा ( गोखरू)
एरण्डी स्योनाक अरलू ये दश कषाय
अनुवासन (सुगंधिकारक) होतेहैं॥५०॥
ज्योतिष्मतीक्षवकमिरचपिप्पली
विडङ्गशियुसर्षपापामार्गतण्डुल
श्वेतामहाश्वेताइतिदशेमानिनि
शिरोविरेचनोपगानिभवन्ति ॥ ५१ ॥
इति षट्वं॰ः कषायवर्गः।
ज्योतिष्मती (मालकांगनी) छत्राक
मिरच पीपल वायविडंग सिहंजना सरसों
अपामार्ग ( ओंगा ) तंडुल श्वेता महा-
श्वेता ये दश कषाय शिरके विरेचनकारक
होतेहैं ॥ ५१ ॥
यह सातकषायोंका वर्ग है ।

जम्बवाम्रपञ्चवमातुलुङ्गाम्लवदरदा
डिमयवयष्टिकोशीरमृद्गाजाइति
दशेमानिछदींनिग्रहाणिभवन्ति५२
जामुन आमकेपते मातुलुंग(बिजोरा)
इमली वेर अनार जौं मुलहटी उशीर
चंदनकी मिट्टीखील ये दश कषाय
वमनको रोकतेहैं ॥ ५२ ॥
नागरभन्वयवासकमुस्तपर्पटक
चन्दनिकिरातितक्कगुडूचीही
वेरधान्यकपटोलानीतिदशेमा
नितृष्णानिग्रहाणिभवन्त५३
सूंठ धवासा मोथा पित्तपापडा चंदन
चिरायता गिलोह हाऊवेर धनियां परवल
ये दश तृषाकी रोकतेहैं ॥ ५३ ॥
शटीपुष्करमूलवदरबीजकण्टका
रिकावृहतीवृक्षरुहाभयापिप्पली
दुरालभाकुलीरथ्रडञ्चइतिदशेमा
मानिहिक्कानिग्रहाणिभवन्त५४
इतित्रिकःकषायवर्गः।
शटी ( कचूर ) पोहकरमूल वेरकी
गुठली कटेहलीवडी आकाशवेल हरडे
पीपल दुरालभा ( चिरिचटा ) कुलीर-
शृंगी ( काकडासिंगी) ये दश हिचकीको
रोकतेहैं ॥ ५४ ॥
यह तीनकषायोंका वर्गहैं ।
प्रियंगवनन्ताम्रास्थिकट्वङ्गलोधमो
चरससमङ्गाधातकीपुष्पपझाप
translation:
(32)
From the Charaka Samhita

GROUPS OF DECOCTION HERBS

[Verse 48 — Stool-firming decoctions:]
Munakka (dried grapes), Kesar (saffron), Kashmari, Parushaka (falsa), Harade (haritaki), Amla (Indian gooseberry), Baheda (bibhitaki), Kamalvera, Hauvera, and Pilu — these ten decoctions are astringent (stool-binding). ॥48॥

[Verse 49 — Enema-preparatory herbs:]
Trivrit, Bilva, Pippali, Kushtha, Sarshapa, Vacha, Vatsaka fruit, Shatapushpa, Madhuka, and Madanaphala — these ten are known as asthapaniya (useful for retention enemas). ॥49॥

[Verse 49 commentary:]
Harade, Bel, Peepal, Kut, Sarso (mustard), Vacha, Vansakaphala, Saunf (fennel), Mahua, and Menaphala — these ten decoctions are stool-binding. ॥49॥

[Verse 50 — Anuvasana enema herbs:]
Rasna, Suradaru (devadaru), Bilva, Madana, Shatapushpa, Vrischira, Punarnava, Ashvadanshtra, Ghrimantha, and Shyonaka — these ten are used as anuvasana (oil-enema) adjuncts. ॥50॥

[Commentary:]
Rayasana, Devadaru, Bel, Menaphala, Saunf, Bichu-grass, Santi, Ashvadanshtra (Gokhru), Erand (castor), Shyonak, and Aralu — these ten decoctions are for anuvasana (fragrance-producing) enemas. ॥50॥

[Verse 51 — Errhine/head-purging herbs:]
Jyotishmati, Kshavaka, Maricha (pepper), Pippali, Vidanga, Shigru, Sarshapa, Apamarga seeds, Shveta, and Mahashveta — these ten are used as errhine (head-cleansing) adjuncts. ॥51॥

Here ends the sixth group of decoction herbs.

[Commentary:]
Jyotishmati (Malkangni), Chatrak, Mircha, Peepal, Vaividang, Sahajana, Sarso (mustard), Apamarg (Onga), Tandul, Shveta, and Mahashveta — these ten decoctions cause purgation through the head. ॥51॥

This completes the group of seven decoction categories.

[Verse 52 — Anti-emetic decoctions:]
Jambu (jamun), Amra (mango), Pancha, Matulunga, Amla, Vadara, Dadima (pomegranate), Yava (barley), Yashti (licorice), Ushira, and Mrittika (clay) — these ten curb vomiting. ॥52॥

[Commentary:]
Jamun, unripe mango, Matulunga (citron/bijoura), tamarind, ber, pomegranate, barley, mulahati (licorice), ushir, sandalwood, and clay pills — these ten decoctions check vomiting. ॥52॥

[Verse 53 — Anti-thirst decoctions:]
Nagara (ginger), Bhanvya, Vasaka, Musta, Parpataka, Chandanika, Kirata (chirayata), Tikta, Guduchi, Hrivera, Dhanyaka, and Patola — these ten relieve thirst. ॥53॥

[Commentary:]
Dry ginger, Dhavasa, Motha, Pittapapda, Sandalwood, Chirayata, Giloy, Hauvera, Coriander, and Parval — these ten decoctions check thirst. ॥53॥

[Verse 54 — Anti-hiccup decoctions:]
Shati, Pushkaramula, Vadara seeds, Kantakarika, Brihatī, Vriksharuha, Abhaya, Pippali, Duralabha, Kulirathrd — these ten are hiccup-suppressants. ॥54॥

Here ends the third group of decoction herbs.

[Commentary:]
Shati (Kachur), Pokhar-root, Ber kernel, Katehli-badi, Akashbel, Harade, Peepal, Duralabha (chirichata), and Kulirshringi (Kakdasingi) — these ten check hiccups. ॥54॥

This completes the group of three decoction categories.

सूत्रस्थानम् । ( ३३ )

म्केशराणीतिदशेमानिपुरीषसंग्रहणानिभवन्ति ॥ ५५ ॥

चिरौंजी अनंता (जवासा) आमकी गुठली कूटलोध मोचरस(मजीठ)समंगाधाइकेफूल पझाख कमलकी केशार ये दश मलको रोकतेहैं ॥ ५५ ॥

जम्बुशल्कीत्वक्कच्छुरामधूक शाल्मलीश्रीवेष्टकभृष्टमृतपयस्योत्पलतिलकणाइतिदशेमानिपुरीषविरजनीयानिभवन्ति ॥ ५६ ॥

जामुन शल्कली (चीढ) की त्वचा कच्छुरा(जवासा कचूर) महुआ सेंभल श्रीवेष्टक (कुंदुरु) भुनी मिट्टी जल कमल तिल पीपल ये दश मलको स्वच्छ करतेहैं ॥ ५६ ॥

जम्बवाम्रमुक्षवटकपीतनोदुम्बराश्वत्थभल्लातकाश्मन्तकसोमवल्काइतिदशेमानिमूत्रसंग्रहणानिभवन्ति ॥ ५७ ॥

जामुन आम पिलखन बड़ कैथ गूलर पीपल भल्लातक (भिलावे) अश्मंतक (बहेड़ा) सोमवल्क ये दश मूत्रका संग्रह (रोक) करतेहैं ॥ ५७ ॥

वृक्षादनोश्वदंष्ट्रावमुकोशीरपाषाणभेद्दर्भकुशपमोत्पलनलिनकुमुदसौगंधिकपुण्डरीकशतपत्रमधुकप्रियंगुधातकीपुष्पाणीतिदशेमानिमूत्रविरेजनीयानिभवन्ति॥५८

वृक्षाकाशगुन्द्रोत्कटमूलानीतिदशेमानिमूत्रविरेचनीयानिभवन्ति ॥ ५९ ॥

इति पञ्चकः कषायवर्गः ।

मैनफल अश्वदंष्ट्रा (गोख रू) वसुक उशीर (खस) पाषाणभेद् दर्भ कुश (कास)गुंद्र उत्कट इनकी जड़ ये दश मूत्रके शोधक होतेहैं । कुमुद पद्म उत्पल नलिन सौगंधिक पुष्प पुंडरीक शतपत्र महुआ फूल प्रियंगु धाईके पुष्प ये दश मूत्रके विरेचनकारक होतेहैं ॥५८ ॥ ५९ ॥

यह पांच कषायोंका वर्गहै।

श्राक्षाभयामलकपिप्पलीदुरालभाशृंगीकण्टकारिकारिरकावृश्चीरपुनर्नवातामलकयइतिदशेमानिकासहराणिभवन्ति ॥ ६० ॥

मुनक्कादाख हरडे आंवले पीपल चिरचिटा काकडाशिंगी कटेहली विच्छुघास सांठी आंवले ये दश कासको नष्ट करतेहैं ॥ ६० ॥

शटीपुष्करमूलाम्लवेतसैलाहींगव गुरुसुरसातामलकीजीवन्तीचण्डाइतिदशेमानिश्वासहराणिभवन्ति ॥ ६१ ॥

शटी (कचूर) पोहकरमूल अमल-वेत इलायची हींग अगर सुरसा (तुलसी) आमलकी जीवंती (हरडे) चंडा ये दश श्वास हरतेहैं ॥ ६१ ॥

[Verse 55]
These ten substances are known as stool-binding (mala-sangrahaniya):

Chironji, Ananta (Javasa), mango kernel, Kutaja bark, Mocharasa (Majith), Samanga, Dhai flower, Padmakh, lotus pistil, and Kesar — these ten check (bind) the stools.

[Verse 56]
These ten substances are known as stool-purifying (purisha-virajaniya):

The bark of Jamun, Shallaki (Chidh), Kachhura (Javasa/Kachur), Mahua, Shembhal, Shrivestaka (Kunduru), roasted clay, water lotus, sesame, and Peepal — these ten cleanse the stools.

[Verse 57]
These ten substances are known as urine-binding (mutra-sangrahaniya):

Jamun, mango, Pilakhan, Banyan, Kaitha, Gular, Peepal, Bhallatak (Bhilave), Ashmantaka (Baheda), and Somavalka — these ten check (retain) urine.

[Verse 58]
These ten substances are known as urine-purifying (mutra-virajaniya):

Vriksha-adana, Gokshura, Vasuka, Ushira (Khas), Pashanabheda, Darbha, Kusha, Padma, Utpala, Nalina, Kumuda, Saugandhika flower, Pundarika, Shatapatra, Mahua flower, and Priyangu and Dhai flowers — these ten purify the urine.

[Verse 59]
These ten substances are the roots of Vriksha, Akasha, Gundra, and Utkata — these are known as diuretics (mutra-virecaniya).

This concludes the group of five astringent (Kashaya) categories.

Mango raisin (Munakka), Harade, Amla, Pippali, Chirchita, Kakadashinghi, Katehali, Scorpion-grass (Vichhughas), Santhi, and Amla — these ten destroy cough (kasa).

[Verse 60]
Shati (Kachur), Pokharmoola, Amlaveta, Cardamom, Asafoetida, Agaru, Surasa (Tulsi), Amalaki, Jivanti (Harade), and Chanda — these ten relieve asthma (shvasa).

[Verse 61]
This completes the relevant group.

text:
( ३४ )

पाटलाग्निमन्थिबिल्वश्योणाककाश्मर्यकण्टकारिकाबृहतीशाालपण्णीपृश्निपर्णीगोश्रुकाइतिदशेमानिशोथहराणिभवन्ति ।। ६२।।

पाठल (अग्निमंथ) अरणी बेल श्योणाक काश्मरी कटेहली बडीकटेहली शालपणीं पृश्निपणीं गोखरू ये दश शोथको हरतेंहैं ६२

शारिवाशर्करापाठामिञ्षाद्राक्षापीलपरुषकाभंयामलकिविमीतकानीतिदशेमानिज्वरहराणिभवन्ति ६३

शारिवा ( गुलसरके बीज ) शर्करा ( सीरिखस्त ) पाठा मजीठ दाख पीछु पंक्ष ( फालसे ) हरड़े आंवले बहेड़ा ये दश ज्वरको हरतेंहैं ॥ ६३ ॥

द्राक्षाखर्जूरिपयालबदरदाडिमभल्गुपरुषकेश्रुयवयष्टिकाइतिदशेमानिश्रमहराणिभवन्ति।।६४।।

इति पञ्चकः कषायवर्गः ।

मुनकादाखखजूर चिरौंजी बेर अनार फल्गु परुषक (फालसे) ईख जौं मुलहटी ये दश श्रमको हरतेंहैं ॥ ६४ ॥

यह पांच कषायोंका वर्ग है ।

लाजाचन्दनकाश्मर्यफलमधुकशर्करानीलोत्पलोशिरशारिवागुड़ूचीहींविराणीतिदशेमानिदाहप्रशमनानिभवन्ति ।। ६५ ।।

लाजा चंदन काश्मरीका फल महुआ

शर्करा नील उत्पल उशीर ( खस ) शारिवा गिलोय हाऊबेर ये दश दाहको शांत करतेंहैं ॥ ६५॥

तगरागुरुधान्यकश्तुङ्क्वेरभूतिकवचाकण्टकारिकाग्निमन्थश्योणाकिपिप्पल्यइतिदशेमानिशीतप्रशमनानिभवन्ति ।। ६६ ।।

तगर अगर धानियां शृंगवेर भूतिक वच कटेहली अग्निमंथ श्योनाक पीपल ये दश शीतको शांत करतेंहैं ॥ ६६ ॥

तिन्दुकिपियालबदरखदिरकदरसतपर्णिश्वकर्णाऽर्जुनासनारिमेदाइतिदर्शेमान्युदर्दंमश्मनानिभवन्ति ६ ७

तेंदू चिरौंजी बेर खैर कुंदर सत्तपर्णे अश्वकणे (सांल) अर्जुन असन अरिमेद ये दश उदर्दको शांत करतेंहैं ॥ ६७ ॥

विदारिगन्धापृश्निपर्णीबृहतीकण्टकारिकेरण्डकाकोलीचन्दनोशिरैलामधुकानीतिदशेमान्यङ्गमर्दप्रशमनानिभवन्ति।। ६८ ।।

विदारिगंधा पृश्निपणी कटेहली कंटकारी अरंड काकोली चंदन उशीर (खस) इलायची मधुआ ये दश अंगमर्दको शांत करतेंहैं ॥ ६८ ॥

पिप्पलीपिप्पलीमूलचव्याचेत्र कश्तुङ्क्वेरमिरचाजमोदाजगन्धाजाजीगण्डीराणीतिदशेमानिश्रूलप्रशमनानिभवन्ति ।। ६९ ।।

इति पञ्चकःकषायवर्गः ।
translation:
(Page 34)

[Verse 62] Patala, Agnimanth, Bilva, Shyonaka, Kashmari, Kantakarika, Brihati, Shalapparni, Prishniparni, and Gokshura — these ten herbs alleviate edema (shotha).

Commentary: Patala (Agnimanth), Arani, Bilva, Shyonaka, Kashmari, Katehali (small), Katehali (large), Shalapani, Prishniparni, Gokharu — these ten relieve swelling. [62]

[Verse 63] Shariva, Sharkara, Patha, Manjishtha, Draksha, Pilu, Parushaka, Bhamyamalaki, and Vimitaka — these ten alleviate fever (jvara).

Commentary: Shariva (seeds of Gulsar), Sharkara (candy sugar), Patha, Majith, Dakha, Pikhu (Phalsa), Harade, Amla, Bahera — these ten relieve fever. [63]

[Verse 64] Draksha, Kharjura, Piyala, Badara, Dadima, Bhalguperushaka, Ikshu, Yava, and Yashtika — these ten relieve fatigue (shrama).

This is the group of the five astringent (kashaya) categories.

Commentary: Munakka, Dakh, Khajur, Chironji, Ber, Anar, Falgu, Parushak (Phalsa), Ikh, Jau, Mulahti — these ten relieve fatigue. [64]

This is the group of the five astringents (kashaya).

[Verse 65] Laja, Chandana, Kashmarya-fruit, Madhuka, Sharkara, Nilotpala, Ushira, Shariva, and Guduchi — these ten alleviate burning sensation (daha).

Commentary: Laja, Chandan, Fruit of Kashmari, Mahua, Sugar, Blue lotus, Khus (Ushira), Shariva, Giloy, Haubera — these ten relieve burning sensation. [65]

[Verse 66] Tagara, Agaru, Dhanyaka, Shringavera, Bhutika, Vacha, Kantakarika, Agnimanth, Shyonaka, and Pippali — these ten alleviate cold (shita).

Commentary: Tagar, Agar, Dhania, Shringavar (ginger), Bhutak, Bach, Katehali, Agnimanth, Shyonak, Pippali — these ten relieve cold. [66]

[Verse 67] Tinduka, Piyala, Badara, Khadira, Kadara, Sataparna, Ashvakarna, Arjuna, Asana, and Arimeda — these ten alleviate skin eruptions (udarda).

Commentary: Tendu, Chironji, Ber, Kher, Kundar, Satparne, Ashvakane (Sal), Arjun, Asan, Arimedh — these ten relieve skin eruptions. [67]

[Verse 68] Vidarigandha, Prishniparni, Brihati, Kantakarika, Eranda, Kakoli, Chandana, Ushira, Ela, and Madhuka — these ten alleviate body-ache (angamarda).

Commentary: Vidarigandhaa, Prishniparni, Katehali, Kantakaari, Arand, Kakoli, Chandan, Khus (Ushira), Cardamom, Madhua — these ten relieve body ache. [68]

[Verse 69] Pippali, Pippali-mula, Chavya, Chitraka, Shringavera, Maricha, Ajamoda, Ajagandha, Jaji, and Gandira — these ten alleviate colic pain (shula).

Here ends the fifth group of the astringent (kashaya) category.

text:
Digitized By SIddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha
सूत्रस्थानम् ।                                                        ( ३५ )

पीपल पीपलामूल चव्य चीता शृंगवेर
मिरच अजमोद अजगंधा अजाजी(जीरा)
गंडीर ये दश शूलको शांत करतेहैं॥ ६९॥
यह पांच कषायोंका वर्ग है ।

मधुमधुकरुधिरमोचरसमृत्कपाल
लोध्रगैरिकभियंगुशर्करालाजाइति
दशेमानिशोणितस्थापनानिभव
न्ति ॥ ७० ॥

सहत महुआ रुधिर मोचरस मृत्क-
पाल लोध गेरु प्रियंगु शर्करा लाजा ये
दश रुधिरके स्थापन होतेहैं ॥ ७० ॥

शालकटुफलकदम्बपष्मकतुङ्गमो
चरसिशिरीषवंजुलैलावालुकाशो
काइतिदशेमानिवेदनास्थापनानि
भवन्ति ॥ ७१ ॥

शाल कायफल कदंब पद्माखं तुरंग
मोचरस सिरस बंजुल पलवा बालुका
अशोक ये दश वेदना ( दर्द ) के स्थापक
होतेहैं अर्थात् बढ़ने नहीं देतेहैं ॥ ७१॥

हिंगुकैटर्य्यिरिमेदवचाजीर्कवय:
स्थागोलोमीजटिलापलङ्कूषाशो
करोहिण्यइतिदशेमानिसंज्ञास्था
पनानिभवन्ति ॥ ७२ ॥

हींग कैटर्य्ये अरिमेद ( विट्खदिर )
बच जीरा वयस्था गोलोमी जटिला
पलंकषा (लाख) अशोक रोहिणी ये दश
संज्ञाके स्थापन होते हैं अर्थात् सावधानी
रखते हैं ॥ ७२ ॥

ऐन्द्रीब्राह्मीशतवीर्य्यासहस्रवीर्य्यां
मोघाव्यथाशिवारिष्टावाञ्यपुष्पी
विष्वक्सेनकान्ताइतिदशेमानिभ्र
जास्थापनानिभवन्ति ॥ ७३ ॥

इंद्री ( इंद्रायण ) ब्राही शतवीर्यां
( सौंफ ) सहस्रवीर्यां शतावर अमोघा
अव्यथा ( बडी हरडे ) हरडे अरिष्टा
वाञ्यपुष्पी-विष्वक्सेन कांता ये दश
प्रजा ( संतान ) केस्थापन होतेहैं॥७३॥

अमृताभयाधात्रीमुक्ताश्वेताजीव
न्त्यतिरसामण्डूकपर्णीस्थरापुन
र्नवाइतिदशेमानिवयस्थापनानि
भवन्ति ॥ ७४ ॥

इति पञ्चकःकषायवर्गः ।
गिलोय हरडे आंवला मुक्ता श्वेता
जीवंती अतिरसा मंडूकपर्णी स्थिरा पुन-
र्नवा-( विषखपरा ) ये दश अवस्थाके
स्थापन होतेहैं ॥ ७४ ॥

यह पांच कषायोंका वर्ग है ।
इति पञ्चकषायशतान्याभिसम
स्यपञ्चाशन्महाकषायाःमहता
ञ्चकषायाणां लक्षणोदाहरणार्थं
व्याख्याताभवन्ति ॥ ७५ ॥

ये पांचसो कषायोंमेंसे संक्षेप करके
पचास कषाय-बडे २ कषायोंके लक्षण
और उदाहरणके लिये वर्णन कियेहैं॥७५॥

नहिविस्तररूपप्रमाणमस्तिनचाप्य
तिसंक्षेपोऽल्पबुद्धीनांसामर्थ्यतो

Sutrasthana (Chapter on Fundamental Principles)                    (35)

Pippala (long pepper), Pippalamula (root of long pepper), Chavya, Chita, Shringavera (ginger), Mircha (pepper), Ajamoda, Ajagandha, Ajaji (cumin), Gandira — these ten pacify colic pain. (69)
This is the group of five astringents.

Madhu (honey), Madhuka, Rudhira (blood), Mocharasa, Mrittika (clay), Kapala, Lodhra, Gaurika, Priyanghu, Sharkara (sugar), Laja — these ten are the stanchers of bleeding, and are known as the ten blood-stopping agents. (70)

Sehata (Mahoa), Rudhira, Mocharasa, Mrittikakpal, Lodha, Geru, Priyanghu, Sharkara, Laja — these ten are the stoppers of blood. (70)

Shala, Katufala, Kadamba, Padmakha, Turanga, Mocharasa, Shirisha, Vanjula, Elava, Valuka, Ashoka — these ten are the pain-checking agents known as Vedanasthapana. (71)

Shala, Kayaphala (Kataphala), Kadamba, Padmakha, Turangamocharasa, Shirisha, Vanjula, Palava, Valuka, Ashoka — these ten check pain, that is, they prevent it from increasing. (71)

Hingu (asafoetida), Kaitarya, Irimeda, Vacha, Ajirka, Vaya, Sthagolomі, Jatila, Palankusha, Ashokarohinī — these ten are the consciousness-restoring agents known as Sanjnasthapana. (72)

Hingu (asafoetida), Kaitarya, Irimeda (Vitkhadira), Vacha, Jira, Vayastha, Golomi, Jatila, Palankasha (lac), Ashoka, Rohini — these ten restore consciousness, that is, they maintain alertness. (72)

Aindri, Brahmi, Shataveerya, Sahasraveerya, Amogha, Avyatha, Shiva, Arishta, Vanjyapushpi, Vishvaksena, Kanta — these ten are the life-stabilizing agents known as Prajasthapana. (73)

Indri (Indrayana), Brahmi, Shataveerya (fennel), Sahasraveerya, Shatavar, Amogha, Avyatha (large haritaki), Harade, Arishta, Vanjyapushpi, Vishvaksena, Kanta — these ten promote progeny (offspring). (73)

Amrita, Abhaya, Dhatri, Mukta, Shveta, Jivanti, Atirasa, Mandukparni, Sthira, Punarnava — these ten are the age-stabilizing agents known as Vayasthapana. (74)

Thus ends the group of Panchaka Kashaya.
Giloya, Harade, Amalaki, Mukta, Shveta, Jivanti, Atirasa, Mandukparni, Sthira, Punarnava (Vishakhapara) — these ten stabilize bodily condition (youth). (74)

This is the group of five astringents.
Thus, from the five hundred astringents, fifty major groups of astringents have been described in brief, for the purpose of explaining the characteristics and examples of the major astringent groups. (75)

These five hundred astringents have been condensed into fifty, and the characteristics and examples of the major groups have been described herein. (75)

Neither is an exhaustive elaboration possible, nor is extreme brevity suitable given the limited capacity of less advanced intellects —

पकल्पतेतस्मादनितसंक्षेपेणानिति
विस्तरेणचोदिष्टाः।एतावन्तोह्यल्प

क्योंकि विस्तारका कोई प्रमाण नहीं
है–और अत्यंत संक्षेपभी अल्प बुद्धियोंके

कियेहैं–इतनेही कषाय अल्पबुद्धियोंके
व्यवहारके लिये और बुद्धिमानोंके अनुक्त
अर्थके ज्ञानार्थं जो सुंदर लक्षण अनुमान
और युक्तिमें कुशलहैं–बहुतहैं–इति ७६

एवंवादिनंभगवन्तमात्रेयमिग्वि

कर्तृकरणकार्य्यसंप्रयुक्तंतद्द्रौ

translation:
( 36 )
[From the Charaka Samhita]

[Verse 76]:
Therefore it has been stated here neither too briefly nor too elaborately. This much is sufficient — for the practical use of those of lesser intelligence, and for those skilled in inference, reasoning and the understanding of implied meanings who are of higher intellect — to convey what has not been explicitly stated. Thus ends verse 76.

[Commentary on verse 76]:
Because there is no fixed limit to elaboration, and extreme brevity is not suitable for those of lesser capacity, the description has been given avoiding both extremes — extreme brevity and extreme elaboration. This much about the kasha-yas (medicinal decoctions) is sufficient: for the practical use of those of lesser intelligence, and for those of higher intelligence who are skilled in inference and reasoning to understand the implied meaning — there are many such. Thus 76.

[Verse 77]:
Thus spoke Agnivesha to the revered Atreya: "O Lord, five hundred kashayas cannot be completed by these alone, for the same ingredients appear in various mahakashayas." Thus verse 77.

[Commentary on verse 77]:
While the revered Atreya was speaking thus, Agnivesha said: "O Lord, five hundred kashayas cannot be completed by these alone, because the same constituent herbs appear in various mahakashayas — that is, the same medicines come back in different combinations." Thus 77.

[Sanskrit prose passage]:
Then the revered Atreya replied to him: "O Agnivesha, a wise man should not view it in this way. Even a single person, by performing various functions, acquires many designations. Just as a person is capable of performing many actions, and with each action he performs, through the connection of agent, instrument and result, he acquires a specific secondary name — so too should medicinal substances be viewed. If one were to obtain a single substance endowed with the qualities capable of performing all functions, then who would desire to teach other substances to students? — but such a single substance does not exist." Thus 78.

[Verse 79]:
Here are the summary verses:
From whatever substances and by whatever means the six hundred types of purgatives have been described here in summary — likewise their sixfold classification is established here. Thus verse 79.

In this, the verses are: from whichever substances the six hundred purgative substances have been collected and described in this text, those substances are the six bases of these. (79)

"Excepting salt, these are known as Kashaya (astringents); hence the five-fold source of Kashayas is described." (80)

Setting aside salt, these are called Kashayas; thus the origin of Kashayas is described as being of five kinds. (80)

"And again, the preparation of these has been described as five-fold; the great Kashayas are enumerated as fifty." (81)

Similarly, their preparation has also been described as of five kinds, and the major Kashayas are said to be fifty. (81)

"Five hundred Kashayas have also been described, section by section; and there is no fixed limit of elaboration as to their characteristics and meaning." (82)

And five hundred Kashayas have also been described section by section for the purpose of defining their characteristics, and there is no fixed measure of elaboration. (82)

"An extremely brief treatment is not adequate for the purpose; therefore, for those of lesser intellect, this is neither too condensed nor too elaborate." (83)

And an extremely brief treatment is not suitable for the purpose; therefore, for those of lesser intellect, it is neither too condensed nor too elaborate. (83)

"This group of fifty Kashayas is set forth for the practical use of those of dull intellect and for the enhancement of the understanding of the learned." (84)

And this is for the practical use of those of dull intellect and for sharpening the understanding of the learned — this group of fifty Kashayas has been described. (84)

"One who knows the application of these in external and internal conditions, their combination and their separation — that one is the best among physicians." (85)

One who knows the application of these in external and internal functions, and also their combination and separation, is the foremost among physicians. (85)

The fourth chapter, named Bheshaja-chatushka Shad-virechana-shataashritiya, is hereby concluded.
Thus ends the Bheshaja-chatushka.

Now begins the Fifth Chapter.
Now we shall explain the chapter called Matrashitiya (on the proper measure of food).
We now describe the Matrashitiya chapter.

Thus has the Venerable Atreya said:
This has been stated by the Blessed Atreya.
One should eat in proper measure. The measure of food depends upon the strength of one's digestive fire. The amount of food that one has eaten, when it does not disturb the bodily wind and digests at the proper time — that is the measure of one's proper food quantity.

translation:
(Page 38 of the Charaka Samhita)

One must know this: Among food substances, shali rice, shashtika rice, mudga (green gram), lava (quail), kapinjala (partridge), ena (antelope), shasha (hare), sharabha (a deer), shambara (deer) and similar items are by nature light, yet they still require consideration of proper measure (matra). Similarly, food substances like milk preparations, masha (black gram), aquatic and marshy meats, and other foods that are by nature heavy also require measure. Thus it is not without reason that heaviness and lightness are attributed to substances. Light substances are rich in the qualities of wind and fire, while heavy substances are rich in the qualities of earth and water (soma). Therefore, light substances, by virtue of their own qualities, are said to kindle the digestive fire (agni) and cause little harm even when consumed to satiation. Heavy substances, however, do not have the nature of kindling the digestive fire, and when consumed beyond measure in an unusual manner, even those used with satiation become vitiated, unless there is strength of digestive fire and exercise. This measure, which depends on the digestive fire and bodily strength, does not mean that the nature of the substance is irrelevant — for heavy substances, it is taught that one should eat only one-third to one-half of satiation. For light substances too, one should not consider it entirely beneficial to eat to full satiation with regard to the proper use of digestive fire, because with respect to measure —

Thus the measure that is determined in accordance with one's digestive capacity, when properly followed without disturbing one's natural constitution, promotes strength, complexion, happiness, and longevity for the person.

इसमें ये श्लोकभीहैं कि मोटे चावलों-
काभी चूर्ण जिससे गरिष्ठहै तिससे भोजन
किये पीछे इसको न खाय और जो भूखाहै
वह मात्रासे खाय ॥ २ ॥

वछूरंशुष्कशाकानिशालूकानिबि
सानिच । नाभ्यस्येद्वौरवान्मांसं
कृशनैवोपयोजयेत् ॥ ३ ॥

मांस सूकेशाक शालूक बिस इनको
नखाय–गुरुहोनेसे मांसका अभ्यास न करे
और न कृश मनुष्यको मांसदे ॥ ३ ॥

कुिर्चिकांश्विकलाटांश्वशौकरंगव्य
माहिषे । मत्स्यानृदधिचमाषां
श्चयवकांश्वनशीलयेत् ॥ ४ ॥

कुर्चिक किलाट ( फटादूध ) सूकर
गौ भैंस इनके मांस मत्स्य दधि उड्द जों
इनलोभी विशेषकर न खाय ॥ ४ ॥

षष्टिकाचृशालिमुद्गांश्वसैन्धवाम
लकेयवाचृ । आन्तरीक्षंपयःस
पिर्जिङ्गलंमधुचाभ्यसेत् ॥ ५ ॥

साठीचावल तंडुल मूंग सींधानून

आंवले जौ आकाश ( वर्षा ) काजल
घी और जंगलका सहत इनका अभ्यास
करे ॥ ५ ॥

तचिनित्यंप्रयुञ्जीतस्वास्थ्यंयेनानु
वर्तते । अजातानांविकाराणाम
नुत्पत्तिकरञ्चयत् ॥ ६ ॥

और जिस द्रव्यसे स्वस्थता बनीरहे
उसको नित्य खा। जो शरीरमें विनाउत्पन्न
किये विकारोंको पैदा न करे उसकोभीखा६

अतऊर्ध्वशरिरस्यकार्यमभ्यञ्ज
नादिकम् । स्वस्थवृत्तमिभिप्रेत्य
गुणतःसंप्रवक्ष्यते ॥ ७ ॥

इससे आगे शरीरके अभ्यंजन आदि-
का कार्य स्वस्थताके वृत्तांतको जानकर
गुणसे वर्णन करतेहैं ॥ ७ ॥

सौवीरमञ्जनंनित्यंहितमक्ष्णोःअ्
योजयेत् । पञ्चरात्रेऽष्टरात्रेवा
स्रावणार्थेरसाञ्जनम् ॥ ८ ॥

प्रतिदिन हितकारी चंदनका अंजन
नेत्रोंमें लगावे पांचरात्रमें वा अष्टरात्रमें
जल निकासनेके लिये रसका अंजन जो
लगावे ॥ ८ ॥

निहिनेत्रामयंतस्यविशेषात्श्लेष्म
तोभयम् । दिवातञ्चप्रयोक्तव्यं
नेत्रयोस्तीक्ष्णमञ्जनम् ॥ ९ ॥

उसको विशेषकर कफसे भय और
नेत्ररोग नहीं होता और तीक्ष्ण अंजनको
नेत्रोंमें दिनमें लगावे ॥ ९ ॥

translation:
Sutra-sthana (Chapter 39)

[Verse 1] Eating food without disturbing one's natural constitution enhances strength, complexion, and well-being.

[Verse 2 - Sanskrit] Heavy, ground foods and flattened rice — one who has just eaten should not consume them again, while one who is hungry may eat them in proper measure.

[Commentary on verse 2] Among the verses here is the teaching that even the flour of coarse rice, which is heavy, should not be eaten again after a full meal; but one who is hungry may consume it in measured quantity.

[Verse 3 - Sanskrit] Dried vegetables, lotus roots, lotus stems, and the like — one should not habitually eat them. Meat should not be given excessively, nor should it be given to an emaciated person.

[Commentary on verse 3] Meat, dried greens, lotus tubers, and lotus stems — these should not be eaten. Because they are heavy, one should not make a habit of meat, and one should not give meat to an emaciated person.

[Verse 4 - Sanskrit] Kurchika, kilata, the flesh of pig, cow, and buffalo, fish, curd, black gram, barley, and canine flesh — these should not be made a habit.

[Commentary on verse 4] Kurchika (curdled milk solids), kilata (condensed milk), flesh of pig, cow, buffalo, fish, curd, black gram, and barley — these especially should not be eaten habitually.

[Verse 5 - Sanskrit] Shashtika rice, shali rice, green gram, rock salt, amla (Indian gooseberry), barley, rainwater, milk, the herb jingala, and honey — these should be regularly used.

[Commentary on verse 5] Shashtika rice, tandula rice, green gram, rock salt, amla, barley, rainwater, ghee, and forest honey — these should be used regularly.

[Verse 6 - Sanskrit] One should daily use that which maintains health and does not give rise to diseases that have not yet appeared; such substances should also be eaten habitually.

[Commentary on verse 6] That substance by which good health is maintained, consume that daily. Whatever does not cause disorders to arise in the body without reason — eat that too.

[Verse 7 - Sanskrit] Hereafter, the practices concerning the body such as anointing (abhyanga) and related activities will be described with their qualities, keeping in view the principles of healthy living.

[Commentary on verse 7] From here onward, the practices for the body such as anointing and related activities are described with their qualities, with knowledge of the account of healthy living.

[Verse 8 - Sanskrit] Sauviranjana (a beneficial collyrium) should be applied to the eyes every day. For the purpose of promoting secretion, rasanjana (extract collyrium) should be applied every five or eight nights.

[Commentary on verse 8] Apply the beneficial sandalwood collyrium to the eyes daily. Every five nights or every eight nights, apply rasanjana collyrium for the purpose of drawing out excess fluid.

[Verse 9 - Sanskrit] This especially protects against eye diseases and fear of kapha (mucous disorders). Sharp (tikshna) collyrium should be applied to the eyes during the daytime.

[Commentary on verse 9] By this, fear of kapha and eye disease does not arise. Sharp collyrium should be applied to the eyes during the day.

text:
( ४० )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।
Digitized By Slddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

विरेकंदुर्वेलादिष्ठरादित्यंप्राप्य सीदति । तस्मात्स्नाप्यंनिशायान्तुष्टुवमअनिमष्यते ॥ १० ॥

विरेचनसे दुर्बल हुई दृष्टि सूर्यकी प्राप्ति होनेपर नष्ट होजातीहै तिससे जलनिकासनेका अंजन रात्रिके विषे विशेषकर इष्टहै ॥ १० ॥

ततःश्लेष्महरंकर्महितंदृष्टेःप्रसादनम् ॥ ११ ॥

फिर कफहारक कर्म दृष्टिकी प्रसन्नताका कला हितहै ॥ ११ ॥

यथाहिकणकादीनामिलनांविविधात्मनाम् । धौतानांनिर्मलाशुद्धिस्तैलचेलकचादिभिः ॥ १२ ॥

जैसे अनेक प्रकारके मलीन कणक आदिजो धोयेहैं उनकी निर्मल शुद्धि तेल वस्त्र केश आदिसे होती है ॥ १२ ॥

एवेनेत्रेषुमर्त्यानामअनाश्च्योतनादिभिः । दृष्टिर्निराकुलाभातिनिर्मलेनभसींदुवत् ॥ १३ ॥

इस प्रकार मनुष्योंके नेत्र आदिमें अंजन और धोने आदिसे ऐसी निराकुल दृष्टि प्रकाशित होतीहै जैसे निर्मल आकाशमें चंद्रमा होताहै ॥ १३ ॥

हरेणुकांप्रियंगुञ्चपृथ्वीकांकेशरंनखम् । हीवेरंचन्दनंपत्रंवगे लोशीरपद्मकम् ॥ १४ ॥

हरेणु अर्थात् महदी वा निर्गुंडीके बीज–प्रियंगु पृथ्वीक ( इलायची ) केशर नख हाऊबेर चंदन पत्रज दालचिनी इलायची खस पद्माख ॥ १४ ॥

ध्यामकंमधुकंमांसिगुग्गुल्वगुरुशिंकंरम् । न्यग्रोधोदुम्बराश्वत्थपुंक्षलोघ्रत्वचःशुभाः ॥ १५ ॥

ध्यामक ( रोहिससोंधिया ) महुआ मांसी गुग्गुलु अगर मिसरी वड गूलर पीपल पीलखन लोध इनकी त्वचा नेत्रोंके अंजनमें हितहैं ॥ १५ ॥

वन्यंस्वर्जरसंमुस्तंशैलेयंकमलोत्पले । श्रीवेष्टकंशङ्खकीञ्चशुकबर्हमथापिच ॥ १६ ॥

वनकी खजूरकारस मोथा चंदन कमल उत्पल श्रीवेष्टक ( सरलकागोंद ) शङ्खकी ( शाखई ) तोतेका पंख ॥ १६ ॥

पिष्ट्वालिम्पेच्छरिषकांतांवर्तिंय वसिनभाम् । अंगुष्टसंमितांकुञ्च्यादष्टांगुलसमांभिषक् ॥ १७ ॥

इनको पीस जौके समान बत्ती बनाकर लेप करै वह बत्ती अंगुल भरकी होवा आठ अंगुलकी हो ऐसी वैद्य बनावै ॥ १७ ॥

शुष्कांविगभांतांवर्तिंसेधूमनेत्रार्पितांनरः । क्षेहाकामिञ्चसंपुष्टांपिबेत्प्रायोगिकींसुखाम् ॥ १८ ॥

गर्भ रहित सूंकी उस बत्तीको धूमको मनुष्य नेत्रोंमें लगावै और अग्निमें फूंककर घी मिलाकर प्रयोगसे पीवै तो सुखकारी होतीहै ॥ १८ ॥

translation:
(Page 40 of the Charaka Samhita)

Verse 10: When the vision, weakened by purgation (virechana), is harmed by exposure to the sun, it perishes. Therefore, the collyrium (anjana) that draws out moisture is especially recommended for use at night.

Verse 11: After that, the action that removes kapha (phlegm) is beneficial for the clarity of vision.

Verse 12: Just as various kinds of soiled grains and other things, when washed with oil, cloth, and hair, become pure and clean —

Verse 13: — similarly, by applying collyrium and washing the eyes of human beings, the vision becomes as clear and untroubled as the moon shining in a cloudless sky.

Verse 14: The following ingredients are enumerated: harenu (henna or nirgundi seed), priyangu, prithvika (cardamom), keshara (saffron), nakha (a fragrant shell), hauvera, chandana (sandalwood), patraja (cinnamon leaf), dalchini (cinnamon), ilayachi (cardamom), khasa (vetiver), and padmakha.

Verse 15: Dhyamaka (rohisa grass), madhuka (licorice), mansi (spikenard), guggulu (bdellium resin), aguru (agarwood), misri (sugar), vata (banyan), gular (cluster fig), pippala (sacred fig), pilakhan (a fig variety), and lodhra — the bark of these is beneficial as collyrium for the eyes.

Verse 16: Also: the juice of the wild date palm, motha (nut grass), chandana (sandalwood), kamala (lotus), utpala (blue lotus), shrivestaka (resin of the deodar or pine), shankhi (conch shell variety), and the feather of a parrot.

Verse 17: Having ground all these together, make a wick (vartika) similar in shape to a barleycorn; the physician should form it to be one finger-breadth in diameter and eight finger-breadths in length.

Verse 18: A man should apply the smoke of this dried wick to his eyes, and then, having ignited it in fire and mixed it with ghee, drink it as a therapeutic measure. This brings comfort and well-being.

text:
मंत्रस्थानम् ।
( ४१ )
Digitized By Slodhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

वसाधृतमधुच्छिद्रैयुंक्तियुक्तैवरौषधैः । वितेनमधुरकैःकृत्वाबत्तेहिकींधूममाचरेत् ॥ १९ ॥

वसाकां धी मोम और युक्तिसे युक्त श्रेष्ठ मधुर औषध इनकी बत्ती बनाकर घृत मिलाकर धूम ले ॥ १९ ॥

श्वेताज्योतिष्मतीचैवह्रिताल्ंमनःशिला । गन्धाश्वागुरुपत्राधा धूमोमूर्द्धिविरेचनम् ॥ २० ॥

श्वेता(फोडी) ज्योतिष्मती (मालकांनगी) हड़ताल मनसिल गंधा ( चंपाकी कली )अगर पत्रज इनका धूम मस्तकके विरेचनको करताहै ॥ २० ॥

गौरवंशिरसःशूलंपीनसार्द्धिवभेदकौ । कर्णोक्षिशूलंकासश्वहिक्काश्वासौगलग्रहः ॥ २१ ॥

शिरका भारापन पीनस आधे शिरका फूटना कान और नेत्रोंका शूल कास हुचकी श्वास गलग्रह ॥ २१ ॥

दन्तदौर्बल्यमास्नावःश्रोत्रघ्राणाक्षिदोषजः । पूतिघ्राणास्यगन्धश्वदन्तशूलमरीचकः ॥ २२ ॥

दांतोंका दौर्बल्य कान नेत्र नाक इनमें से जलका जाना नासिकाकी दुर्गंध मुखकी दुर्गंध दांतोंका शूल अरुचि २२

हनुमन्याग्रहःकण्डूःकिमयःपाण्डुतामुखे । श्लेष्मप्रसेकोवैस्वर्च्यंगलशुण्डयपिजिह्विका ॥ २३ ॥

ढोडीका जकडना खुजली किमि मुखकी पांडुता कफका प्रसेक ( वृद्धि ) स्वरका बिगडना गलगंड जिह्वाका जकडना २ ३

खालित्यंपिअरत्वञ्चकेशानांपतन्नतथा । क्षवथुश्वासिततन्द्राचबुद्धेर्मोहोऽतिनिद्रता ॥ २४ ॥

गंजापन पिंजरता केशोंका पडना क्षवथु अत्यंत तंद्रा बुद्धिका मोह अत्यंत निद्रा ॥ २४ ॥

धूमपानात्पशाम्यन्तिबलंभवतिचाधिकम् । शिरोरुहकपालानामिन्द्रियाणांस्वरस्यच ॥ २५ ॥

ये सब पूर्वोक्त औषधियोंके धूम्रपानसे शांत होतेहैं और अधिक बल होताहै केश कपाल इंद्रिय स्वर इनमें बल होताहै २५ ॥

नचवातकफात्मानोबलिनोऽप्युच्छ्वंजनुजाः । धूमरक्तकपालस्य व्याधयःस्युःशिरोगताः ॥ २६ ॥

और वात, कफ प्रकृतिके मनुष्यकेभी बलवान् होनेसे जत्रुके ऊपरके विकार शिरमें विकार इससे नहीं होते कि कपाल धूमसे रक्त होजाताहै ॥ २६ ॥

प्रयोगपानेतस्याष्टौकालाःसम्परिकीर्तिताः । वातश्लेष्मसमुत्क्लेशःकालेष्वेषुहिलक्ष्यते ॥ २७ ॥

उसके पीनेके प्रयोगमें आठ काल कहेहैं क्यों कि वात कफका क्लेश इन्हीं कालोंमें दीखताहै ॥ २७ ॥

translation:
[Chapter heading: Mantra-sthana, page 41]

Verse 19:
Using fat (vasa), ghee, honey, and appropriate medicinal substances of the best and sweet variety, one should make a wick and, after mixing ghee, inhale the smoke. (19)

Verse 20:
Shveta (a plant), Jyotishmati (Malkangni/Celastrus), Haritala (orpiment), Manashila (realgar), Gandha, Agaru, and Patraja — the smoke of these performs purgation/cleansing of the head. (20)

Verse 21:
Heaviness of the head, headache, sinusitis, half-sided headache, pain in the ears and eyes, cough, hiccup, breathlessness, and constriction of the throat — (21)

Verse 22:
Weakness of teeth, discharge from the ears, disorders of the ears, eyes, and nose, foul smell in the nose, bad odor of the mouth, toothache, loss of taste — (22)

Verse 23:
Stiffness of the lower jaw, itching, worms in the mouth, pallor of the face, excessive secretion of phlegm, hoarseness of voice, goiter, stiffness of the tongue — (23)

Verse 24:
Baldness, reddish discoloration of hair, hair-fall, sneezing, extreme drowsiness, confusion of intellect, and excessive sleep — (24)

Verse 25:
All the above conditions are pacified by inhalation of smoke from the previously mentioned medicinal substances, and moreover, strength is gained in the hair, skull, sense organs, and voice. (25)

Verse 26:
Even in persons of vata-kapha constitution who are strong, diseases situated in the head above the collar-bone do not occur, because the skull becomes well-supplied with blood through the smoke-inhalation. (26)

Verse 27:
Eight times (kala) are described for the practice of this smoke-inhalation therapy. This is because the disturbance of vata and kapha is observed during these specific times. (27)

text:
( ४२ )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।
Digitized By Slddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

स्नात्वासुक्तवासमुद्धृत्यक्षुत्वाद
न्तान्विघृष्यच।नावनाञनिन्द्रा
न्तेचात्मवान्धूमपोभवेत् ॥ २८॥

ज्ञान भोजन लिखना छीकना दांतोंको
घिसना दौड़ना अंजन निद्रा इनके अंतमें
बुद्धिमान् मनुष्य धूम्र पानकरै ॥ २८ ॥

तथावातकफात्मानोनभवन्त्युच्छृं
जञुजाः । रोगास्तस्यतुपेयाःस्यु
रापानास्त्रिस्त्रयस्त्रयः॥ २९॥

तो वात कफ प्रकृतिके मनुष्यको
जञुके ऊपरके रोग नहीं होते
और पीनेसे तीनों बस्ति पीनेके योग्य
होजातीहै ॥ २९ ॥

परंद्विकालपायीस्यादह्नःकालेषु
बुद्धिमान् । प्रयोगेऽसैहिकेत्वेवं
विरेच्यंत्रिःशतुःपिवेत् ॥ ३० ॥

और बुद्धिमान् मनुष्य दिनके कालोंमें
दोसमयमें धूमपान करै और एवंवा-
रकी विधि घृत आदि पीनके प्रयोगमें हैं
और विरेचन औषधियोंको तो तीन या
चारवार पीवै ॥ ३० ॥

हृतकण्ठेन्द्रियसंशुद्धिर्लघुत्वंशर
सःशमः । यथेरितानांदोषाणांस
म्यक्पीतस्यलक्षणम् ॥ ३१ ॥

इससे हृदय कंठ इंद्रिय इनकी शुद्धि
और शरकी लघुता और उन दोषोंकी
शांति होतीहै जो पिहले कहेहैं यह
अच्छे धूमपानका लक्षणहै ॥ ३१ ॥

बाधिर्यमान्ध्यमूकत्वंरक्तपिनंशि
रोभ्रमम् । अकालेचातिपीतस्य
धूमःकुर्याद्युपद्रवान् ॥ ३२ ॥

और बिना समय अत्यंत जो धूम्र
पान करताहै उसको ये उपद्रव धूम्रपान
करताहै कि बधिरता मंदता मूकता रक्त
पित्त शिरमें भ्रम ॥ ३२ ॥

तत्रेष्टंसर्पिषःपानंनावनाञनतर्पं
णम् । स्नैहिकंधूमजेदोषेवायुःपि
त्तानुगोयदि ॥ ३३ ॥

उनमें घीका पीना नावन अंजन
तर्पण ये इष्टहैं ( करने ) स्नेहके धूमसे
पैदा हुये दोषमें यदि वायुपित्तके अनु-
कूल होजाय तो ॥ ३३ ॥

शीतन्तुरक्तपित्तेस्याच्छ्लेष्मिप
त्तेविरूक्षणम् । परन्वतःप्रवक्या
मिधूमोयेषांविगर्हितः ॥ ३४॥

रक्तपित्तमें शीत हो जाताहै और श्लेष्म
पित्तमें विरूक्षण हो जाताहै–इससे आगे
उनका वर्णन करतेहैं जिनको धूम्रपान
निंदितहै ॥ ३४ ॥

निविरिक्तःपिवेद्धूमंनक्तेबिस्तक
मंणि । नरक्तीनिविषेणाचोनंशो
चीनचगर्भिणी ॥ ३५ ॥

कि विरेचन और बस्तिकर्म किये
पीछे धूम्रकोन पीवैं और रक्तका विकारी–
विषसे दुःखी–शोकवान् गर्भवती स्त्री–ये
धूम्रपान न करैं ॥ ३५ ॥

translation:
( 42 )
From the Charaka Samhita

[Verse 28]
After bathing, putting on clean clothes, cleaning the teeth, performing sneezing therapies, nasal application, and anointing the eyes — after attending to sleep — an intelligent person should take medicated smoke inhalation.

Commentary on verse 28: A wise person should take smoke inhalation after the acts of eating, writing, sneezing, cleaning the teeth, running, applying collyrium, and sleeping.

[Verse 29]
Thus for persons of Vata and Kapha constitution, diseases above the collarbone do not arise, and through drinking (the smoke), all three — the types suitable for drinking — become fit for basti (enema) use as well.

Commentary on verse 29: People of Vata-Kapha constitution will not suffer from diseases above the collar-bone; and through the three modes of intake, all three modes become fit for use.

[Verse 30]
A wise person should use smoke inhalation at two periods of the day. In the procedure of purgation, one should inhale three or four times.

Commentary on verse 30: A wise person should take smoke at two periods of the day. The procedure involving ghee and similar substances is among the methods. For purgative medicines, one should inhale three or four times.

[Verse 31]
Purification of the heart, throat, and sense organs; lightness of the head; and calming of the doshas previously described — these are the signs of properly administered smoke inhalation.

Commentary on verse 31: Thereby, purification of the heart, throat, and sense organs is achieved; lightness of the head occurs; and those doshas mentioned earlier are pacified. These are the characteristics of good smoke inhalation.

[Verse 32]
Deafness, blindness, muteness, hemorrhagic disorders, and vertigo in the head — these are the adverse effects produced by smoke inhalation taken at the wrong time or in excess.

Commentary on verse 32: One who takes smoke inhalation untimely or excessively will suffer these adverse effects: deafness, dullness, muteness, blood-bile disorder, and dizziness in the head.

[Verse 33]
In such cases, drinking of ghee, nasal therapy, collyrium, and soothing applications are recommended. If the dosha arising from oily smoke follows the course of Vata-Pitta, these remedies are appropriate.

Commentary on verse 33: Drinking ghee, nasal therapy, collyrium, and soothing applications are the recommended remedies. When doshas arising from oily smoke become favorable to Vata-Pitta, these are to be used.

[Verse 34]
In rakta-pitta (hemorrhagic disorder), a cooling treatment is applied; in Kapha-Pitta, a drying treatment is applied. Further on, those for whom smoke inhalation is contraindicated will be described.

Commentary on verse 34: In blood-bile disorder, cooling occurs; in Kapha-Pitta, drying occurs. Now the author will describe those for whom smoke inhalation is forbidden.

[Verse 35]
One who has undergone purgation should not inhale smoke at night, nor one with an eye disorder, nor one suffering from blood disorders, nor one afflicted by poison, nor one who is grief-stricken, nor a pregnant woman — these should not take smoke inhalation.

Commentary on verse 35: After purgation or enema therapy, one should not take smoke. Those with blood disorders, those suffering from poison, the grief-stricken, and pregnant women should not take smoke inhalation.

translation:
Verse 36: [Smoking/inhalation therapy is contraindicated] in fatigue, intoxication, indigestion due to bile disorder (āmapittа), wakefulness, fainting, thirst, and emaciation. (36)

Commentary on 36: [It should not be used in cases of] exertion, intoxication, āmаpitta, wakefulness, fainting, thirst, emaciation, and wounds.

Verse 37: [It is contraindicated] after drinking milk, after taking unctuous substances or honey, after eating with curds — and also in conditions of roughness (rūkṣatā) and anger. (37)

Commentary on 37: After drinking wine, milk, after taking unctuous and honey preparations, and after eating with curds — in conditions of dryness and anger. (37)

Verse 38: [Contraindicated] in palate disorders, wasting, timira (eye disease), head injury, śaṅkhaka (disease of the temples), rohiṇī (throat disease), prameha (urinary disorders), and madātyaya (alcoholism). (38)

Commentary on 38: In palate disorders, wasting, timira, head injury, śaṅkhaka, rohiṇī, prameha, and madātyaya. (38)

Verse 39: A person who, out of delusion, uses smoke therapy at these prohibited times — his diseases become severe and terrible due to the misuse of smoke. (39)

Commentary on 39: A person who out of confusion performs inhalation therapy at these forbidden times will suffer serious diseases worsening due to the misuse of smoke. (39)

Verse 40: One who is fit for smoke therapy should inhale through the nose and mouth for disorders of the head, nose, and eyes; for disorders of the throat, one should inhale through the nose and expel through the mouth. (40)

Commentary on 40: A person suitable for smoke therapy should inhale through nose and mouth for disorders of the head, nose, and eyes; for throat disorders, inhale through the nose and vomit out through the mouth. (20/40)

Verse 41: When one drinks mouthfuls of smoke through the mouth, one should not expel it through the nose — because smoke that travels in the reverse direction quickly destroys the eyes. (41)

Commentary on 41: When one drinks mouthfuls of smoke through the mouth, one should not expel it through the nose — because smoke going in the reverse direction quickly destroys the eyes. (41)

Verse 42: One whose limbs and eyes are tender, whose mind is well composed — such an intelligent person should, closing one nostril, inhale smoke through the nose three times. (42)

Commentary on 42: A person whose limbs and eyes are soft, whose mind is properly stable — such a wise person, blocking one opening of the nose, should inhale smoke through the nose three times. (42)

Verse 43: The tube (netra) for eye treatment measures twenty-four of one's own finger-widths; for oleation (snehana) treatment it is thirty-two finger-widths; for other uses it is considered half of that. (43)

Commentary on 43: For nasal/eye treatment the tube is twenty-four finger-widths; for oleation treatment thirty-two finger-widths; for other purposes half of that is recommended. (43)

Verse 44: [The smoke tube] measured equal to three soft knuckle-joints, the tip of a jujube stone, equal in substance to a basti-tube — such a smoke-tube (dhūmanetra) is praised and recommended. (44)

Commentary on 44: [The smoke tube should be] of the measure of three soft internodal segments (parvan), equal to the tip of a jujube stone, of the same material as the basti tube —

In the Charaka Samhita

And smoke from a substance similar to the eye is the best for the eyes. (44)

Smoke that has traveled far, that has been filtered through joints of reed, and that has been made subtle through a tube — when taken in the proper measure and at the proper time — does not harm the sense organs. (45)

When taken far out, filtered through the joints of a tube, made fine — smoke taken in proper measure and time does not harm the sense organs. (45)

When the chest, throat, and head become light, and the phlegm (kapha) also becomes reduced, then inhaling smoke at that time is considered excellent. (46)

When the chest, throat, and head become light and the phlegm decreases, inhaling smoke at that time is declared most beneficial. (46)

One whose voice is not perfectly clear, whose throat has phlegm, and whose head is heavy and congested — for such a person, smoke not yet inhaled is to be condemned (i.e., smoking is contraindicated). (47)

One whose voice is not very clear, who has phlegm in the throat, and whose head is congested — for that person, the uninhaled smoke is called condemned (inadvisable). (47)

When the palate, the crown of the head, and the throat become dry and painful, when there is thirst, fainting, and excess bleeding in a person — (48)

When the palate, crown, and throat are dry and painful, and there is thirst, confusion, and excess blood flow in a person — (48)

And when the head spins excessively and fainting occurs in that person, and the sense organs are distressed — these are the adverse effects from excessive use of medicated smoke. (49)

These disturbances — excessive dizziness in the head, fainting, and distress to the sense organs — arise from excessive use of medicated smoke. (49)

In the rainy season, and in the three seasons — Pravrit (early rains), Sharad (autumn), and Vasanta (spring) — fine medicated nasal oil should not be used; and one should not use it when clouds are present in the sky. (50)

In the rainy season, small quantities of oil and in the three seasons — Pravrit, Sharad, and Vasanta — one should not administer it; and when there are no clouds in the sky, (50)

One who performs nasal therapy (nasya karma) in the proper season, as prescribed — their eyes, nose, and ears are not damaged. (51)

One who performs nasya karma at the proper time as prescribed — their eyes, nose (olfactory faculty), and ears are not destroyed. (51)

The hairs and beard of such a person do not become white or tawny; nor do the hairs fall out — rather they grow especially well. (52)

And that person's hair and beard do not become white or yellow, nor do the hairs fall out; on the contrary, they grow especially well. (52)

Stiffness of the neck muscles, headache, facial paralysis, lock-jaw, rhinitis, splitting headache, and trembling of the head — all these are pacified. (53)

शिरा और शिरके कपालोंकी संधि
स्नायुमें खुजली ये सब नावनसे प्राप्त
हुये अधिक बलको प्राप्त होतेहैं ॥५४॥

मुखंभसन्नोपिचतंस्वरःस्निग्धःस्थि
रोमहान् । सर्वेंद्रियाणांवैमल्यं
बलंभवतिचाधिकम् ॥ ५५ ॥

मुख प्रसन्न होताहै स्वर स्निग्ध
और अधिक स्थिर होताहै सब इंद्रिय
निर्मल होतीहैं और अधिक बल होताहै॥५५

नचास्यरोगाःसहसाभभवन्त्यूर्ध्व
जत्रुजाः । जीर्य्यतश्चोत्तमाङ्गेव
जरानलभतेबलम् ॥ ५६ ॥

और उस मनुष्यके जत्रुके ऊपरके
रोग सहसा नहीं होते और जीर्ण समयमें
उत्तम अंग ( मूद्धा ) में जरा बल नहीं
करती ॥ ५६ ॥

चन्दनागुरुणीपत्रंदाव्वींत्वक्मधु
कंबलाम् । प्रपौण्डरीकंसूक्ष्मैलां
विडङ्गंबिल्वमुत्पलम् ॥ ५७॥

चंदन अगर पत्रज दारुहलदीकी

त्वचा सहत बळा कमल छोटी इलायची
वायिविडंग बेल उत्पल ॥ ५७ ॥

हीवेरमभयंवन्यंत्वड्ःमुस्तंसारि
वांस्थिराम् । सुराढ्ंपृशिपणींश्च
जीवन्तींश्शतावरीम् ॥ ५८॥

हाऊबेर वनकी हरडे मोथा सारिवा
स्थिरा ( शालपणीं ) देवदारु पृशिपणी
पिठवन जीवंती (हरडे) शतावर ॥५८॥

हरेणुंत्रुहतींन्याघींसुरभींपञ्चकेशा
रम् । विपाचयेच्छतगुणमाहेन्द्रे
विमलेऽम्भासि ॥ ५९ ॥

हरेणु मोथा कटेहली व्याधी(बडी कटे
हली ) सुरभी ( चंपा ) पञ्चकेशर इन
सबको तेलसे सौगुने वषाके निर्मल जलमें
पकावे ॥ ५९ ॥

तैलाद्दशगुणंशेषंकषायमवतारये
त् । तेनतैलंकषायेणदशकत्वोंवि
पाचयेत् ॥ ६० ॥

तेलसे दश गुणे शेषकषायको उता-
रले उस कषायमें दशवार तेलको
पकावे ॥ ६० ॥

अथास्यदशमेपाकेसमांशंछागलं
पयः । दद्यादेषोनुतैलस्यनावनी
यस्यसंविधः ॥ ६१ ॥

फिर इसके दशमें पाकमें बराबरका
बकरीका दूध डालदे यह नावन (नस्य)
कर ने योग्य तैलकी विधिहै ॥ ६१ ॥

तस्यमात्रांश्रयुञ्ञीततैलस्यार्द्धपलो
