translation:
( 66 )
From the Charaka Samhita
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

Trijah. The sage declared all of the foregoing in the chapter on non-suppression of urges. || 67 ||
As composed by Agnivesha and redacted by Charaka:
This is the chapter on non-suppression of natural urges.

And in the manner described regarding the use of digha, the son of Atri (the sage) has described all the foregoing in this chapter on the non-suppression of natural urges. || 67 ||

Here ends the seventh chapter, "On Non-Suppression of Natural Urges," composed by Agnivesha, redacted by Charaka, and rendered into commentary by Mihara Chandra.

The Eighth Chapter.
Now we shall explain the chapter called Indriyopakramaniya (concerning the approach to the sense organs).
Thus spoke the blessed Atreya.

After this, the chapter called Indriyopakramaniya is described. The blessed Atreya has stated it thus:

Here indeed there are five sense organs, five substances of the sense organs, five seats of the sense organs, five objects of the sense organs, and five cognitions of the sense organs — this has been stated in the section on the sense organs. Some further say that the mind, known as sattva, is beyond the senses, and all the endowments of the soul are dependent on it, and all activities are subject to it. || 1 ||

In this world, it is certain that there are five sense organs; there are five substances of the sense organs; there are five seats of the sense organs; there are five objects of the sense organs; and there are five cognitions of the sense organs — this has been stated in the section on the sense organs. And some say that the mind, called sattva, is supersensory; all the soul's endowments are under its control, and all activities are under its control. || 1 ||

The mind is the witness and ground of the activities of the sense organs. Because of their engagement with their own objects, and due to deviation and distraction, there is a multiplicity of sattva in one person. Because of the combination of the qualities of rajas, tamas, and sattva, there is not a singular multiplicity — since what is multiple cannot function in one person at one moment among many. || 2 ||

The activities of the sense organs serve as the evidence (witness) of their operations. Due to the divisions of self-interest, sense-object engagement, resolve, and deviation, there exist many kinds of sattva in a single person. Through the combination of the qualities of rajas, tamas, and sattva, they are not truly multiple — because multiplicity cannot operate in one person at the same moment. || 2 ||

Therefore the activity of all the sense organs takes place across multiple times. Whatever quality continuously accompanies a person, that quality of sattva, the sages call his predominant sattva, by reason of its abundance and predisposition. || 3 ||

Therefore, the activity of all the sense organs occurs at different times. Whatever quality of sattva remains constant in a person, the sages, by reason of its predominance, call that his sattva quality. || 3 ||

The sense organs, led by the mind, become capable of grasping their objects. Of these, the eye and ear [the text continues on the next page]

त्वग्घाणरसनंस्पर्शनिमितपञ्चेन्द्रियाणि ॥ ४ ॥

मनको आगे करके सब इंद्रिय विषयोंके ग्रहण करनेमें समर्थ होती हैं उसमें चक्षु श्रोत्र घ्राण रसना स्पर्शन ये पांच इंद्रियहैं ॥ ४ ॥

पञ्चेन्द्रियद्रव्याणिखंवायुज्योतिरापोभूरिति । पञ्चेन्द्रियाधिष्ठानान्यक्षिणीकर्णौनासिकेजिह्वात्वक्चेति ॥ ५ ॥

और आकाश वायु ज्योती जल भूमि ये पांच इंद्रियोंके द्रव्यहैं और नेत्र कर्ण नासिका जिह्वा त्वचा ये पांच इंद्रियोंके अधिष्ठानहैं ॥ ५ ॥

पञ्चेन्द्रियार्थाःशब्दस्पर्शरूपरसगन्धाः ॥ पञ्चेन्द्रियबुद्धयश्चक्षुबुद्धयादिकाःस्ताः ॥ ६ ॥

शब्द स्पर्श रूप रस गंध ये पांच इंद्रियोंके विषयहैं पांच इंद्रियोंकी बुद्धि चक्षु बुद्धि आदिहैं ॥ ६ ॥

पुनरिन्द्रियेन्द्रियार्थस्वतवात्मसञ्चकर्षजाः ॥ ७ ॥

फिर इंद्रिय इंद्रियार्थ स्वतः आत्मा इनके संबंधसे उत्पन्नहैं ॥ ७ ॥

क्षणिकानिश्चयात्मकाश्चेत्येतत्पञ्चपञ्चकम् । मनोमनोर्थोबुद्धिरात्माचेत्यध्यात्मद्रव्यगुणसग्रहः

शुभाशुभप्रवृतिनिवृत्तिहेतुश्चद्रव्याश्रितंकर्मयदुच्यते किंयेति ॥ ८ ॥

क्षणिक और निश्चयात्मक ये पांच २ होतेहैं मन, मनका विषय, बुद्धि, आत्मा यह अध्यात्म द्रव्य गुणोंका संग्रह है और यही शुभ अशुभकी प्रवृति और निवृतिका हेतु द्रव्याश्रित कर्म जो कहाता है वह क्रियाहै ॥ ८ ॥

तत्रानुमानगन्धानांपञ्चमहाभूतविकारसमुदायात्मकानामिषतामिन्द्रियाणांतेजश्चक्षुषोश्रोत्रेनभःघ्राणेक्षितिरापोरसनेस्पर्शनेऽनिलोविशेषेणोपदिश्यते ॥ ९ ॥

उसमें अनुमानसे जाननें योग्य जो पांच महाभूतोंके विकार समुदायरूप इंद्रियहैं उनमें तेज चक्षुमें श्रोत्रमें आकाश घ्राणमें भूमि जल रसनामें और स्पर्शनमें पवन इनका विशेषकर उपदेश करतेहैं ॥ ९ ॥

तत्रयदात्मकिमिन्द्रियंविशेषाच्चदात्मकमेवार्थमनुधावति । तत्स्वभावाद्विभुत्वाच्च ॥ १० ॥

translation:
Mantra-Sthana (Chapter on Fundamentals), Page 67

Verse 4: The five sense organs are those pertaining to skin (touch), nose (smell), tongue (taste), eye (sight), and ear (hearing).

Commentary 4: With the mind leading, the senses become capable of grasping all their respective objects. Those five senses are: eye, ear, nose, tongue, and skin.

Verse 5: The five elemental substances of the sense organs are space, air, fire, water, and earth. The five seats of the sense organs are the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin.

Commentary 5: Space, air, fire, water, and earth are the elemental substances of the five sense organs, and the eye, ear, nose, tongue, and skin are their respective seats.

Verse 6: The five objects of the senses are sound, touch, form, taste, and smell. The five sense-cognitions are visual cognition and so forth.

Commentary 6: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell are the objects of the five senses, and the five sense-cognitions begin with visual cognition.

Verse 7: Again, the senses, their objects, the self — all arise from the conjunction of these with one another.

Commentary 7: The senses arise from the mutual connection of the senses, their objects, and the self.

Verse 8: These groups of five are of two kinds: momentary and determinative. Mind, the object of mind, intellect, and soul — this is the aggregate of the qualities of spiritual substance. That which is called action grounded in substance, which is the cause of the arising and cessation of auspicious and inauspicious activity, is what is meant by action.

Commentary 8: These exist in two sets of five: momentary and determinative. Mind, the object of mind, intellect, and soul constitute the collection of qualities of spiritual substance. This very collection is the cause of the inclination toward and withdrawal from good and bad, and the action grounded in substance that is spoken of — that is what action means.

Verse 9: Among these, the five sense organs — knowable by inference, constituted by the aggregate of modifications of the five great elements — are specially taught thus: fire is predominant in the eye, space in the ear, earth in the nose, water in the tongue, and wind in the skin.

Commentary 9: Among those, the five sense organs, which are knowable by inference and are constituted by the aggregate of modifications of the five great elements — in these, fire is specially present in the eye, space in the ear, earth in the nose, water in the tongue, and wind in the skin.

Verse 10: Among these, whatever element a sense organ is constituted of, it pursues only the corresponding object of that element — this follows from the nature and pervasiveness of that element.

Commentary 10: Whichever element constitutes a given sense organ, that sense organ pursues the corresponding object of that element, due to its inherent nature and by virtue of being all-pervading.

[The page ends mid-verse]: From wrong use, disuse, and excessive use of those objects, the mind-accompanied sense organ undergoes disorder...

translation:
( 68 )
Charaka Samhita

[Verse 11]
All the sense organs, having fallen into disorder through excessive use, disuse, or wrong use of their objects — in a manner contrary to one's own intellect — become instruments for the destruction of that intellect. (11)

[Verse 12]
Upon proper use (samyoga), the senses, having returned to their natural state, nourish the intellect accordingly. (12)

[Verse 13]
The function of the mind is to contemplate objects. In that process, equal, excessive, or deficient wrong use of both the mind and the intellect becomes the cause of natural constitution (prakriti) and its disorders (vikriti). (13)

[Verse 14]
When there is suffering (annutapa) in the senses and the mind, one should make effort through these very causes — with a view to removing that suffering and restoring the natural state. (14)

[Verse 15]
This is how it is: by the proper conjunction of the senses with their objects, by examining actions correctly through the intellect, by proper guidance regarding place, time, and qualities of the self, and by avoiding what is contrary to these — the person who desires his own welfare should, in all ways and at all times, remain grounded in memory (of right conduct) and always practice right conduct. For that practice at once accomplishes two aims: health and mastery of the senses. (15)

[Verse 16]
That right conduct (sadvritta) will now be described in full:
One should honor the gods, cattle, Brahmins, teachers, elders, accomplished masters, and preceptors. One should tend the sacred fire. One should keep prescribed medicines. One should touch water at the two daily junctures (dawn and dusk). In places of bodily impurity, one should wash the feet regularly and maintain cleanliness. Three times a fortnight one should trim hair, beard, and nails. One should always wear clean garments, be cheerful, and be fragrant. (16)

He gives instruction in complete right conduct — it is as follows: One should worship the gods, cows, Brahmins, teachers, elders, accomplished ones, and preceptors. One should perform the Agnihotra fire ritual. One should wear prescribed medicines. One should bathe at both prescribed times of day. One should repeatedly keep clean the places of bodily impurity and the feet. Three times in a fortnight one should remove facial hair, head hair, beard, and nails. One should always wear fresh garments and remain fragrant with flowers. (16)

One of virtuous appearance, with well-groomed hair, who applies oil regularly to the head, ears, and feet; who uses medicated smoke; who speaks first with a pleasant countenance; who hastens to assist in difficult situations; who performs sacrifices, gives gifts, offers salutations at crossroads, presents offerings, honors guests, offers funeral oblations to the ancestors, and speaks beneficial, measured, and sweet words at the right time; who keeps his own soul and spiritual duty under control; who is firm in principle, not envious of results; who is free from anxiety and fear; who is intelligent, modest, highly enthusiastic, skillful, patient, of good character, devout, humble, and wise; who serves those senior in learning, lineage, age, accomplished masters, and preceptors; who carries an umbrella, a staff, maintains silence, wears sandals, and walks with eyes cast only a yoke's length ahead. (17)

One who maintains auspicious conduct, avoids dirty garments, bones, thorns, impure hair, heaps of husks, ashes, skulls, bathing grounds, and places of offerings; who avoids excessive exertion and exercises with moderation; who is a friend to all living beings; who pacifies the angry, reassures the frightened, and protects the destitute; who is truthful and devoted to conciliation; who bears harsh words from others without retaliation; and who perceives the virtue of peace. (18)

One should maintain auspicious behavior — abandon places of condemned garments, bones, thorns, impure hair, heaps of husks, ashes, skulls, bathing spots, and offering grounds; give up exercise that causes excessive fatigue; remain a friend to all living beings; pray for the angry; give confidence to the frightened; nurture the destitute —

translation:
(Page 70 — Charaka Samhita)

Verse 18:
Speak truth. Consider peace to be paramount. Bear harsh words from others with patience. Destroy anger. Perceive the virtues of tranquility.

Verse 19 (Sanskrit):
One should be the destroyer of the causes of passion and hatred. One should not speak falsehood. One should not take another's wealth. One should not covet another's wife. One should not delight in enmity with others. One should not commit sin, nor become sinful even among sinners. One should not speak of others' faults. One should not reveal others' secrets.

Verse 19 (Hindi commentary):
Destroy the causes of passion and hatred. Do not speak lies. Do not take another's wealth. Do not desire another's wife. Do not take pleasure in another's prosperity or in enmity. Do not commit sin, do not become sinful among sinners, do not speak of others' faults, and do not make public the secrets of others.

Verse 20 (Sanskrit):
One should not sit in the company of the irreligious, of enemies of kings, of the insane, the fallen, the cruel, the killers, the petty, or the wicked. One should not ride a wicked vehicle. One should not sit on a seat as high and hard as one's knees.

Verse 20 (Hindi commentary):
Do not sit in the company of the irreligious or the enemies of kings, and do not sit with the insane, the fallen, murderers, the petty, and the wicked. Do not ride wicked vehicles. Do not sit on a seat that is as high and hard as the knees.

Verse 21 (Sanskrit):
One should not lie on a bed that is without proper covering, is ruined, ugly, or uneven. One should not wander on uneven mountain peaks. One should not climb trees. One should not plunge into fierce rushing water. One should not resort to the shade of a solitary tree. One should not move about near fire hazards. One should not laugh loudly. One should not release flatulence with sound. One should not yawn, sneeze, or laugh with uncovered mouth. One should not pick the nose. One should not grind the teeth against each other. One should not bite the nails. One should not strike bones together. One should not scratch lines in the earth. One should not cut grass. One should not crush clods of earth.

Verse 21 (Hindi commentary):
Do not sleep on a bed that is without covering, ruined, ugly, or uneven. Do not wander on uneven mountain peaks. Do not climb trees. Do not plunge into fiercely flowing water. Do not resort to the shade of a solitary tree. Do not move about near fire hazards. Do not laugh loudly. Do not release wind audibly. Do not yawn, sneeze, or laugh with an open mouth. Do not pick the nose. Do not grind the teeth against each other. Do not bite the nails. Do not strike bones. Do not scratch on the ground. Do not cut grass. Do not crush clods of earth.

सूत्रस्थानम् (७१)

मिथ्यामेध्यमशस्तऋनाभिविक्षेत् नहुंकुर्य्याच्छवम् । नचैत्यध्वज गुरुपूज्याशस्तच्छायामाकामेत् नक्षपास्वमरसदनचैत्यचत्वरचतुष्पथोपवनश्मशानायतनान्यासेवेत् । नैकःशून्यगृहंनाटवीमनुप्रविशेत् । नपापवृत्तान्स्वीयमित्र भृत्यान्भजेत् । नोत्तमैर्विरुध्येत् नावरानुपासीतनिजझ्ंरोचयेत् । नाऽनार्य्यमाश्रयेत् । नभयमुत्पादयेत् । नसाहसितिस्वमप्रजागर ह्नानपानाशनान्यासेवेत् । नोच्चैर्जानुस्थिरतिष्ठेत् । नव्यालानुपसपेन्दंष्ट्रूणःनिविषाणिनः । पुरो वातातपावश्यायितप्रवातान्ज झ्यात्किलिनारभेत् । नानिभृतोऽभिषुपासीत । नोच्छिष्टोनाधःकृत्वाऽप्तापयेत् । नाविगतक्लमोनानाघुतवदनोननघ्रउपस्पृशेत् । न ह्नानशाटच्यास्पृशेदुत्तमाङ्गम् । नकेशाघ्राण्यभिहन्यात् । नोपस्पृशेतएवावाससीविधृयात् । नास्पृष्ठारत्नाज्यपूज्यमङ्गलसुमनसोऽभिनिष्कामेत् । नपूज्यमङ्गलान्यपसव्यंगच्छेत् । नेतराण्यनुदक्षिणम् ॥ २२ ॥

निगुणोंके संगोंमें चेष्ठा न करै–तारागण अग्नि अपवित्र प्रशस्तसे भिन्न इनके संमुख न देखै–शवको हुंकार शब्द न कहै–चैत्य ध्वजा गुरु पूज्य अश्रेष्ठ इनकी छायामें न जाय–रात्रिके समयमें देव मंदिर चैत्य चत्वर–चतुष्पथ पवन श्मशान इतने स्थानोंमें न वसे–एकाकी शून्य घर और वनमें प्रवेश न करे और पापी स्त्री मित्र भृत्योंका सेवन न करै–उत्तमोंके संग विरोध न करै–छोटोंकी सेवा न करै कपटमें रुचि न रक्खै–अनार्यका आशरय न ले–किसीके लिये भयको पैदा न करै–और साहस अत्यंत स्वप्न जागरण ह्नान पान भोजन इनको अधिक न करै–ऊपरकी जानु किये चिरकालतक न बैठे–सर्प–दंष्ट्री सींगवाले इनके पीछे न भागै–पूर्वकी पवन धूप अवश्यय (शीत) अति प्रवाह (पवन) इनको त्याग दे–कलहको न करै–अग्निहोत्र धारण किये बिना अग्निकी उपासना न करै–न उच्छिष्ठ होकर नीचे रखकर अग्निसे न तापे ग्लानिको त्यागे बिना मुखको धोये बिना और नमहुआ अग्निका स्पर्श न करै ह्नानकी धोतिसे उत्तम अंगका स्पर्श न करै केशोंके अग्रभागोंको न काटै न स्पर्शकरै देवखोंको धारणकरै रत्न घी पूज्य मंगलपुष्प इनका स्पर्श कियेबिना घरसे बाहिर न निकसै पूज्य और मंगलकी वस्तुओंके वामभागसे गमन न करै और अन्योंके दक्षिण भागको न जाय ॥ २२ ॥

नारत्नपाणिर्नाह्नातोनोपहतवासा
translation:
Sutrasthana (Chapter 71)

One should not look at inauspicious, impure, or blameworthy persons or things. One should not make a threatening sound ("hum") at a corpse. One should not seek the shadow of a flagpost, idol-shrine, teacher, or venerable person who is inauspicious. At night one should not dwell in temples, crossroads, cremation grounds, gardens, or sacred sites. One should not enter an empty house or forest alone. One should not associate with sinful friends or servants. One should not quarrel with superiors, nor serve inferiors, nor take delight in deception. One should not seek refuge with ignoble persons. One should not cause fear in anyone. One should not indulge excessively in boldness, sleep, wakefulness, bathing, drinking, or eating. One should not sit for long periods with knees raised. One should not run after snakes, fanged or horned animals. One should avoid easterly wind, heat, dew, and excessive drafts. One should not quarrel. One should not worship fire without maintaining the sacred fire-rite. One should not expose fire to being polluted by leaning over it in an impure state. Without removing fatigue, washing the face, and with unwashed hands, one should not touch fire. One should not touch the upper body with the bathing cloth. One should not strike or smell the ends of hair. One should not go outside without first touching gems, ghee, venerable items, and auspicious flowers. One should not pass to the left side of venerable and auspicious objects, nor go to the south side of others. ॥ 22 ॥

One who has not adorned himself with gems, has not bathed, and is wearing soiled clothes —

translation:
(Page 72 — Charaka Samhita, dietary and conduct rules, chapters 23–25)

One should not eat without having first made oblations and offered to the gods, without having offered to the ancestors, without having given to one's teachers, guests, and dependants; without wearing garlands and fragrant substances; without having washed hands, feet, and face; with an impure mouth; facing the wrong direction; in a distracted state; in an unclean place or at an improper time; in a crowded assembly; without having first offered to the fire; without having sprinkled the food with water accompanied by sacred mantras; while criticizing the food; or food that has been offered with contempt or disrespect. Nor should one eat leftover or stale food — except for meat, green vegetables, dried vegetables, and other such permitted items. (23)

One should not eat everything indiscriminately — except for ghee (clarified butter), honey, salt, and similar items — one should not consume them all together. One should not eat a single grain or morsel alone. (24)

At night one should not eat curd, and one should not eat sattu (roasted flour) alone; nor after a meal, nor excessively, nor twice in succession, nor with water in between — one should not consume sattu under such circumstances. (25)

One should not eat food that has been spoiled or corrupted by insects and the like. One should not go to sleep with tears in one's eyes or with unsatisfied natural urges. One should not be engaged in other activities when bodily urges arise. One should not pass wind, spit, or urinate facing the wind, water, fire, a Brahmin, a teacher, or an idol. One should not urinate on a public road, nor in the presence of people, nor at mealtime. One should not spit or discharge phlegm during recitation of prayers, during homa (fire offerings), during study, during bali (ritual offerings), during auspicious ceremonies, or while holding something. One should not disrespect one's prosperity. One should not be overly trusting. One should not reveal secrets to those who are unworthy. One should not approach or associate improperly with women during their menses, with the sick, or with those of inauspicious appearance or conduct...

translation:

Sutrasthana (Chapter on Fundamental Principles) (73)

[Sanskrit verse 26:]
One who is emaciated, one whose desires are unfulfilled, one who belongs to a different lineage, one who is at a sacred tree, crossroads, in the wind, at a cremation ground, near water, medicine, a brahmin, a teacher, a divine temple — in these places at the time of twilight, exceedingly prohibited; on impure lunar days, having taken medicine without resolve, without joy, without having eaten, having eaten excessively, being in a disordered state, afflicted by the urge to urinate, fatigued by exertion, exercise, fasting, or lassitude — one should not engage in sexual intercourse in front of all. ॥ 26 ॥

[Hindi commentary on verse 26:]
One should not snatch away and eat in the company of brahmins, and having become harsh, one should not drink water, eat food, or sleep. One should not become attached to other activities hastily. One should not spit, pass wind, excrete feces or urine in front of wind, fire, water, the moon, the sun, brahmins, or one's teacher. One should not urinate on the road. In human settlements, at various times during japa (recitation), homa (fire ritual), study, or auspicious rites, one should not discharge phlegm or mucus. One should not show disrespect, and one should not place excessive trust; one should not reveal secret matters to others. One should not indulge in mental anguish. And with a menstruating woman, a sick woman, an impure woman, one of inferior conduct, a foolish woman, one without desire, one who desires another man, another man's wife, or one of a different kind — with all such women, and from a place other than the natural passage, at sacred trees, crossroads, in the wind, at cremation grounds, near water, medicine, brahmins, teachers, or temples — at the time of twilight, during highly prohibited lunar days, having consumed medicine without resolve, without joy, without food, or after overeating, being in a disordered state, afflicted by the urge to urinate, fatigued by exertion, exercise, fasting, or lassitude — before all others — one should not engage in sexual intercourse. ॥ 26 ॥

[Sanskrit verse 27:]
One should not slander the good and one's teachers. One who is impure should not perform sorcery rites, worship of sacred trees and revered objects, or engage in study. One should refrain when there is a windstorm, when the directions are ablaze, when there is thunder, an earthquake, a great festival, a falling meteor, the approach of a great planet, on the eighth lunar day, at twilight, or when one's voice is mute. One's recitation should not be done with a voice that is newly broken, excessively slow, excessively fast, dragging, overly timid, too loud, or too low. One should recite with a moderate, steady voice. One should not milk beyond the proper time. One should not break one's daily observances. ॥ 27 ॥

[Hindi commentary on verse 27:]
One should not slander good people and one's teachers. When impure, one should not perform sorcery (such as death rites), worship of sacred trees and revered objects, or engage in study. When distressed by the sound of lightning and when the directions appear ablaze, during the destruction of fire at twilight, during an earthquake — [continues on next page]

( ७२ )
चरकसंहिताभाषा १

केकंपमे महान् उत्सवमें उल्काके पड़नेपर | रुचि न करै गुह्य वस्तुको छिपावै–किसीका
महान् ग्रहोंके उपगमनमें नष्टचंद्र तिथिमें | तिरस्कार न करै अहंकारी नहो–चतुर
संध्याओंके समयमें गुरुके मुखसे श्रवण | अचतुर न हो किसीकी असूया (निंदा)
किये बिना–और अत्यंत अधिकता जिसके | न करै चतुरोंके संग विवादको न करै
अंतमें हो जो स्वरसेहीन हो जिसके पद | गौओंपर दंडको न उठावै–और वृद्ध
पृथक् २ न हो अत्यंत शीघ्र और विलंबसे और क्रीबरूपसे अत्यंत ऊंचे अत्यंत | गुरु–गण ( पिता आदि ) राजा इनकी
नीचे स्वरसे इतने प्रकारसे अध्ययनको न | निंदा न करै न इनके संग अत्यंत बोले–
करे–समयका अत्यंत द्रोह न करै (वृथा न | बांधवोंमें अनुरक्तके कष्टके अद्वितीय
खोवै ) नियमको न छोड़ै ॥ २७ ॥ | गुह्यके जो ज्ञाताहैं उनको वाहिर न करै२८

न नक्तंनादेशेचरेत् ॥ नसन्ध्या | नाधीरोनात्युच्छ्रितसत्वःस्यात् ।
स्वंन्यवहाराध्ययनस्त्रीस्वमसेवी | नाभृतभृत्योनविश्वब्धास्वजनोनैकःसुखी ॥ नदुःखशीलाचारो
स्यात् । नबालवृद्धलुब्धमूर्खशिष्टक्लीवैःसहसर्यंकुर्यात् ॥ न | पचारोनसर्वैविश्वम्भी । नसर्वांभिशड्की ॥ नसर्वकालिविचारी ॥
मयवूतवेश्यामसङ्गरुचिःस्यात्। | नकार्य्यकालमतिपातयेत् ॥ ना
नगुहंविवृणुयात् ॥ नकञ्चिदव | परीक्षितमाभिनिवेशेत् । नेन्द्रि
जानीयात् । नाहंमानिस्यात् । | यवशगःस्यात् ॥ २९ ॥
नदक्षोनादक्षिणोनासूयकोनदक्षिणान्परिवदेत् ॥ नगवांदण्डमु | अधीर अत्यंत ऊंचे सत्व गुणवान्
यच्छेत् ॥ नवृद्धान्नगुरून्नग | नहो भृत्योंके पालनको न त्यागै जिसका
णान्नरृपान्वाधिक्षेपवनचा | अपने जनोंको विश्वास न हो ऐसा और
तिब्रूयात्॥नबान्धवानुरक्तकछ्ञा | एक सुखी न रहै और दुःख शील आच-
द्वितीयगुह्यज्ञान्बहिःकुर्यात्२८ | रण उपचार न रहै सबको विश्वास न दे
| ऐसा न रहे जिससे सब शंका मानें सर्व
रात्रिमें और कुदेशमें न विचरै–संध्या | काल में विचारवान् न रहे कार्यके समयका
ओंमें भोजन अध्ययन स्त्री शयन इनका | अवलंघन न करै बिना परीक्षा किये
सेवन न करै–बालक वृद्ध लोभी मूर्ख | आग्रहको न करै इंद्रियोंके वशमें नरहै२९
क्लेशित नपुंसक इनके संग मित्रता न |
करै, मदिरा जूआ वेश्या इनके प्रसंगमें | नचञ्चलमनोभामयेत्।नंबुद्धीन्द्रि
| याणामतिभारमादध्यात् ॥ न
| चातिदीर्घसूत्रिस्यात् । नकोध
translation:
(72)
Charaka Samhita, Commentary, Part 1

One should not study in the following circumstances: during great festivals; when meteors fall; at the arrival of great planets; on the day of the lost moon; at twilight hours without having heard from one's teacher; when the text is extremely excessive; when it is without melody; when the syllables are not distinct; when it is recited extremely rapidly or with extreme delay; when it is recited in an unnaturally high or unnaturally low pitch — in all these conditions one should not study. One must not waste time needlessly and must not abandon discipline. (27)

One should not wander in the night or in forbidden places. At twilight one should not eat, study, attend to women, or sleep. One should not befriend children, the aged, the greedy, the foolish, the distressed, or eunuchs. One should not associate with gamblers, drunkards, or prostitutes.

One should not reveal secrets. One should not disrespect anyone. One should not be arrogant. One should not be incompetent, nor ungrateful, nor given to finding fault with the competent. One should not strike cattle with a stick. One should not insult or verbally abuse the elderly, teachers, learned men, or kings. One should not quarrel with the clever. One should not raise a stick against cows. One should not speak ill of elders, teachers, nobles, or kings. One should not reveal the private secrets of those dear companions who are uniquely trusted with one's innermost matters. (28)

One should not be impatient, nor excessively haughty in spirit. One should not neglect the maintenance of servants. One should not be such that one's own people have no trust in one. One should not be content in solitary happiness alone. One should not be habitually sorrowful in conduct. One should not pretend to trust everyone. One should not be suspicious of all. One should not deliberate at all times indiscriminately. One should not let the proper time for action pass by. One should not persist in a course of action without examination. One should not be a slave to the senses. (29)

One should not allow the mind to become restless. One should not overburden the intellect and the senses. One should not be one who endlessly procrastinates. One should not be given to anger...

( ७५ )

हर्षावनुविदध्यात् । नशोकमनु

पञ्चपञ्चकमुदिष्टंमनोहेतुचतुष्टय
म्।इन्द्रियोपक्रमेऽध्यायेसद्वृत्त

translation:
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha
Sutrasthana 1
(75)

One should not give way to excessive joy; one should not come under the sway of grief; one should not feel elation when something is accomplished, nor feel despondency when it is not. One should constantly remember one's own natural constitution. One should be resolute in understanding the causes of things. One should steadily begin from the root cause. One should not place excessive reliance on what has already been done. One should not abandon one's vitality. One should not dwell on criticism. ॥30॥

(Hindi commentary on verse 30:) The mind should not be confused by restlessness; one should not burden the senses excessively; one should not be a chronic procrastinator; one should not be overcome by anger or exhilaration; one should not fall under the sway of grief. When a task succeeds, one should not become overjoyed, and when it fails, one should not sink into despondency. One should repeatedly remember one's own natural constitution. One should maintain firm conviction in the power of causes, and steadily undertake those causes. One should not have the conceit that "I have accomplished this." One should not abandon one's vitality, and should not dwell on criticism. ॥30॥

One should not perform the fire-oblation with clarified butter, whole grains, sesame, kusha grass, or mustard seeds while in a state of impurity. While seeking blessings for oneself, one recites: "O Fire, do not depart from my body; O Wind, nourish my vital breaths; O Vishnu, give me strength; O Indra, give me vigor; O auspicious Waters, enter into me." Touching water with the mantra beginning "Apo hishtha..." one should wipe the lips twice, sprinkle water on the feet, touch the head and the openings of the body, and touch with water the heart and the head. One should be devoted to brahmacharya, knowledge, charity, friendliness, compassion, joy, and peace. ॥31॥

Here are the summarizing verses:

The five groups of five have been taught — the mind, the four causes, and the complete code of conduct for the senses — all of this is set forth in this chapter on conduct. ॥32॥

(Hindi commentary:) In this chapter the five-times-five topics are described: the mind, the four causes, and the complete teaching of right conduct for the senses. ॥32॥

One who properly and fully follows the code of healthy living as described here remains free from disease for a full hundred years and is not deprived of longevity. ॥33॥

(Hindi commentary:) One who properly practices the code of healthy living as truly described here remains free from disease for a hundred years...

रहित होकर अवस्थासे हीन नहीं

इति स्वस्थवृत्तचतुष्कः अग्निवेशकृते तंत्रे
चरकमति संस्कृते पं॰मिहिरचन्द्रकृत माषा
विवृतौ इंद्रियोपक्रमणीयो नामाष्टमोऽ
ध्यायः ॥ ८ ॥

अथनवमोऽध्यायः ।

अथातःखुड्डाकचतुष्पादमध्या
यंव्याख्यास्यामः ॥

इतिह्स्माहभगवानात्रेयः ॥

अब खुड्डाक चतुष्पाद अध्यायकावर्णन
करतेहैं–यह भगवान् अत्रेयजिने कहाहै

भिषग्द्रव्याण्युपस्थातारोगिपाद
चतुष्टयम् । गुणवत्कारणंज्ञेयंवि
कारव्युपशान्तये ॥ १ ॥

कि, वैद्य द्रव्य उपस्थाता रोगी
ये चारों पाद गुणवान् होंयतो विकारकी
शांतिके लिये कारण समझना ॥ १ ॥

विकारोधातुवैषम्यंसाम्यंप्रकृति
रुच्यते । सुखसंज्ञकमारोग्यंवि
कारोदुःखमेवच ॥ २ ॥

धातुओंकी विषमताको विकार और
समताको प्रकृति कहतेहैं सुखको आरोग्य
और दुःखको विकार कहतेहैं ॥ २ ॥

चतुर्णांभिषगादीनांशस्तानांधातु
वैकृते । प्रवृत्तिर्धातुसाम्याथाँचि
कित्सेत्यभिधीयते ॥ ३ ॥

उत्तम जो चारों वैद्य आदिहैं उनकी
जो धातुओंके विकारमें धातुओंकी समता
के लिये प्रवृत्तिहै उसको चिकित्सा कहतेहैं

श्रुतेपर्य्यवदातृत्वंबहुशोदष्टकर्मि
translation:
( 76 )
In the Charaka Samhita.

[Left column:]

Not deprived of any state, one does not become diminished. || 33 ||

He who is regarded as good by the virtuous fills the world of men with his fame; thus dharma and artha — these lead to the liberation of beings. || 34 ||

The one of meritorious deeds attains the worlds of the virtuous through pious actions. Therefore all persons should practice this code of conduct at all times. || 35 ||

Whatever else has not been mentioned here but is worthy of highest respect — that too Atreya always approves. || 36 ||

Thus ends the Section on Healthy Conduct. This is the Eighth Chapter called Indriyopakramaniya in the treatise composed by Agnivesha, revised by Charaka, and rendered into the vernacular by Pandit Mihirachandra. || 8 ||

[Right column:]

Now Begins the Ninth Chapter.

Now we shall explain the Chapter on the Four Pillars (Khuddaka-chatushpada).

Thus spoke the Blessed Atreya:

The physician, the medicine, the attendant, and the patient — these four constitute the four pillars. They should be understood as possessing good qualities, for they are the means to the alleviation of disease. || 1 ||

The imbalance of the bodily constituents (dhatus) is called disease; their balance is called natural health. The state of happiness is called freedom from disease; and disease itself is misery. || 2 ||

The activity of these four — the physician and the rest — directed at restoring balance to the bodily constituents when they have become disordered, is called treatment (chikitsa). || 3 ||

The physician should be thoroughly learned, possessing comprehensive knowledge — having heard extensively, being highly accomplished in the eight branches of medicine...

text:
Digitized By Shree Ananda Pongditri Gyaan Kosha ( ७७ )

ता । दाक्ष्यंशौचमितिज्ञेयंवैद्येगुणचतुष्टयम् ॥ ४ ॥
श्रुतकापर्यवदाता ( निश्चयवान् ) हो बहुतसे कर्म जिसने देखेहों चतुरता औरशौचहोये चारगुण वैद्यमें होतेहैं ॥ ४ ॥
बहुतातत्रयोग्यत्वमनेकविधकल्पना । सम्पचेतिचतुष्कोऽयंद्रव्याणांगुणउच्यते ॥ ५ ॥
अधिकता और उनमें योग्यता और अनेक प्रकारकी कल्पना और संपदा ये चार द्रव्यों ( औषधिके ) गुण कहेहैं ५
उपचारज्ञतादाक्ष्यमनुरागश्भर्तरि । शौचञेतिचतुष्कोऽयंगुणः परिचरेर्जने ॥ ६ ॥
उपचार (सेवा)काज्ञान चतुराई स्वामीमें प्रीति और शौच ये चार गुण सेवक मनुष्यमें कहेहैं ॥ ६ ॥
स्मृतिर्निर्देशकारित्वमभीरुत्वमथापिच । ज्ञापकत्वञ्चरोगाणामातुरस्यगुणाःस्मृताः ॥ ७ ॥
स्मरण–आज्ञाको करना और अभीरता और रोगोंका बोधक ये चार गुण आतुरमें कहे हैं ॥ ७ ॥
कारणषोडशगुणंसिद्धोपादचतुष्टयम् । विज्ञाताशासितायोकाष्ठानंभिषगत्रतु ॥ ८ ॥
ये सोलह गुण चारों पाद सिद्धिमें कारण होते हैं और इनमें विशेष कर ज्ञाता शिक्षक योजनकर्ता जो भिषक्है वह प्रधान है ॥ ८ ॥

पक्तौहिकारणंपक्तुर्यथापात्रेन्धनानलाः । विजेतुर्विजयेभूमिश्वमुःअहरणानिच ॥ ९ ॥
जैसे पाचकके पकानेमें पात्र इंधन अग्नि कारण हैं और विजयकर्ता के विजयमें भूमि सेना और शस्त्र कारण है ॥ ९ ॥
आतुराभास्तथासिद्धोपादाःकारणसंज्ञिताः । वैद्यस्यातिथिकित्सायांप्रधानकारणंभिषक् ॥ १० ॥
तिसी प्रकार आतुरआदि चारों पाद सिद्धिमें कारण कहे हैं–इससे वैद्यक को चिकित्सामें प्रधान कारण भिषक् होताहै ॥ १० ॥
मृद्दण्डचक्रसूत्राधाःकुम्भकाराहतेयथा । नावहन्तिगुणवैद्याहतेपादत्रयंतथा ॥ ११ ॥
मिट्टी दंड चक्र सूत्र आादि जैसे कुंभ कारके विना गुणको नहीं देते अर्थात् घटको नहीं बनासकते तिसी प्रकार वैद्यके विना तीनों पाद गुणदायक नहीं होते ॥ ११ ॥
गन्धर्वपुरवन्नाशंयद्विकाराःसुदारुणाः । यान्तिचेतरेवृद्धिमाशुपायप्रतीक्षणः ॥ १२ ॥
जिससे महान् दारुणभी विकार गंधर्वपुरके समान नाशको और इतर (आरोग्य) जोहैं वे वृद्धिको उसके प्राप्त होतेहैं जो शीघ्र उपायको करताहै ॥ १२ ॥

translation:
Page 77

[Verse 4]
Dexterity and cleanliness — these are known as the four qualities of the physician.
One who is learned, has witnessed many procedures, possesses cleverness, and has cleanliness — these four qualities belong to the physician. (4)

[Verse 5]
Abundance, suitability among them, preparation in many forms, and excellence — these four are said to be the qualities of medicinal substances (drugs). (5)

[Verse 6]
Knowledge of service, dexterity, affection toward the master, and cleanliness — these four are said to be the qualities of the attendant. (6)

[Verse 7]
Memory, following instructions, fearlessness, and the ability to communicate about diseases — these four are said to be the qualities of the patient. (7)

[Verse 8]
These sixteen qualities of the four factors are the cause of success in treatment. Among these, especially the physician who is learned, instructing, and coordinating is paramount. (8)

[Verse 9]
Just as in cooking, the vessel, fuel, and fire are the causes for the cook; and for the conqueror, the land, army, and weapons are the causes for victory — (9)

[Verse 10]
Similarly, the patient and the other three factors are designated as causes; but in the physician's treatment, the physician himself is the primary cause. (10)

[Verse 11]
Just as clay, the stick, the wheel, and the thread cannot yield their qualities without the potter — that is, they cannot make a pot — similarly, without the physician, the other three factors do not become beneficial. (11)

[Verse 12]
Therefore, even the most dreadful disorders vanish like a phantom city, and other conditions (that are curable) advance toward recovery, for one who promptly resorts to the proper remedy. (12)

text:
( ७८ )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

सतिपादत्रयेज्ञाज्ञौभिषजावत्रका
रणम् । वर्मात्माहुतोज्ञेननिच
कित्साप्रवर्तिता ॥ १३ ॥
तीन पादोंके होनेपर पंडित और मूर्ख
वैद्य चिकित्सामें कारणहै–उनमें पंडित
अपने आत्माकी होमको वर मानताहै
परंतु चिकित्सामें प्रवृत्त नहीं होता॥ १३॥
पाणिचाराथचाक्षुर्ज्ञानाम्रीत
भीतवत् । नौमांरितवशेवाज्ञोभि
षक्चरितकर्मसु ॥ १४ ॥
जलके प्रचारसे जैसे चक्षु तैसे अज्ञा-
नसे भीतसेभी भीतके समान होताहै और
पवनके वेगसे जैसे नौका डगमग होतीहै
इसीप्रकार मूर्ख वैद्य कर्मोंको करताहै १४

यहच्छयासमापन्नमुत्ताभ्योनिय
तायुषम् । भिषग्मानौनिहन्त्या
शुशतान्यनियतायुषाम्॥ १५॥
जिसकी अवस्था नियत है अकस्मात
प्राप्तहुये उसको नीरोग करकेभी अभि-
मानी वैद्य उन सैकड़ोंको शीघ्र मॉर
देताहै जिनकी अवस्थाका निश्चय नहीं
है ॥ १५ ॥
तस्माच्छास्त्रेऽर्थविज्ञानेभवृतौक
र्मदर्शने । भिषक्चतुष्टयेयुक्तःप्रा
णाभिसरउच्यते ॥ १६ ॥
तिससे शास्त्र अर्थकाविज्ञान प्रवृति
कर्मदर्शन इन चारोंमें जो युक्त वैद्यहै
उसको प्राणाभिसर कहतेहैं ॥ १६ ॥

हेतौलिङ्गेप्रशमनेरोगाणामपुनर्भ
वे । ज्ञानंचतुर्विधंयस्यसराजाहु
भिषक्तमः ॥ १७ ॥
हेतु लिंग शांति रोगोंका फिर न
होना इनचारों प्रकारोंका जिसको ज्ञानहै
उस उत्तम भिषक्को राजा कहतेहैं १७।
शस्त्रशास्त्राणिसिलंगुणदोषप्रवृ
त्तये । पात्रापेक्षीन्यतःप्रज्ञांचि
कित्सार्थेविशोधयेत् ॥ १८॥
शस्त्र और शास्त्र और जल ये गुण
दोषकी प्रवृतिके लिये पात्रकी अपेक्षा कर-
तेहैं इससे चिकित्साके लिये बुद्धिकी
शुद्धिको करै ॥ १८ ॥
विद्यावितर्कोविज्ञानंस्मृतिस्तत्प
रताक्रिया । यस्येतेषड्गुणास्त
स्यनसाध्यमितवर्तते ॥ १९ ॥
विद्या वितर्क विज्ञान स्मृति तत्परता
क्रिया ये छःगुण जिसमें हैं वह साध्यका
अवलंघन नहीं करताहै ॥ १९ ॥
विद्यामितःकर्मदिष्टिरभ्यासःसिद्धि
राश्रय: । वैद्यशब्दाभिनिष्पत्तौ
बलमेकैकमप्यद: ॥ २० ॥
विद्या बुद्धि कर्मेमें दृष्टि अभ्यास
सिद्धि आश्रय वैद्य शब्दकी सिद्धिमें ये
एक २ भी समर्थ हैं ॥ २० ॥
यस्यत्वेतेगुणाःसर्वेसन्तिविद्या
दयःशुभाः । सवैद्यशब्दसंभूत
महेन्नृाणिसुखप्रदः ॥ २१ ॥
translation:
( 78 )
From the Charaka Samhita

Verse 13:
When three-quarters [of the qualities of a physician] are absent, both the learned and the ignorant physician become the cause [of harm]. The learned one considers his own self-offering as a boon, yet does not actually proceed with treatment. (13)

Verse 14:
Just as one who is ignorant moves like eyes guided only by touch, fearful as one who is afraid of fear itself, and just as a boat is tossed about by the force of wind — so does the ignorant physician carry out his procedures. (14)

Verse 15:
A conceited physician who treats one whose lifespan is fixed and whose condition has arrived suddenly — even if he cures that person — will quickly destroy hundreds of those whose condition is not certain. (15)

Verse 16:
Therefore, the physician who is proficient in the four qualities — knowledge of the scriptures, understanding of their meaning, application in practice, and observation of results — is called a Pranabhisara (one who brings life). (16)

Verse 17:
The one who has fourfold knowledge — of the cause, the signs, the alleviation of diseases, and their non-recurrence — is acclaimed by the king as the best of physicians. (17)

Verse 18:
Instruments, scriptures, and water all depend upon the vessel [patient/context] for the expression of their good and bad qualities. Therefore, for the purpose of treatment, one should purify one's own intellect. (18)

Verse 19:
Learning, reasoning, direct knowledge, memory, diligence, and practice — whoever possesses these six qualities finds nothing incurable standing in his way. (19)

Verse 20:
Learning, intellect, discernment in practice, experience, attainment, and support — each of these individually is sufficient for the fulfillment of the title "physician." (20)

Verse 21:
But one in whom all these auspicious qualities — beginning with learning — are fully present, being truly worthy of the title "physician," becomes a great bestower of happiness upon human beings. (21)

text:
सूत्रस्थानम् ।
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangori Gyaan Kosha
( ७२ )

जिसमें ये विद्या आदि संपूर्ण शोभन गुण हैं वह उत्तम वैद्य शब्दके योग्य होनेसे प्राणियोंके सुखका दाताहै २१॥
शास्त्रंज्योतिःप्रकाशार्थंदर्शनंबुद्धिरात्मनः । ताभ्यांभिषक्सुयुक्ताभ्यांचिकित्सन्नापराध्यति ॥ २२ ॥
ज्योतिके प्रकाशार्थ शास्त्रका दर्शन और अपनी बुद्धि, योग्य इन दोनोंसे चिकित्सा करता हुआ वैद्य अपराधका भागी नहीं होता ॥ २२ ॥
चिकित्सितेत्रयःपादायस्माद्वैद्यव्यपाश्रयाः । तस्मात्प्रयत्नमातिष्ठेद्भिषक्स्वगुणसम्पदे २३
चिकित्साके तीनोंपाद जिससे वैद्यके आश्रयहैं तिससे वैद्य अपने गुणोंकी संपदामें महान् यत्न करै ॥ २३ ॥
मैत्रीकारुण्यमार्तेषुशक्येप्रीतिरुपेक्षणम् । प्रकृतिस्थेषुमूतेषुवैद्यवृत्तिश्चतुर्विधेति ॥ २४ ॥
मित्रता और रोगियों पर दया शक्य रोगीमें प्रीति और स्वस्थ मनुष्योंकि उपेक्षा यह चार प्रकारकी वैद्योंकी वृत्तिहैं इति ॥ २४ ॥
तत्रश्लोकौ ॥
भिषगृजितांचतुष्पादंपादःपादश्च तुर्गुणः । भिषक्प्रधानंपादेष्योयस्माद्वैद्यस्तुयद्गुणः ॥ २५ ॥

इसमें ये दो श्लोकहैं कि भिषक्के जीतने हारोंके चारों पादहैं और पाद२में चार २ गुणहैं पादोंसे वैद्य प्रधानहै जिससे वैद्यभी उसी गुणवान् होताहै ॥ २५ ॥
ज्ञानानिबुद्धिब्राह्मीचिभिषजांयाचतुर्विधा । सर्वमेतच्चतुष्पादेखुङ्केसम्प्रकाशितमिति ॥
खुङ्डाकचतुष्पादाध्यायःसमाप्तः ॥ ९ ॥
ज्ञान और ब्राह्मी बुद्धि जो वैद्योंकी चार प्रकारकी होतीहै यह सब इस खुङ्डाक चतुष्पाद अध्यायमें भलीप्रकार प्रकाशित कियीहै ॥
खुङ्डाक चतुष्पादाध्यायः समाप्तः ॥ ९ ॥

दशमोध्यायः ।
अथातोमहाचतुष्पादमध्यायंव्याख्यास्यामः । इतिहस्माहभगवानात्रेयः ॥
इसके अनंतर महाचतुष्पाद अध्यायका वर्णन करतेहैं, यह भगवान् अत्रेयने कहाहै–
चतुष्पादंषोड्शकलंभेषजमिति भिषजोभाषन्ते । यदुकंपूर्वाध्यायेषोड्शगुणमितितदेषजम् । युक्तियुक्तमलमारोग्यायेतिभगवान्पुनरेवसुरात्रेयः ॥ १ ॥
कि चतुष्पाद भेषज सोलह कलाकाहै यह वैद्य कहतेहैं जो पहिले अध्यायमें कहाहै कि सोलह गुणहैं वह भेषज युक्तसेहीय युक्त तो आरोग्यके लिये

translation:
SUTRASTHANA (Chapter on Fundamentals)

He who possesses all these excellent qualities such as learning and others is worthy of the title "superior physician" and thereby becomes a bestower of happiness to all living beings. (21)

Scripture serves as the light of illumination; perception serves as the light of the self. A physician well-equipped with both of these commits no offense while practicing medicine. (22)

Since the three padas (components) of treatment depend upon the physician, the physician should therefore strive with great effort toward the perfection of his own qualities. (23)

Friendliness toward all, compassion toward the afflicted, joy toward the curable, and equanimity toward the incurable — these are the four modes of conduct for a physician. (24)

Here are two verses: The four padas that the physician has conquered, each pada having four qualities — among all the padas the physician is foremost, because the physician possesses those very qualities. (25)

The four kinds of knowledge and brahmic intelligence of physicians — all of this has been well illuminated in this Khundaka Chatushpada chapter.

The Khundaka Chatushpada Chapter is concluded. (9)

TENTH CHAPTER

Now we shall explain the Maha-Chatushpada chapter. Thus spoke the Blessed Atreya:

The physicians declare that medicine (bheshaja) is fourfold and consists of sixteen parts. That which was previously described as possessing sixteen qualities — that same medicine, when properly applied, is sufficient for the restoration of health. Thus again declares the Blessed Atreya, son of Surā. (1)

What is this — that the fourfold medicine has sixteen kalās (parts)? The physicians say so. As was stated in the previous chapter, those sixteen qualities belong to medicine: medicine that is properly and rationally employed is sufficient for the attainment of health...

text:
चरकसंहितायाम् ।
Digitized By Slddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

( २८ )

समर्थ है यह भगवान् पुनर्वसु आत्रेय कहतेहैं ॥ १ ॥

नेतिमैत्रेयः किंकारणंदश्यन्तेह्यातुराः केचिदुपकरणवन्तश्चपारिचारकसम्पन्नाश्चात्मवन्तश्चकुशलैश्चिभिषग्भिरनुष्ठिताः समुत्तिष्ठमानास्तथायुक्ताश्चापरेभ्रियमाणास्तस्माद्देषजमकिञ्चित्करंभवति २

आरोग्यके लिये समर्थ नहीं यह मैत्रेय कहतेहैं क्या कारणहै कि कोई २ आतुर ऐसे दीखतेहैं उपकरणवाले-सेवकोंसे संपन्न आत्मावान् और कुशलवैद्योंसे चिकित्सत भली प्रकार उत्तिष्ठमान ( नीरोग ) और तिसी प्रकारसे युक्तभी अन्य भ्रियमाण दीखतेहैं तिससे भेषज अकिंचित्कर ( निष्फल ) है ॥ २ ॥

तथा ॥ शम्भेसरासिचप्रसिक्तमल्पयुदकम् ॥ नच्यांस्यन्दमानायांपांशुभानेपांशुमुष्टिप्रकीर्णेइति ॥ तथापरेदश्यन्तेअनुपकरणाश्चापारिचारिकाश्चानात्मवन्तश्चाकुशलैश्चिभिषग्भिरनुष्ठिताः समुत्तिष्ठमानाः । तथायुक्तिभ्रियमाणाश्चापरेयतश्चप्रतिकुर्वन्सिद्धचितप्रतिकुर्वंच्रियतेअप्रतिकुर्वंच्रियतेततश्चिन्त्यतेभेषजमभेषजेनाविशिष्टमितिमैत्रेयः ॥ ३ ॥

सो ऐसेहै शस्त्र ( कुंड ) और सरमें सींचा अल्पजल-वहती हुई नदीमें पांशुधानमें पांशुकी मुष्टि प्रकीर्ण करदी तो कुछ नहीं करसकती-तैसेही अपरभी दीखतेहैं कि उपकरणसे रहित-परिचारकसे शून्य आत्मावानोंसे भिन्न अकुशल वैद्योंसे चिकित्सत भली प्रकार उत्तिष्ठमान होजातेहैं तैसेही युक्तअपरिभ्रियमाण दीखतेहैं जिस प्रतीकार करताहुआसिद्धिकोभी प्राप्त होताहै-और प्रतीकार करताहुआ मरताभीहै और प्रतीकार नहीं करताभी मरता है तिससे चिंताकी जाती है कि भेषज अभेषजसे विशिष्ट नहींहै यह मैत्रेय कहतेहैं ॥ ३ ॥

मिथ्याचिन्त्यतइत्यात्रेयः किंकारणंयेह्यातुराः षोडशगुणसमुदितेनानेनभेषजेनोपप्रथमानाइत्युक्तंतदनुपप्रद्धनिहिभेषजसाध्यानांव्याधीनांभेषजमकारणंभवति । येपुन रातुराः केवलाद्देषजादेतेसमुत्तिष्ठन्तेनतेषांसम्पूर्णभेषजोपदादानायसमुत्थानिविशेषोऽस्तियथाहि पितत्पुरुषंसमर्थमुत्थानायोत्थापयन्पुरुषोवलमस्योपादध्यात् । साक्षिपतरमपरिक्षिप्तएवोत्तिष्ठेतद्वत्संपूर्णभेषजोपलम्भादातुराः । येचातुराः केवलाद्देषजादिभ्रिय न्तेनचसर्वएवतेभेषजोपप्रचाः स
translation:
Charaka Samhita

(28)

"This is what the capable Bhagavan Punarvasu Atreya says." (1)

"No," says Maitreya. "What is the reason? For we see that some patients, provided with all necessary equipment and attendants, possessed of a sound constitution, and treated by skilled physicians, recover and rise to health; while others, similarly situated, die. Therefore medicine accomplishes nothing." (2)

This is illustrated thus: Just as water sprinkled sparingly into a pit or stream, or a handful of dust scattered into flowing dust-laden water, can accomplish nothing — so too we see, on the other hand, patients lacking equipment, without attendants, of compromised constitution, treated by unskilled physicians, nevertheless recover completely; while others, despite proper treatment, die. One who applies remedies may sometimes achieve success, and sometimes die despite treatment, and sometimes dies even without treatment. From this it is concluded that medicine is no better than non-medicine — so says Maitreya. (3)

"You think wrongly," replies Atreya. "What is the reason? Those patients who recover while being treated with this medicine endowed with sixteen qualities — it has been stated that for diseases curable by medicine, medicine is indeed a cause of recovery. As for those patients who recover from medicine alone, there is no particular superiority in their having received complete medicine — just as a strong man, capable of rising on his own, rises even without help from another who tries to lift him; but if additional support is given, he rises more easily. So too patients recover on account of complete medicine. And those patients who die from medicine alone — not all of them have received proper medicinal treatment..."

मुनिठेरनृनिहसर्वेव्याधयोभव
त्युपायसाध्याः ॥ ४ ॥

मिथ्याही चिंता करतेहैं यह आत्रेय
कहतेहैं क्या कारण है कि जो मनुष्य
आतुर सोलहगुने संपूर्ण इस भेषजसे युक्त
भी मरतेहैं इत्यादि जो कहाहै सो ठीक
नहीं क्योंकि भेषजकी साध्य जो व्याधी हैं
उनका भेषज अकारण नहीं होता–और
जो आतुर केवल भेषजके बिना भली
प्रकार उठिष्ठ मानहोतेहैं उनका संपूर्ण
भेषजके उपपादनके लिये विशेष
उद्योग नहींहै–जैसे कि पतित समर्थ

उसमें बलका उपाधान (सहारा) करताहै
वह फिर अत्यंत शीघ्र बिनाक्लेशके उठ
जाताहै तैसेही संपूर्ण भेषजके उपलंभसे
आतुर शीघ्र उठ जातेहैं–और जो आतुर
केवल भेषजसे मरतेहैं वे संपूर्ण, भेषजसे
उपन्न नहीं होते और जो उठतेहैं वहां
कुछ संपूर्ण व्याधि उपाय साध्यनहीं होतीथ

त्थापयितुम् । परीक्ष्यकारिणो

कार्येनापवाधोभवति । सम्पा
दयितिचेष्टकार्यम् । तथाभि
षक्स्वगुणसम्पन्नउपकरणवान्वी

पराधःसम्पादयन्येवातुरमारोग्ये

और उपायसे साध्य व्याधियोंको बिना

translation:
Digitized By Slogende Sampiri Gyaan Kosha
(81)

All diseases can be cured through the proper means — Aphorism 4

Those who think wrongly raise this objection, saying: What is the reason that a person who is afflicted and has been given the complete prescribed medicine sixteen-fold still dies? And so on. What is stated thus is not correct, because the medicine for diseases that are curable by medicine is never without effect. And for those patients who recover well even without medicine, there is no particular need to administer the full complement of medicines — just as when a fallen but capable man is being helped up by another, that helper provides support, and the man rises again very swiftly and without difficulty. In exactly the same way, patients recover quickly when supplied with all the medicines. And those patients who die from medicine alone do not arise from the complete medicine, and those who do recover — in their case the disease was not fully curable by means alone.

[Sanskrit verse:] For diseases curable by proper means, there is no success without those means; and for incurable diseases there is no collection of medicines at all, for an accomplished physician is not able to raise a dying patient. Those who act after proper examination are indeed skilled — just as one who knows the path of the arrow, who is a constant practitioner in the discharge of arrows, taking up the bow and releasing the arrow, is not obstructed in a great task at very close range, and accomplishes the desired task. In the same way, a physician who is endowed with his own qualities, furnished with instruments, and who begins his actions after careful examination, removes the curable disease (destroys it) and restores health to the patient. Therefore it is not the case that medicine is not superior to non-medicine — Aphorism 5.

And this is directly evident to us: that with medicine intended for the healthy, we treat the sick; we nourish the emaciated with what belongs to the robust, and the weak — Aphorism 6.

translation:
( 82 )
From the Charaka Samhita

One should treat the weak patient with mild medicines, the strong patient with strong medicines, and should nourish and strengthen the emaciated and feeble. (6)

We shall reduce the obese; we shall treat with cold one who is overcome by heat; we shall treat with warmth one overcome by cold; we shall replenish the diminished bodily constituents; we shall reduce those in excess; treating diseases by means opposite to their root cause, we shall properly restore the natural constitution. Acting thus, this entire collection of medicines becomes most excellent to us. (7)

And here are the verses:
The physician who knows the distinction between curable and incurable diseases, who acts with wisdom, and who begins treatment at the right time — he assuredly achieves the desired result. (8)

This verse states: One who knows the distinction between curable and incurable diseases, who performs treatment with intelligence, and who undertakes action at the proper time — such a person certainly accomplishes the task. (8)

The physician who treats an incurable disease inevitably suffers loss of his own interest, his learning, his reputation, and incurs blame and loss of wealth. (9)

A curable disease is of two kinds — easily curable and difficult to cure; and the incurable is also of two kinds — manageable (worth observing/palliating) and unapproachable (not to be taken up for treatment). (10)

Among the curable diseases, there is a three-fold classification according to mild, medium, and severe degree; but for those that are definitively incurable, there is no such alternative. (11)

One in whom the causative factors, premonitory symptoms, and manifest symptoms are all mild, and in whom the bodily constituents susceptible to vitiation do not have qualities similar to the aggravated dosha, and in whom there is no constitutional fault — such a case is curable. (12)

और चतुष्पाद भेषजकी उपपत्ति हो ये
सुखसाध्यके लक्षणहैं ॥ १४ ॥

निमित्तपूर्वरूपाणांरूपाणांमध्यमे
बले । कालप्रकृतिदुष्टानांसामा
न्योऽन्यतमस्यच ॥ १५ ॥

निमित्त पूर्वरूप रूप इनका बल
मध्यम हो काल प्रकृति दोष इनमें किसी
एककी सामान्यता हो ॥ १५ ॥

गर्भिणीवृद्धबालानांनात्युपद्रवपी
डितम् । शस्त्रक्षाराभिकृत्याना
मनवंकृच्छ्रदोषजम् ॥ १६ ॥

गभिणी वृद्ध बालक इनको अत्यंत
उपद्रवकी पीडा नहो–शस्त्र क्षार अभिका
कृत्य ये पुराने हों और कृच्छ् दोषसे
उत्पन्न हों ॥ १६ ॥

विद्यादेकपथंरोगंनातिपूर्णचतु

ष्पदम् । द्विपथंनातिकालंवाक
च्छ्साध्यंद्विदोषजम् ॥ १७ ॥

उसको एकपथ रोग जानै जिसके
अत्यंत पूर्ण चतुष्पाद न हों और जो
अतिकालका न हो उस द्विदोषज और
कृच्छ् साध्यको द्विपथ जानै ॥ १७ ॥

शेषत्वादायुषोयाप्यमसाध्यंपथ्य
सेवया । लब्ध्वाल्पसुखमल्पेन
हेतुनाशभवर्तकम् ॥ १८ ॥

आयुका शेष होनेपर याप्य नामके
असाध्यका पथ्यके सेवनसे उपचार करै–
अल्प सुखको प्राप्त होकर अल्पही हेतुसे
जो शीघ्र मृत्त हो जाताहैं ॥ १८ ॥

गम्भीरंबहुधातुस्थंमर्मसन्धिस
माश्रितम् । नित्यानुशायिनंरोगं
दीर्घकालमवस्थितम् ॥ १९ ॥

गंभीर और बहुत धातु और मर्म–
संधियोंमें स्थित और नित्य अनुशायी–
दीर्घकालके टिके ॥ १९ ॥

विद्याद्विदोषजंतद्वत्प्रत्याख्ये
यंत्रिदोषजम् । कियापथमित
कान्तंसर्वमागोनुसारिणम् २०

उस रोगको द्विदोषज जानै वह और
तिसी प्रकार त्रिदोषज रोग प्रत्याख्यान
( नांही ) करनेयोग्य हैं– क्रिया करनेके
अयोग्य और सबमागोंका अनुसारी
होवे तो ॥ २० ॥

translation:
(Page 83 — Sutrasthana)

Verse 13:
When the qualities of the season are not balanced with the dosha, when the dosha is not amenable to treatment, when the disease follows a single course, when the disease is new, and when there are no complications — these are the signs.

Verse 14:
When at the time of origin only one dosha is involved, when the body is capable of tolerating all medicines, and when the four limbs of treatment (physician, medicine, attendant, patient) are well established — these are the characteristics of a disease that is easily curable (sukhasadhya).

Verse 15:
When the causative factors, premonitory signs, and manifest symptoms are of middling strength, and when only one among season, constitution, and vitiated dosha is common — that too is a sign of easy curability.

Verse 16:
When pregnant women, the elderly, or children are not excessively tormented by complications, and when the condition is not caused by weapons, alkalis, or cauterization, and has not become chronic, and arises from a single dosha — these are signs of a manageable case.

Verse 17:
Know that disease which lacks complete fourfold support and has not become excessively prolonged to be of the "single path" type. That which arises from two doshas and is krichhra-sadhya (difficult to cure) should be understood as "dual path."

Verse 18:
When the lifespan is diminishing, the condition called yapya (palliable but not curable) is managed through proper regimen. Such a patient gains only a little relief, and from only a slight cause may quickly succumb to death.

Verse 19:
A disease that is deep-seated, located in many tissues, situated in vital points (marmas) and joints, constantly recurring, and persisting for a long time —

Verse 20:
— know such a disease to be caused by two doshas; similarly, a disease caused by three doshas is not fit for treatment (pratyakhyana — to be rejected for cure). If the disease is not amenable to any therapeutic procedure and spreads through all channels of the body, it is incurable.

text:
( ८ )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।

औत्सुक्यारितसंमोहकरिमिन्द्र
यनाशनम् । दुर्बलस्यसुसंवृद्धं
व्याधिंसारिष्टमेवच ॥ २१ ॥

उत्साह अरित संमोह इनका कती
और इंद्रियोंका नाशक–और दुर्बलमनु
ष्यके अत्यंत बढी और अरिष्टसहित
व्याधि इनकोभी त्यागदे ॥ २१ ॥

भिषजाञाकृपरीक्ष्यैविकाराणां
सुलक्षणम् । पश्चात्कार्यसमा
रम्भःकार्येषुसाध्येषुधीमता२ २
इस पूर्वोक्त प्रकारसे विकारोंके लक्षणोंकी
परीक्षा करके पश्चात बुद्धिमान् वैद्यसाध्य
रोगियोंकी चिकित्सका प्रारंभ करे॥ २२॥

साध्यासाध्यविभागज्ञोयःसम्यक्
प्रतिपत्तिमान् । नसमैंत्रेयतुल्या
नांमिथ्याबुद्धिमकल्पयेदिति २३
हे मैत्रेय साध्य असाध्यके विभागका
ज्ञाताः जो उत्तमज्ञानवान् वैद्य है वह
तुल्य रोगोंमें मिथ्या बुद्धिकी कल्पना
नकरे–इति ॥ २३

तत्रश्लोकौ ।
इहैौषधंपादगुणाःप्रभावौभेषजा
श्रयः । आत्रेयमैत्रेयमतीमतिद्वै
विध्यनिश्चयः ॥ २४ ॥
उसमें ये दो श्लोक हैं इसमें औषध पाद
गुण भेषजका प्रभाव आत्रेय और मैत्रेय
की बुद्धियोंमें दो प्रकारकी मतिका
निश्चयहै ॥ २४ ॥

चतुर्विंधविकल्पाश्चण्याध्यःस्व
स्वलक्षणाः । उक्तामहाचतुष्पा
देंयेष्वायतंभिषग्जितमिति२५
अग्नीत्यादि ॥ महाचतुष्पादाध्यायःसमाप्तः॥

चार प्रकारके विकल्प अपने २ लक्ष
णकी व्याधि ये सब महा चतुष्पाद
अध्यायमें कहीहैं जिनके अधीन वैद्यका
जय है ॥ २५ ॥
अग्नी दत्यादि॰महाचतुष्पादाध्यायःसमास: ॥ १० ॥

एकादशोऽध्यायः ।
अथातिस्तैषणीयमध्यायंव्या
ख्यास्यामः ॥ इतिह्स्माहभग
वानात्रेयः ।

इसके अनंतर तिस्रेषणीय अध्यायको
कहते; हैं यह भगवान् आत्रेयने कहा है–

इहखलुपुरुषेणानुपहतसत्त्वबुद्धि
पौरुषपराक्रमेणहितामिहचासुमिम्
थलोकेसमनुपश्यतातिस्रएषणाः
पर्येष्टव्याभवन्ति ॥ १ ॥

इस संसारमें जिसके सत्व बुद्धि पुरु
षार्थ पराक्रम विद्यमानहैं उस पुरुष को
इस लोक और पर लोकके हितको भली
प्रकार देखकर तीन एषणा ( इच्छा )
मानने योग्य हैं ॥ १ ॥

तत्था । प्राणैषणाधनैषणापर
लोकैष्णेतिआसान्तुखल्वेषणा
नांप्राणैषणांतावत्पूर्वतरमापयेत
translation:
( 8 )
In the Charaka Samhita.

Enthusiasm, aversion, and delusion destroy the sense faculties. In a weak person, a disease that has greatly advanced and is accompanied by fatal signs — these too should be abandoned [by the physician as incurable]. ॥ 21 ॥

After properly examining the characteristics of diseases as described above, the wise physician should then begin treatment of patients whose diseases are curable. ॥ 22 ॥

O Maitreya, a physician who is truly knowledgeable — who knows the proper distinction between curable and incurable [diseases] — should not entertain false notions about diseases that are alike. ॥ 23 ॥

There are two verses here: In this [chapter], the fourfold basis of medicine, the qualities of drugs, the power of medicaments, the views of Atreya and Maitreya — the determination of these two types of understanding is established. ॥ 24 ॥

The four kinds of [therapeutic] options, each with their own characteristics, have been described in the Mahachatushpada chapter — it is under these that the physician's victory [over disease] lies. ॥ 25 ॥
Thus ends the Mahachatushpada chapter. ॥ 10 ॥

The Eleventh Chapter.
Now we shall explain the chapter called Trisreshaniya [the three desires]. Thus spoke the Lord Atreya:

Here in this world, a person whose resolve, intellect, courage, and vigor are unimpaired — after rightly examining what is beneficial both in this world and the next — should pursue three Eshanas (desires/quests). ॥ 1 ॥

These are: the desire for life (Praneshana), the desire for wealth (Dhaneshana), and the desire for the next world (Paralokeshana). Of these three desires, one should first address the desire for life —

कस्मात्प्राणपरित्यागेहिसर्व
त्यागः । तस्यानुपालनंस्वथ
स्यस्वस्थवृत्तिरातुरस्यविकारप्र
शमनेऽप्रमादस्तदुभयमेतदुक्तव
क्ष्यतेच । तथथोक्तमनुवर्तमानः
प्राणानुपालनादीर्घमायुरवामो
तीति ॥ प्रथमैषणाव्याख्याता
भवति ॥ २ ॥

वे ऐसे हैं कि प्राणैषणा धनैषणा
और परलोकैषणा अर्थात् प्राण धन
परलोक इनकी इच्छा–इन तीनों एषणा-
ओंमें सबसे पहिले प्राणको एषणा को
प्राप्तहो ( देखै ) क्योंकि प्राणके परित्या-
गमें सबका परित्याग होताहै–उस प्राणका
पालन यह है कि स्वस्थकी स्वस्थवृत्ति–
रोगी को रोगकी शांतिमें अप्रमाद वे दो-
नों ये कहे और आगे कहेंगे–तिससे
यथोक्तरीतिसे बताव करता हुआ प्राणों
के पालनसे दीर्घ अवस्था को प्राप्तहो-
ताहै पहिली एषणा का वर्णन होचुका।

अथद्वितीयांधनैषणामापठ्यते ।
प्राणेभ्योह्यनन्तरंधनमेवपर्येष्टव्यं
भवति । नह्यतःपापात्पापीयो
ऽस्तियदनुपरकणस्यदीर्घमायुः
तस्मादुपकरणानिपर्येष्टुंयतेत
तत्रोपकरणोपायानुव्याख्या-
स्यामः ॥ ३ ॥

अब दूसरी धनकी एषणाको कहते
हैं–कि प्राणोंके अनंतर सब प्रकारसे
धनकी इच्छा करनी क्योंकि इस पापसे
परे कोई पापी नहीं कि उपकरण(सामग्री)
से रहित मनुष्य दीर्घ अवस्थाको प्राप्तहो
तिससे उपकरणोंकी इच्छाके लिये यत्न
करै उसमें उपकरणोंके उपायोंको कह-
तेहैं ॥ ३ ॥

तथथा । कृषिपाशुपाल्यवाणि
ज्यराजोपसेवादीनि । यानिचान्यानिपसतामिवगृहीतानिकर्मा
णिवृत्तिपुष्टिकराणिविद्यात्तान्या-
रभेतकरुम्।तथाकुर्वन्दीर्घजीवि-
तमनुवसतःपुरुषोभवतीति ॥ द्वि
तीयाधनैषणाव्याख्याताभवति४

वे ये हैं कि, कृषि पशुओंकी पालना
वाणिज्य राजसेवा आदि और जो
अन्यभी सत्पुरुषोंके अनिंदित-जीविकाकी
पुष्टिके कर्ता कर्म समझें उनकेभी करनेका
प्रारंभ करै–तिस प्रकार करताहुआ दीर्घ
जीवितको भोगता हुआ पुरुष होताहै
दूसरी धनैषणाको कहचुके ॥ ४ ॥

अथतृतीयांपरलोकैषणामापयेत
संशयश्चात्रकथंभविष्यामइतश्यु
तान्वेतिकुतःपुनःसंशयइतिउच्य
तेसन्तिहेकेप्रत्यक्षपराःपरोक्षत्वा
त्पुनर्भवस्यनास्तिक्यमाश्रिताः
सन्तिचागमप्रत्ययादेवपुनर्भवमि

translation:
Why is the abandonment of life the abandonment of everything? Its preservation — maintaining health for the healthy person, and diligent care for the sick person's recovery from disease — these two matters have been stated and will be stated further. Thus, following what has been prescribed, one who properly tends to the preservation of life attains long life. Thus the first Esana (desire/quest) has been explained. (2)

These three are: Praneshana (the desire for life), Dhaneshana (the desire for wealth), and Paralokeshana (the desire for the afterlife) — that is, the desire for life, wealth, and the next world. Among these three desires, one should first attend to the desire for life, because when life is abandoned, everything is abandoned. The preservation of that life consists in maintaining the health of the healthy person and the diligent treatment of the sick — both of these have been mentioned and will be mentioned again. By thus tending to life in the manner prescribed, one attains long life. The description of the first desire is now complete.

Now the second desire — for wealth — is stated: After life, one should seek wealth by every means, for there is no sin worse than this: that a person without means (equipment/resources) should attain long life. Therefore one should strive to acquire the means, and the ways of acquiring those means are explained here. (3)

These are: agriculture, animal husbandry, trade, service to kings, and whatever other occupations are regarded by good people as respectable livelihoods that sustain and nourish existence — one should undertake those. A person who lives thus engaged enjoys a long life. The second desire, Dhaneshana, has now been explained. (4)

Now regarding the third desire — for the next world (Paralokeshana): The doubt here is: "How shall we be after departing from here — will we reach those realms or not? From where does this doubt arise?" It is said: there are those who, taking only direct perception as authoritative and regarding the next birth as not directly perceptible, take refuge in atheism; and there are those who, on the basis of scriptural authority, accept rebirth —

text:
( ८६ )

च्छिन्तश्रुतिभेदाच्च । मातरंपितर्श्चैकेमन्यन्तेजन्मकारणंस्वभावंपरिनिर्माणंयदृच्छाञ्चापरेजनाइत्यतःसंशयः। किंनुखल्वस्तिपुनर्भवोनवेति ॥ तत्रबुद्धिमान्नास्तिक्यबुद्धिंजह्यात्विचिकित्साञ्च । कस्मात्प्रत्यक्षंह्यल्पमनल्पमप्रत्यक्षमस्तियदागमानुमानयुक्तिभिरुपलभ्यते ॥ येरेवतावदिन्द्रियैःप्रत्यक्षमुपलभ्यतेतान्येवसन्तिचाप्रत्यक्षाणि ॥ ५ ॥

अब तीसरी परलोकेषणाको प्राप्त हो इसमें संशयहै कि इस देहको त्यागकर कैसे होंगे वा न होंगे–संशय पुनः क्योंहै इसमें कहतेहैं कि कोई मनुष्य प्रत्यक्षको मानतेहैं क्योंकि पुनर्जन्म तो परोक्षहै–नास्तिकतामेंभी आशित कोई है आगम ( शास्त्र)के प्रमाणसे और श्रुतिके भेदसे कोई पुनः जन्मको चाहतेहैं–और कोई मनुष्य माता पिताको–कोई स्वभावको–कोई परमेश्वरकी रचना को और अपर मनुष्य यदृच्छा ( अकस्मात् ) को पुनः जन्मका कारण कहते हैं इससे संशय है–कि पुनर्भवहै वा नहीं– उसमें बुद्धिमान् मनुष्य नास्तिकताकी बुद्धिको और संशय को त्यागदे–क्योंकि प्रत्यक्ष अल्पहै और अप्रत्यक्ष बहुत है जो आगम अनुमान युक्तियोंसे जाना

जाताहै और जिन इंद्रियोंसे प्रत्यक्ष जाना जाताहै वे इंद्रियही अप्रत्यक्ष हैं ॥ ५ ॥

सताञ्चरूपाणामतिसन्निकर्षाद्तिविप्रकर्षादावरणात्करणदौर्बल्यान्मनोऽनवस्थानात्समानाभिहारादिभभावादतिसौक्ष्म्याच्च प्रत्यक्षानुपलब्धिः ॥ तस्मादपरीक्षितमेतदुच्यतेप्रत्यक्षमेवास्तिनान्यदस्तीतिश्रुतयश्चैतानकारणंयुक्तिविरोधात् ॥ ६ ॥

और अत्यंत समीप अति दूर आवरण इंद्रियों की दुर्बलता मनकी असावधानी समानोंका अभिहार ( मेल ) अभिभव ( तिरस्कार ) अत्यंतसूक्ष्मता इनसे विद्यमानभी रूप आदिका प्रत्यक्ष नहीं होता तिससे तुम यह परीक्षाको छोड कर कहते हो कि प्रत्यक्षहीहै अन्य नहीं है–और ये श्रुतिभी हैं कि युक्तिके विरोधसे कारण नहीं होता ॥ ६ ॥

आत्मामातुःपितुर्वायःसोपत्यंयदिसञ्चरेत्। द्विविधंसञ्चरेदात्मासर्वोवावयवेनवा ॥ ७ ॥

माता पिताका जो आत्माहै उसका संचार यादि अपत्यमेंहो तो दो प्रकारके आत्माका संचार संपूणं रूपसे होगा वा अवयव रूपसे ॥ ७ ॥

सर्वेश्चेत्सञ्चरेन्मातुःपितुर्वोमरणं भवेत् । निरन्तरंनावयवःकश्चि
translation:
( 86 )

And because of conflicting scriptural statements: some consider the parents to be the cause of birth, some consider one's own nature (svabhava), some consider the will of God, and others consider pure chance (yadriccha) as the cause of rebirth — hence there arises doubt. Therefore one should ask: does rebirth exist or not? A wise person should abandon the attitude of atheism and doubt, because what is directly perceptible is little, and what is imperceptible is vast — that which is known through scriptural testimony, inference, and reasoning. And those very sense organs by which things are perceived directly are themselves imperceptible. || 5 ||

Now, proceeding to the third inquiry — that concerning the afterlife — doubt arises here: after leaving this body, what will one become, or will one become nothing? Why does this doubt arise? It is said: some people accept only direct perception, because rebirth is beyond the senses; some, even among atheists, rely on the authority of scripture (shastra) and on distinctions in scriptural testimony and thus desire rebirth; some attribute birth to parents, some to inherent nature, some to the creation of God, and some to chance. From all this arises the doubt — does rebirth exist or not? A wise person should abandon the disposition of atheism and doubt, because direct perception is limited and what lies beyond direct perception is vast — known through scripture, inference, and reasoning.

What is directly perceived, and those very sense organs through which things are known directly — those sense organs themselves are imperceptible. || 5 ||

Because of things being too close, too far, obstructed, due to weakness of the sense organs, due to distraction of the mind, due to similarity of qualities, due to being overwhelmed, or due to extreme subtlety — even existing forms and such are not directly perceived. Therefore it is untested and unsound to say that only what is directly perceived exists and nothing else — and the scriptures also confirm this: such a position is opposed to reasoning. || 6 ||

And when something is extremely near, or extremely far, or when there is obstruction, weakness of the sense organs, inattention of the mind, similarity among objects (assimilation), suppression (being overpowered), or extreme subtlety — even forms that are actually present are not directly perceived. So you abandon proper examination and say only direct perception is valid and nothing else exists — but the scriptures too affirm that this cannot be the reason, as it is contrary to reasoned argument. || 6 ||

If the soul of the mother or of the father were to transmit itself into the offspring, it would transmit either entirely or in parts. || 7 ||

If the soul of the mother or father is transmitted into the offspring, that transmission of the soul would be either complete (as a whole) or in the form of a portion (part). || 7 ||

If it transmits completely from the mother or the father, then death of that parent would result. And no continuous partial [transmission is possible…]

text:
मन्त्रस्थानम् १

(८७)

Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

त्वसूक्ष्मस्यचात्मनः ॥ ८ ॥

संपूर्ण आत्माका संचार कहोगे तो माता वा पिताका मरण होजायगा और सूक्ष्मरूप आत्माका कोई निरंतर अवयव नहीं है ॥ ८ ॥

बुद्धिर्मनश्चनिर्णीतेयथैवात्मातथैवते । येषाञ्चैषामतिस्तेषांयोनिनोस्तिचतुर्विंधा ॥ ९ ॥

और निर्णय किये हुये बुद्धि और मनभी वैसेहीहैं जैसा आत्माहै जिन पुरुषोंकी यहमतिहै तिनके मतमें चार प्रकारकी योनि नहीं है ॥ ९ ॥

विधात्वस्वाभाविकंषण्णांधातूनांयत्स्वलक्षणम् । संयोगेचविवियोगे चतेषांकर्मैवकारणम् ॥ १० ॥

छओं धातुओंका जो अपना २ लक्षणहै उसको स्वभावसे उत्पन्न जाने उन धातुओंके संयोग और वियोगमें कर्म ही कारणहै ॥ १० ॥

अनादेश्चेतनाधातोर्नैषंयतेपरिनिर्मितिः । परआत्मासचेद्धेतुरिष्टोऽस्तुपरिनिर्मितिः ॥ ११ ॥

अनादि चेतनारूप जो परमेश्वरकी रचनाहै वह धातुओंसे नहीं होसकतीहै परम जो आत्मा वह हेतु परके निर्माणमें इष्ट रहो ॥ ११ ॥

नपरीक्षानपरीक्ष्येनकर्तांकारणं

नच नदेवानंषयः सिद्धाः कर्मक मर्मफलंनच ॥ १२ ॥

न परीक्षाहै न परीक्षाके योग्य कोई पदार्थहै न कर्ता है नकारणहै न देवताहैं न ऋषिहैं न सिद्धहैं न कर्महैं न कर्मका फलहै ॥ १२ ॥

नास्तिकस्यास्तिनैवात्मायदच्छोपहतात्मनः । पातकेभ्यःपरञ्चैत पातकंनास्तिकग्रहः ॥ १३ ॥

और यदच्छासे नष्ठहै बुद्धिजिसकी ऐसे नास्तिककी आत्माभी नहींहै यह नास्तिकका ज्ञान पातकोंसे परे पातकहै १३

तस्मान्मतिंविमुच्येताममार्गप्रस्तांबुधः । सतांबुद्धिप्रदीपेनपश्येत्सर्वंयथातथमिति ॥ १४ ॥

तिससे बुद्धिमान् मनुष्य कुमार्गमें फैली इस मतिको छोडकर सत्पुरुषोंकी बुद्धिरूप दीपकसे सबको यथायोग्य देखे ॥ १४ ॥

द्विविधमेवखलुसर्वंसच्चासच्चतस्य चतुर्विंधापरीक्षा । आप्तोपदेशः प्रत्यक्षमनुमानंयुक्तिश्चेति १५॥

और निश्चयसे सब सत् असत्रूपसे दोप्रकारकहै उसकी परीक्षा चार प्रकार कीहै कि आप्तोंका उपदेश प्रत्यक्ष अनुमान और युक्ति ॥ १५ ॥

आप्तास्तावत् ।

रजस्तमोभ्यांनिर्मुक्तास्तपोज्ञान

translation:
MANTRA-STHANA, Chapter 1

(Page 87)

Verse 8: Regarding the subtle self (sukshma atman):
If you say that the complete soul moves entirely, then the mother or father would die. And the subtle-form soul has no continuously abiding limb or part. (8)

Verse 9: Intellect (buddhi) and mind (manas), as determined, are exactly like the soul — so too are they. Those whose conviction this is, in their view the four kinds of birth (wombs) do not exist. (9)

Verse 10: The six constituent elements (dhatus) each have their own inherent nature and characteristic qualities. In their combination and separation, action (karma) alone is the cause. (10)

Verse 11: The creation of the beginningless conscious element (chetan dhatu), which is the work of the Supreme Lord, cannot come from the material elements alone. The supreme Soul, that cause, should remain the desired basis for the creation of others. (11)

Verse 12: There is no examination, there is nothing worthy of examination, there is no agent, there is no cause, there are no gods, no sages, no adepts, no actions, and no fruits of action. (12)

Commentary on 12: The atheist (nastika) holds this view — that there is no soul, no examiner, no worthy object of examination, no doer, no cause, no gods, no sages, no perfected beings, no karma, and no fruit of karma.

Verse 13: For the atheist whose intellect is corrupted by mere chance, there is truly no soul. This conviction of the atheist is a sin beyond all other sins. (13)

Commentary on 13: The one whose intellect is destroyed by mere randomness — such an atheist has, in effect, no soul. The knowledge of such an atheist is a transgression beyond all transgressions.

Verse 14: Therefore, the wise person should abandon this intellect that has spread along the wrong path, and with the lamp of the intelligence of good people, should see all things as they truly are. (14)

Verse 15: In sum, everything is of two kinds only — real (sat) and unreal (asat) — and the examination of these is of four types: the testimony of reliable authorities (apta-upadesa), direct perception (pratyaksha), inference (anumana), and reasoning (yukti). (15)

Regarding reliable authorities (aptas): They are those who are free from rajas (passion) and tamas (inertia), and who possess tapas (austerity) and knowledge (jnana)...

बलेनये । येषांत्रिकालममलज्ञा
नमभ्याहतंसदा ॥ १६ ॥
प्रथम आसतों ये हैं कि जो तप ज्ञान
के बलसे रजोगुण तमोगुणसे रहितहैं
और जिनका त्रिकाल निर्मल ज्ञान,सदैव

आप्ताःशिष्टविबुद्धास्तेतेषांवाक्य
मसंशयम् । सत्यंवक्ष्यन्तितेक

हैं उनका वाक्य असंशयहै वे सत्य कहेंगे

आत्मेन्द्रियमनोऽर्थानांसन्निकर्षा
त्प्रवर्तते । व्यक्तादात्वेयाबु

यते । विह्निनिगूढोधूमेनमैथुनंगर्भ

translation:
( 88 )
From the Charaka Samhita
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

Those whose pure knowledge of the three times (past, present, future) is ever unassailed by force — 16

Those who are foremost, who are free from rajas and tamas by the power of penance and knowledge, and whose knowledge of the three times is ever pure and free from destruction — this is verse 16.

The learned, the virtuous, and the awakened ones — they are the authoritative (apta); their words are beyond doubt. They will speak the truth; since they are free from rajas and tamas, why would they speak untruth? — 17

The contact of the self, the senses, the mind, and objects gives rise to what is called direct cognition (pratyaksha). The cognition that arises from what is manifest and immediate is called pratyaksha — 18

Prior to this direct perception, inference (anumana) operates in three modes across the three times: hidden fire is inferred from smoke, and sexual union is inferred from the perception of a foetus — 19

In this way, the wise determine the past — the fruit from the seed — and the future not yet arrived; and likewise, seeing a fruit from a seed, the intelligent person understands the lineage — 20

From the combination of irrigation, seed, and season, the growth of crops comes about; this is yukti (reasoned inference). Similarly, from the combination of the six dhatus (fundamental elements), the formation of the embryo takes place — 21

From the combination of the churning vessel, the churning stick, and the churner, fire is produced — this too is yukti. And yukti, when properly applied with all four limbs (of treatment) complete and sound, is capable of destroying disease — 22

That intellect which perceives effects arising from the combination of many causes — that is yukti; it should be understood as operating across the three times, and by it the three aims of life (dharma, artha, and kama) are accomplished — 23

This examination (pariksha) is the method; there is no other. By it everything is examined. Both the real and the unreal are to be examined through it, and through it the fact of rebirth is also established — 24

यही परीक्षाहै अन्य नहीं जिससे सब
की परीक्षा (ज्ञान) होतीहै और परीक्षाके
योग्य सत् असत्हैं और तिससे पुनर्भव

तत्रागमस्तावद्वेदोयश्चान्योऽपि
कश्चिद्वेदार्थादिवपरीतःपरीक्षकैः
प्रणीतः । शिष्टानुमतोलोकानु

अदोषोंसे पुनर्जन्मका अभाव धर्मके

दृष्टोपदिष्टपुनर्भवइतिव्यवस्येदेवं

धर्मके द्वारोंमें जो तत्परहैं और

ये नष्टहैं और ब्रह्ममें तत्पर आत्म कर्मके
ज्ञाता और जिनके सत्व बुद्धिका प्रचार
वर्तमानहै ऐसे पूर्वे और उनसेभी पूर्व

translation:
(Page 89)

This alone is the examination — there is no other — through which the examination (knowledge) of all takes place, by which the fit and the unfit are discerned, and from which rebirth (birth again) arises. ॥ 24 ॥

Among these sources of knowledge, the Veda is the primary Agama (authoritative text). Whatever else has been composed by examiners in accordance with the meaning of the Veda, accepted by the learned, operating for the welfare of people, and constituting established doctrine — that too is Agama. It is obtained from Agama itself. Charity, austerity, sacrifice, truth, non-violence, and celibacy — these are declared in the gateways of Dharma as conducive to prosperity and liberation, free from the faults of those whose sattva (goodness) is not corrupted, leading to the absence of rebirth. ॥ 25 ॥

In this, the Agama is the Veda, and whatever else has been composed by examiners in accordance with the meaning of the Veda, accepted by the learned, operating for the welfare of people — that established doctrine is also Agama. And from the Agama, charity, austerity, sacrifice, truth, non-violence, and celibacy — all these are obtained as causes of prosperity and liberation. The absence of rebirth for those of excellent sattva, free from faults, is nowhere described as contrary to the gateways of Dharma. 25

Those who are devoted to the gateways of Dharma, who have abandoned fear, passion, hatred, greed, delusion, and pride, who are dedicated to Brahman, who are knowers of the actions of the self, whose sattva and intellect are presently active — such ancient sages, and those even more ancient, endowed with divine vision, having directly perceived and taught the doctrine of rebirth — one should understand it thus, and it is also perceived directly. ॥ 26 ॥

Children of parents resemble them; yet among those of equal birth, there are differences in complexion, voice, form, character, intellect, and fortune. Birth in high or low families, states of servitude or lordship, pleasure and pain, length of life — the inequality of lifespan seen here, the spontaneous behaviors of infants untrained — crying, suckling, smiling, fear, and the like — these arising as signs of the persistence of karmic tendencies, the special fruition of similar karma, some having greater or lesser mental capacity, memory of past lives, the return here and the perception of beings who have departed — all this indicates that one's own karma, done by oneself, inseparable from one, indestructible, carried from the previous body, linked to one's celestial connections, produces its fruit. From that fruit another seed is inferred, and from that seed again a fruit. ॥ 27 ॥
