translation:
(Page 113, Sutrasthana, Chapter 1)

Verse 68:
One whose digestive organ (grahani) has excessive pitta, and whose digestive fire is very powerful — the oleating substance (sneha) drunk by such a person is rapidly incinerated by the force of that fire, like fuel thrown into flames.

Commentary 68: When a person's grahani contains excess pitta and the digestive fire is very strong, the oleating substance consumed by that person is quickly turned to ash by the power of the fire.

Verse 69:
Having consumed the prescribed measure of the linctus (leha), the strengthened person nourishes his vital essence (ojas). The fire combined with the oleating substance then produces intense thirst accompanied by complications.

Commentary 69: Having consumed the prescribed measure of the oleating preparation, the person becomes strong and his ojas is elevated; the fire, combined with the oleating substance, produces intense thirst along with complications.

Verse 70:
Even the greatest of remedies is not capable of calming a person who is saturated with oleating substances; if he does not drink very cold water, he will be burned (consumed by the internal fire).

Commentary 70: For a person who has been overtaken by oleating substances, even the most potent remedies are insufficient for relief; if he does not drink very cold water, he will be consumed.

Verse 71:
Just as a serpent dwelling in a hollow is consumed by the fire of its own venom — so too, if thirst arises before the oleating substance has been digested, the physician should induce vomiting.

Commentary 71: Just as a serpent in a hollow is burned by the fire of its own poison, similarly if thirst arises before the oleating substance is digested, the physician must induce emesis.

Verse 72:
After drinking cold water and eating dry food, one should induce emesis. Ghee should not be given alone in pure pitta conditions, and especially not when pitta is combined with ama (undigested matter).

Commentary 72: After drinking cold water and consuming dry food, emesis should be induced. Ghee should not be administered when pitta alone is vitiated, and particularly not when pitta is combined with ama.

Verse 73:
The ghee spreads through the entire body, destroys consciousness, and can cause death. The resulting conditions are: drowsiness, distress, bloating, fever, rigidity, and loss of consciousness.

Commentary 73: The ghee pervades the whole body and, destroying awareness, can be fatal. The conditions that arise are: torpor, severe distress, abdominal distension, fever, rigidity, and absence of consciousness.

Verse 74:
The conditions include: afflictions of the abdominal organs, itching, pallor (pandu), hemorrhoids, anorexia, thirst, abdominal enlargement, disorders of the grahani (digestive organ), heaviness, and inability to speak.

Commentary 74: Disorders of the viscera, itching, pallor, piles, loss of appetite, thirst, abdominal enlargement, grahani disorders, heaviness, and suppression of speech.

Verse 75:
Colic, disorders due to ama, and other such conditions arise from improper administration of oleating therapy. In such cases, emesis is most recommended, as is sudation and awaiting the appropriate time.

Commentary 75: Colic and disorders from ama all arise from errors in oleation therapy; in such cases, emesis is the best remedy, along with sudation and waiting for the right moment.

[The page ends mid-verse with the beginning of the next verse on proper assessment of strength and understanding.]

text:
( ११४ )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।

मेवच । तकारिष्टप्रयोगश्चरूक्षपानासेवनम् ॥ ७६ ॥

प्रतिपत्ति ( ज्ञान ) व्याधिका बल जानकर संसन करावै–तत्का अरिष्ट प्रयोग रूखे पान और अन्नका सेवन७६

मूत्राणांत्रिफलायाश्चस्नेहव्यापत्तिभेषजम् । अकालेचाहितश्चैवमात्रायानचयोजितः ॥ ७७ ॥

मूत्र त्रिफलासे जो स्नेहके नाशको औषध–असमयमें और अहित और मात्राके बिना भक्षण किया स्नेह मिथ्या७७

स्नेहोमिथ्योपचाराचव्यापयेतातिसेवितः। स्नेहात्प्रस्कन्दनोजन्तुभिरात्रोपरतःपिबेत् ॥ ७८ ॥

प्रचारसे और अत्यंत सेवनसे मार देताहै–स्नेहसे शुष्क जंतु तीन रात्रिके अनंतर स्नेहको पीवै ॥ ७८ ॥

स्नेहञ्चद्रवमुष्णञ्चत्र्यहंभुक्तवारसौदनम् । एकाहोपरतस्तद्द्भुक्तवाप्रच्छर्दैनंपिबेत् ॥ ७९ ॥

स्नेह द्रव उष्णको तीन दिन खाकर रसौदन भक्षण करै और तैसेही एकदिन उपरामसे भोजन करके प्रच्छर्दनको पीवै ॥ ७९ ॥

स्यात्तुसंशोधनार्थायवृत्तिःस्नेहेविरिक्तवत् । स्नेहिद्विषःस्नेहनित्यामृदुकोष्ठाश्चयेनराः ॥ ८० ॥

और संशोधनके लिये स्नेहमें वतांव विरेचनके समानहै जो स्नेहके द्रेषीहैं जो स्नेहको नित्य खातेहैं जिन मनुष्योंका कोष्ठ मृदुहै ॥ ८० ॥

क्लेशासहामथनित्यास्तेषामिष्टाविचारणा । लावतैतितिरमायूरंसवाराहकौकुटाः ॥ ८१ ॥

जो क्लेशको सह सकतेहैं जो मदिरा नित्य पीतेहैं उनकी विचारणा इष्टहै–लाव तितिर मयूर वराह कुक्कुट ॥ ८१ ॥

गव्यजोरभमात्स्याश्चरसाःस्वस्नेहनिहिताः । यवकोलकुलत्थाश्च स्नेहाःसगुडशर्कराः ॥ ८२ ॥

गौ अज उरभ्र मत्स्य इनके रस अपने स्नेहनमें हितेहैं–जौ कोल कुलथी गुड शकेरा इनके स्नेह ॥ ८२ ॥

दाडिमंदधिसव्योषंरससंयोगसंग्रहः । स्नेहयन्तितिलाःपूर्वैजग्धाःसस्नेहफाणिताः ॥ ८३ ॥

दाडिम दधि व्योष यह रसके संयोगका संग्रह है प्रथम भक्षण किये और स्नेहसे फाणित किये तिलभी स्नेहसे युक्त करतेहैं ॥ ८३ ॥

कुशराश्वबहुस्नेहास्तिलकाम्बलिकास्तथा। फाणितंशृङ्गवेरश्च तैलञ्चसुरयासह ॥ ८४ ॥

और कुसर और काले तिल तैसेही अत्यंत स्निग्ध होतेहैं और फाणित शृंगवेर और मदिराके संग तैलको ८४
translation:
( 114 )
From the Charaka Samhita.

And also the use of Arishta preparations and the consumption of rough (dry) food and drink. (76)

Knowing the strength of the disease through proper understanding, one should administer Arishta preparations along with light food and dry grains. (76)

The remedy for improper administration of snehana (oleation) with urine and triphala: when taken at the wrong time, in an unsuitable manner, or without proper measurement, the snehana becomes ineffective. (77)

Improperly administered snehana, when used excessively, can be fatal. One whose body has been dried out by organisms should drink oleating substances again after three nights. (78)

One should consume warm liquid oleating substance for three days along with meat-soup and rice; after resting for one day, having eaten a meal, one should then take an emetic. (79)

For the purpose of purification, the regimen regarding oleating substances is similar to that of purgation. Those who dislike fats, those who consume fats daily, and those who have a soft stomach (80) —

Those who cannot tolerate hardship, and those who drink wine regularly — for them the recommended diet is: lava (common quail), partridge, peacock, boar, and domestic fowl. (81)

The juices of cow, goat, sheep, and fish are beneficial when prepared with their own fats. Barley, jujube, horse-gram, jaggery, and sugar — these are the oleating substances for them. (82)

Pomegranate, curd, and the three-spice combination — this is a collection of juice combinations. Sesame seeds eaten before, combined with molasses and fat, also increase oleation. (83)

Kusha grass preparations, sesame of many kinds, tila-kambala preparations, molasses, ginger, and oil taken together with wine — (84)

text:
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha
सूत्रस्थानम् । (११५)

पिबेदृक्षोघृतैमांसैर्जीर्णेश्रीयाच्च भोजनम् । तैलंसुरायामण्डेनव सांमज्जानमेवया ॥ ८५ ॥

रूक्षमनुष्य पीवैं जीर्णे होनेपर घी मांस सहित भोजन करै—सुराके मांडके संग तैलको वा वसा और मज्जाको पीवै ८५॥

पिबेत्सफाणितंक्षीरंनरःस्निह्यति वातिकः । धारोष्णंस्नेहसंयुक्तं पीत्वासलवणंपयः ॥ ८६ ॥

और फाणित दूधको पीकर वातिक मनुष्य स्नेह युक्त होताहै—धारोष्ण स्नेहसे और लवणसे युक्त दूधको पीकर ॥ ८६ ॥

नरःस्निह्यतिपीत्वावासरंदध्वःसफाणितम् । पाञ्चप्रसृतिकीपेयापायसोमाषमिश्रकः ॥ ८७ ॥

वा फाणित दधि केसर (तोड) को पीकर मनुष्य स्नेहसे युक्तहोताहै दूधकी पांच प्रसृति पीने योग्यहैं और उडद युक्त ॥ ८७ ॥

क्षीरसिद्धोबहुस्नेहःस्नेहयेदिचराचरम् । सर्पिस्तैलवसामज्जातण्डुलप्रसृतेःकता ॥ ८८ ॥

दूधकी सिद्ध (मावा) अतिस्नेहसे युक्त होकर शीघ्री मनुष्यको स्नेह युक्त करतेहै सिपे (घी) तैल वसा मज्जा इनको प्रसृतिभर तंडुलोंमें बनाकर॥ ८८॥

पाञ्चप्रसृतिकीपेयापेयासनेहनामिच्छता । ग्राम्यानुपोदकंमांसंगुडंदधिपयस्तिलान् ॥ ८९ ॥

पांच प्रसृति स्नेहनका अभिलाषी मनुष्य पीवै—ग्रामका अनूपजल मांस गुड दधि दूध तिल ॥ ८९ ॥

कुष्ठीशोषीप्रमेहीचस्नेहनेनप्रयोजयेत् । स्नेहैर्यथास्वंतानिसिद्धैःस्नेहयेदविकारिभिः ॥ ९० ॥

इनको कुष्ठी शोषी प्रमेही स्नेहनके लिये भक्षण न करैं यथास्व (स्वाभाविक) सिद्ध स्नेहजो अविकारीहैं उनसे उनको स्नेहसे युक्त करै ॥ ९० ॥

पिप्पलीभिर्हरीतकयासिद्धैर्विफलयापिवा। द्राक्षामलकयूषाभ्यांदध्नाचाम्लेनसाधयेत् ॥ ९१ ॥

अथवा पीपल हरड़े त्रिफला इनसे सिद्ध स्नेहोंसे स्नेहित करैं द्राक्षा आँवले इनके यूषोंसे दधि वा अम्लसे साधन करै ॥ ९१ ॥

व्योषगर्भीभिषक्स्नेहंपीत्वास्निह्यतितञ्चरः । यवलोककुलत्थानां साःक्षीरंसुरादधि ॥ ९२ ॥

व्योषहै गर्भमें जिसके ऐसे स्नेहको भिषक् मिलाकर मनुष्यको स्निग्ध करता है जो लौका कुलथी इनके रस दूध मदिरा दधि ॥ ९२ ॥
translation:

Sutrasthana (Chapter on Fundamental Principles), Page 115

Verse 85:
One who is lean should drink ghee with meat after digestion, and should take oil mixed with the lees of wine (sura), along with marrow. [85]
Commentary: A lean person, after digestion has occurred, should eat food together with ghee and meat; or should drink oil mixed with the lees of sura (fermented liquor) and also drink marrow. [85]

Verse 86:
By drinking phanita (a preparation of sugarcane) mixed with milk, a vata-predominant person becomes unctuous. Similarly, one should drink warm milk mixed with fat and salt. [86]
Commentary: By drinking phanita together with milk, a person of vata constitution becomes unctuous. One should drink milk that is warm and combined with fat and salt. [86]

Verse 87:
A person also becomes unctuous by drinking phanita mixed with curd and kesara (saffron/costus). The peya (thin gruel) of five prasriti measure mixed with urad (black gram) is recommended. [87]
Commentary: By drinking phanita, curd, and costus together, a person becomes unctuous. Five prasriti (a unit of measure) of milk gruel is the appropriate quantity, and it should be combined with black gram. [87]

Verse 88:
Milk prepared (reduced) with a large quantity of fat quickly makes even animate and inanimate things unctuous. It is prepared by cooking ghee, oil, fat, and marrow with a prasriti measure of rice. [88]
Commentary: Milk reduced (into condensed form) with an abundance of fat quickly renders a person unctuous. Ghee, oil, fat, and marrow — each in the measure of one prasriti — should be prepared together with rice. [88]

Verse 89:
One who desires snehanam (oleation therapy) with five prasriti should drink: water from village/marshy-land animals, meat, jaggery, curd, milk, and sesame. [89]
Commentary: One desirous of oleation with five prasriti should drink: water from village or marshy regions, meat, jaggery, curd, milk, and sesame. [89]

Verse 90:
Those suffering from kushtha (skin diseases), shosha (consumption/wasting), and prameha (urinary disorders) should be treated with oleation. They should be made unctuous using fats that are properly prepared and free from disturbing qualities, each appropriate to their condition. [90]
Commentary: Kushtha patients, those with wasting disease, and those with urinary disorders should not consume these substances for oleation; rather, they should be made unctuous using fats that are naturally prepared and free from disturbing properties, each suited to their individual condition. [90]

Verse 91:
Alternatively, one may use fats prepared with pippali (long pepper), haritaki (chebulic myrobalan), or triphala. These may also be prepared using the juice of grapes and amalaki (Indian gooseberry), or with curd and sour substances. [91]
Commentary: Alternatively, fats prepared with long pepper, haritaki, and triphala should be used for oleation. One may prepare them using the decoctions of grapes and amalaki, or with curd or other sour substances. [91]

Verse 92:
The physician should prepare a fat in which vyosha (the three pungents: ginger, pepper, and long pepper) is incorporated, and by this make the person unctuous. The vehicle for this includes the juices of bottle gourd and horse gram, along with milk, wine, and curd. [92]
Commentary: A fat preparation in which vyosha (the three pungents) is contained — the physician should use this to render a person unctuous. The accompaniments are: the juices of bottle gourd and horse gram, milk, wine (madira), and curd. [92]

text:
( ११६ )

क्षीरःसर्पिश्वतिसछंस्नेहनीयंघृतो
त्तमम् । तैलमञ्जावसासार्पिबंदर
त्रिफलारसैः ॥ ९३ ॥

और दूध घी इनसे सिद्ध जो उत्तम
घृतहैं स्नेहन करने योग्य है तैल मज्जा
वसा घीको बेर त्रिफलाके रसोंमें सिद्ध
करके ॥ ९३ ॥

योनिशुक्रदोषेषुसाधयित्वाप्रयो
जयेत् । गृह्नात्यम्बुयथावर्त्मप्रव
त्यधिकंयथा ॥ ९४ ॥

योनि शुक्रके दोषोंमें दे जैसे वर्त्म
जलको ग्रहण करले जैसे अधिक जल
निकसै ॥ ९४ ॥

यथाग्निर्जीर्य्यतिस्नेहस्तथाश्रवति
चाधिकः । यथावाक्लेयमृतिप
ण्डमासिंचंत्वरयाजलम् ॥ ९५ ॥

और जैसे अग्निजीर्ण होतीहै और
स्नेह अधिक करताहै जैसे आद्र मिट्टीका
पिंड सींचनेसे शीघ्र जलको झरताहै ९५

श्रवातिश्रंसतेस्नेहस्तथात्वारितसे
वितः । लवणोपहिताःस्नेहाःस्ने
हयन्त्यचिराञ्चरम् ॥ ९६ ॥

तैसे शीघ्रतासे सेवन किया स्नेहपतित
होजाताहै लवणसे युक्त स्नेह शीघ्री
मनुष्यको स्निग्ध करतेहैं ॥ ९६ ॥

तञ्चयिभष्यन्यरूक्षश्रसूक्ष्मउष्णं
व्यवायिच । स्नेहमग्रेप्रयुञ्जीतत

तःस्वेदमनन्तरम् ॥ स्नेहस्वेदो
पपञ्चस्यसंशोधनमथेतरिमिति ९७

उस स्नेहको अभिष्यंदी और अरूक्ष
मनुष्य सूक्ष्म उष्ण व्यवायी स्नेहको प्रथम
खा फिर स्वेदन करें स्नेह और स्वेद से
युक्त को इतर संशोधनदै ॥ ९७ ॥इति॥

तत्रश्लोकः ॥

स्नेहविधिःकृत्स्नव्यापतिसिद्धः
सभेषजा । यथाप्रश्नंभगवतांव्या
हृतंचान्द्रभागिना ॥ ९८ ॥

स्नेहाभ्यायःसमाप्तः ।

उसमें यह श्लोकहै कि सब स्नेहोंकी
विधि भेषजसहित व्यापित्तकी सिद्धि यह
सब भगवान् चांद्रभागीने प्रश्नके अनु-
सार वर्णन कियाहै ॥ ९८ ॥

स्नेहाध्यायःसमाप्तः ॥ १३॥

चतुर्दशोऽध्यायः ।

अथातःस्वेदाध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः।

इति हस्माह भगवानात्रेयः।

अब स्वेदाध्यायका वर्णन करतेहैं
यह भगवान् आत्रेय कहतेहैं ॥

अतःस्वेदाःप्रवक्ष्यन्तेयेयेंयथावत्
प्रयोजितैः। स्वेदसाध्याःप्रशाम्य
न्तगदावातकफात्मकाः ॥ १ ॥

इसके अनंतर स्वेदोंको कहते हैं
जिनके यथावत् प्रयोग करनेसे वात
कफके वे रोग शांत होंतेहैं जो स्वेदसे
साध्य हैं ॥ १ ॥
translation:
( 116 )

Milk, ghee, and the excellent medicated ghee prepared from these — along with oils, marrow, fat, and ghee prepared with the juice of jujube and triphala — are suitable for oleation therapy. (93)

And ghee, milk, and so forth: from these the finest ghee suitable for oleation is prepared; oil, marrow, and fat are likewise prepared with the juice of jujube and triphala. (93)

In disorders of the female genital organs and of semen, these should be prepared and administered. Just as water is absorbed by the eyelid, so the excess fluid is drawn out. (94)

Just as fire is digested and the oil increases, so like a moist lump of clay that quickly drips water when more is poured upon it. (95)

Likewise, when administered quickly, the oil drips away; and when oils are combined with salt, they lubricate a person swiftly. (96)

That oil which is non-roughening, subtle, warm, and penetrating should first be taken, and after that sudation should be applied. The combination of oleation and sudation constitutes the purification of the five; the other is otherwise. (97)

Here is the verse:

The entire procedure of oleation, together with medicines, accomplishes the removal of disorders — all this has been described by the venerable Chandrabhagin in response to questions. (98)

The chapter on oleation is concluded. (Chapter 13)

Chapter Fourteen.

Now we shall explain the chapter on sudation (fomentation/sweating therapy).

Thus spoke the venerable Atreya.

Now the chapter on sudation is being described — this the venerable Atreya declares.

Now the various sudation therapies are described; when properly applied, they pacify diseases of the nature of vata and kapha that are amenable to sudation. (1)

After this, the sweating therapies are described: by their proper application, those diseases of vata and kapha that are curable by sweat become pacified. (1)

( ११७ )

स्नेहपूर्वंप्रयुकेनस्वेदेनाविर्जितेऽनिले । पुरीषमूत्रेतांसिनसञ्जनित
कथञ्च ॥ २ ॥

स्नेह पूर्वक स्वेदसे जब वायु नष्ट
होजाता है तब किसीप्रकार भी मल मूत्र
वीर्य आसक्त नहीं होते ॥ २ ॥

शुष्काण्यपिहिकाष्ठानिस्नेहस्वेदो
पपादनैः । नमयन्तियथान्यायं
किंपुनर्जीवतोनराच् ॥ ३ ॥

शुष्ककाष्ठभी स्नेह और स्वेदके कर-
नेसे यथा योग्य नव जातेहैं तो जीवते
मनुष्य क्यों नहीं नम्र होंगे ॥ ३ ॥

रोगर्तुव्याधितापेक्षोनात्युष्णोऽति
मृदुर्नच । द्रव्यवान्कल्पितोदेशे
स्वेदःकार्य्यकरोमतः ॥ ४ ॥

रोग ऋतु व्याधि इनके अनुसार अति
उष्ण अति मृदुसे अच्छे देशमें द्रव्योंसे
किया स्वेद कार्य कारी कहाहै ॥ ४ ॥

व्याधौशीतशरीरेनचमहान्स्वेदो
महाबलो। दुर्बलेदुर्बलःस्वेदोमध्य
मेमध्यमोहितः ॥ ५ ॥

व्याधि शीत शरीर ये तीनों महा
बलवान् होंयतो महान् स्वेद–इनके दुबल
होनेपर दुबल और मध्यममें मध्यम हित
होताहै ॥ ५ ॥

वातश्लेष्मणिवातेवाकफेवास्वेद
इष्यते । स्निग्धरूक्षस्तथास्निग्धो
ऽरूक्षश्चाप्युपकल्पितः ॥ ६ ॥

वात श्लेष्ममें वा वातमें वा कफमें
वह स्वेद इष्टहै जो स्निग्ध रूक्ष वा स्निग्ध
वा अरूक्ष द्रव्योंसे कियाहो ॥ ६ ॥

आमाशयगतेवातेकफेपकाशयाश्रिते । रूक्षपूर्वोहितःस्वेदःस्नेहपूर्वस्तथैवच ॥ ७ ॥

आमाशयमें तो वातहो और कफ
पकाशयमें होयतो रूक्ष पूर्वक और तैसेही
स्नेह पूर्वक स्वेद हित होताहै ॥ ७ ॥

वृषणौहृदयंदृष्टीस्वेदयेन्मृदुनैववा।
मध्यमंवंक्षणौशेषमङ्गावयवंमिष्टः ॥ ८ ॥

वृषण हृदय दृष्टि इनमें स्वेद मृंदु
द्रव्यसे करें बंक्षणोंमें मध्यम स्वेद और
शेष अंगमें यथेष्ट करै ॥ ८ ॥

सुशुद्धैर्नकैः पिण्डचागोधूमानाम
थापिवा । पञ्चोत्पलपलाशैर्वि
स्वेयःसंवृत्यचक्षुषी ॥ ९ ॥

शुष्क तित्तोंसे भलीप्रकार स्वच्छ
जीर्ण वक्षोंसे वा गेहूंकी पिंडीसे वा पञ्च
उत्पल पलाशोंसे नेत्रोंको मींचकर स्वेद
करावै ॥ ९ ॥

मुक्तावलीभिःशीताभिःशीतलैर्भाजनैरपि। जलाद्रैर्जलजैहस्तैःस्व

translation:
(Page 117)

Verse 2: When the wind-humor (vata) has been subdued by fomentation applied after oleation, then feces, urine, and semen do not become retained in any way. (2)

Verse 3: Even dry pieces of wood can be made supple by the application of oil and fomentation in the proper manner — how much more easily then can living persons be made flexible? (3)

Verse 4: Fomentation performed in the proper place, with appropriate medicinal substances, neither excessively hot nor excessively mild, and suited to the disease, the season, and the specific condition of the patient, is considered effective. (4)

Verse 5: When the disease, the cold condition of the body, and the patient's constitution are all of great strength, strong fomentation is prescribed; when they are weak, gentle fomentation is used; and when moderate, moderate fomentation is beneficial. (5)

Verse 6: Fomentation is desired in conditions of vata-kapha combined, vata alone, or kapha alone. It may be administered using unctuous substances, dry substances, or a combination thereof, as appropriate. (6)

Verse 7: When vata is located in the stomach (amashaya) and kapha is located in the small intestine (pakashaya), fomentation preceded by dry treatment is beneficial in the first case, and fomentation preceded by oleation is beneficial in the second. (7)

Verse 8: The testes, the heart, and the eyes should be fomented only with gentle substances; the groins should receive moderate fomentation; and the remaining parts of the body may be fomented as required. (8)

Verse 9: Using well-dried clean old grain boluses, or wheat-flour boluses, or the five varieties of palasha flowers, one should apply fomentation to the body with the eyes kept closed. (9)

Verse 10: By applying garlands of cool pearls, or cool vessels filled with water, or with hands moistened with water and lotus leaves, touching the region of the heart...

चरकसंहितायाम् ।

हस्तोंसे स्वेद लेते हुए मनुष्यके हृदयका
स्पर्श करै ॥ १० ॥
शीतशूलव्युपरमेस्तम्भगौरवविनि२
हे। सआतेमार्दवेस्वेदेस्वेदनादिर
तिर्मता ॥ ११ ॥
शीतल स्तंभ गौरव इनकी शांति
और नाश होनेपर और स्वेदमें मृदुताके
होनेपर स्वेदनसे विराम कहाहै ११
पित्तप्रकोपोमूच्छोचशरीरसदनं
तृषा । दाहस्वेदाङ्गदौबल्यम
तिस्निघ्धस्यलक्षणम् ॥ १२ ॥
पित्तका प्रकोप और मूच्छों शरीरका
सदन ( जकड़ना ) तृषा दाह स्वेद किये
अंगोंमें दुर्बलता ये अत्यंत स्निग्धके
लक्षणहैं ॥ १२ ॥
उक्तस्तस्याश्रितीयेयोग्रैष्मिकःस
र्वशोविधिः। सोडितिस्विन्नस्यक
र्त्व्योमधुरःस्निग्धशितलः॥ १३ ॥
उसके आश्रयसे जो ग्रीष्म कालमें
संपूर्ण कहींहै वह मधुर स्निग्ध शीतल
विधि अति स्विन्नके लिये करनी॥१३॥
कषायमयिनित्यानांगभिण्यारक्त
पित्तिनाम् । पित्तिनांसातिसारा
णांरूक्षाणांमधुमेहिनाम् ॥ १४ ॥
जो मनुष्य कषाय मदिराको नित्य
पीतेहैं गर्भिणी रक्तपिती पित्ती अतिसारी
रूक्ष मधुमेहीहैं ॥ १४ ॥
विदग्धभष्टनाडीनांविषमयविका

रिणाम् । शान्तानांनष्टसंज्ञानां
स्थूलानांपित्तमेहिनाम् ॥ १५ ॥
विदग्धसे जिनकी नाडी भ्रष्टहैं विष
मयका जिनको विकार है जो शांतहैं
जिनकी संज्ञा नष्ट है जो स्थूलहैं जिनको
पित्तसे प्रमेह रोग है ॥ १५ ॥
तृष्यतांक्षुधितानाञ्चक्रुद्धानांशो
चतामपि । कामलयुदिरिणाञ्चैव
क्षतानामाढ्यरोगिणाम् ॥ १६ ॥
तृषित और क्षुधितहैं क्रुद्ध और
शोचते हुयेहैं—कामला उदर रोगी जोहैं
जो क्षतहैं आढ्य रोगीहैं ॥ १६ ॥
दुर्बलातिविशुष्काणामुपक्षीणौ
जसांतथा । भिषकैमिरिक्षाणा
ञ्चनस्वेदमवतारयेत् ॥ १७ ॥
दुर्बल अति शुष्कहैं जिनका ओज
क्षीणहैं—जिनको तिमिर रोगहै इतने मनु-
ष्योंको वैद्य स्वेद न करावै ॥ १७ ॥
प्रतिश्यायेचकासेचहिक्काश्वासे
प्वलाघवे। कर्णमण्यांशिरःशूले
स्वरभेदेगलग्रहे ॥ १८ ॥
प्रतिश्यायमें कासिक्का और श्वासमें
अलाघवमें—कर्णकी मणि शिरका शूल
स्वरभेद गल ग्रह ॥ १८ ॥
अर्दितैकाङ्गसर्वाङ्गपक्षाघातेवि
नामके। कोष्ठानाहिविबन्धेषुशुका
यातेविजृम्भके॥ १९ ॥

translation:
( 118 )
From the Charaka Samhita

One should touch the heart of the person while taking sweat from the hands. || 10 ||

When coldness, stiffness, and heaviness subside, and when softness appears in the sweat, one should stop the sudation treatment. || 11 ||

Aggravation of pitta, fainting, prostration of the body, thirst, burning sensation, sweating, and weakness in the limbs — these are the signs of excessive oleation. || 12 ||

The procedure described in relation to summer season — for those who have been excessively sweated, it should be performed in a manner that is sweet, unctuous, and cooling. || 13 ||

Those who habitually drink astringent liquors; pregnant women; those suffering from raktapitta (bleeding disorders), pittaja conditions, diarrhea; those who are lean and emaciated; those suffering from diabetes (madhumeha) — || 14 ||

Those whose digestive fire is corrupted and whose pulse is vitiated; those afflicted with toxic conditions; those who are calm and torpid; those who have lost consciousness; those who are obese; those suffering from pittaja prameha — || 15 ||

Those who are thirsty, hungry, angry, or grieving; those suffering from jaundice (kamala), abdominal disorders, injuries, or the disease of the wealthy (adhya roga) — || 16 ||

Those who are weak, excessively dry, whose vital essence (ojas) is depleted, and those whom the physicians have identified as suffering from eye disorders — for all these persons, the physician should not administer sudation. || 17 ||

In coryza (pratishyaya), cough (kasa), hiccup (hikka), dyspnea (shvasa), and in conditions of lightness; in pain in the ears and head, hoarseness of voice, and obstruction of the throat — || 18 ||

In facial paralysis, hemiplegia, and complete paralysis; in conditions of obstruction and constipation in the bowels; in yawning — || 19 ||

text:
मत्रस्थानम् । ( ११२ )
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

एक अंगमें पीडित और सर्वांग और पक्षके आघातमें विनामकमें कोष्ठ आनाह विबंध शुकाघात–विजृंभकमें ॥ १९ ॥

पार्श्वपृष्ठकटीकुक्षिसंग्रहेगृधसीषु च । मूत्रकृच्छेमहत्वेचमुष्कयोरङ्कुमर्दके ॥ २० ॥

पार्श्व पृष्ठ कटि कुक्षी इनके संग्रहमें गृधसींमें मूत्रकुच्छ्रमें अंडकोशोंकी वृद्धिमें अंगमर्दमें ॥ २० ॥

पादोरुजानुजङ्घार्तिसंग्रहेश्वयथावपि । खञ्जीष्वामेषुशीतेचवेपथौ वातकण्टके ॥ २१ ॥

पाद उरु जंघा जानु इनके अत्यंत संग्रहमें श्वयथुमें–खली आम शीत कंप वात कंटक इनमें ॥ २१ ॥

सङ्कोचायामश्लेषुस्तम्भगौरवसुतिषु । सर्वाङ्गेषुविकारेषुस्वेदनं हितमुच्यते ॥ २२ ॥

संकोच आयाम शूलमें–स्तंभ गौरव सुतिमें संपूर्ण अंगोंके विकारमें स्वेदन हित कहाहै ॥ २२ ॥

तिलमाषकुलत्थाम्लघृततैलामिषौदनैः । पायसैःकसरैर्मांसैःपिण्डस्वेदंप्रयोजयेत् ॥ २३ ॥

तिल माष कुलथी अम्ल तैल मांस ओदन पायस कुसर मांस ये उसको दें जिसको पिंडसे स्वेद करना हो ॥ २३ ॥

गोखरोष्ट्रवराहाश्वशकृद्भिःसतुषैर्यवैः । सिकतापांशुपाषाणकरीषयसपूटकैः ॥ २४ ॥

गौ खर ऊंट वराह अश्व इनका मल और तुषों सहित जौ सिकता पांसु पाषाण शुष्क गोमय लोहिक पुट ॥ २४ ॥

श्लैष्मिकान्स्वेदयेत्पूर्वैर्वातिकान्समुपाचरेत् । द्रव्याण्येतानि शस्यन्तेयथास्वंप्रस्तरेष्वपि ॥ २५ ॥

इनसे कफवालोंको स्वेद करावै और वातरोगियोंकी पहिलेसे चिकित्साकरै–यही द्रव्य यथायोग्य प्रस्तरणोंमेंभी श्रेष्ठ है ॥ २५ ॥

भूगृहेषुचजेन्ताकेषूष्णगर्भगृहेषुच । विधूमाङ्गारतमेष्वभ्यक्तःस्वयतितनासुखम् ॥ २६ ॥

और भूगृहों ( गर्त ) में जेन्ताकोंमें और उष्ण गर्भके गृहोंमेंभी विधूम अंगारोंसे तपायेहुयोंमें अभ्यंगकतां मनुष्य सुखसे स्वेदित होता है ॥ २६ ॥

ग्राम्यानूपौदकंमांसंपयोबस्तिशिरस्तथा । वराहमध्यपित्तामृक्स्नेहवित्तलतण्डुलान् ॥ २७ ॥

ग्रामका अनूपजल मांस दूध भेडका शिर वराहकेमध्य पित्तका रुधिर स्नेहके तिल तंडुल ॥ २७ ॥

इत्येतानिसमुत्काथ्यनाडीस्वेदंप्रयोजयेत् । देशकालंविभागज्ञो युक्त्यपेक्षोभिषक्कमः ॥ २८ ॥

translation:
CHAPTER ON SWEATING THERAPIES (Sveda Sthana) — Page 112

[Verse 19]
When a single limb is afflicted, or the entire body, or when there is injury to one side of the body, or when there is stiffness, abdominal distension, constipation, hiccough, or yawning — [sudation is indicated].

[Verse 20]
In pain and stiffness of the flanks, back, waist, and groins, in sciatica, in dysuria, in enlargement of the scrotum, and in body-ache — [sudation is beneficial].

[Commentary on 20]
In stiffness of the flanks, back, waist, and groins, in sciatica, in dysuria, in swelling of the testes, and in body-ache — [sudation is recommended].

[Verse 21]
In pain and contraction of the feet, thighs, calves, and knees, in edema, in lameness, in conditions of cold, trembling, and vata-kantaka (a foot disease) — [sudation is indicated].

[Commentary on 21]
In severe contraction of the feet, thighs, calves, and knees — in edema, in vata disorders involving coldness, trembling, and vata-kantaka — [sudation is recommended].

[Verse 22]
In contraction, extension, pain in the joints, stiffness, and heaviness, and in all disorders of all the limbs, sudation is declared beneficial.

[Commentary on 22]
In contraction, extension, pain, stiffness, and heaviness — in disorders of all the limbs — sudation is said to be beneficial.

[Verse 23]
For pinda-sveda (bolus sudation), one should use sesame, black gram, horse gram, sour substances, ghee, oil, meat, cooked rice, milk preparations, rice gruel, and meat preparations.

[Commentary on 23]
Sesame, black gram, horse gram, sour substances, oil, meat, cooked rice, milk preparations, rice gruel, and meat — these are given to the one for whom bolus sudation is to be performed.

[Verse 24]
The dung of cow, donkey, camel, boar, and horse, mixed with husked barley, sand, dust, stones, dried cow-dung cakes, iron slag — [these are used for other forms of sudation].

[Commentary on 24]
The dung of cow, donkey, camel, boar, and horse — mixed with husked barley, sand, dust, stones, dried cow-dung, and iron — these form the materials for certain sudation procedures.

[Verse 25]
The former materials are used to induce sweating in those with kapha disorders; the treatment of vata patients should be managed with the appropriate substances — these same materials are also excellent when used as bedding in sudation procedures.

[Commentary on 25]
Sweating should be induced in kapha patients using the former materials, while vata patients should first receive appropriate treatment. These same substances are equally excellent when used as spread materials for sudation.

[Verse 26]
In underground chambers, in jentaka (a sudation chamber), and in rooms with intense heat — a person who has been anointed (abhyanga) sweats comfortably when exposed to smokeless charcoal heat.

[Commentary on 26]
In underground pits, in jentaka chambers, and in very hot rooms — a person who has received oil massage sweats comfortably when placed near smokeless burning coals.

[Verse 27]
The flesh of village, marshy-land, and aquatic animals, milk, the head of a goat, the fat from the middle of a boar, bile mixed with blood, fatty substances, sesame, and rice — [these are used for nadi-sveda].

[Commentary on 27]
Village water, marshy-land meat, milk, the head of a sheep, the central fat of a boar, bile mixed with blood, fatty sesame, and rice.

[Verse 28]
These materials, having been decocted, should be used by the physician for nadi-sveda (tube sudation). The physician who is knowledgeable about the proper place, time, and method — and who exercises careful judgment — should employ these therapies accordingly.

text:
( १२० )
नाकसंदितायाम् ।
Digitized By Siddhantta eGangoth Gyaan Kosha

इन सबका काथ करके नाडी स्वेद
को करावे—देशकालके विभागका ज्ञाता
युक्तिमान् उत्तम वैद्य ॥ २८ ॥

वारणाघृतकैरण्डिशृगमूलकसर्ष
पैः । वासावंशकरञ्जार्कपत्रैरश्मा
न्तकस्यच ॥ २९ ॥

वारण अमृतके ( गिलोय ) एरंड
सहिंजना सरसों वासा तुलसी वंश करंज
अर्कपत्र अश्मांतक ( बहेडा ) ॥२९॥

शोभाञ्जनकशेरीयमालतीसुरसा
जकैः । पत्रैरुत्काथ्यसिलिलेंना
डीस्वेदंप्रयोजयेत् ॥ ३० ॥

सौभांजन कसेरु मालती सुरसा
अजकै इनके पत्तोंके जलको पकाकर
नाड़ी स्वेदको करावै ॥ ३० ॥

भूतीकपञ्चमूलाभ्यांसुरयादिघम
र्तुना॥ पत्रैरंलैश्चसस्नेहैनाडीस्वेदं
प्रयोजयेत् ॥ ३१ ॥

भृतीक पंचमूलोंसे सुरासे दधिके
मस्तुसे और स्नेहसिहत अम्लके पत्तोंसे
नाडीस्वेदको करावै ॥ ३१ ॥

एतएवचिनिर्यूहाःप्रयोज्याजाल
कोष्ठके । स्वेदनार्थंघृतक्षीरतैल
कोष्ठांश्चकारयेत् ॥ ३२ ॥

यही नियूह जालकोष्ठमें प्रयोग करने
स्वेदनके लिये घृत दूध तैल इनके कोष्ठ
बनवावै ॥ ३२ ॥

गोधूमशकलेश्चूर्णैर्वानामम्लसं
युतैः । सस्नेहिकण्वलवणैरुपना
हःप्रशस्यते ॥ ३३ ॥

गेहूंके टुकड़ोंसे और अम्लसे मिले
जोके चूर्णोंसे स्नेह सिहत किराव (मदिरा-
का बीज द्रव्य) लवण इनसे उपनाह
(लेप वा बंधन) उत्तम होताहै ॥ ३३ ॥

गन्धैःसुरायाःकिंशेनजीवन्त्याश
तपुष्पया । उमयाकुष्ठतैलाभ्यां
युकयाचोपनाहयेत् ॥ ३४ ॥

गंधोंसे सुराके कीटसे जीवंती ( हरड़े )
सौंफ उमा ( हलदी वा अलसी ) कूट
तैल मिलाकर उपनाह करैं ॥ ३४ ॥

चर्मिभिश्चोपनद्धव्यःसलोमिभिरपू
तिभिः । उष्णवीर्यैरलाभेतुकौ
शेयाविकशाटकैः ॥ ३५ ॥

और लोमसिहत अपिवत्र चमोंसेभी
उपनाह करावै—वह न मिलेतो कौशेय
( रेशम ) और ऊनकी शाडीसे करें ३५

रात्रौबद्धंदिवामुञ्चेत्मुञ्चेद्रात्रौ
दिवाकृतम् । विदाहपरिहाराथं
स्यात्प्रकर्षतुशीतले ॥ ३६ ॥

रात्रिमें बँधे हुयेको दिनमें खोल दे
और दिनमें किये को रात्रिमें खोल दे—
विदाहके दूर करनेके लिये शीतलमें प्रकर्ष
करै अर्थात् अधिक सेवन करैं ॥ ३६ ॥

सङ्कूरःमस्तरोनाडीपारिषेकोऽवगा

translation:
( 120 )
[From the Charaka Samhita]

A physician who is knowledgeable about the divisions of place and time, and who is skillful and wise, should administer nasal/tube-fomentation (nadi sveda) using the decoctions of all these. ॥ 28 ॥

[Verse 29:] With vāraṇa (elephant plant), ghee, castor, drumstick root, mustard, vāsā (Adhatoda), bamboo, karañja, calotropis leaves, and bāheḍā (Terminalia bellirica). ॥ 29 ॥

Vāraṇa, giloy (Tinospora), castor, drumstick, mustard, vāsā, tulsi, bamboo, karañja, calotropis leaf, bāheḍā — [these are the materials]. ॥ 29 ॥

[Verse 30:] With the leaves of shobhāñjana (Moringa), kaśeru (sedge), mālatī (jasmine), surasa (basil), and ajaka — boil them in water and administer nadi sveda (tube fomentation). ॥ 30 ॥

Moringa, sedge, jasmine, basil, ajaka — cook the leaves of these in water and administer nadi sveda. ॥ 30 ॥

[Verse 31:] With bhūtīka and the five roots (panchamūla), with surā (fermented liquid), with the sour buttermilk whey, and with sour leaves combined with fat/oil — administer nadi sveda. ॥ 31 ॥

Bhṛtīka with the five roots, with surā, with the top layer of curd (mastu), and combined with fat and sour leaves — administer nadi sveda. ॥ 31 ॥

[Verse 32:] These same decoctions are to be used in the jālakoṣṭha (lattice-chamber steam box). For the purpose of sweating, chambers using ghee, milk, and oil should also be constructed. ॥ 32 ॥

These same decoctions should be used in the jālakoṣṭha (steam chamber); and for fomentation, chambers filled with ghee, milk, and oil should be prepared. ॥ 32 ॥

[Verse 33:] A poultice (upanāha) made with powdered wheat pieces mixed with sour substances, combined with fat and the grains of kiraṇa (a fermented grain substance) and salt, is highly recommended. ॥ 33 ॥

Using pieces of wheat flour mixed with sour things, along with fat, kiraṇa (a seed from wine-making), and salt — this poultice (upanāha, i.e., a medicated bandage or application) is excellent. ॥ 33 ॥

[Verse 34:] With the fragrances of surā (fermented liquid), with kīṭa (an insect product), jīvantī (harṛe/Terminalia), śatapuṣpā (fennel), umā (turmeric or linseed), combined with kuṣṭha (Saussurea) and oil — apply as an upanāha. ॥ 34 ॥

Using the fragrant substances from fermented liquid, combined with jīvantī (harṛe), fennel, umā (turmeric or linseed), ground together with kuṣṭha and oil — apply as a poultice. ॥ 34 ॥

[Verse 35:] The upanāha should be bound with hides that still have their hair and are not putrid, which have warm potency. If these are not available, use silk or woolen cloth. ॥ 35 ॥

A poultice should also be applied using hairy, non-putrid hides — if those are unavailable, use silk or woolen cloth. ॥ 35 ॥

[Verse 36:] What is bound on at night should be removed during the day, and what is applied during the day should be removed at night. To remove the burning sensation (vidāha), the application should be continued in a cool manner, that is, used more extensively. ॥ 36 ॥

Whatever is bandaged at night should be opened in the day, and whatever is applied during the day should be removed at night. To relieve burning, one should continue its use in a cooling manner, that is, increase its application. ॥ 36 ॥

[Continues:] Saṅkūra, mastara, nāḍī pāriṣeka (tube irrigation/pouring), and avagā— [text continues on next page]

text:
सुत्रस्थानम् । ( १२१ )
Digitized By Siddkanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

हनम् । जेन्ताकोष्मघनःकर्षुकु
टीभुःकुम्भिकैवच ॥ ३७ ॥
शंकर, प्रस्तर, नाडी स्वेद–परिसेक,
अवगाहन, जेंताक, पत्थर घन, कर्ष,
कुटी, भू, कुंभिका ॥ ३७ ॥
कूपोहोलाकइत्येतेस्वेदयन्तित्र
योदश । तान्यथावत्प्रवक्या
मिसर्विनैवानुपूर्वशः । इति ॥ ३८ ॥
कूप, होलाक, ये तेरह स्वेद करातेहैं
इन सबको यथार्थ रीतिसे क्रम पूर्वक
कहताहूं–इति ॥ ३८ ॥
तत्रवस्त्रान्तरितैरवस्त्रान्तरितैर्वापि
पिण्डैर्यथोकैरुपस्वेदनंशङ्करस्वे
दइतिविद्यात् ॥ ३९ ॥
ऊनमें वस्त्रके भीतर किये हों वा न
किये हों ऐसे पूर्वोक्त पिंडोंसे जो उपस्वेदन
वह शंकरस्वेद जानना ॥ ३९ ॥
शूकशमीधान्यपुलाकानांवेशवा
रायसकुशरोत्कारिकादीनांवाप्र
स्तरेकौशेयाविकोत्तरप्रच्छदेपञ्चा
ङ्गुलोरुबुकार्कपत्रप्रच्छदेवारस्व
भ्यक्तसर्वगात्रस्यशयानस्योपारि
स्वेदनंप्रस्तरस्वेदइतिविद्यात् ४०
शूक शमी धान्य पुलाक इनके वा
वेशवार लोहा कुशर उत्कारिका आदिके
ऐसे विस्तरपर जो रेशम उनसे ढका हो वा
पंचागुल रुबुक अर्केके पत्ते इनसे ढका हो

उसपर सब गात्रमें अभ्यंग कराकर शयन
कतींके ऊपर जो स्वेदन वह प्रस्तरस्वेद
जानना ॥ ४० ॥
स्वेदनद्रव्याणांपुनर्मूलफलपत्रभ
ङ्गादीनां मृगशकुनिपिशितशिरः
स्पदादीनामुष्णस्वभावानांवाय
थार्हमंललवणस्नेहोपसंहिता नां
मूत्रक्षीरादीनांवाकुम्भ्यांबाष्पम
नद्वमन्यासुतक्थितानांनाळ्या
शरेषीकावंशदलकरञ्जार्कपत्रान्य
तमकृतयागजाग्रहस्तसंस्था नया
व्यामदीर्घयाव्यामाद्धेदीर्घयावा
व्यामचतुर्भागाष्टभागमूलाग्रपरि
णाहस्रोतासार्वतोवातहरपत्रसंवृ
तिच्छद्याद्विभ्विर्विविनासितया
वातहरासिद्धस्नेहाभ्यक्तगात्रोबा
ष्पमपहरेत् । बाष्पोह्यूर्ध्वगामी
विहलचण्डवेगस्त्वचमिवदहन्छु
खंस्वेदयतीतिनाडीस्वेदः ॥ ४१ ॥

translation:
Sutra-sthana (Chapter on Fundamentals), page 121.

[Verse 37]
...hana. The jentaka (steam-chamber), koṣhma-ghana (heat-dense enclosure), karṣhu (pit), kuṭī (hut), bhū (earth), and kumbhikā (pot) — [these are the types of sudation]. ॥37॥

[Commentary on 37:]
Śaṃkara, Prastara, Nāḍī, Sveda — Pariseka (pouring), Avagāhana (immersion), Jentāka, Patthar-ghana (stone-heat), Karṣha, Kuṭī, Bhū, Kumbhikā — these are the thirteen. ॥37॥

[Verse 38:]
Kūpa (pit) and Holāka — these thirteen types of sudation — I shall now describe each one in proper order. ॥38॥

[Commentary on 38:]
Kūpa, Holāka — these thirteen sudations — I shall explain each in due order. ॥38॥

[Verse 39:]
Sudation applied by means of boluses (piṇḍas), either wrapped in cloth or unwrapped, as previously prescribed — that is known as Śaṃkara-sveda (bolus sudation). ॥39॥

[Commentary on 39:]
Whether the previously described boluses are wrapped in cloth or not — the fomentation given with them is called Śaṃkara-sveda. ॥39॥

[Verse 40:]
Sudation produced by having the patient, fully anointed all over the body, lie upon a bed made of śūka (awned grain husks), śamī, grain chaff, pulāka, or alternatively of veśavāra, iron, kuśara, utkārikā, and so on, covered with silk, or covered with leaves of the five-leafed variety, arka-leaves, or similar coverings — that is to be understood as Prastara-sveda (bed sudation). ॥40॥

[Commentary on 40:]
Śūka, śamī, grain, pulāka — or veśavāra, iron, kuśara, utkārikā and similar materials — spread as a bed and covered with silk, or covered with pañcāṅgula, rubuka, or arka leaves — upon that, after anointing the entire body, the patient lies and receives sudation — this is known as Prastara-sveda. ॥40॥

[Verse 41:]
For the materials of sudation — roots, fruits, leaves, broken parts and so forth; flesh from deer, birds, head and feet and so on — those that are hot in nature — combined as appropriate with sour, salty, and unctuous substances — milk, urine and so on — are cooked in a pot (kumbhī) so that steam issues forth. A tube (nāḍī), made of one of the following — reed (śara), īṣīkā (a grass), bamboo strips (vaṃśadala), karañja, or arka leaves — fashioned to resemble an elephant's trunk, of a length of one vyāma (fathom) or more, or three-quarters or one-eighth of that, its circumference measured from base to tip, with all its openings covered by wind-dispelling leaves, treated with oil prepared from wind-dispelling herbs — through this tube the steam is to be directed onto the body. For steam, being upward-moving, fierce and swift in force, burns the skin like fire, yet when properly directed through this tube it causes perspiration — this is called Nāḍī-sveda (tube sudation). ॥41॥

[Commentary on 41:]
The materials for sudation — roots, fruits, leaves, and broken parts; flesh of deer, birds, head, feet and so on that are hot in nature; combined suitably with sour, salty, and unctuous substances — these together with urine, milk and so on are cooked in a pot from which steam issues. A tube made from one of — reed, īṣīkā grass, bamboo strips, karañja or arka leaves — fashioned like an elephant's trunk...

माद्धैलंबीहो व्यामके चतुभागका जिसका
मूलहो मूलाग्रके प्रमाणका जिसमें स्रोत
( छिद्र ) हों और जिसका छिद्र चारों-

करे–वह बाष्प ऊपरकी न जाकर नष्ट
चंड वेग ( शनैः ) त्वचाको नहीं दग्ध
करता हुआ सुखसे स्वेद करता है यह

नायुत्काथैःसुखोष्णैःकुम्भीवार्षु

जो वातिकहैं वा अधिक वातिकहैं
उन मूल आदिकोंके सुखोष्ण काथोंसे
कुंभी वायुलिका वा पनाडी इन पात्रोंको
पूर्ण करके यथोक्त सिद्ध स्नेहसे अभ्यक्त
गात्रको वस्त्रोंसे ढककर सेचन करावै यह
परिषेकहै ॥ ४२ ॥

वातहरोत्काथक्षीरतैलघृतपिश
तरसोष्णसलिलकोष्ठकावनाहस्तु
यथोक्तएवावगाहः ॥ ४३ ॥

और वात हारी काथ किये दूध–

कमें जो स्नान वह यथार्थ अवगाहहै॥४३

अथजेन्ताकंचिकीर्षुर्भूमिपरीक्षे
त । तत्रपूर्वस्यांदिश्युत्तरस्यांवा

तमस्यकूलेदक्षिणपश्चिमेवासूपती

दङ्मुखंवाभिमुखतीर्थेकूटागारं
कारयेत् ॥ ४४ ॥

इसके अनन्तर जेन्ताक स्वेदको
चाहता हुआ मनुष्य भूमिकी परीक्षा करै
उसमें पूर्व वा उत्तर दिशामें वर्त्तमान गुण-
वाले श्रेष्ठकाली व सुवर्णकी मट्टीके भू-

स्थानोंमें किसी एकके कूलपर दक्षिण व

किये भूमिभागमें जलसे सात व आठ

Charaka Samhita

[Left column — prose commentary in Hindi on verses 21–43:]

[On Nadi-sveda, verse 21:]
...equal in size and a vyama in length, or half a vyama in length — made of a quarter-vyama measure at its root, having openings (channels/holes) covered on all four sides with leaves that destroy vata, bent two or three times — through that tube, after anointing the body with the medicated oil that is well known for destroying vata, the steam should be received. The steam does not escape upward, and without burning the skin with a fierce force, it gently produces perspiration. This is Nadi-sveda (tube-sweating). ॥ 21 ॥

[Verse 42 — Parisheka:]
For those who are vata-predominant or highly vata-predominant, the vessels called kumbhi, vayulika, or panadi should be filled with a warm decoction of mula (roots) and similar herbs; the body already anointed with the prescribed medicated oil should then be covered with cloth and sprinkled (with that decoction). This is Parisheka (sprinkling/affusion). ॥ 42 ॥

[Verse 43 — Avagaha:]
A warm bath in vessels containing a decoction of vata-relieving herbs, milk, oil, ghee, and meat-broth — this, as prescribed, is Avagaha (immersion bath). ॥ 43 ॥

[Right column — Sanskrit verse 44 and Hindi commentary:]

[Verse 44:]
One who wishes to construct a Jentaka (sweat-chamber) should first examine the ground. In that ground — situated toward the east or north, endowed with good qualities, having black soil or golden-colored soil, on the bank of any one among reservoirs of water such as ponds, lakes, and the like, on the southern or western side, at a beautiful ghat/landing, on a level and well-divided plot of ground — having measured out seven or eight aratnis (cubits) from the water, he should have a kuta-agara (domed house/secret enclosure) built, facing east or facing north, toward the ghat. ॥ 44 ॥

[Hindi commentary on verse 44:]
After this, a person wishing to prepare Jentaka-sveda should examine the ground. He should choose land that lies to the east or north, endowed with good qualities, of black or golden soil, on the bank of some water-body such as a pond or lake, on the southern or western side at a fine ghat, on a level and well-divided plot. He should have a kuta-agara — that is, a closed enclosure — built seven to eight aratnis (arm-lengths) from the water, facing east or facing north, toward the ghat. ॥ 44 ॥

text:
मंत्रस्थानम् । ( १२३ )
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

रस्यचतुःकिष्कुमात्रपुरुषप्रमाणं मृणमयकन्दुसंस्थानंबहुसूक्ष्मिच्छ्रमङ्गारकोठकान्तंसिपधानंकारयेत् ॥ ४५ ॥

ऊँचाईके विस्तारसे अधिकसे अधिक सोलह हाथभर गोल मिट्टीके ऐसे पर कोठेसे युक्त हो जिसमें अनेकझरोंखे हों इसकूटागारकेभीतर चारोंतरफ हाथभर ऊंची भीतकी पिंडी बनवावे उसमें किवाड़ न लगवावे और इस कूटागारके मध्यमें चार किष्कुमात्र पुरुषके प्रमाणका मिट्टीका कन्दके आकारका जिसमें बहुत छिद्रहों और ऐसे जलको ढकने सहित अगारकोष्ठको बनवावे ४५

तञ्च खादिराणामाशवकर्णादीनां वाकाष्ठानांपूरियत्वाप्रदीपयेत् । सयदाजानीयात्साधुदग्धानिका ष्ठानिगतधूमानिअवतप्तञ्च केवलम् भिनातदिग्गृहंस्वेदयोग्येनचोष्म णायुक्तिमिति ॥ ४६ ॥

उसमें खैर बच अश्वकर्ण आदि पवित्र काष्ठोंको भरकर अग्नि लगादे जब उसको ऐसा जानले कि काष्ठ भली प्रकार जल चुके और धूम नहीं रहा वह अग्निका घर केवल अग्निसे तप्त है और स्वेदके योग्य उष्णसे युक्त है ॥४६॥

तत्रैनंपुरुषंवातहराभ्यक्तगात्रंवस्त्रा वच्छन्नंप्रवेशयेत्यवेशयंश्चैनमनुशि

ष्यात् । सौम्यप्रिवेशकल्याणायारोग्यायचेति । प्रविश्यचैनांपिण्डिकामिघरुह्यपाश्वींपरपाश्वों ष्यांयथासुखंशयीथाःनचतवया स्वेदमूच्छोंपरीतेनापिसतापिण्डकैषाविमोक्तव्यात्माआप्राणोच्छासात् । भ्रश्यमानोह्यतःपिण्डकावकाशाद्वारमनिधगच्छ न्स्वेदमूच्छोंपरीततयासघःप्राणान्जह्याः ॥ ४७ ॥

तब उसमें इस पुरुषको वातहारी अभ्यंगको कराकर और वस्त्रोंसे ढककर प्रवेश करावे और प्रवेश कराता हुआ इसको यह शिक्षा दे कि हे सौम्य कल्याण और आरोग्यके लिये इस घरमें प्रवेश कर और प्रविष्ट होकर इस पिंडीपर बैठ कर सुखपूर्वक दोनों पाश्वोंमें शयनकर और स्वेदकी मूच्छों होनेपरभी प्राणोंके स्वास आने पर्यंत यह पिंडका न छोडना क्योंकि इस पिंडिकाके स्थानसे अष्ट हुआ यदि दूर पर न जायगा तो स्वेद की मूच्छासे युक्त होनेसे शीघही प्राणोंको त्याग देगा ॥ ४७ ॥

तस्मात्पिण्डकामेनांनकथञ्चन मुञ्चेथाःत्वंयदाजानीयाःविगता भिष्यन्दमात्मानंसम्यक्श्रुतस्वे दिपच्छंसर्वशोतोविमुक्तंलघुभूत

[Verse 45]
One should construct a round clay chamber (koshtha), shaped like a root-vessel (kandu), of a height and width of sixteen arm-lengths (hasta), with many small perforations, fitted with a cover for retaining heat, and finished smoothly on the inside. Within this sweat-house, on all four sides, a raised clay platform (pindi) of one arm-length height should be built, without doors, and in the center of this sweat-house a clay hollow furnace shaped like a bulb, with many perforations and a cover, should be constructed. [45]

[Verse 46]
This furnace should be filled with the woods of khadira (acacia), ashvakarna, and similar sacred trees, and then ignited. When one perceives that the wood has burned thoroughly, the smoke has cleared, and only the glowing embers remain — that the fire-chamber is now heated by pure heat alone and is fit for sweating therapy — [then proceed]. [46]

[Hindi commentary on 45-46:]
A round clay chamber of at most sixteen arm-lengths in height and breadth, fitted with a room having many ventilation openings, should be built. Inside this sweat-house, on all four sides, a clay platform of one arm-length height should be made, without doors. In the center of the sweat-house, a clay furnace shaped like a bulb, four arm-lengths in size, with many holes and a cover, should be constructed. [45]
Fill it with the sacred woods of khadira, vach, ashvakarna, and so forth, and light the fire. When one judges that the wood has burned properly, the smoke has gone, and the fire-house is heated by pure fire alone and is ready for sweating, then proceed. [46]

[Verse 47]
Then let this man, whose body has been anointed with oils that pacify the wind (vata), and who has been covered with cloth, enter the chamber. As he enters, instruct him thus: "O gentle one, enter this house for your well-being and for health. Having entered, mount this platform and lie down comfortably on both sides. Even if you feel faint from the sweating, do not leave this platform until your breath (prana) continues to come — for if one who has slipped from the platform goes even a short distance away from it, he will quickly lose his life from the faintness induced by the sweat." [47]

[Hindi commentary on 47:]
Then the man, having been given an oil massage with oils that pacify vata and having been covered with cloth, should be made to enter the chamber. As he enters, he should be instructed: "O gentle one, enter this house for your well-being and health. Having entered, sit on this platform and lie comfortably on both sides. Even if you become faint from the sweating, do not leave this platform as long as your breath continues — because if one who has fallen from the platform goes even a little distance away, he will quickly lose his life from the faintness caused by the sweat." [47]

[Verse 48, beginning:]
Therefore, do not leave this platform under any circumstances. When you perceive that the discharge has ceased, that you feel well-sweated throughout your body, free from all obstructions, and feeling light...

तोदकमुपस्पृशेथाः । अपगतस
न्तापक्रमस्तुमुहूर्तात्सुखोष्णेनवा
रिणायथान्यायंपरिषिक्तोऽश्रीया
इतिजेन्ताकस्वेदः ॥ ४८ ॥

तिससे इस पिंडिकाको कदाचित् न
छोडिये और जब तू अपने देहको ऐसा
जाने कि स्वेद नहींहै और स्वेदका जल
झर चुके किसी स्रोतमें नरहै और देह
लघु होजाय और विबंध स्तंभ सुति
वेदना गौरव ये नष्ट होजांय फिर उस
पिंडिकाका अनुसरण करताहुआ द्वारमें
प्राप्त होजाइयो और निकस कर चक्षु-
ओंकी रक्षाके लिये शीघ्रही शीतल जल
का स्पर्श न करियो और जब संतापका
खेद दूर होजाय तब मुहूर्तके अनंतर
सुखोष्ण जलसे यथा योग्य सेचन करके
स्नान करियो यह जेंताकस्वेदहै ॥ ४८ ॥

शयानस्यप्रमाणनघनामश्मयीं
शिलाम् । तापियत्वामारुतैर्वैदि
रिभिःसंप्रदीपितैः ॥ ४९ ॥

प्रमाणसे शयन करते हुये मनुष्यको
पत्थरकी घनशिला को वात नाशक जलते
हुये काष्ठोंसे तैयारकर ॥ ४९ ॥

व्यपोह्यसवानिङ्गारान्प्रोक्ष्यचै

वोष्णवारिणा।तांशिलामथकुवीं
तकैःषयाविकसंस्तराम् ॥ ५० ॥

सब अंगोंको छोडकर उष्ण जलसे
छिडककर उस शिला पर रेशम ऊनका
विस्तरकरके ॥ ५० ॥

तस्यांस्वभ्यक्तसर्वाङ्गःशयानः
स्वियतेसुखम् । रौरवाजिनकौ
षेयभावाराचैस्मुसंवृतः ॥ ५१ ॥

उस पर सब अंगोंमें अभ्यंग करके
शयन करे तो सुखसे स्वेदको प्राप्त
होताहै और उस समय रुरुमृगका चर्म
रेशम भावार इनसे आच्छादित रहै ५१॥

इत्युक्तोऽश्मघनस्वेदःकर्षूंस्वेदःअ
वक्ष्यते । खानयेच्छयनस्याधः
कर्षूंस्थानविभागिवित् ॥ ५२ ॥

यह अश्म घन स्वेदकहा अब कर्षू
स्वेदको कहते हैं कि स्थानके विभागका
ज्ञाता शयन करते हुयेके नीचे कर्षू(गढा)
खुदवावे ॥ ५२ ॥

दीतैर्धूमैरङ्गारैस्तांकर्षूंपूरयेत्ततः।
तस्यामुपरिशय्यायांस्वपनूस्विव
धितनासुखम् ॥ ५३ ॥

जलतेहुये निर्धूम अंगारोंसे उस
कर्षूको भरदे उसके ऊपर शय्यापर
सोताहुआ मनुष्य सुखसे स्वेदको प्राप्त
होताहै ॥ ५३ ॥

अनत्युत्सेधविस्तारांवृताकारा

translation:
( 124 )

FROM THE CHARAKA SAMHITA

[Continuing the description of Jentaka Sveda — steam therapy using a heated chamber:]

When the binding, stiffness, tingling, pain, and heaviness have all disappeared, follow the attendant out through the door. Once outside, do not immediately expose the eyes to cold water — protect them carefully. After the heat-distress has subsided, wait a moment, then bathe by pouring comfortably warm water over the body as appropriate. This is the Jentaka Sveda. ॥ 48 ॥

[Verse 49:] Have a dense stone slab, proportioned to fit the lying person, heated by ignited wind-dispelling (vata-destroying) logs.

[Commentary on verse 49:] Prepare a dense stone slab proportioned to accommodate a reclining person, heating it with burning wood that destroys wind (vata). ॥ 49 ॥

[Verse 50:] After removing all the embers and sprinkling the slab with warm water, spread upon it a covering of silk and wool.

[Commentary:] After clearing away the coals and sprinkling the stone with hot water, spread silk and woolen fabric over it. ॥ 50 ॥

[Verse 51:] The person, having been fully anointed with oil on all limbs, lies down on it and comfortably attains perspiration, while being covered with the hide of the ruru deer, silk, and other coverings.

[Commentary:] After anointing all the limbs with oil, the person lies down and comfortably sweats, remaining covered with the hide of the ruru deer, silk fabric, and similar coverings. ॥ 51 ॥

[Verse 52:] This concludes the Ashmaghana Sveda (stone-slab sudation). Now the Karshu Sveda is described. One who knows the proper division of locations should have a pit (karshu) dug beneath the place where the patient will lie.

[Commentary:] This was the Ashmaghana Sveda. Now describing the Karshu Sveda: an expert in spatial positioning should have a pit dug beneath the patient's resting place. ॥ 52 ॥

[Verse 53:] Fill that pit with smokeless, burning coals. Then, on a bed placed above it, the patient lies down and comfortably attains perspiration.

[Commentary:] Fill the pit with glowing, smokeless embers; the person lying on a bed placed above this pit comfortably attains perspiration. ॥ 53 ॥

[The verse continues:] The pit should be of moderate depth and width, circular in shape —

text:
मन्त्रस्थानम् ।
( १२५ )
Digitized By Siddhamal Gangotri Gyaan Kosha

मलोचनाम् । घनिभिर्तिकुटीञ्च
त्वाकुष्ठायैःसम्प्रलेपयेत् ॥ ५४ ॥
और जिसका अत्यंत ऊंचा विस्तार
नहो गोल आकारहो जिसमें झरोखा नहो
जिसकी भित्ति सघन हो ऐसी कुटी बना-
कर त्रिकुटाआदिसे लेपन करा दे ५४

कुटीमध्येिषक्शय्यांसवातीणि
ञ्चोपकल्पयेत् । प्रावाराजिन
कौषेयकुत्थकम्बलगोलकैः ५५॥
और कुटीके मध्यमें सुंदर बिछौना
जिसका ऐसी शय्याको बिछादें जो शय्या
प्रावार मृगछाला रेशमीवस्त्र कुत्थकंबल
गोलक इनसे युक्तहो ॥ ५५ ॥

हसन्तिकाभिरङ्गारपूर्णिभिस्ता
ञ्चसर्वशः । परिवार्य्यान्तरारोहे
दभ्यक्तःस्वयतेसुखम् ॥ ५६ ॥
और शय्याके चारों तरफ अंगारोंसे
पूर्ण अँगीठी रखदे अभ्यंग करके उस
शय्यापर स्थित मनुष्य सुख स्वेदको
प्राप्त होताहै ॥ ५६ ॥

यएवाश्मघनस्वेदाविधिभूमौसएवतु ।
प्रशस्तायांनिवातायांसमायासुप
दिश्यते ॥ ५७ ॥
जो अश्म घन स्वेदकी विधिहै वही
स्वेदकी विधि प्रशस्त और पवन रहित
समान भूमिमें कहतेहैं ॥ ५७ ॥

कुम्भींवातहरकाथपूणांभूमौनिखा
तयेत् । अर्द्धभागंत्रिभागंवाशय
नंतञ्चोपरि ॥ ५८ ॥

वातके नाशके द्रव्योंक काथसे पूर्ण
कुंभीको भूमिमें गाडदे उसके ऊपर अर्द्ध
भाग वा त्रिभागपर शय्याको स्थापन
कर दे ॥ ५८ ॥

स्थापयेदासनंवापिनातिसान्द्रप
रिच्छदम् । अथकुम्भ्यांसुसन्त
मान्प्रक्षिपेदयसोगुडाञ् ॥ ५९ ॥
वा ऐसा आसन रखदे जिसका बिछौना
अत्यंत गीला न हो फिर कुंभीमें भली
प्रकार तपाकर लोहा और गुडको पत्य-
रोंको डालदे ॥ ५९ ॥

पाषाणान्वोष्मणातेनतत्स्थःस्व
यतिनासुखम् । सुसंवृताङ्गःस्व
यङ्गःञेहैरनिलनाशनैः ॥ ६० ॥
उस शय्यापर स्थित मनुष्य सुखसे
स्वेदको प्राप्त होताहै और वह मनुष्य
वातनाशक स्नेहोंसे अभ्यंग करै और
अंगोंको भलीप्रकार ढककर बैठे ॥ ६०॥

कूपंशयनविस्तारंद्विगुणञ्चापिवे
धतः । देशेनिवातेशरतेचकुर्य्या
दन्तःसुमार्जितम् ॥ ६१ ॥
शय्याके विस्तारका वा वेधसे द्विगुण
कूप वातरहित सुंदर देशमें भीतरसे
मार्जन सहित बनवावै ॥ ६१ ॥

हस्त्यश्वगोखरोष्ट्राणांकरीषैर्दग्ध
पूरितें । स्ववच्छन्नःससंस्तीर्णेि
भ्यक्तःस्वयतिनासुखम् ॥ ६२॥
हाथी अश्व गौ खर ऊंट इनके जले

translation:
(Chapter on Therapeutic Procedures, page 125)

Verse 54:
One should apply a paste of the drugs including Trikuta (three pungents) and Kushtha (Saussurea lappa) to a hut that is not excessively tall, not circular in shape, has no windows, and whose walls are thick. Such a hut should be thus prepared and plastered. (54)

Verse 55:
In the middle of the hut, a fine bed should be arranged. The bed should be furnished with coverings made of a Pravara (a type of woolen wrap), deer skin, silk cloth, Kuttha (a coarse fabric), blankets, and rounded cushions. (55)

Verse 56:
The bed should be surrounded on all sides with braziers full of glowing coals. After performing an oil massage (abhyanga), the patient lying on that bed comfortably attains sudation (therapeutic sweating). (56)

Verse 57:
The same method that is prescribed for the Ashma-ghana (stone-block) sudation applies equally when performed on level ground that is protected from wind, in a suitable location. (57)

Verse 58:
A pot (kumbhi) filled with a decoction of vata-dispelling herbs should be buried in the ground. The patient's bed should then be placed over it, covering either half or two-thirds of the pot above ground level. (58)

Verse 59:
Alternatively, a seat may be placed there whose covering is not excessively wet. Then, pieces of iron and lumps of jaggery, well-heated, should be dropped into the pot along with stones. (59)

Verse 60:
The person seated on that bed then comfortably attains perspiration from the steam rising from those heated stones. The patient should anoint the body with oils that dispel vata, and should sit with the limbs well covered. (60)

Verse 61:
A pit should be dug in a sheltered, wind-free, pleasant location, with a diameter twice the width of the bed, and its interior should be well cleaned and smoothed. (61)

Verse 62:
The pit should be filled and heated with the dried dung of elephant, horse, cow, donkey, and camel. The patient, well-covered and lying on a properly spread bed, comfortably attains perspiration. (62, continues)

text:
( १२६ )

इुये करीषोंसे पूर्ण कूपमें भली प्रकार
बिछोना करके गात्रोंको वस्त्रोंसे ढककर
अभ्यंग करनेसे मनुष्य सुखसे स्वेदको
प्राप्त होताहै ॥ ६२ ॥

धीतिकान्तुकरीषाणांयथोक्तानां
प्रदीपयेत् । शयनान्तःभ्रमाणेन
शय्यामुपरितत्रच ॥ ६३ ॥

पूर्वोक्त करीषोंको धीतिका ( हेरी )
को शय्याके भीतर ले प्रमाणसे जलावे
वह जब भली प्रकार जलजाय और
विधूम होजाय तब उसके ऊपर शय्या-
को बिछावे ॥ ६३ ॥

सुदग्धायांविधूमायांयथोक्तामुप
कल्पयेत् । स्ववच्छन्नःस्वपंस्त
त्राभ्यक्तःस्वयितनासुखम् ६४ ॥

भली प्रकार गात्रको ढककर अभ्यंग
करके उस शय्यापर सोताहुआ मनुष्य
सुखसे स्वेदको प्राप्त होता है ॥ ६४ ॥

होलाकस्वेदइत्येषसुखःभोकोमह
षिणेति । इतित्रयोदशविधःस्वे
दोऽग्निगुणसंश्रयः ॥ ६५ ॥

यह सुखदायी होलाकस्वेद मह-
षिणे कहाहै यह अग्निके गुणोंके आश्रयसे
तेरह प्रकारका स्वेद है ॥ ६५ ॥

व्यायामउष्णसदनंगुरुभावरणंक्षु
धा । बहुपानंभयक्रोधातुपनाहा
हवातपाः ॥ ६६ ॥

और व्यायाम उष्ण स्थान भारी
प्रावरण क्षुधा अधिकपान भय क्रोध
उपनाह संग्राम आतप ॥ ६६ ॥

स्वेदयन्तिदशैतानिनरमग्निगुणाढ
ते । इत्युक्तोद्विविधःस्वेदःसंयुक्तो
ऽग्निगुणैनंच ॥ ६७ ॥

ये दश अग्निगुणोंके बिनाभी मनु-
ष्यको स्वेदसे युक्त करते हैं अग्निके
गुणोंसे युक्त और अयुक्त यह दो प्रका-
रका स्वेद कहा ॥ ६७ ॥

एकाङ्गसर्वाङ्गतःस्निग्धोरूक्षस्त
थैवच । इत्येतत्त्रिविधंद्वंद्वस्वे
दमुद्दिश्यकीतितम् ॥ ६८ ॥

एक अंगमें वा सर्वांगमें स्निग्ध और
रूक्ष यह दो प्रकारका द्वंद्व स्वेदका
कहाहै ॥ ६८ ॥

स्निग्धःस्वेदैरुपक्रम्यःस्निग्नःप
थ्याशनोभवेत् । तदहःस्विन्नगा
त्रस्तुव्यायामंवर्जयेन्नरइति ॥ ६९ ।

स्निग्ध स्वेदोंसे युक्त होकर स्विन्न
मनुष्य पथ्य भोजन करके सुखी होताहै
स्वेदको प्राप्त हुआ मनुष्य उसदिन
व्यायामको वर्ज दे इति ॥ ६९ ॥

तत्र श्लोकाः ।

स्वेदोयथाकार्यकरोहितोयेभ्यश्च
यद्विधः । यत्रदेशेयथायोग्योदेशो
रक्ष्यश्चयोयथा ॥ ७० ॥
translation:
(Page 126)

By filling a pit with dried cow-dung and properly spreading a bed in it, covering the limbs with cloth, and then performing oil massage, a person comfortably attains perspiration. (62)

One should kindle the dried cow-dung and the wick (heri) as prescribed. The bed is then placed above it, inside the sleeping space. (63)

The prescribed cow-dung is placed inside the bed-chamber as instructed, lit with a wick (heri) in the proper measure; when it is well-burned and smokeless, the bed should be spread over it. (63)

Covering the body well and performing oil massage, the person lies on that bed and comfortably attains perspiration. (64)

This comfortable fomentation known as Holaka-sveda is described by the great sages. Thus, the thirteen types of fomentation based on the properties of fire have been enumerated. (65)

Exercise, hot place, heavy covering, hunger, excessive drinking, fear, anger, tight bandaging, battle, and exposure to sun — (66)

These ten induce perspiration in a person even without the properties of fire. Thus, fomentation has been described as of two kinds: that which is combined with properties of fire, and that which is not. (67)

Applied to one limb or to the whole body, with oleation or without oleation — this dual (dvandva) form of fomentation has been described in three ways. (68)

A person who has received oleation should be treated with unctuous fomentation; after sweating, the person should eat wholesome food and become comfortable. On that day, the person who has undergone fomentation should abstain from exercise. (69)

Now the summary verses:

Fomentation is beneficial when administered appropriately — its type, the region where it is applied, and which region is to be protected — (70)

text:
Digitized By Siddh Gyaan Kosha ( १२७ )

उसमें ये श्लोकहैं जैसे स्वेद कार्य-
कारी होताहै जिनसे और जैसा हितहै
जिस देशमें जैसा योग्य है जो देश जैसे
रक्षाके योग्यहै ॥ ७० ॥

स्विन्नातिस्विन्नरूपाणितथातिस्वि
न्नभेषजम्। अस्वेद्याःस्वेदयोग्या
श्चस्वेद्द्रव्याणिकल्पना ॥ ७१ ॥

स्विन्न अतिस्विन्नकेरूप और अति
स्विन्नकी औषध स्वेदके अयोग्य और
स्वेद योग्य स्वेदके द्रव्योंकी कल्पना॥७१

त्रयोदशविधःस्वेदोविनादशविधो
ऽग्निना । संग्रहेणचषट्स्वेदाःस्वे
दाध्यायेनिदिशिताः ॥ ७२ ॥

और संग्रहसे तेरह प्रकारके स्वेद-
और अग्निके विना दश प्रकारका स्वेद
और संग्रहसे छःप्रकारका स्वेद स्वेदा-
ध्यायमें दिखायेहैं ॥ ७२ ॥

स्वेदाधिकारेयद्वाच्यमुक्तमेतन्म
हर्षिणा । शिष्यैस्तुप्रतिपत्तव्यमु
पदेष्टापुनर्वसुरिति ॥ ७३ ॥

अग्नीत्यादि ॥ स्वेदाध्यायःसमाप्तः ।

ये सब स्वेदाधिकारमें कहने योग्य-
महर्षि ने कहेहैं और शिष्योंको जानने

translation:
( 128 )
From the Charaka Samhita.

When a calamity becomes manifest, even the buying and selling of medicines becomes difficult, and the timely stockpiling (collection) of medicines as appropriate is not easy. Saying this, Agnivesha spoke to Bhagavan Atreya: [Verse 1]

"O Bhagavan, should not a knowledgeable physician from the very beginning make arrangements in such a way that the medicine is certain to succeed when applied exclusively? For the accomplishment of all actions depends on proper application, and failure too arises from improper application. Whether one undertakes an action properly or improperly, success or failure follows as a rule — because without correct understanding, knowledge becomes equal to ignorance." [Verse 2]

The meaning: O Bhagavan, a learned physician should conduct treatment in such a way that the medicine will certainly succeed, because the accomplishment of all actions through proper application is desirable, and disease (mishap) arises from improper application. An action begun properly or improperly will by rule reach success or failure respectively, for knowledge without proper practice becomes equal to ignorance. [Verse 2 — commentary]

Then Bhagavan Atreya replied to him: "It is indeed possible for us, or for others equal to us, O Agnivesha, to make such arrangements that the medicine succeeds with certainty through proper application — and there is no one here who can adequately teach the excellence of that application, nor anyone capable of grasping and retaining what has been taught regarding this medicine in this manner." [Verse 3]

"Or, having heard and grasped it, one should apply it again accordingly. For the subtle distinctions of place, medicine, season, strength, body, diet, wholesomeness, mind, constitution, and age are very fine indeed." [Verse 4]

The meaning: After hearing and understanding, one is empowered to know and to apply — because the varying states of dosha (humor), medicine, place, time, strength, body, diet, wholesomeness, mind, constitution, and age are extremely subtle. [Verse 4 — commentary]

"These matters, even when carefully contemplated, are capable of confusing the intellect of a pure and highly intelligent person — how much more so the intellect of one of limited understanding?" [Verse 5]

The meaning: These things, even upon reflection, confuse the mind of a person of clear and great intelligence — how then would they not confuse the mind of one of lesser intelligence? [Verse 5 — commentary]

तस्मादुभयमेतद्यथावदुपदेक्ष्यामः । सम्यक्प्रयोगश्चौषधानां व्यापञानाञ्चव्यापत्साधनानिसिद्धिषूत्तरकालम् । इदानींतावत् संभारान्विविधानिपसमासेनोपदेक्ष्यामः ॥ ६ ॥ तथथा ॥

तिससे इन दोनोंका यथार्थ उपदेश करेंगे और औषधोंके भली प्रकार प्रयोगकों और व्यापनोंकी व्यापत्तिके साधनोंको सिद्धियोंको उत्तरकालमें कहेंगे अब तो प्रथम अनेक प्रकारके संभारोंको संक्षेपसे कहतेहैं ॥ ६ ॥

दढंनिवातंप्रवातैकदेशंसुखभिवचारमनुपत्यकंधूमातपरजसामनभिगमनीयमनिष्टानाञ्शब्दस्पर्शरसरूपगन्धानांसोपानोदूखलमुसलवर्चःस्थानस्नानभूमिमहानसोपेतंवास्तुविद्याकुशलःअशस्तंग्रहमेवतावत्पूर्वमुपकल्पयेत् ॥ ७॥

वे ऐसेहैं कि–दृढ बात रहित प्रबातका एकदेश मुखसे विचरने योग्य पर्वतके समीप न हो धूम आतप रज ये जिसमें न जाते हों और अनिष्ट शब्द स्पर्श रस रूप गंध जिसमें नहों–जिसमें सोपान( सीढी) ऊंचा ऊखल मुसल मलस्थान स्नान भूमि महानस ये सब होंय वास्तु विद्यामें कुशल मनुष्य प्रथम श्रेष्ठ गृहकीही सिद्धि करै ॥ ७ ॥

ततःशीलशौचाचारातुरागदाक्ष्यप्रादक्षिण्योपपञानुपचारकुशलान्सर्वकर्मसुपर्यवदातान्सूपौदनपाचकस्नापकसंवाहकोत्थापकसंवेशकौषधपेषकांश्चपरिचारकान्सर्वकर्मस्वप्रतिकूलान्तथागीतवादित्रोझापकश्लोकगाथाख्यायिकेतिहासपुराणकुशलानभिभाषणानुमतांश्चदेशकालविदःपरिषद्यांश्च । तथालावकपिञ्जल शशहिरणेणकालपुच्छकमृगमातृकोरभान् ॥ ८ ॥

फिर शील शौच आचार–अनुराग चतुरता–श्रेष्ठता इनसे युक्त सब कुशल कर्मोंमें शुद्ध; द्विदला ओदनके पाचक स्नापक संवाहक उत्थापक संवेशक अर्थात् न्हाने उठाने दबाने और सुलाने वाले और औषधियोंके पीसनेवाले सब कर्मोंमें अनुकूल सेवकोंको और गीत वादित्र उझापक श्लोक गाथा आख्यायिका इतिहास पुराण इनमें कुशल अभिभाषायके जाननेवाले और अनुमत देश कालके ज्ञाता सभासदोंको और लाव कपिञ्जल शश हिरण एण कालपुच्छ मृग मातृक उरभ इनको ॥ ८ ॥

Therefore we shall explain both of these properly. The correct use of medicines and the means for overcoming failures in treatment shall be described later, after achieving success. For now, we shall briefly describe the various requisite materials. (Verse 6)

From this, we will give proper instruction on both these matters — on the proper use of medicines and on the means of overcoming complications — and we will describe the methods of attaining success later. But first, let us briefly describe the many kinds of necessary preparations. (6)

The expert in the science of architecture (vastu-vidya) should first prepare a superior dwelling that is sturdy, sheltered from wind, situated in a pleasant locality, not near a mountain cleft, free from smoke, harsh sunlight and dust, free from unwanted sounds, touch, taste, sight and smells, and equipped with a staircase, mortar and pestle, a place for excretion, a bathing area, and a kitchen. (7)

Such a dwelling is: one that is sturdy, free from drafts, situated in a pleasant part away from mountainsides through which one may move freely, where smoke, sunlight and dust do not enter, where there are no unpleasant sounds, touches, tastes, sights or smells, and which has steps (stairs), mortar, pestle, a lavatory, a bathing area, and a kitchen. One skilled in the science of architecture should first accomplish the finest of dwellings. (7)

Then he should arrange attendants who are endowed with good conduct, cleanliness, proper behavior, devotion, skill, dexterity, and proficiency in all services — cooks of dal and rice, those who bathe the patient, those who massage him, those who help him rise, those who help him to bed, those who grind medicines — all servants amenable to every duty; and also those skilled in songs, music, recitation of verses, narratives, history and the Puranas, who know the appropriate speech, and who are knowledgeable about time and place, and are fit for an assembly. Also: lava-birds, partridges, rabbits, deer, black-tailed deer and sheep. (8)

[The verse at the bottom of the page begins:] Those Gandharva-women, the virtuous, the non-afflicted, the living, those provided with proper grass-shelters and water...

(Page 130 — Charaka Samhita)

[Verse 9 — Sanskrit portion:]
The vessels for rinsing the mouth and drinking water; pitchers, bowls, pots, jars, large and small water-pots, ladles, dishes for cooking and churning; leather goods, threads, cotton items, and the like; seats and couches — all these should be properly arranged. Spreads, coverlets, and pillows fit for sleeping should be provided. The therapeutic procedures of oleation (sneha), sudation (sveda), massage (abhyanga), anointing (pradeha), affusion (parisheka), application of pastes (anulepana), emesis (vamana), purgation (virechana), retention enema (anuvasana), head-evacuation (shiro-virechana), and urethral treatment (mutrocchara) — all the implements for these should be at hand, well-washed, smooth, of middle hardness, and numbering six. The fumigation tube (dhumannetra), the enema tube (basti-netra), the urethral tube (uttarabasti-netra), the kusha-grass bundle, the balance and weights, ghee, oil, fat, marrow, honey, treacle (phanita), salt, fuel, water, mead (sidhu), wine (sura), barley-water, rice-water (tushodaka), maireya, medaka, curds, whey of curds, takra, sour gruel, and urine — all these should be kept ready. ॥9॥

[Hindi commentary on verse 9:]
A cow that gives milk, is gentle, free from disease, whose calf is living — such a tawny-colored cow whose three points (teats, etc.) are good, and water — should be provided; along with vessels: the achamani cup, water-pot, storage jar, gem-pot, pitcher, cauldron, large pot, small pot, bowl, ladle, churning vessel, leather goods, cloth, thread, cotton, and so forth; and couches and seats arranged so as to include materials for adornment, with fine spreads, coverlets, and pillows fit for lying upon. For the treatments of oleation, sudation, massage, anointment, affusion, emesis, purgation, retention enema, head-evacuation, and urethral procedures — the articles required should be clean, smooth, and of moderate firmness. Conch-shells, fumigation pipes, enema nozzles, urethral nozzles, kusha-grass, balance-pans and weights, ghee, oil, fat, marrow, honey, treacle, salt, fuel, water, mead, wine, barley-water, maireya, medaka, curds, whey, buttermilk, sour gruel, and urine — all these. ॥9॥

[Verse 10 — Sanskrit portion:]
Similarly, shali rice, shashtika rice, mudga beans, masha beans, barley, yava grain, kulattha pulse, badara fruit, mridvika (grape), kashmari, parushaka, abhaya (haritaki), amalaki, vibhitaka — and various other materials for oleation and sudation therapies; substances that are laxative, digestive, carminative, pacifying for vata, and named as medicines — as well as whatever else is relevant to any condition, all these accessories should be enumerated and kept. Whatever is required for comfort and enjoyment of the patient, that too should be arranged. ॥10॥

translation:
(Page 131, Sutrasthana)

And in the same way: rice (Santhi variety), mung bean, daddu (a grain), barley, kulthi (horse gram), sesame, ber (jujube), munakka (raisins), asmari (gravel-dissolving herbs), aparusha (phalsa fruit), harade (haritaki), baheda (bibhitaki), amla — these, along with various kinds of oleating (sneha) and sudation (sveda) substances, and likewise emetic, laxative, and dual-acting (both upper and lower) — appetizing, digestive, pacifying, and vata-alleviating medicines as described — and whatever else is known to be useful against any incidental complication, and whatever is needed for the patient's comfort — all of this should be gathered together. (Verse 10)

Then the physician should administer to that person the oleation and sudation treatments as prescribed in the authoritative texts. If during this period any severe mental or physical illness suddenly arises, one should first make every effort to relieve that illness; having cured it, one should then treat the patient with the same procedures for the same duration as before. Then, having seen that the patient is free from mental illness, has slept comfortably, has digested his food well, has bathed his head, has anointed his body, is wearing a garland and clothed in fresh garments — one who is a devotee of the gods, fire, the twice-born (brahmins), the teacher, elders, and the physician — at an auspicious constellation, lunar day, karana, and muhurta (auspicious moment), after having brahmins perform the svastivachana (benedictory rite) and after the drink has been consecrated with their blessings — combined with honey, madhuka (licorice), saindhava (rock salt), and phanita (raw sugar) — one should administer the prescribed dose of the decoction of madana fruit (emetic nut). (Verse 11)

The measure of the dose of the madana fruit decoction, as well as the measures of all the purificatory (samshodhana) preparations, must be determined individually for each person. The administered purificatory dose is considered appropriate when it effectively removes the pathological doshas. (Verse 12)

( १३२ )

होतेहैं जिसको जितना संशोधन पीया हुआ विकारके दोष नाशार्थ योग्यहो १२॥

नचातियोगायोगायतावदस्यमात्राप्रमाणविदितव्यंभवति ॥ १ ३॥

और अतियोग और अयोगके लिये इसको मात्राका प्रमाण जानने योग्य नहींहैं ॥ १३॥

पीतवन्तन्तुखल्वेनंमुहूर्तमनुकांक्षेत् । तस्ययदाजानीयात्स्वेदशादुर्भिवेणदोषप्रविलयनमापद्यमानं लोमहर्षेणचस्थानेभ्यःप्रचलितं कुक्षिसमधमानेनचकुक्षिमनुगतं हछासास्यश्रवणाभ्यामपिचतोछ्ईमुखीभूतमथास्मैजानुसममसम्बाधंसुप्रयुक्तास्तरणोत्तरप्रच्छदोपधानंस्वापाश्रयमासनमुपवेष्टुंभयच्छेत् ॥ १४ ॥

पीनेके अनंतर इसकी मुहूर्तमात्र प्रतीक्षा करैं जिस समय स्वेदके पैदा होनेसे दोषोंके नाशको हुआ जानैं और स्वेद रोमोंके हर्षसे स्थानोंमें प्रचलित और कुक्षिके सम्यक् आध्मानसे कुक्षिमें प्राप्त हछास (हृत्पीडा) मुखका स्रवण इनसे अपिचत ऊर्ध्वमुख बैठे हुयेको फिर जानु समान करावै और बाधासे रहित आस्तरण आच्छादन उपधान इनको अच्छी तरह लगाकर शयनके आसनको बैठनेके लिये दे ॥ १४ ॥

प्रतिग्रहांशोपचारयेत् । ललाट प्रतिग्रहेपाश्वेपिग्रहणेनाभिमपीडनेपृष्ठोन्मर्दनेचअभ्युपकमनीयाः सुहृदोऽनुमताःप्रवतेरन् । अथैनमनुशिष्यात् । विवृतोष्ठतालुकण्ठो नातिमहत्वाभ्यायमेनवेगानुदीर्णिनुदीरयन्किञ्चिदवनम्यशीवामूर्च्छशरीरमुपवेगमप्रवृतान्प्रवर्त्यनसुपिलिखितनखाभ्यामङ्गुलीभ्यामुत्पलकुमुदसौगन्धिकनालैर्वाकएठमनिभिस्पृशन्सुखंप्रवर्त्तयस्वेति ॥ १५ ॥

और अतिमहोंसे उपचार (सेवा) करावै मस्तकके पकडने पाश्वोंके ग्रहण करने नाभीके पीडनमें पृष्ठके उन्मईनमें ऐसे मित्रोंको यत्नमें लगावै जो वहांसे पृथक् न हों और अनुमत हों–फिर इसको यह शिक्षा दे कि ओष्ठ तालु कंठ इनको न ढकना और अत्यंतमहान् व्यायामसे ऊपरकी वेगोंको न बढाइयो–किंचित् ग्रीवाको नवाकर ऊर्ध्व शरीरकी तरफ वेगको न प्राप्त हुयी रखियो–सुंदर लिखितहैं नख जिनके ऐसी अंगुलीयोंसे और उत्पल कुमुद सौगंधिक इनकी नालोंसे कंठका स्पर्श न करियो–इस प्रकार सुखसे वतांव करियो ॥ १५ ॥

सतथाविधंकुभ्यिचतोऽस्यवेगान्प्रतिग्रहगतानवेक्षेतावहितःवेग

[Verse 12:] The purificatory dose given to a patient is appropriate for eliminating the disorders of that patient proportionally.

[Verse 13:] Neither excess nor deficiency of dose can be understood without knowing the proper measure; thus the exact quantity cannot be determined without this knowledge.

[Verse 14:] After the patient has drunk the medicine, one should wait for approximately one muhurta (about 48 minutes). When one recognizes that the dosha-elimination has begun through the following signs — sweating, horripilation spreading from its sites, proper distension of the abdomen, feeling in the abdomen, palpitation of the heart, salivation of the mouth — then the patient, who has been seated upright, should be made to sit with knees level, and should be provided with a well-arranged seat fitted with mattress, covering, and pillow, comfortable for reclining, free from any obstruction.

[Verse 15:] One should attend to the patient by supporting the head, holding the sides, pressing the navel region, and massaging the back. For this purpose, trusted friends who are approved and who will not leave the patient's side should be engaged. Then one should instruct the patient thus: "Do not cover the lips, palate, and throat; do not intensify the upward urges through excessive exertion; bend the neck slightly and do not allow the force to travel upward toward the body; and do not touch the throat with fingers whose nails are well-trimmed, nor with the stalks of utpala, kumuda, and saugandhika lotuses — proceed gently and comfortably."

[Beginning of next verse:] One who is attentive should observe the upward urges of such a patient as they occur...

translation:
(Page 133)

[Verse 16]
By recognizing the special characteristics of vega (urges/impulses), the physician skilled in yoga (proper administration), ayoga (under-administration), and atiyoga (over-administration) should observe the vegas carefully. One who is the observer of the special characteristics of vega understands the appropriate action to be taken through its signs. Therefore, having become alert, one should observe the vegas. (16)

[Verse 17]
In cases of atiyoga and ayoga, the distinguishing signs are recognized as follows: when there is withdrawal from some source, or when there is merely a displacement of the medicament, or when the vegas become bound — these are the signs of yoga (proper effect). (17)

[Prose commentary on verse 17]
There, the distinguishing signs of extreme atiyoga and ayoga are such that in some cases there may be withdrawal, or there may only be displacement of the medicine and binding of the vegas — these are the signs of yoga. (17)

[Verse 18]
The signs of proper yoga (right therapeutic action) are: timely movement, appropriate reduction of the doshas, and maintenance of one's own equilibrium. By yoga, one should recognize the distinction of sharp, mild, and moderate according to the measure of the dosha. By excess of yoga (atiyoga), the signs are: frothiness, appearance of blood with reddish tinge. These complications arising from atiyoga and ayoga should be understood: bloating (adhmanа), discharge, obstruction of the heart, weakness of the limbs, loss of vitality, displacement, rigidity, and progressive complications. (18)

[Prose commentary on verse 18]
At the proper time, extreme great movement should not occur — that is, one should perform moderate treatment, removing the doshas appropriately and maintaining equilibrium. These are the signs of proper yoga. Through yoga, distinguishing the sharp, mild, and moderate according to the measure of the dosha — and by excess of yoga: frothiness and reddish appearance are signs of atiyoga. In atiyoga arising from such causes, one should recognize these complications: bloating, discharge, obstruction of the heart, weakness of the limbs, loss of life-force, displacement, rigidity — these are the complications. (18)

[Verse 19]
Having carefully examined the patient being treated, with hands, feet, and face well washed, one should comfort the patient for a moment, then administer one of the pacifying fumigations (dhumas) from among those of the purgative class, according to capacity, make the patient drink water again, and have him touch water. Having sprinkled the patient with water, one should lead him into a windless room, have him lie down, and then instruct him accordingly. (19)

translation:
( 134 )
From the Charaka Samhita

And having seen this emaciated person through yogic means, wash his hands, feet, and face thoroughly, give him confidence for a moment, and then, according to his strength, administer one of the oleation-purgation-pacifying smoke inhalations, and again have him touch water. After he has touched water, bring him into a draught-free place, have him lie down, and then give this instruction: [Verse 19]

Speaking very loudly, sitting for too long, standing for too long, walking excessively, anger, grief, cold, heat, dew (fog/frost), excessive wandering — traveling in a vehicle, sexual intercourse, not sleeping at night, sleeping in the day — and incompatible, undigested, unsuitable, untimely, unpleasant, too little, too heavy, irregular food — and suppressing or forcing bodily urges — all these things one should not even mentally engage with, and while abstaining from all of these, one should take all meals in the prescribed manner. Let him do it accordingly. [Verse 20]

Loud speech, excessive sitting, excessive standing, excessive walking, anger, grief, cold, heat, dew, excessive wind, traveling in a vehicle, sexual intercourse, not sleeping at night, sleeping in the day, and incompatible, indigestible, unsuitable, untimely, unpleasant, too little, too heavy, irregular food — suppressing or forcing urges — all these things he should not indulge in even mentally, and consuming all foods accordingly — let him do exactly that. [Verse 20]

Then, in the evening or the following day, after sprinkling him with comfortably warm water, cook the old red shali rice well, and beginning with the liquid gruel (manda), give him warm yavagu (rice gruel) to drink, judging his digestive strength. In the same manner, in the second, third, and fourth time-periods, give the same kind of shali rice preparation as thin gruel (vilepī) with warm water, in the second session without fat or salt, or with mild salt to eat. Similarly, at the fifth and sixth time-periods, and at the seventh time-period in the same prescribed manner, give him well-roasted and well-cooked shali rice, with warm water as a drink, with diluted fat and mild salt, and with mudga (green gram) soup. In the eighth and ninth time-periods in the same way, and at the tenth time-period, feed him with the meat-broth of one of the following — lāvaka (partridge), piñjala, and others — made with water and a little salt, with substance added. Warm water as a drink — in this same manner, at the eleventh and twelfth time-periods as well. [Verse 21]

After this, in the evening or on the following day, sprinkle him with comfortably warm water, and from the old red shali rice, cooking it well, beginning with the liquid extract (maṇḍa), give him warm yavagu (rice gruel) to drink, observing his digestive strength, and likewise in the second and third [periods]...

text:
सूत्रस्थानम् ।
( १३५ )
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

अन्नकालमें पिछलेै चौथे अन्नकालमें तो वैसेही शालितंडुलोंकी मांड उतारी विलेपीको उष्णजल समेत और जिसमें स्नेह लवण न हों वा उसको भोजन करावे–इसी प्रकार पांचमें छठे अन्नकालमें करावे–सातमें तो. अन्नकालमें वैसेही शालियोंको दो प्रसृति मांड निकासे ओदनको उष्ण जलके अनुपानसे और अल्प जिसमें स्नेह लवण हों ऐसे अल्प मूंगके यूषके संग भोजन करावे ऐसेही आठमें नवमें कालमें करावे–दशमें अन्नकालमें तो लाव कपिंजल आदिमेंसे किसी एकके मांसरसके संग वा उदक लवण जो उत्तम हैं उनके साथ पूर्वोक्त भोजन करावे उष्ण जलके अनुपानको दे–ऐसेही एकादश द्वादश अन्नकालमें करावे ॥ २१ ॥

अतऊर्ध्वं मन्नगुणानुक्रमेणोपभुञानिससमरात्रेणपकृतिभोजनमागच्छेत् ॥ २२ ॥

इसके अनंतर सात रात्रतक क्रमसे अन्न गुणोंको भोजन करें तो प्रकृतिके भोजनपर आजायगा ॥ २२ ॥

अथैनंपुनरेवस्नेहस्वेदाभ्यामुपवाहानुपहतमनसमभिसामीक्ष्यसुखोषितंसुप्रजीर्णभक्तंकृतहोमवंलिमङ्गलजप्यप्रायश्चित्तिमष्टितिथिनक्षत्रकरणमुहूर्तेंब्राह्मणाचर्वस्तिवाचयित्वात्रिवृतकल्कमक्ष

मात्रांयथाहारलोडमभितिवनितिंपाययेत् ॥ २३ ॥

इसके अनंतर फिर इसको स्नेह स्वेद कराकर अनुवहन गमनमें समर्थ देखकर सुखसे वास भली प्रकार भोजनके पाककों देखकर होम बलि मंगल जप प्रायश्चित इनके करनेके अनंतर इष्ट तिथि नक्षत्र करण मुहूर्तमें ब्राह्मणोंसे स्वस्ति वाचन कराकर निसोथके चूर्णकी अक्षमात्राको यथायोग्य शुद्ध लोहसार सहित नम्रतासे पान करावे ॥ २३ ॥

प्रसमीक्ष्यदोषभेषजदेशकालबलशरीराहारासात्म्यसत्वप्रकृतिवयसामवस्थान्तराणिविकारांश्चस्म्यक्विरेक्त्सैनंवमनोनेकनधूमवजेंनिविधनोपापदयेदाबलवर्णमतिलाभात् ॥ २४ ॥

और दोष भेषज देश काल बल शरीर आहार असात्म्य सत्व प्रकृति वय ( आयुः ) इनकी अन्य अवस्थाओंको भलीप्रकार विकारोंको देखकर और भलीप्रकार विरेचन कराये इसको वमनमें कहे हुये धूम विजेंत विधिसे चिक्त्सा तबतक करे जबतक बल वर्ण पूर्वके समान आवें ॥ २४ ॥

बलवर्णोपप्रचैनंमनुपहतमनसमभिंसमीक्ष्यसुखोषितंसुप्रजीर्णभक्तंशिरःस्नातमनुलिप्तगात्रंश्रि
