translation:
( 184 )
From the Charaka Samhita

And that same properly applied sleep brings happiness to the body and improves one's condition in the way that buddhi-yoga (the discipline of wisdom) brings a person to perfection through union with the self. || 38 ||

Those who are exhausted by singing, study, women, carrying loads, and travel; those suffering from indigestion, those who are injured, those who are emaciated, the aged, the young, and the weak. || 39 ||

A person worn out by singing, study, intoxicating drinks, women's company, burdens, and travel — such a one who is indigestion-afflicted, wounded, emaciated, old, young, or feeble. || 39 ||

Those afflicted with thirst, diarrhea, colic, hemorrhoids, and dyspnea; those with abdominal pain, the emaciated, the fallen, those who have been struck, the insane, those exhausted by travel, and those who have been kept awake. || 40 ||

Those suffering from thirst, diarrhea, and colic; those with respiratory and abdominal disorders; the emaciated, the fallen, the injured, and the insane — those exhausted by travel and by wakefulness. || 40 ||

And those overcome by anger, grief, fear, and delusion, who are weakened by fatigue, and those accustomed to sleeping during the day — all these persons may sleep during the day at all times. || 41 ||

Through the equilibrium of the bodily elements (dhatus), strength arises in them. Kapha (phlegm) is nourished, and thereby stability and longevity are attained. || 42 ||

When those who consume dry foods have increased vata (wind), when kapha is stable, and when the nights are very short — at such a time, daytime sleep is recommended. || 43 ||

In seasons other than summer, daytime sleep causes kapha and pitta to become aggravated; therefore in those seasons daytime sleep is not commendable. || 44 ||

The obese, those who habitually use oily substances, those with excess phlegm, those suffering from phlegmatic disorders, those afflicted by dushivisha (a kind of slow poison), and those suffering from poisoning — these should never sleep during the day. || 45 ||

Halimaka (a type of jaundice/liver disorder), headache, heaviness and stiffness of the limbs, body aches, destruction of the digestive fire, and a feeling of coating over the heart — || 46 ||

Halimaka, headache, heaviness of the limbs, body ache, destruction of the digestive fire, and a coating of the heart. || 46 ||

सूत्रस्थानम्।
( १८५ )

शोथारोचकहड्डासपीनसार्द्विभेदकाः । कोठाश्विपडकाःकण्डूस्तन्द्राकासोगलामयाः॥ ४७॥

शोफ अरोचक हछास पीनस अर्द्विभेदक कोठाक पिड़क कंडू तंद्रा कास गलेके रोग ॥ ४७ ॥

स्मृतिबुद्धिप्रमोहाश्वसंरोधःश्वोत सांज्वरः । इन्द्रियाणामसामर्थ्यं विषवेगप्रवर्तनम् ॥ ४८ ॥

स्मृति और बुद्धिका प्रमोह–श्वोतोंका संरोध ज्वर–इंद्रियोंका असामर्थ्य विषके वेगकी प्रवृति ॥ ४८ ॥

भवेत्रृणांदिवास्वपमस्याहितस्यनिषेवणात् । तस्माच्छिताहितंस्वमं बुद्धयास्वप्यात्सुखंबुधः॥४९॥

ये सब मनुष्योंको अहितकारी दिवा स्वप्नके करनेसे होते हैं तिससे बुद्धिमान मनुष्य हित अहित स्वप्नको जानकर शयन करे ॥ ४९ ॥

रात्रौजागरणंरूक्षंस्निग्धमस्वपनं दिवा । अरूक्षमनिभिष्यन्दत्वासीनप्रचलायितम् ॥ ५० ॥

रात्रिमें जागरण दिनमेंन सोना रूक्ष भोजन स्निग्ध भोजन और बैठना और अति चलना अरूक्ष और अनभिष्यन्दी भोजन ॥ ५० ॥

देहवृत्तौयथाहारःतथास्वमःसुखो

मतः । स्वमाहारसमुत्येचस्थौल्यकाश्येविशेषतः ॥ ५१ ॥

देहकी वृत्तिमें यथायोग्य आहार और संक्षेपसे स्वप्न करे क्योंकि स्थूलता और कृशता विशेषकर स्वप्न और आहारसे होते हैं ॥ ५१ ॥

अभ्यञ्गोत्सादनंस्नानंग्राम्यानूपौदकरसाः । शाल्यचंसदिघक्षीरं स्नेहोमघमनःसुखम् ॥ ५२ ॥

अभ्यंग आच्छादन स्नान ग्रामके अनूप ( सजल देशके ) जल और रस दधिसहित चावल दूध स्नेह मदिरा मनका सुख ॥ ५२ ॥

मनसोऽनुगुणागन्धाःशब्दाःसंवाहनानिच । चक्षुषस्तर्पणंलेपःशिरसोवदनस्यच ॥ ५३ ॥

मनके अनुकूल गंध और शब्द और यान चक्षुका तर्पण शिर और मुखका लेप ॥ ५३ ॥

स्वास्तीर्णंशयनंवेश्मसुखंकालेरतोचितः । आनयन्तिचिराच्चिद्राप्नष्टायानिमित्ततः ॥ ५४ ॥

सुंदर बिछौनेकी शय्या समय २ में यथायोग्य घरका सुख ये सब शीघ्रही निमित्तसे नष्ट हुई निद्राको ले आतेहैं॥५४

कायस्यिशरसश्चैविरेकश्छर्दनंभयम् । चिन्ताकोधस्तथाधूमो व्यायामो रक्तमोक्षणम् ॥ ५५ ॥

translation:
Page 185 — Sutrasthana (Chapter on General Principles)

Verse 47:
Edema, loss of appetite, hiccups, nasal congestion, splitting pains, skin eruptions, wheals, itching, stupor, cough, and diseases of the throat — these are the disorders [caused by improper sleep].

Verse 48:
Loss of memory and intellect, obstruction of breathing, fever, weakness of the sense organs, and the aggravation of the effects of poison — these too result [from improper sleep habits].

Verse 49:
All these conditions arise in people through the practice of daytime sleep that is harmful to them. Therefore, a wise person, having discerned which sleep is beneficial and which is harmful, should rest accordingly.

Verse 50:
Keeping awake at night, not sleeping during the day, consuming dry food, consuming unctuous food, sitting idly, walking excessively, eating food that is neither too dry nor causing excess moisture — [these affect sleep and health].

Verse 51 (continued from bottom of left column):
According to the condition of the body, sleep should correspond to diet, and one should sleep in moderation, because obesity and emaciation arise especially from sleep and diet.

Verse 52:
Oil massage, rubbing and kneading the body, bathing, the waters and broths of marshy and aquatic regions, rice with curd, milk, unctuous substances, wine, and mental happiness —

Verse 53:
Fragrances pleasing to the mind, agreeable sounds, massage of the body, soothing of the eyes, application of pastes to the head and face —

Verse 54:
A well-spread comfortable bed, a pleasant dwelling, enjoyment appropriate to the time — all these things quickly restore sleep that has been lost for any reason.

Verse 55:
Purgation of the body and head, emesis, fear, anxiety, anger, smoking (medicated fumigation), exercise, and bloodletting —

( १८६ )
Digitized By अरकसंहितायाम् Jaan Kosha

देह और शिरका विरेचन छर्दें भय
चिंता क्रोध धूम व्यायाम रक्तमो
क्षण ॥ ५५ ॥

उपवासःसुखाशय्यासत्वौदाग्यंत
मोजयः । निद्राप्रसङ्कमिहतंवार
यन्तिसमुत्थितम् ॥ ५६ ॥

उपवास सुखकी शय्या सत्वगुणकी
वृद्धि तमोगुणका जय ये सब अहित-
कारी आते हुये निद्राके प्रसंगको वारण
कर देते हैं ॥ ५६ ॥

एतएवचविज्ञेयानिद्रानाशस्यहेत
वः । कार्येकालोविकारश्चप्रकृ
तिर्वायुरेवच ॥ ५७ ॥

येही निद्राके नाशके हेतु जानना—
कि कृशता कालके विकार प्रकृति
और वायु ॥ ५७ ॥

तमोभवाश्लेष्मसमुद्भवाचमनःश
रीरश्रमसम्भवाच । आगन्तुकी
व्याध्यनुवर्तिनीचरात्रिस्वभावप्र
भवाचिन्द्रा ॥ ५८ ॥

तमो गुणसे उत्पन्न कफसे उत्पन्न—
मन शरीर श्रम इनसे उत्पन्न—आगंतुकी
व्याधिकी अनुवर्तिनी—रात्रिके प्रभावसे
उत्पन्न इतने प्रकारकी निद्रा होतीहै ५८

रात्रिस्वभावप्रभवामतायातांभू
तधात्रींप्रवदन्तिनिद्राम् । तमो
भवामाहुरघस्यमूलंशेषंपुनव्याधि
षुनिर्दिशन्ति ॥ ५९ ॥

जो रात्रिके प्रभावसे उत्पन्न निद्राहै
उस निद्राको भूत धात्री कहतेहैं तमसे
उत्पन्न निद्रापापका मूलहै शेष निद्रा-
ओंको व्याधियोंमें कहतेहैं—इति ॥५९॥

तत्र श्लोकाः ।

निन्दिताःपुरुषास्तेषांयौविशेषेण
निन्दितौ । वक्ष्यामिकारणंदोषा
स्तयोनिंन्दितभेषजम् ॥ ६० ॥

उसमें ये श्लोकहैं कि जो पुरुष निंदि-
तहैं उनमें ये दो विशेषकर निंदितहैं—
उनका कारण कहूंगा उनके दोष--निन्दि-
तोंकी औषध ॥ ६० ॥

येभ्योयदाहितानिद्रायेभ्यश्चाप्य
हितायदा । अतिनिद्रानिद्रयोश्च
भेषजंयद्वाचसा ॥ ६१ ॥

जिनको जब, निद्राहितहै और जिनको
जब अहित अतिनिद्रा और अनिद्राकी
औषध—निद्रा जिससे होतीहै ॥ ६१ ॥

यायायथाप्रभावाचनिद्रातत्सर्वे
मत्रिजः । अष्टौनिनिन्दितसंख्याते
व्याजहारपुनर्वसुः ॥ ६२ ॥

इति योजनाचतुष्केअष्टौनिन्दितायो
नाम एकविंशोअध्यायः ।

जो २ और जैसे उत्पन्न और प्रभा-
वकी निद्राहै उस सबको अत्रिज भगवान्
पुनर्वसु अष्टौ निर्मित नामके अध्यायमें
वर्णन करते भये ॥ ६२ ॥

इति योजनाचतुष्के अष्टौनिन्दितयोअध्यायः ॥ २१॥

translation:
( 186 )

[Verse 55] Purgation of the body and head, vomiting, fear, anxiety, anger, smoke, exercise, and blood-letting — these are the causes [of sleep disturbance].

[Verse 56] Fasting, a comfortable bed, the increase of the sattva quality, and the conquest of the tamo quality — all these, being inimical, ward off the occasion of sleep when it arises. (56)

[Verse 57] These very things should be understood as the causes of the destruction of sleep: emaciation, the derangements of time, the nature of the individual, and wind (vata). (57)

[Verse 58] Sleep arises from tamas, from the increase of kapha (phlegm), from fatigue of the mind and body, from an incidental disease, from following the nature of night — sleep arises in these many ways. (58)

[Verse 59] The sleep that arises from the natural influence of night — that sleep is called "Bhuta-dhatri" (the nurse of living beings). The sleep born of tamas is said to be the root of sin; the remaining types of sleep are described in relation to diseases. (59)

Now the verses (shlokas) on this topic:

[Verse 60] Among persons who are to be blamed (condemned), two are especially to be blamed. I will state the reasons for them, their faults, and the remedies for those who are condemned. (60)

[Verse 61] For whom sleep is beneficial and when, and for whom it is harmful, and when — and the remedy for excessive sleep and sleeplessness — that by which sleep is produced. (61)

[Verse 62] Whatever sleep there is, arising from whatever cause and influence — all of that Punarvasu, son of Atri (the divine sage), has declared to be eightfold, enumerated as the eight condemned ones. (62)

Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, called "The Eight Condemned," in the group of four sections known as Yojana-chatushka.

text:
Digitized By Sūtrasthānam Jyotri Gyaan Kosha ( १८७ )

द्वाविंशोऽध्यायः ।
अथातोलंघनबृंहणीयमध्यायं
व्याख्यास्यामः

इसके अनंतर लङ्घन बृंहणीय अध्या-
यको कहते हैं–

तपःस्वाध्यायनिरतानात्रेयःशिष्य
सत्तमान् । षडिमेवश्यमुखानुक्
वान्परिचोदयन् ॥ १ ॥

कि तप और स्वाध्यायमें तत्पर-प्रधान
हैं अग्निवेश जिनमें ऐसे उत्तम शिष्योंको
अत्रिके पुत्र पुनर्वसु प्रेरते हुए कहते
भये ॥ १ ॥

लंघनंबृंहणंकालेरूक्षणंस्नेहनंत
था । स्वेदनंस्तम्भनंचैवजानीते
यःसवैभिषक् ॥ २ ॥

कि समयपर लंघन और बृंहण
रूक्षण और स्नेहन-स्वेदन और स्तंभन
इनको जो जानता है वही वैद्य है ॥ २ ॥

इतितमेवमुक्तवन्तंभगवन्तमात्रेय
मग्निवेशउवाच । भगवंल्लंघनंकि
स्वलंघनीयाश्चकीदशाः । बृंहणं
बृंहणीयाश्चरूक्षणीयाश्चरूक्षणम्३

इस प्रकार कहते हुए भगवान्
आत्रेयको अग्निवेश बोले कि हे भगवन्
लंघन किसको कहते हैं और लंघनके
योग्य कौनहैं और बृंहण क्याहै बृंहणके
योग्य कौन हैं रूक्षण और रूक्षणके
योग्य कौन हैं ॥ ३ ॥

स्नेहनंस्नेहनीयाश्चस्वेदाःस्वेद्याश्च
केमता । स्तम्भनंस्तम्भनीयाश्च
वक्तुमर्हसितद्गुरो ॥ ४ ॥

स्नेहन और स्नेहनके योग्य-स्वेद और
स्वेदके योग्य स्तंभन और स्तंभनके
योग्य कौनहैं इन सबको हे गुरो हमारे
प्रति वर्णन करो ॥ ४ ॥

लंघनप्रभृतीनांश्चषण्णामेषांसमास
तः । कृताकृतातिवृत्तानांलक्षणं
वक्तुमर्हसि ॥ ५ ॥

और लंघन आदि इन छःओंकाकृत
अकृत-और अतिवृत्तोंका लक्षण हमारे
प्रति आप कहनेके योग्य हो ॥ ५ ॥

गुरुरुवाच ।

यत्किञ्चिल्लाघवकरंदेहेतल्लङ्घनं
स्मृतम् । बृंहत्वंयच्छरीरस्यज
नयेत्तच्बृंहणम् ॥ ६ ॥

गुरु बोले कि-जो देहमें किंचित्
लाघव करे उसे लंघन कहते हैं और
जो शरीरकी वृद्धिको करे उसे बृंहण
कहते हैं ॥ ६ ॥

रौक्ष्यंस्वरत्वंवैषयंयत्कुर्यात्तद्वि
रूक्षणम् । स्नेहनंस्नेहिःस्यन्दमा
द्वक्लेदकारकम् ॥ ७ ॥

और जो रूक्षता खरता वैषघ (फुटना)
इनको करे–उसे रूक्षण कहतेहैं जो-स्नेह
निष्यन्द–मार्दव–क्लेदनको करे–उसे–
स्नेहन कहतेहैं ॥ ७ ॥

translation:
Chapter Twenty-Two

Now we shall explain the chapter on Langhana (lightening/reduction therapy) and Brinhana (nourishing/building therapy).

After this, the chapter on Langhana and Brinhana is presented:

[Verse 1] Atreya, ever devoted to austerity and self-study, urged his foremost disciples with these words. (1)

That is to say: Agnivesha and the other excellent disciples of Punarvasu, son of Atri, who were foremost in devotion to austerity and self-study, were urged by their teacher as follows. (1)

[Verse 2] One who knows in proper time and context: Langhana (lightening), Brinhana (nourishing), Rukshana (drying), Snehana (oleation), Svedana (fomentation), and Stambhana (astringency/checking) — that person alone is a true physician. (2)

That is: the one who knows, at the right time, Langhana and Brinhana, Rukshana and Snehana, Svedana and Stambhana — that person is a true physician. (2)

When the venerable Atreya had spoken thus, Agnivesha said: "O Lord, what is Langhana, and who are the proper candidates for Langhana? What is Brinhana, and who are the candidates for Brinhana? What is Rukshana, and who are the candidates for Rukshana?" (3)

[Verse 4] "What is Snehana, who are the candidates for Snehana, what are Sveda (sudation therapies), who are candidates for Sveda, and what is Stambhana, who are its candidates — O Teacher, please explain all of this to us." (4)

[Verse 5] "And please explain briefly the characteristics of these six — beginning with Langhana — when properly performed, incompletely performed, and when excessively performed." (5)

The Teacher spoke:

[Verse 6] "Whatever produces lightness in the body is known as Langhana. And whatever promotes increase and growth of the body is called Brinhana." (6)

The teacher said: that which produces lightness in the body is called Langhana; that which promotes the growth of the body is called Brinhana. (6)

[Verse 7] "That which produces dryness, roughness, and fissuring is Rukshana. That which causes oleation, fluidity, softness, and moistening through unctuous substances is Snehana." (7)

That which brings about dryness, roughness, and cracking is called Rukshana; that which brings about unctuousness, flowing quality, softness, and moisture is called Snehana. (7)

( १८८ )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।
Digitized By Sidhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

स्तम्भगौरवशीतघ्नस्वेदनंस्वेदकारकम् । स्तम्भनंस्तम्भयतियद्र
तिमन्तंचलंध्रुवम् ॥ ८ ॥
जो—स्तम्भ—गौरव-शीत-इनके नाशको
और स्वेदको करै उसे—स्वेदन कहतेंहैं—
जो गतिमान्का स्तम्भन—और चलको
ध्रुव करै उसे स्तंभन कहतेंहैं ॥ ८ ॥
लघ्वुष्णतीक्षणविषदंरूक्षंसूक्ष्मखं
रंसरम् । किठनञ्चैवयद्द्रव्यंप्राय
स्तल्ङ्घनंस्मृतम् ॥ ९ ॥
जो द्रव्य, लघु, उष्ण, तीक्षण, विषद
रूक्ष, सूक्ष्म, खर, सर, और किठन हो
वहभी प्रायःलंघनहीं कहाहै ॥ ९ ॥
गुरुशीतमृदुस्निग्धंबहुलंसूक्ष्मपि
च्छिलम् । प्रायोमन्दंस्थिरंसू
क्षमंद्रव्यंबृंहणमुच्यते ॥ १० ॥
गुरु, शीत, मृदु, स्निग्ध, बहुल, सूक्ष्म
पिच्छिल, मन्द, स्थिर, सूक्ष्म, जो द्रव्य
प्रायः हों उसेभी बृंहण कहतेंहैं ॥१०॥
रूक्षंलघुखरंतीक्षणमुष्णंस्थिरम
पिच्छिलम् । प्रायशःकिठनञ्चैव
यद्द्रव्यंताद्विरूक्षणम् ॥ ११ ॥
रूक्ष, लघु, खर, तीक्षण उष्ण, स्थिर
अपिच्छिल, और किठन जो हों, वह
द्रव्यभी प्रायःरूक्षण होताहै ॥ ११ ॥
द्रवंसूक्ष्मंसरंस्निग्धंपिच्छिलंगुरु
शीतलम् । प्रायोमन्दंमृदुचयद्द्र
व्यंतस्नेहनमतम् ॥ १२ ॥

द्रव, सूक्ष्म, सर, स्निग्ध, पिच्छिल,
गुरु, शीतल, मन्द, मृदु, जो द्रव्यहै
वहभी प्रायः स्नेहन होताहै ॥ १२ ॥
उष्णंतीक्षणंसरंस्निग्धंरूक्षंसूक्ष्मंद्र
वंस्थिरम् । द्रव्यंगुरुचयत्प्रायःत
द्विस्वेदनमुच्यते ॥ १३ ॥
उष्ण, तीक्षण, सर, स्निग्ध रूक्ष, सूक्ष्म
द्रव, स्थिर, और गुरु जो द्रव्यहैं उसेभी
प्रायःस्वेदन कहतेंहैं ॥ १३ ॥
शीतंमन्दंमृदुश्लक्षणरूक्षंसूक्ष्मंद्र
वंसरम् । यद्द्रवंलघुचोदिष्टंप्राय
स्तत्स्तम्भनंस्मृतम् ॥ १४ ॥
शीतल, मंद, मृदु,श्लक्ष्ण, रूक्ष, सूक्ष्म
द्रव, सर लघु जो द्रव्यहो उसको प्रायः
स्तंभन कहतेंहैं ॥ १४ ॥
चतुष्पकाराःसंशुद्धिःपिपासामारु
तातपौ । पाचनान्युपवासश्चव्या
यामश्चेतिलंघनम् ॥ १५ ॥
चार प्रकारकी संशुद्धि होतीहै पिपासा
मारुत आतप पाचन उपवास और
व्यायाम ये लंघनेहैं ॥ १५ ॥
प्रभूतश्लेष्मापित्तास्रमलाःसंदुष्टमा
रुताः । बृहच्छरीराबलिनोलंघ
नीयाविशुद्धिभिः ॥ १६ ॥
बढे हुएहैं कफ पित्त रुधिर मल
जिनके दुष्ट वातके स्पर्शसे बढाहै शरीर
जिनका और बलवान् हों तो विशो-
धनसे लंघन करने योग्यहैं ॥ १६ ॥

From the Charaka Samhita
Digitized By Sidhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

That which destroys stambha (immobility), heaviness, and cold, and which causes sweating, is called svedana (sudation); and that which stabilizes what is moving and makes the unsteady fixed is called stambhana (arresting). ॥ 8 ॥

That substance which is light, hot, sharp, clear, dry, fine, rough, and flowing, and also hard — that is generally called langhana (lightening/fasting therapy). ॥ 9 ॥

That substance which is heavy, cold, soft, unctuous, dense, minute, slimy, slow, stable — such a substance is generally called brimhana (nourishing/building therapy). ॥ 10 ॥

That substance which is dry, light, rough, sharp, hot, stable, non-slimy, and hard — such a substance is generally called rukshana (drying therapy). ॥ 11 ॥

That substance which is liquid, fine, flowing, unctuous, slimy, heavy, cool, slow, and soft — such a substance is generally considered snehana (oleation/unctuous therapy). ॥ 12 ॥

That substance which is hot, sharp, flowing, unctuous, dry, fine, liquid, stable, and heavy — such a substance is generally called svedana (sudation therapy). ॥ 13 ॥

That substance which is cold, slow, soft, smooth, dry, fine, liquid, flowing, and light — such a substance is generally known as stambhana (arresting therapy). ॥ 14 ॥

There are four kinds of purification: thirst, wind, heat of the sun, and digestive agents; and fasting and exercise — these constitute langhana (lightening therapies). ॥ 15 ॥

Those whose kapha (phlegm), pitta (bile), blood, and waste products are greatly increased, whose vata is corrupted by contact with these, and whose bodies are large and who are strong — such persons are suitable candidates for langhana through purificatory procedures. ॥ 16 ॥

सूत्रस्थानम् १।
( १८२ )
Digitized By Siddhantu Gangotri Gyaan Kosha

येषांमध्यबलारोगाःकफपित्तस
मुत्थिताः । वम्यतीसारहृद्रोगिव
सूच्यलसकज्वराः ॥ १७ ॥
और जिनके कफ, पित्तसे उठे हुए
रोग मध्यबलहैं और वमन अतीसार
हृद्रोग, विसूचि, अलसक, ज्वर ॥१७॥
विबन्धगौरवोद्रारहृछासारोचका
द्यः । पाचनैस्तान्भिषक्ज्ञः
प्रायेणादावुपाचरेत् ॥ १८ ॥
वीबन्ध, उद्रार, हृछास, अरुचि आादि
हों, उन सबको बुद्धिमान् वैद्य, प्रथम,
प्रायः पाचनोंसे चिकिसित करै ॥ १८॥
अतएवयथोदिृष्टायेषामल्पबला
गदाः । पिपासानिग्रहस्तेषामुपे
वासस्थातन्जयेत् ॥ १९ ॥
और येही पूर्वोक्त रोग जो अल्पबल
होंय तो उनको पिपासाके निग्रह और
उपवाससे जीतै ॥ १९ ॥
रोगान्जयेन्मध्यबलान्न्यायामातपमारुतैः । बलिनांकिंपुनयें
षांरोगाणामवरंबलमृ॥ २० ॥
मध्य बल, रोगोंको, व्यायाम, आतप
मारुतसे जीतै और बलवानोंको तो
जिन रोगोंमें छोटाभी बलवालोहै क्या
कथा है ॥ २० ॥
त्वग्दोषिणांप्रमीढानांस्निग्धाभि
ष्यन्दिद्वृंहिणाम् । शिशिरेलंघनं
शस्तमिपवातविकारिणाम् ॥ २१

त्वचाओंके दोषी प्रमीढ( स्रीमें अति
रमण) स्निग्ध अभिष्यंदी और बृंहणवान्
जन और वातके विकारी इनको शिशिर
अवस्थामें लंघन श्रेष्ठहै ॥ २१ ॥
अदिग्धविद्धमक्षिृष्टवयःस्थंसात्म्य
चारिणाम् । मृगमत्स्यविहङ्गा
नांमांसंसंबृंहणमुच्यते ॥ २२ ॥
अदिग्ध ( कुश ) विद्ध अक्षिष्ट और
वयस्थ ( नवीन ) जो सात्म्यचारी मृग
मत्स्य विहंगोंका मांस उसे बृंहण कहते
हैं ॥ २२ ॥
क्षीणाःक्षताःकशावृद्धादुर्बलानि
त्यमढ्वगाः । स्रीमयनित्याग्रीष्मे
चवृंहणीयानराःस्मृताः॥ २३ ॥
जो मनुष्य, क्षीण, क्षत, वृद्ध दुर्बल
नित्य मार्गगामी, नित्य स्रीभोगी हैं वे
ग्रीष्म ऋतुमें बृंहणके योग्य कहेंहैं २३
शोषाशोग्रहणिदोषैर्व्याधिभिःक
शिताश्चये । तेषांकव्यादमांसा
नांबृंहणालाघवोरसाः ॥ २४ ॥
शोक अर्श,मिहणी दोष, इन व्याधि-
योंसे जो कुशहैं, उनको मांसके भक्षकके
मांसके रसही बृंहण और लाघव कहेंहैं२४
स्नानमुत्सादनंस्त्रंमोमधुराःलेहव
रतयः शर्कराक्षीरसर्पोिषसवेंषां
विद्धिंबृंहणम् ॥ २५ ॥
और स्नान उत्सादन ( वर्द्धन ) मधुर

Verse 17: Those whose diseases arising from kapha and pitta are of moderate strength — vomiting, diarrhea, heart disease, visuchika (cholera-like illness), alasaka (intestinal torpor), and fever — these are of medium strength.
Commentary: Those whose diseases arising from kapha and pitta are of moderate strength, including vomiting, diarrhea, heart disease, visuchika, alasaka, and fever. (17)

Verse 18: Constipation, heaviness, belching, hiccup, anorexia and so forth — the wise physician should, as a general rule, first treat these with digestives.
Commentary: Where there is constipation, belching, hiccup, loss of appetite and such conditions, a wise physician should first treat them with digestives. (18)

Verse 19: And these very diseases described above, when they are of little strength, should be conquered by restraint of thirst and by fasting.
Commentary: These same previously mentioned diseases, if they are of little strength, should be overcome by restraining thirst and by fasting. (19)

Verse 20: Diseases of moderate strength should be conquered by exercise, sunlight, and wind. What then of those diseases of strong persons that are of even lesser strength?
Commentary: Diseases of moderate strength are overcome by exercise, sunlight, and wind. As for strong persons, diseases that have even little strength — what need be said of those? (20)

Verse 21: For those with skin disorders, those who are excessively given to sexual intercourse, those who use unctuous and nourishing foods, and those afflicted with wind disorders — fasting (langhana) in the winter season is best.
Commentary: For those with skin afflictions, those who are excessively given to sexual intercourse, those who use unctuous and nourishing substances, and those with wind disorders — fasting in the winter season is most appropriate. (21)

Verse 22: The flesh of deer, fish, and birds that are lean (not obese), unwounded, not emaciated, of prime age, and accustomed to their natural habitat — this is said to be nourishing (brinhana).
Commentary: Flesh of deer, fish, and birds that is lean (kusa), unwounded, not wasted, of proper age (youthful), and from creatures living in their natural habitat — such flesh is called brinhana (nourishing). (22)

Verse 23: Those who are emaciated, injured, aged, weak, habitual long-distance travelers, and those who indulge constantly in sexual pleasure — these people are considered suitable for nourishing (brinhana) therapy, especially in summer.
Commentary: Persons who are emaciated, wounded, aged, weak, those who travel constantly, and those who constantly indulge in sexual activity are considered fit for nourishing treatment, especially in the summer season. (23)

Verse 24: Those who are emaciated by consumption (shosa), hemorrhoids (arsha), sprue (grahani), and other disorders — for them, the broths of flesh-eating animals' meat serve as both nourishing and lightening agents.
Commentary: Those who are wasted by grief, hemorrhoids, sprue disorders, and such diseases — for them, the broths made from the meat of flesh-eating animals are said to be both nourishing and lightening. (24)

Verse 25: Bathing, massage (utsadana), sweet preparations for licking (leha), sugar, milk, ghee — know all of these to be nourishing (brinhana).
Commentary: Bathing, massage (enhancement of the body), sweet...

( १९० )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।
Digitized By Sidhanta & Gangotri Gyaan Kosha

स्नेह और बस्ति शर्करा घी दूध ये
सभके लिये बृंहण जानना ॥ २५ ॥

कटुतित्तकषायाणांसेवनंत्रीष्व
संयमः । खलीपिण्याकतक्राणां
मध्वादीनांचरूक्षणम् ॥ २६ ॥

और कटु तित्त कषाय इनका सेवन
त्रियोंमें अधिक प्रवृति खल पिण्याक
तक, मधु आदिका सेवन रूक्षण, कहा-
ताहै ॥ २६ ॥

अभिष्यन्दामहादोषाममर्स्थाव्या
धयथ्थये ।ऊरूस्तम्भभूतयोर्रूक्ष
णीयानिदर्शिताः ॥ २७ ॥

और अभिष्यंद जो महादोषहैं और
मर्मकी जो व्याधि ऊरुस्तम्भ आदिदेहें वे
रूक्षणके योग्य कहीहैं ॥ २७ ॥

स्नेहाःस्नेहियतव्याश्चस्वेदाःस्वेदया
श्चयेनराःस्नेहाध्यायेमयोकास्ते
स्वेदाध्येचसविस्तराः ॥ २८ ॥

स्नेह, स्नेहके योग्य स्वेद स्वेदके
योग्य जो नर हैं, वे मैं स्नेहाध्याय और
स्वेदाध्यायमें विस्तारसे कहेहैं ॥ २८ ॥

द्रवंतनुसरंशयावच्छीतौकरणमौष
धम् । स्वादुतित्तंकषायञ्चस्तम्भ
नंसर्वेमेवतत् ॥ २९ ॥

द्रव, तनु, सर, शीतकारी, औषध,और
स्वादु,तित्त कषाय ये सब स्तंभन कहा-
ताहै ॥ २९ ॥

पित्तक्षाराग्निदग्धायेवम्यतीसार
पीडिताः । विषस्वेदातियोगार्त्तिः
स्तम्भनीयास्तथापराः ॥ ३० ॥

जो पित्त क्षार अग्निसे दग्धहैं वमन
और अतिसारसे पीडितहैं विष और
स्वेदके अत्यन्त योगसे दुःखीहैं ऐसे नर

वातमूत्रपुरीषाणांविसर्गेणाचलाघ
वे । हृदयोद्वारकण्ठास्यशुद्धौत
न्द्राक्षमेगते ॥ ३१ ॥

और यहां लाघवमें, वात मूत्र, पुरी,
षका होना हृदय उद्वार, कण्ठ, मुख,
इनकी शुद्धि, और तन्द्राकी ह्रानिका
नाश ॥ ३१ ॥

स्वेदेजातिरुचौचैवक्षुतिपिपासासहो

translation:
( 190 )
From the Charaka Samhita

Verse 25: Sneha (oleation), basti (enema), sugar, ghee, and milk — all of these should be understood as nourishing (brimhana) therapies.

Verse 26: The use of pungent, bitter, and astringent substances should be restrained in the three cases. The use of oilcakes, buttermilk, honey, and the like is drying (rukshana). This is so stated.

Verse 27: For treating the great disorders arising from abhishyanda (excess moisture/secretion) and the diseases of vital points, and for conditions such as thigh-stiffness (urustambha), drying therapies have been indicated here.

Verse 28: The oleating substances, those fit for oleation, the sudation substances, and those fit for sudation — all of these persons I have described in detail in the chapter on oleation and the chapter on sudation.

Verse 29: That which is liquid, subtle, mobile, cooling, medicinal, and that which is sweet, bitter, and astringent — all of these together constitute stambhana (astringent/blocking) therapy.

Verse 30: Those who have been burned by bile, alkalis, or fire; those afflicted by vomiting and diarrhea; those suffering greatly from poison and excessive sweating — such persons are fit candidates for stambhana (styptic/astringent) therapy.

Verse 31: The signs of its success are: the proper passage of wind, urine, and feces; lightness of the body; purity of the heart, throat, and mouth; and the elimination of drowsiness.

Verse 32: Sweating, the arising of taste/appetite, increased hunger and thirst, and the absence of inner discomfort — these are the signs by which the physician recognizes that the prescribed fasting (langhana) has been properly accomplished.

Verse 33: Breaking pain in the joints, body ache, cough, dryness of mouth, loss of hunger, loss of appetite, thirst, and weakness in the ears and eyes — these are the signs indicating the need for langhana (fasting/lightening therapy).

मनसःसम्भमोऽभीक्ष्णमूर्ध्वंवायु
स्तमोहृदि। देहाग्निबलनाशश्चलं
घनेऽतिकृतेभवेत् ॥ ३४ ॥

मनमें वारंवार भ्रम, ऊर्ध्वगामीवायु,
हृदयमें तम, देह, और अग्निके बलका
नाश, ये सब अत्यंत लंघन करनेसे
होतेहैं ॥ ३४ ॥

बलंपुष्टिचुपलम्भश्चकाश्र्यंदोषिवव
जिंतम्। लक्षणंवृहितेस्थौल्यम
तिचात्यर्थवृहिते ॥ ३५ ॥

बल–और पुिष्टका लाभ, और दोषोंसे
रहित कृशता, ये बृंहणके लक्षणहैं और अ-
त्यन्त बृंहणका लक्षण अति स्थूलताहैं ३५

कृताकृतस्यिचह्नंयछिंघितेतच्छिरू
क्षिते। स्तिम्भितःस्याढलेलब्धेय
थोकैश्चामयैर्जितैः ॥ ३६ ॥

कृत और अकृत लंघनके जो चिन्हहैं
वेही रूक्षितके हैं स्तम्भन किया मनुष्य
बलके लाभसे यथोक्त रोगोंके जीतने
पर॥ ३६ ॥

श्यावतास्तब्धगात्रत्वमुद्वेगोहनुसं
ग्रहः। हृदचोनिग्रहश्चस्यादितस्त
म्भितलक्षणम् ॥ ३७ ॥

श्यामरंग ( कृष्ण ) गात्रका स्तंभन
उद्वेग हनुसंयह हृदय और मलका निग्रह
ये अतिस्तम्भितके लक्षणहैं ॥ ३७ ॥

लक्षणंचकृतानांस्यात्षण्णामेषांस

मासतः। तदौषधीनांव्याधीनाम
शमोवृिद्धिरेववा ॥ ३८ ॥

और नहीं किये हुए इन छःओंका
संक्षेपसे ये लक्षणहैं कि उनकी औषधि
होनेपर व्याधियोंकी अशान्ति और वृद्धि
होना ॥ ३८ ॥

इतिषट्सर्वरोगाणांमोक्काःसंय
गुपक्रमाः । साध्यानांसाधनेसि
द्धामात्राकालानुरोिघनइिति३९ ॥

सब रोगोंके ये उपक्रम जो साध्योंके
साधनमें सिद्ध मात्रा और कालके अनु-
रोधसे सिद्धहैं कहे इति ॥ ३९ ॥

भवति चात्र ।

दोषाणांबहुसंसर्गात्सङ्कीर्य्यन्ते
हुपक्रमाः। षट्त्वंतुनातिवर्चन्ते
चित्वंवातादयोयथा ॥ ४० ॥

इसमें ये श्लोकहैं कि–बहुत दोषोंके
संसर्गसे उप क्रमोंकाभी संक्रम होजातेहैं
परन्तु छः का अति वर्तन इसप्रकार
नहीं करते जैसे वात आदि तीनका
अवलंघन नहीं करते ॥ ४० ॥

द्रव्यिर्मिलुघनाध्यायेव्याख्याताः
षडुपक्रमाः । यथाप्रश्नंभगवता
चिकित्सायैःप्रवर्तिता ॥ ४१ ॥

इति योजनाचतुष्केलंघनबृंहणियो नाम
द्वाविंशोऽध्यायःसमाप्तः ।
translation:
Verse 34:
Repeated confusion of the mind, upward movement of wind (vata), darkness in the heart, and destruction of the body's digestive fire and strength — all these result from excessive fasting (langhana). || 34 ||

Verse 35:
Gain of strength and nourishment, and freedom from doshas along with leanness — these are the signs of proper brimhana (nourishing therapy); and extreme obesity is the sign of excessive brimhana. || 35 ||

Verse 36:
The signs of both performed and unperformed langhana are also those of rukshana (drying therapy). One who has received stambhana (styptic/arresting therapy) is recognized by the gain of strength and by the overcoming of the diseases as described. || 36 ||

Verse 37:
Darkening (blackish discoloration) and rigidity of the body, anxiety, constriction of the jaw, and suppression of the heart and of excretions — these are the signs of excessive stambhana. || 37 ||

Verse 38:
In brief, the signs of these six therapies when they have not been properly applied are: the non-pacification and increase of diseases even after medicines are given. || 38 ||

Verse 39:
Thus, these six upakramas (therapeutic procedures) for the liberation from all diseases are declared. They are proven effective for curable diseases when applied in proper dose and at the proper time. || 39 ||

Here also it is said:

Verse 40:
When multiple doshas are combined, the upakramas become mixed. Yet the six do not transgress their boundaries in the same way that vata and the other doshas do not overstep theirs. || 40 ||

Verse 41:
The six upakramas, as explained in the chapter on substances for langhana and brimhana, have been expounded by the revered teacher in answer to the questions, and are set forth for the purpose of treatment. || 41 ||

Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, named "The Fourfold Application of Langhana and Brimhana," in the Chikitsa-sthana.

चरकसंहितायाम् ।
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

ये छः उपक्रम–इस अध्यायमें भगवान्ने प्रश्के अनुसार वर्णन किये जिनसे चिकित्साकी प्रवृत्तिहै ॥ ४१ ॥

इति योजनाचतुष्के लंघन बृंहणीयोऽध्यायः समासः २२

त्रयोविंशोऽध्यायः ।

अथातः सन्तर्पणीयमध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः ।

इसके अनन्तर सन्तर्पणीय अध्यायका वर्णन करतेहैं ॥

सन्तर्पयितयः स्निग्धैर्मधुरैर्गुरुपिच्छलैः । नवान्नैर्नवमद्यैश्चमांसैश्चानूपवारिजैः ॥ १ ॥

जो मनुष्य, स्निग्ध, मधुर, गुरु, पिच्छल, नवीनअन्न और नवीन मदिरा और अनूप जलसे उत्पन्नमांस ॥ १ ॥

गोरसैर्गौडिकैश्चान्नैः पिष्टकैश्चाति मात्रशः । चेष्टाद्वेषीदिवास्वमश्य्यासनसुखेरतः ॥ २ ॥

इनसे अपनी आत्माको तृप्त करताहै और गोरस, गुडसहितअन्न, पाष्टिके पदार्थ, इनको अत्यंत सेवन करै है–चेष्टाका द्वेषी–दिनमें शयन और शय्या आसनके सुखमें रत जो है ॥ २ ॥

रोगास्तस्योपजायन्तेसन्तर्पणनिमित्तजाः । प्रमेहकण्डूपिडकाःकोठपाण्डूमयज्वराः ॥ ३ ॥

उस मनुष्यको संतर्पणके निमित्तसे ये रोग होते हैं कि प्रमेह कंडू पिडका कोठ पांडुरोग ज्वर ॥ ३ ॥

कुष्ठान्यामप्रदोषाश्चमूत्रकुच्छ्रं रोचकम् । तन्द्राक्लैब्यमितिस्थौल्यमालस्यंगुरुगात्रता ॥ ४ ॥

कुष्ठ और आमप्रदोष, मूत्रकुच्छ्र अरुचि, तंद्रा क्लैब्य, अतिस्थूलता, आलस्य, गुरुगात्र ॥ ४ ॥

इन्द्रियेश्रोतसांरोधोबुद्धेर्मोहःप्रमीलकः शोफाश्चैवंविधाश्चान्येशीघ्रमप्रतिकुर्वतः ॥ ५ ॥

इंद्रिय और श्रोतोंमें रोध बुद्धिकामोह, प्रमीलक, शोफ और इसी प्रकारके अन्य रोग उसके होतेहैं जो शीघ्र चिकित्सा नहीं करताहै ॥ ५ ॥

शस्तमुछेखनंतेषांविरेकोरक्तमोक्षणम् । व्यायामश्चोपवासश्चधूमाश्चस्वेदनानिच ॥ ६ ॥

उनके शस्त्रका उछेखन विरेचन रक्तमोक्षण व्यायाम उपवास धूम स्वेदन ॥ ६ ॥

सक्षौद्रश्चाभयामासः भायोरूक्षान्नसेवनम् । चूर्णप्रदेहायेचोक्काः कण्डूकोठिविनाशनाः ॥ ७ ॥

और शहत मिलाकर हरडेका भक्षण और प्रायः रूक्ष अन्नका सेवन करै और कंडू कोडके विनाशक जो चूर्ण प्रदेह कहे हैं ॥ ७ ॥

translation:
( 192 )
In the Charaka Samhita.
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

These six therapeutic measures were described in this chapter by the Lord in response to questions, from which the practice of treatment proceeds. || 41 ||

Thus ends the twenty-second chapter on Langhana (reduction therapy) in the group of four chapters on therapeutic management.

The Twenty-Third Chapter.

Now we shall explain the chapter on Santarpana (over-nourishment).

The following are the means of over-nourishment: unctuous, sweet, heavy, and slimy substances; new grain, new wine, and the meat of marshy and aquatic animals. || 1 ||

A person who satisfies himself with these — and with dairy products, jaggery-mixed foods, and flour-based preparations in excessive quantities — who is averse to physical activity, who sleeps during the day and is devoted to the comfort of bed and seat. || 2 ||

In such a person, diseases arising from over-nourishment occur: urinary disorders, itching, skin eruptions, urticaria, anemia, and fever. || 3 ||

Also skin diseases, disorders of undigested matter, difficulty in urination, loss of appetite, drowsiness, impotence, excessive obesity, laziness, and heaviness of the body. || 4 ||

Obstruction of the sense organs and channels, clouding of the intellect, drowsiness, and edema — these and other such diseases afflict one who does not treat them promptly. || 5 ||

Recommended treatments for these are: emesis, purgation, bloodletting, exercise, fasting, medicated smoking, and sudation. || 6 ||

Also, consuming haritaki (chebulic myrobalan) mixed with honey, regular use of rough/dry food, and powders and pastes declared to be destroyers of itching and skin eruptions. || 7 ||

text:

सूत्रस्थानम् ।
( १९३ )

त्रिफलारग्वधंपाठांसमपणसवत्सकमू । मुस्तनिम्बंसमदनंजलेनोत्किथतंपिबेत् ॥ ८ ॥

उनमें त्रिफला अमलतास पाठा सप्तपण वत्सक मोथा नीम मदन इनका जलमें काथ करके पीवै ॥ ८ ॥

तेनमोहादयोयान्तिनाशमभ्यस्य तांभ्रुवमू । मात्राकालप्रयुक्तेनसन्तर्पणसमुत्थिताः ॥ ९ ॥

उससे अभ्यासी मनुष्योंके मोह आदि वे अवश्य नष्ट होते हैं जो मात्रा और कालके प्रमाणसे संतर्पणसे हुये हैं ॥९॥

मुस्तमारग्वधःपाठात्रिफलादेवदारुच । श्वदंष्ट्राखदिरोनिम्बोहिरड्रात्वकूचवत्सकात् ॥ १० ॥

मोथा अमलतास पाठा त्रिफला देवदारु श्वदंष्ट्रा (गोखरू) खदिर नीम हिरड्रा त्वक् वत्सक (इंद्रजौ) ॥१०॥

रसमेषांयथादोषभातःप्रातःपिबेञ्चरः।सन्तर्पणकृतैःसर्वैर्व्याधिभिर्विप्रमुच्यते ॥ ११ ॥

इनके रसको दोषके अनुसार मनुष्य प्रातःकालके समय नित्य पीवै तो संतर्पणकी की हुई व्याधियोंसे विशेषकर छुट्टाहै ॥ ११ ॥

एभिश्चोद्वर्तनेनोद्र्षस्नानयोगोपयोजितैः । त्वग्दोषाःप्रशमयान्ति तथाक्लेहोपसंहितैः ॥ १२ ॥

इनके उबटने उद्धर्ष स्नान इनके स्नेहसहित उपयोगसे त्वचाके दोष शांत होते हैं ॥ १२ ॥

कुष्ठगोमेदकिहिङ्गुकौञ्चास्थित्र्यूषणवचामू । वृषकेलेश्वदंष्ट्रांचखराह्वाश्मभेदिकम् ॥ १३ ॥

कूट गोमेद हींग कौंचके अस्थि उषक (खारीनोन) वच तृष (बांसा) इलायची गोखरू खाराश्वा (मोरकी शिखा) पाषाणभेद ॥ १३ ॥

तक्रेणदधिमण्डेनबदरामलरसेनवा । मूत्रकृच्छ्रमेहश्वपीतमेतद्वयोहित ॥ १४ ॥

इनको मट्ठा दाधिका मंड बेर और अमलीके रससे पीवै तो मूत्रकृच्छ्र और प्रमेहको नष्ट करते हैं ॥ १४ ॥

तकाभयाप्रयोगैश्वत्रिफलायास्तथैवच । अरिष्टानांप्रयोगैश्वयान्तिमेहादयःशममू ॥ १५ ॥

मट्ठा और हरड़ेके प्रयोगसे और त्रिफलासे अरिष्ठा (कुटकी) के प्रयोगोंसे प्रमेह आदि शांतिको प्राप्त होते हैं ॥ १५ ॥

त्र्यूषणत्रिफलाक्षौद्रंकिमिञ्नसाज्मोदकम् । मन्थोऽयंसक्तवःम पिहितोलोहोदकाप्लुतः । ज्योष्विदङ्गंशयूणित्रिफलाकटुगोहिणी ॥ १६ ॥

Sutrasthana (Chapter on Fundamental Principles)

[Verse 8]
Triphala, Aragvadha (Cassia fistula), Patha, Sapta-parna, Vatsaka, Musta, Nimba (neem), and Madana — these should be boiled in water and the decoction drunk.

Among these: Triphala, Amaltas (Cassia fistula), Patha, Saptaparna, Vatsaka, Musta, Neem, Madana — boil all of these in water and drink the decoction. (8)

[Verse 9]
By this practice, conditions such as delusion and related disorders are destroyed — provided the preparation has been taken with proper dose and timing — and disorders arising from over-nourishment (santarpana) are eliminated.

By this practice, conditions such as delusion are certainly destroyed in regular users, provided the dose and timing are properly followed, for those disorders caused by over-nourishment. (9)

[Verse 10]
Musta, Aragvadha, Patha, Triphala, Devadaru, Shvadamshtra, Khadira, Nimba, Hiradhara, bark of Vatsaka (Indrayava) —

Musta, Amaltas, Patha, Triphala, Devadaru, Shvadamshtra (Gokhru), Khadira, Neem, Hirda, bark, Vatsaka (Indrajau). (10)

[Verse 11]
The juice of these, taken daily at dawn according to the predominant dosha, frees a person from all diseases arising from over-nourishment.

One who drinks the juice of these every morning, according to the dosha, will be freed — especially from diseases caused by over-nourishment. (11)

[Verse 12]
When used as an anointing paste (udvartana), as a scrub (udgharsana), as a bath preparation, or combined with fats (sneha), these same substances pacify disorders of the skin.

Used as a body scrub, as a rubbing application, in bathing, and combined with oils, these pacify skin diseases. (12)

[Verse 13]
Kushtha, Gomeda, Hingu (asafoetida), the bone of Kauncha, Ushaka (salt alkali), Vacha, Trisha (bamboo), cardamom, Gokhru, Kharashva (peacock's crest), Pashanabheda —

These are: Kut, Gomeda, asafoetida, Kauncha bone, Ushar (alkaline salt), Vacha, Trisha (bamboo), cardamom, Gokhru, Kharashva (peacock's crest), Pashanabheda. (13)

[Verse 14]
Taken with buttermilk, whey of curds, or the juice of jujube and tamarind, this combination destroys urinary obstruction (mutrakrcchhra) and urinary disorders (prameha), and is beneficial for the aged.

If these are taken with buttermilk, whey of curds, jujube, and tamarind juice, they destroy urinary obstruction and diabetes. (14)

[Verse 15]
Through the use of buttermilk and Haritaki (chebulic myrobalan), through Triphala likewise, and through the use of Arishta preparations, diabetes and related conditions are pacified.

By using buttermilk and Harad, and Triphala, and through the use of Arishtha (Kutki) preparations, diabetes and related conditions attain relief. (15)

[Verse 16]
Trikatu (three pungents), Triphala, honey, Kimijana, Ajamoda — this preparation called "mantha," made with sattu moistened and soaked in iron-vessel water — [along with] Jyoshna, the limbs, Triphala, pungent [herbs], and Gohini... (16)

चरकसंहितायाम् ।

ञ्यूषण त्रिफला शहत वायिविडंग मला ञ्रीदा । पांडुरोग शोफ मूत्रकुच्छू
अजमोद यह मंथ सत्तू तैल लोहेके अरुचि ॥ २० ॥
जलसे युक्त हित होता है व्योष वाय
विडंग संहंजना त्रिफला कटु रोहिणी १६

बृहत्यैद्वेदहिरोद्वेपाठासातिविषा
स्थिरा । हिङ्गुकेवुकमूलानियवा
नीधान्यचित्रकम् ॥ १७ ॥

दोनों कटेहली दोनों हलदी पाठा
अतिविषा ( अतीस ) स्थिरा हिंगु केवुक
( कवुक वृक्ष ) के मूल अजमायन
धनियां चीता ॥ १७ ॥

सौवर्चलमजाजीञ्रहवुषांचेतितचू
णयेत् । चूर्णतैलघृतक्षौद्रभागाः
स्युर्मानतःसमाः ॥ १८ ॥

सौवर्चल ( कालानोन ) अजाजी
( जीरा ) हवुषी ( हाउवेर ) इनका
चूर्ण करै और चूर्ण तैल घी शहत ये
सब प्रमाणसे समभाग ले ॥ १८ ॥

सक्तुनांषोडशगुणोभागःसन्तर्पणं
पिवेत् । प्रयोगादस्यशाम्यन्त
रोगाःसन्तर्पणोत्थिताः ॥ १९ ॥

और सत्तुओंका सोलहवां भाग इस
संतर्पणको पीवे; इस प्रयोगसे संतर्पणसे
पैदा हुये रोग शांतिको प्राप्त होते हैं १९

प्रमेहामूढवाताश्चकुष्ठान्यशाँसि
कामलाः । ञ्रीहापाण्डवामयःशो
फोमूत्रकुच्छ्रमरोचकः ॥ २० ॥

और प्रमेह मूढवात कुष्ठ अशे का-

हृद्रोगोराजयक्ष्माचकासःश्वासो
गलग्रहः । किमयोग्रहणीदोषाः
श्चैन्यंस्थौल्यमतीवच । नराणां
दीप्यतेचाग्निःस्मृतिर्बुद्धिश्चवर्द्धते २७

हृद्रोग राजयक्ष्मा कास श्वास गल-
ग्रह किमि ग्रहणीके रोग श्वित्र अतिस्थू-
लता ये नष्ट होते हैं और अग्निदीपन
होती है स्मृति और बुद्धि बढ़तीहै २१ ॥

व्यायामनित्योजीर्णाशीयवगोधू
मभोजनः । सन्तर्पणकृतैदोषैर्मु
क्तास्थौल्याद्विमुच्यते ॥ २२ ॥

जो मनुष्य व्यायाम नित्य करै,
जीर्ण अशे जिसके हो यव गोधूमका
भोजन करै तो संतर्पणके किये दोषोंसे

उक्तसन्तर्पणोत्थानामपतर्पणमौ
षधमू । वक्ष्यन्तेसौषधाश्चोद्धूम
पतर्पणजागदाः ॥ २३ ॥

संतर्पणसे हुयोंके अपतर्पणकी औषध
यह कही, अब औषध सहित ऊपरके
अपतर्पणसे भये रोगोंको कहतैहैं ॥ २३ ॥

देहाग्निबलवर्णोजःशुक्रमांसबल
क्षयः । ज्वरःकासातुबन्धश्वपा
र्श्वशूलमरोचकः ॥ २४ ॥
translation:
( 194 )
From the Charaka Samhita

Pippali (long pepper), triphala, honey, vayavidanga, ajamoda — this preparation called mantha (a drink), mixed with sattu (roasted grain flour), oil, and iron-water, is beneficial. Vyosha, vidanga, shigru (drumstick), triphala, and katurohinī — [verse 16].

The plants brihatī, dvipadā, hirā, dvi, pāthā, ativiṣā, sthirā, hingu, kevuka roots, yavānī, dhānya, and chitraka. [17]

Both katehalī, both turmeric, pāthā, ativiṣā (atis), sthirā, hingu, kevuka (kavuka tree) roots, ajamāyana (ajwain), coriander (dhaniā), and chitā (chitraka). [17]

Sauvarchala (black salt), ajājī (cumin), havuṣī (hauvera) — make a powder of these. The portions of powder, oil, ghee, and honey should be equal in measure. [18]

Sauvarchala (black salt), ajājī (cumin), havuṣī (hauvera) — make a powder of these, and take powder, oil, ghee, and honey all in equal measure. [18]

One should drink sattu in a quantity sixteen times that of the (other ingredients) as santarpaṇa (a nourishing preparation). By this use, the diseases arising from santarpaṇa (over-nourishment) are pacified. [19]

And one should drink this santarpaṇa with one-sixteenth part of sattu; by this practice, diseases born of excessive nourishment attain pacification. [19]

Prameha (urinary disorders), mūḍhavāta (suppressed wind), kuṣṭha (skin diseases), hemorrhoids, kāmalā (jaundice), splenomegaly, pāṇḍu (anemia), vomiting, edema, dysuria, and anorexia. [20]

And prameha, mūḍhavāta, kuṣṭha, hemorrhoids, and ja-[continued]

Heart disease, rājayakṣmā (tuberculosis), cough, dyspnea, throat obstruction, worm disorders, diseases of the grahaṇī (digestive tract), leucoderma, excessive obesity — all these are destroyed; moreover, the digestive fire is kindled, and memory and intellect increase. [21]

One who exercises daily, who has well-digested food, who eats barley and wheat — such a person is freed from the faults caused by santarpaṇa (over-nourishment) and from restlessness. [22]

The medicine for apatarpaṇa (under-nourishment) for those conditions arising from santarpaṇa (over-nourishment) has been described above. Now the diseases arising from apatarpaṇa together with their remedies will be described. [23]

Santarpaṇa-induced conditions treated by apatarpaṇa have been described; now the diseases arising from apatarpaṇa (under-nourishment) will be enumerated. [23]

Decline of bodily fire, strength, complexion, ojas (vital essence), semen, muscle, and physical strength; fever, cough, constriction, flank pain, and anorexia. [24]

सूत्रस्थानम् ।
( १९५ )

देह अग्निबल वर्ण ओज शुक्र मांस बल इनका क्षय ज्वर कासका योग पार्श्वशूल अरोचक ॥ २४ ॥
श्रोत्रदौर्बल्यमुन्माद:प्रलापाहृदय व्यथा । विण्मूत्रसंग्रह:शूलंजंघोरुत्रिकसंश्रयम् ॥ २५ ॥
श्रोत्रोंमें दुर्बलता उन्माद प्रलाप हृदयकी व्यथा विष्ठामूत्रका संग्रह जंघा ऊरुत्रिक इनमें शूल ॥ २५ ॥
पर्वास्थिसन्धिभेदश्चयेचान्येवातजागदा: । ऊर्ध्वातादय:सर्वे जायन्तेतेऽपतर्पणात् ॥ २६ ॥
पर्व अस्थि सांधि इनका भेद और जो अन्य वातसे उत्पन्न रोग ऊर्ध्वात आदि जो हैं वे सब अपतर्पणसे पैदा होते हैं ॥ २६ ॥
तेषांसन्तर्पणंतज्ञै:पुनराख्यात मौषधम् । यत्तदात्वेसमर्थस्याद भ्यासेवातदिष्यते ॥ २७ ॥
उनकी फिर औषध शास्त्रके ज्ञाताओंने संतर्पण कही है जो तत्कालमें समर्थ है और अभ्यासमें जितना इष्ट है ॥ २७ ॥
सद्य:क्षीणोहिसद्योवैतर्पणेनोपचीयते । नन्तेंसन्तर्पणाभ्यासाचिरक्षीणस्तुपुष्यति ॥ २८ ॥
जो सद्य: क्षीण मनुष्य है वह सद्य: संतर्पणसे वृद्धिको प्राप्त होताहै तिससे

संतर्पणके अभ्याससे चिरकालका क्षीण मनुष्य पुष्ट होताहै ॥ २८ ॥
देहाग्निदोषभैषज्यमात्राकालानुवर्तिना । कार्य्यमत्वरमाणेनभेषजंचिरदुर्बले ॥ २९ ॥
देह अग्नि दोष औषध मात्रा काल इनके जो अनुवर्ती हैं वे चिर दुर्बलतोंमें शनै:२ औषधको करें ॥ २९ ॥
हितामांसरसास्तस्मैपयांसिसच्घृतानिच । स्नानानिबस्तयोऽभ्यंगास्तर्पणास्तर्पणाश्चये ॥ ३० ॥
उसको मांसके रस दूध घृत स्नान बस्ति अभ्यंग और तर्पण अपतर्पण ये सब हितहैं ॥ ३० ॥
ज्वरकासप्रसक्तानांकशानांमूत्रकृच्छ्रणाम् । तृष्यतामूर्ध्वातानांहितंवक्ष्यामितर्पणम् ॥ ३१ ॥
ज्वरकासमें जो प्रसक्तहैं कृश मूत्रकृच्छ्री हैं तृषित ऊर्ध्वात हैं उनके हितकारी तर्पणको कहताहूँ ॥ ३१ ॥
शर्करापिप्पलीतैलघृतक्षौद्रसमांशकै: । सकुद्विगुणितोवृष्यस्तेषांमन्थ:प्रशस्यते ॥ ३२ ॥
शर्करा पीपलामूल घी शहत ये समभागोंदूना सतूहो उनको इनका मंथ श्रेष्ठ होता है ॥ ३२ ॥

Sutrasthana (Section on Fundamental Principles)
(Page 195)

Verse 24: Depletion of the body's digestive fire, complexion, ojas, semen, flesh, and strength; combined with fever, cough, flank pain, and loss of appetite.

Verse 25 (Sanskrit): Weakness of hearing, delirium, incoherent speech, pain in the heart region, retention of stool and urine, and pain localized in the calves, thighs, and sacral region.
Verse 25 (commentary): In the ears — weakness; delirium; incoherent speech; pain in the heart region; retention of stool and urine; and pain in the calves, thighs, and sacral area.

Verse 26 (Sanskrit): Breaking pain in the joints, bones, and articulations, and all other vata-born disorders — upward movement of vata and the rest — all arise from under-nourishment (apatarpana).
Verse 26 (commentary): Breaking of the joints, bones, and articulations, and other diseases arising from vata — upward vata and so on — all are produced by apatarpana (under-nourishment).

Verse 27 (Sanskrit): For those conditions, experts in the science have again prescribed santarpana (nourishing therapy) — that which is capable of acting immediately and, through repeated use, is as desired.
Verse 27 (commentary): For those conditions, those who are knowledgeable in the scriptures have prescribed santarpana, which is effective immediately and, through continued practice, produces as much benefit as desired.

Verse 28 (Sanskrit): One who is suddenly depleted recovers quickly through santarpana; but one who has been depleted over a long time is nourished through continued practice of santarpana.
Verse 28 (commentary): A person who is suddenly weakened gains strength quickly through santarpana; and through its continued practice, one who has been weakened over a long period also becomes nourished.

Verse 29 (Sanskrit): For those chronically weak, the physician should administer medicines gradually, following the body constitution, digestive fire, dosha, dosage, and timing, without haste.
Verse 29 (commentary): Those who follow the body, digestive fire, dosha, medicine, dosage, and time — for those who are chronically weak, medicine should be given gradually, step by step.

Verse 30 (Sanskrit): Beneficial for such a person are: meat broths, milk, ghee, bathing, enemas (basti), massage (abhyanga), nourishing therapies (tarpana), and depleting therapies (apatarpana).
Verse 30 (commentary): Meat broth, milk, ghee, bathing, basti, abhyanga, and tarpana and apatarpana — all these are beneficial for that person.

Verse 31 (Sanskrit): I will now describe the nourishing therapy (tarpana) beneficial for those afflicted with persistent fever and cough, who are emaciated, suffering from urinary difficulty (mutrakrichra), who are thirsty, and who have upward-moving vata.
Verse 31 (commentary): For those afflicted with persistent fever and cough, who are emaciated, suffering from dysuria, who are thirsty, and who have upward vata — I will describe the beneficial tarpana.

Verse 32 (Sanskrit): A beverage (mantha) made of equal parts of sugar, long pepper (pippali root), oil, ghee, and honey — taken once or doubled in quantity — is considered excellent for them.
Verse 32 (commentary): Sugar, pippala root, ghee, and honey in equal parts, doubled as sattu — the mantha prepared from these is the best for them.

पणम् । पिबेन्मारुतविण्मूत्रक
फिपित्तानुलोमनम् ॥ ३३ ॥
सत्तू मदिरा शहत शर्करा यह तर्पण
है मारुत कफ पित्त विण्मूत्र इन सबके
अनुलोम कारक इसको पीवै ॥ ३३ ॥

फाणितंसक्तवःसर्पिर्दधिमण्डोऽ
म्लकाञ्जिकम् । तर्पणंमूत्रकृच्छ्
घ्रमुदावर्तेहरिपिबेत् ॥ ३४ ॥
फाणित सत्तू घी दधि मंड अम्ल
कांजी, मूत्रकृच्छ उदावर्तके नाशक

आंवले मिलाकर मदिराके विकारवान

सौषधाःपरिकीर्तिताः ॥ ३७ ॥

अब विधिशोणितीय अध्यायका

[Verse 33]
One should drink this preparation of sattu (roasted flour), wine, sugar, and molasses — it promotes the normal downward movement of wind, feces, and urine, and pacifies vata, kapha, and pitta. Drink it. (33)

Thus ends the summary verse of that chapter:

[Verse 37]
In this chapter on Santarpaniya (nourishment), the diseases arising from over-nourishment and those arising from under-nourishment have both been described along with their medicines. (37)

Here ends the Santarpaniya chapter, being the twenty-third chapter.

TWENTY-FOURTH CHAPTER

We shall now explain the chapter called Vidhishonitiya (On the Proper Methods Concerning Blood).

[Verse 1]
When blood in a person's body has been properly purified by correct procedure, the methods pertaining to place, time, and individual constitution have been well demonstrated. (1)

[Verse 2]
That purified blood bestows strength, good complexion, happiness, and long life upon the living being. The vital force (prana) follows and depends upon the blood. (2)

[Verse 3]
Blood becomes corrupted by many sharp and hot types of wines and other similar substances, as well as by excessive salt, alkalis, sour things, and pungent substances — (3)

[Verse 3] Blood becomes excessively vitiated when it is sharp, hot, and corrupted by alcohol and similarly corrupted foods, and further vitiated by excessive salt, alkali, sour, and pungent substances.

[Verse 4] Through consumption of kulattha (horse gram), masha (black gram), nishpava (flat beans), sesame, and sesame oil; through consumption of pindaluka (a root), radish and similar roots and vegetables — blood becomes corrupted in all these ways.

[Verse 5] Through consumption of aquatic and marshy-region animals, of creatures that are merely tolerable, of curd, sour whey, meat-broths, alcoholic drinks, and sauviraka (a type of fermented drink) — blood is likewise vitiated.

[Verse 6] Through eating food that is incompatible, undercooked, putrid; through sleeping during the day immediately after eating; through consuming liquid, fatty, and heavy substances — blood is corrupted. So too in pregnant women.

[Verse 7] Through excessive eating, anger, exposure to heat and fire, suppression of the urge to vomit, and failure to undergo therapeutic bloodletting at the proper time — blood is vitiated.

[Verse 8] Likewise, through exertion, physical injury, fever, indigestion, overeating, and by the natural quality of the autumn season — blood becomes corrupted.

[Verse 9] From that corrupted blood, diseases of various kinds arise: ulceration of the mouth, eye diseases, putrid smell from the nose and mouth.

[Verse 10] Gulma (abdominal tumors), upadamsha (venereal sores), visarpa (erysipelas), raktapitta (bleeding disorders), pramilaka (drowsiness of eyes), vidradhi (abscess), raktameha (blood in urine), pradara (menorrhagia), and vatashonita (gout) — all these arise.

[Verse 11] Discoloration of the body, loss of digestive fire, thirst, heaviness of the limbs, burning sensation, extreme weakness, loss of appetite, and pain in the head — these are the symptoms.

स्वेद, शरीरमें दुगँध, मद, कंप, स्वरका क्षय, तन्द्रा, अधिक निद्राका योग, तमका अत्यंत दर्शन ॥ १३ ॥

कण्डू, रोग, कोठ, पिडक, कुष्ठ, चर्मदल, आदि ये सम्पूर्ण विकार शोणितके आश्रयसे जानने ॥ १४ ॥

कुष्यांच्छोणितरोगेषुरक्कपित्तहरींक्रियाम् । विरेकमुपवासंवासावणंशोणितस्यवा ॥ १६ ॥

शोणितके रोगोंमें रक्त पित्त हरनेहारी क्रियाको करैं कि विरेचन, उपवास, रुधिरका स्राव ॥ १६ ॥

बलदोषप्रमाणाद्वाविशुद्ध्यारुधिरस्यवा । रुधिरंस्रावयेञ्जन्तोराशयंप्रसमीक्ष्यवा ॥ १७ ॥
वा बलदोषके प्रमाणसे वा रुधिरकी संशुद्धिसे वा मनुष्यके आशयको देखकर मनुष्यके रुधिरका स्राव करावै ॥ १७॥

translation:
( 199 )

Blood that resembles the fruit of the lac-insect (laksha) or the gunja berry in color should be known as pure blood. (20)

Blood that is neither too hot nor too cold, that is light and digestive-stimulating — such food and drink is beneficial for the body. When blood is diminished in the body, special care must be taken. (21)

A person is said to have pure blood when their complexion and senses are clear and bright, when they desire the objects of the senses such as sound and so forth, when the urge for digestion functions properly, when they are endowed with happiness, nourishment, and strength. (22)

When the channels carrying blood and plasma, whether separately or together, become vitiated, one should know that the waste products (malas) have become disturbed. (23)

In a person whose conduct and diet are impure and whose mind is enveloped by rajas (passion) and moha (delusion), the waste products obstruct the channels and remain lodged there — and from this, diseases arise. (24)

Intoxication (mada), fainting (murchha), and unconsciousness (sannyasa) — in these, the knowledgeable physician should understand that the causative factor, the symptoms, and the alleviation each become progressively more powerful one after another. (25)

When the wind (vayu) reaches the seat of a weak mind, it disturbs the mind and thereby also disturbs the person's consciousness. (26)

In the same manner, pitta and kapha also disturb the mind and bring consciousness into a state of confusion. A more detailed description of this will be given. (27)

One should recognize intoxication (mada) and related conditions by the following signs: incoherent and rapid speech, unsteady and stumbling movements and actions, a dark or reddish complexion, and a hoarse voice. (28)

जो मद, मदिरासे विषसे, और रुधि
रसे उत्पन्नहै ये सम्पूर्ण मद, वात, पित्त,
कफ, इन तीनोंके बिना नहीं होतेहैं ३२

नीलंवायिद्वाकृष्णमाकाशमथ
वारुणम् । पश्यंस्तमःप्रविशित
शीघ्रञ्चप्रतिबुध्यते ॥ ३३ ॥

नील, वा कृष्ण, वा जलके रंगके
आकाशको देखता हुआ मनुष्य मोहमें
प्रविष्ट होजाताहै और शीघ्री बोधको
प्राप्त होजाताहै ॥ ३३ ॥

वेपथुश्वाङ्कमर्दश्वप्रपीडाहृदयस्य
च । काश्यंश्यावारुणाछायामू
च्छोयेवातसम्भवे ॥ ३४ ॥

कम्प अंगका मर्दन हृदयमें पीडा
कुशता श्याव और अरुण कान्ति होय तो
वातके मदमें मूच्छो और आयहोतेहैं ३४

रक्तंहरितवर्णंवाविवयत्पीतमथापि
वा । पश्यंस्तमःप्रविशितसस्वेद
श्चप्रबुध्यते ॥ ३५ ॥

रक्त, हरिद्रुणं वा पीत, रंगके आका-
शको देखता हुआ मोहमें प्रविष्ट होजाता
है और बोधके समयमें स्वेदसे युक्त हो
जाताहै ॥ ३५ ॥

सिपिपासःससन्तापोरक्कपित्ताकु
लेक्षणः । संभिन्नवर्चाःपीताभो
मूच्छोयेपित्तसम्भवे ॥ ३६ ॥

पिपासा और संताप सहित, रक्तपि-
त्तसे व्याकुल नेत्र, भिन्न मल पीली
कांति ये सब पित्तके मदमें मूर्छा और
आयके लिये होतेहैं ॥ ३६ ॥

translation:
( 200 )
From the Charaka Samhita

Verse 28: One who speaks with great difficulty, whose movements are unsteady and faltering, whose complexion is dry, dark, and reddish — such a person should be known as afflicted with mada (intoxication/delirium) arising from vata (wind).

Verse 29 (Sanskrit): One who is angry, speaks harshly, delights in quarrels and fighting, and whose appearance is red, yellow, or white — know that person as afflicted with pitta-mada.

Verse 29 (commentary): One who is filled with anger, speaks roughly, delights in assault and quarrel, and whose appearance is red, yellow, or white — that person should be known as afflicted with mada arising from pitta.

Verse 30 (Sanskrit): One who speaks little, is overcome by drowsiness and laziness, is pale, and is deeply absorbed in contemplation — know that person as afflicted with kapha-mada.

Verse 30 (commentary): One who speaks little, is overcome by drowsiness and laziness, is pale, and is absorbed in meditation — that person should be known as afflicted with mada arising from kapha.

Verse 31: All these symptoms together appear in the mada arising from sannipata (combination of all three doshas). It subsides quickly, like intoxication from wine.

Verse 32 (Sanskrit and commentary): The intoxication spoken of from wine, from poison, and from blood — all these types of mada ultimately depend on vata, pitta, and kapha. Whatever mada arises — from wine, poison, or blood — none of them occur without the involvement of these three: vata, pitta, and kapha.

Verse 33 (Sanskrit and commentary): One who sees the sky as blue, black, or the color of water enters into a state of confusion, and then quickly regains consciousness. Such a person has entered a state of delusion and swiftly recovers awareness.

Verse 34 (Sanskrit and commentary): Trembling, crushing pain in the limbs, distress in the heart, a dark and reddish complexion — when these are present, fainting and other conditions arise in vata-type mada.

Verse 35 (Sanskrit and commentary): One who sees the sky as red, green, or yellow enters into a state of delusion, and upon regaining consciousness is covered in perspiration. Such a person falls into delirium and awakens drenched in sweat.

Verse 36 (Sanskrit and commentary): Accompanied by thirst and burning sensation, eyes disturbed by blood and bile, loose stools, and a yellowish complexion — all these are signs that occur in pitta-type mada, leading to fainting and its consequences.

text:
Digitized By Siddha Bharati Gyaan Kosha ( २०१ )

मेघसङ्काशमाकाशमावृतंवातमोघनैः । पश्यंस्तमःअविशतिचिराचप्रतिबुध्यते ॥ ३७ ॥

मेघके समान और अंधकार मेघोंसे आच्छादित आकाशको देखता हुआ मनुष्य मोहमें प्रविष्ट होताहै और चिरकालमें बोधको प्राप्त होताहै ॥ ३७ ॥

गुरुभिःआवृतैरङ्गैःयथैवार्द्रिणचर्म्मणाःसप्रसेकःसहछ्लासोमूर्च्छियेकफसम्भवे ॥ ३८ ॥

आद्रै चर्मके समान गुरु अंगोंसे आच्छादित मसेक और हछ्लाससे युक्त होय तो कफसे उत्पन्न मदमें मूच्छी आयके लिये होतेहैं ॥ ३८ ॥

सर्वाकृतिःसन्निपातादपस्मारइवागतः । सजन्तुंपातयत्याशुविनाबीभत्सचेष्टितैः ॥ ३९ ॥

सन्निपातसे सब आकार होतेहैं और मानो अपस्मार हो गया तो वह जंतुको भयानक चेष्टाके विनाभी पतन करा देताहै ॥ ३९ ॥

दोषेषुमदमूर्च्छियाःहृतवेगेषुदेहिनाम् । स्वयमेवोपशाम्यन्तिसंन्यासोनौषधैर्विना ॥ ४० ॥

मद और मूर्च्छाके हेतु दोषोंका जब देह धारियोंको वेग होताहैं तब वे औषधोंके बिना स्वयंही शांत हो जातेहैं तो संन्यास रोग तो औषधोंके विना नहीं जाताहै ॥ ४० ॥

वाग्देहमनसांचेष्टामाक्षिप्य;तिबलामलाः । संन्यस्यन्त्वबलंजन्तुप्राणायतनसंश्रिताः ॥ ४१ ॥

अत्यंत बलवान् मल, वाणी देह मन इनकी चेष्टाको दूर करके और प्राणके स्थानमें प्रविष्ट होकर निर्बल जंतुको संन्यास रोग कर देते हैं ॥ ४१ ॥

सनासंन्याससंन्यस्तःकाष्ठभूतोमृतोपमः । प्राणैर्वियुज्यतेशीघ्रमुक्तासयःफलांकियाम् ॥ ४२ ॥

संन्याससे युक्त वह मनुष्य काष्ठभूत मृतकके समान हुआ, शीघ्र फलके दाता क्रियाकोभी छोडकर प्राणोंसे वियुक्त हो जाताहै ॥ ४२ ॥

दुर्गेऽम्भसियथामञ्जद्राजनन्तवरायाबुभः । गृहीयात्तलमशाषंतथा संन्यासपीडितम् ॥ ४३ ॥

दुर्गम, जलमें डूबते हुए पात्रको, नीचे बैठनेसे पिहले जैसे बुद्धिमान् मनुष्य ग्रहण करै, तिसी प्रकार संन्याससे पीडित मनुष्यको वैद्य ग्रहण करेंहैं ॥ ४३ ॥

अञ्जनान्यवपीडाश्धूमःप्रधमनानिच । सूचीभिस्तोदनशस्त्रैदाहः पीडानखान्तरे ॥ ४४ ॥

अंजन अत्यंतपीडा घूम प्रधमन सूचीयोंसे तोद, शस्त्रोंसे दाह नखोंके मध्यमें पीडा ॥ ४४ ॥

Verse 37:
When a person gazes upon a sky covered with clouds and darkness, he enters into a state of delusion, and it is only after a long time that he regains awareness. (37)

Verse 38:
Just as a wet hide becomes heavy, similarly when the limbs feel heavy and weighted, accompanied by excessive salivation and nausea, these are the signs of intoxication arising from kapha (phlegm), leading to unconsciousness. (38)

Verse 39:
All the features of sannipata (combination of three doshas) resemble epilepsy. It causes the afflicted person to fall suddenly, even without the frightful convulsive movements. (39)

Verse 40:
When the doshas that cause intoxication and fainting lose their force in the body, they subside on their own without medicines. But the disease of sannyasa (coma/deep unconsciousness) does not go away without medicines. (40)

Verse 41:
Extremely powerful impurities, having overcome the activities of speech, body, and mind, enter the seat of vital breath and render the creature powerless, producing the disease of sannyasa. (41)

Verse 42:
A person afflicted with sannyasa becomes like a piece of wood, resembling a corpse. He quickly becomes separated from his vital forces, abandoning even those actions that might otherwise yield results. (42)

Verse 43:
Just as a wise man, before a vessel sinks in deep water, grasps its bottom, similarly the physician should take hold of a person afflicted with sannyasa before it is too late. (43)

Verse 44:
The treatments to be applied are: collyrium (eye applications), strong nasal irritants, medicated smoke inhalation, errhines, needling with fine needles, cauterization with instruments, and painful stimulation between the nails. (44)

लुञ्चनकेशलोम्नांचदन्तैदेशनमेव
च । आत्मगुणावघर्षश्चहतारत
स्यावबोधने ॥ ४५ ॥
केश और लोमोंका छुंचन दांतोंसे
दंशन अपने गुत्तका घिसना ये सब
उसके बोधनके लिये नष्ट कहेंहैं ॥४५॥
संमूर्च्छतानितीक्ष्णानिमध्यानि
विविधानिच । प्रभूतकटुतिक्का
नितस्यास्येगालयेन्मुहुः ॥४६ ॥
और तीक्षण संमूर्च्छित नानाप्रकारके
मद्य अत्यंतकटु, तिक्त ये पदार्थ उसके
मुखमें बारंबार डारैं ॥ ४६ ॥
मातुलुङ्गरसंतद्वन्महौषधसमायु
तम् । तद्वत्सौवीरकंदया युक्कम
याम्लकाञ्जिकैः ॥ ४७ ॥
और मातुलुंग ( विजोरा ) का रस
सूंठी सहित और मदिरा अम्ल कांजी
सहित सौवीर (सहँजना) को दे ॥४७॥
हिङ्गुगृष्णसमायुक्तयावत्संज्ञाप्रबो
धनात् । प्रबुद्धसंज्ञमनैश्चलघु
भिस्तमुपाचयेत् ॥ ४८ ॥
और हींग ऊष्ण मिलाकर दे, ये तब
तक दे जबतक संज्ञाका बोध हो, और
जब संज्ञाका प्रबोध हो जाय तब लघु
अन्नोंसे उपचार करें ॥ ४८ ॥
विस्मापनैःस्मारणैश्चिप्रयश्रुतिभि
रेवच । पटुभिर्गीतवादित्रशब्दै
श्चित्रैश्चदर्शनैः ॥ ४९ ॥

और विस्मयकारी स्मरणके कर्ता,
प्रिय शब्दोंका श्रवण और उत्तम गीत
वादित्रोंके शब्द चित्रोंके दर्शन ॥४९॥
संसनोल्लेखनेधूमेरञ्जनैःकवलग्र
हैः । शोणितस्यावसेकैश्चव्या
यामोद्धर्षणैस्तथा ॥ ५० ॥
संसन उल्लेखन धूम अंजन कवलका
ग्रहण, शोणितका अवसेचन व्यायाम
उद्धर्षण ॥ ५० ॥
प्रबुद्धसंज्ञंमतिमानुबद्धमुपाचरे
त् । तस्यसंरक्षितव्यंहिमनःप्र
लयहेतुतः ॥ ५१ ॥
इनसे जब संज्ञा बढजाय तब अनु-
बुद्ध उसकी शुद्धिमान् वैद्य चिकित्सा
करे, उसके मनकी प्रलयके हेतुओंसे
रक्षा करें ॥ ५१ ॥
स्नेहस्वेदोपयन्नानांयथादोषंयथा
बलम् । पञ्चकर्माणिकुर्वीतमू
च्छियेषुमदेषुच ॥ ५२ ॥
स्नेह स्वेदसे उपयुक्तोंकी दोष और
बलके अनुसार जिन मदोंमें मूर्च्छा आय
होतेहैं उनमें पांच कर्मोंको करें ॥५२॥
अष्टाविंशत्यौषधस्योद्धूमथवाति
कसर्पिषः । प्रयोगःशस्यतेतद्वन्म
हतःषट्पलस्यवा ॥ ५३ ॥
अट्ठाइस औषधोंसे पीछे तिक्त घीका
प्रयोग श्रेष्ठ होताहै और तैसेही बड़े षट्
पलका प्रयोग ॥ ५३ ॥

Charaka Samhita

Verse 45:
Pulling the hair and body-hair, biting with the teeth, rubbing one's own body — all these are said to be useless for awakening one who has lost consciousness. (45)

Verse 46:
Various kinds of intoxicating substances mixed together — very pungent and bitter — should be placed repeatedly in that person's mouth. (46)

Verse 47:
The juice of matulunga (citron/bijora) combined with dried ginger, and similarly sauviraka (drumstick/sahanjana) combined with sour fermented rice-water (kanji) and wine — these should be given. (47)

Verse 48:
Give asafoetida mixed with warm substances until consciousness is restored; and when consciousness is restored, treat the patient with light foods. (48)

Verse 49:
By means of surprising and memory-stimulating experiences, by hearing pleasant sounds, by the sounds of excellent songs and musical instruments, and by viewing beautiful pictures — (49)

Verse 50:
Scraping, fumigation, collyrium application, holding medicinal mouthwashes, bloodletting, exercise, and rubbing of the body — (50)

Verse 51:
When consciousness is thus restored, the wise and attentive physician should treat the patient and protect his mind from the causes of mental dissolution. (51)

Verse 52:
Using oleation and sudation therapies, the five purificatory procedures (panchakarma) should be performed according to the specific dosha and strength of the patient in cases of fainting and intoxication. (52)

Verse 53:
After the twenty-eight medicinal herbs, the use of bitter clarified ghee is considered excellent, and similarly the use of a large quantity of six pala weight is recommended. (53)

translation:
(Page 204)

What is the certainty regarding the origin? This is what should be considered first. || 2 ||

Then Kashipati, speaking a meaningful statement in accordance with the opinion of the sages, having offered salutation, said the following in the midst of the assembly. || 3 ||

Whatever the person is, from that same source arise the diseases attributed to him — or do they not? On the king speaking thus, the sage Punarvasu replied: || 4 ||

All of you, whose doubts have been resolved by limitless knowledge and wisdom, are worthy of cutting away the doubt of the king of Kashi. || 5 ||

Before their examination, one named Maudralya (Parikshi) spoke these words: "The person is born of the Atman (Self), and diseases too are born of the Atman — the Atman itself is the cause." || 6 ||

It is that (Atman) which accumulates karma and its fruits, and it is that which experiences them. Without the conscious principle (chetana-dhatu), neither the activity of pleasure nor of pain arises. || 7 ||

In this matter, Sharaloma said: "This is not so, because the Atman cannot ever join itself with disease and suffering by means of itself, since the Atman is averse to suffering." || 8 ||

The mind, known as the satva (consciousness), when pervaded by the qualities of rajas and tamas, becomes the cause of the arising of the body and of its disorders. || 9 ||

Vayovida then said in objection: "This is not so either, because the mind alone cannot be the single cause, nor does the condition of the body and its diseases rest upon the mind alone." || 10 ||

translation:
Page 205 — Putra Sthana (Chapter on Progeny)

[Verse 10] Without a body there is no body; without a body there are no diseases of the body; that is the position of prostration (of the argument).

[Verse 11] All living beings are produced from rasa (vital fluid/essence), and diseases too are of different kinds — they arise from rasa; the waters that carry disease are themselves declared to be the cause of creation.

[Verse 12] Hiranyaksha says: this is not so, because the self (atman) is not described as produced from rasa; the mind is not a sense organ, and hence diseases do not arise from sound and the like.

[Verse 13] The person (purusha) is produced from the six constituents (dhatus), and diseases likewise arise from the six constituents; the aggregate (body) too is constituted of the six constituents — this has been examined and confirmed by the ancient Sankhya philosophers.

[Verse 14] To Kushika who spoke in this manner, Shaunaka replied: How can one be produced from the six constituents without (the involvement of) mother and father?

[Verse 15] A man is born of a man, a cow of a cow, a horse of a horse; hence paternal diseases such as diabetes (meha) and the rest are stated to be causes — they are the causes, not something else.

[Verse 16] Bhadrakapya, however, objects: it is not the case, for a blind man is not necessarily born of a blind man, because in your view the prior production of mother and father themselves could not be accounted for.

[Verse 17] According to this view, a living being is born of karma, and its diseases too are karma-born; for without karma neither the birth of a person nor the arising of diseases is possible.

[Verse 18] Bharadvaja, however, objects: this is not so, because an agent (karta) must exist prior to (performing) an action in this world; and how can a person reap the fruit of a karma that has not yet been performed —

translation:
( 206 )

One does not see the fruit of action in a person-form. || 18 ||

The inherent nature of things is the cause of diseases in persons; just as heat, fluidity, and motion are the natural properties of the elements up to fire. || 19 ||

Kankayana says this is not so, because at the beginning no fruit can arise from mere effort; rather, the accomplishment and non-accomplishment of things comes from their own nature alone. || 20 ||

Brahma, possessed of unlimited will, created Prajapati as his offspring; and Prajapati is continuously the cause of both the sentience and insentience, and of the pleasure and pain, of this world. || 21 ||

The mendicant Atreya says that this is not so, because Prajapati, who is ever the well-wisher of his creatures, would never subject his offspring to suffering. || 22 ||

The person is the knower of time; diseases arise from time; the entire world is subject to time; and time is the cause of everything everywhere. || 23 ||

Then, as the sages were thus disputing, Punarvasu spoke to them: "Do not speak in this way, for the truth is hard to reach when one takes shelter in a single partisan view." || 24 ||

People who go on asserting their arguments and counter-arguments, without reaching any settled conclusions, never arrive at the end of their respective positions — like sesame seeds being pressed without yielding oil. || 25 ||

Therefore, abandoning this cluster of arguments, let one contemplate the inner self. Knowledge does not arise concerning the knowable when the mass of darkness has not been removed. || 26 ||

क्योंकि तमोगुणके स्कंधके नाश हुये बिना ज्ञेयके ज्ञानकी प्रवृति नहीं होती ॥ २६ ॥

येषामेविहभावानांसम्पत्सऄनये ञरम् । तेषामेविपद्च्याधीन्व विधान्समुदीरयेत् ॥ २७ ॥

जीव भावोंकी सम्पदा, मनुष्यको पैदा करती है, उनकीही विपति, नाना-प्रकारकी व्याधियोंको पैदा करती है२७॥

अथात्रेयस्यभगवतोवचनमनुनिशम्यपुनरेवावामकःकाशिपतिरुवाचभगवन्तमात्रेयम् । भगवन् सम्पत्निमित्तजस्यपुरुषस्यविपञ्निमित्तजानांचरोगाणांकिमभिवृद्धिकारणिमिति । तमुवाचभगवानात्रेयोहिताहारोपयोगःएकए वपुरुषस्यअभिवृद्धिकरोभवतिअहिताहारोपयोगःपुनव्याधीनांनिमित्तमिति ॥ २८ ॥

इसके अनन्तर, आत्रेय भगवानके वचनको सुनकर, फिरभी वामक, काशिपति भगवान् आत्रेयको बोले, सम्पदाके निमित्तसे उत्पन्न हुए पुरुषको और विपत्तिके निमित्तसे उत्पन्न हुए रोगोंकी वृद्धिका क्या कारण है, उसको भगवान् आत्रेय बोले कि एक हित आहारका उपयोगही पुरुष की वृद्धि

कारक होता है और अहित आहारका उपयोग व्याधियोंका कारणहै ॥ २८ ॥

एवंवादिनंभगवन्तमात्रेयमिभिवेश उवाच । कथिमहभगवन् ! हिताहितानामाहारजातानांलक्षणम नपवादमिभजानीयाहितसमाऱ्यातानांचैवआहारजातानामिहितसमाऱ्यातानाञ्मात्राकालिकयाभूमिदेहदोषपुरुषावस्थान्तरेषुविपरीतकारित्वमुपलभामहे इति२९

इस प्रकार कहते हुए भगवान् आत्रेयको अभिवेश बोलेकि, हेभगवन् हित अहित आहारोंके समूहका लक्षण बिना अपवाद ( दोष )हम कैसे जानें, अहित नामके जो आहारके समूहहैं और हित नामके जोहैं उनके मात्रा, काल, क्रिया भूमि, देह, दोष, पुरुषकी अवस्था इन सबके मध्यमें विपरीत कार्यको हम देखतेहैं ॥ २९ ॥

तमुवाचभगवानात्रेयः । यदाहारजातमिभिवेश ! समांश्चैवशरीरधातून्रक्तौस्थापयतिविषमांश्समीकरोतिइत्येतद्धितंविद्धिविपरीतमहितमितिएतद्धिताहितलक्षणमनपवादंभवति ॥ ३० ॥

उसके प्रति भगवान् आत्रेय बोलेकि हे अभिवेश–जो आहार समूहोंके मध्यमें समान शरीरकी धातुओंको

translation:
Because without the destruction of the aggregate of the quality of tamas (darkness/inertia), the cognition of what is to be known does not arise. (26)

For those in whom the prosperity of living states leads to misfortune — for them the various diseases born of that adversity should be enumerated. (27)

The prosperity of living states gives rise to the human being, and their adversity gives rise to diseases of many kinds. (27)

Then, after hearing the words of the blessed Atreya, Vamaka, the lord of Kashipati, again spoke to the venerable Atreya: "O Venerable One, what is the cause of the growth of a person born of prosperity, and of diseases born of adversity?" The blessed Atreya replied: "The use of wholesome food alone promotes the growth of a person, while the use of unwholesome food is the cause of diseases." (28)

Thus addressed, Agnivesha spoke to the venerable Atreya: "O Venerable One, how are we to know, without exception, the characteristics of the groups of wholesome and unwholesome foods? We observe that the groups of foods designated wholesome and those designated unwholesome produce contrary effects with respect to quantity, time, action, place, body, humor, and condition of the person." (29)

The blessed Atreya replied to him: "O Agnivesha, that group of foods which brings the body's dhatus (tissues) that are in proper balance to a stable state, and which normalizes those that are imbalanced — know that to be wholesome. The opposite of this is unwholesome. This is the definition of wholesome and unwholesome, without exception." (30)

The blessed Atreya then said to Agnivesha: "He who, among all groups of food, stabilizes the balanced dhatus of the body..."

translation:
( 208 )
In the Charaka Samhita.

One should restore the body to its natural state and equalize the imbalanced dhatus (bodily elements). One should know that food which is beneficial, and what is contrary to it as harmful — this recognition of the beneficial and harmful is the characteristic of what follows. ॥ 30 ॥

When Bhagavan Atreya had spoken thus, Agnivesha said: "Bhagavan! Indeed, as this has been taught, most physicians will understand it." ॥ 31 ॥

In this manner, as the revered Atreya was speaking, Agnivesha said: "O Bhagavan, this teaching cannot be fully understood by all physicians." ॥ 31 ॥

Then Bhagavan Atreya spoke: "O Agnivesha! Those who know the essence of food — in terms of its qualities, substances, actions, all its parts, and its measure and other properties — they alone can understand this teaching. And in the manner in which this has been taught, most physicians will come to understand it, and we shall thus instruct. While citing examples of measure and other properties, many kinds of alternatives arise for them. We shall explain the specific characteristics of food in terms of its defining features and its constituent parts." ॥ 32 ॥

Food in its essence: Food is of one meaning, but by further classification it is of two origins — plant (sthavara) and animal (jangama). It is again twofold according to its beneficial or harmful effects. Its fourfold use is through drinking, eating, chewing, and licking. By the six-fold distinction of taste (rasa), it becomes sixfold. Its twenty qualities are: heavy, light, cold, hot, unctuous, dry, slow, sharp, hard, liquid, soft, firm, clear, slimy, smooth, rough, subtle, gross, dense, and flowing. Due to the innumerable varieties arising from combinations of substances, processes, and their multiplicity, countless preparations become fit for use. The best and most wholesome, as well as the most unwholesome for human beings — all of these we shall explain properly. Thus, red rice (lohita shali) is the most wholesome and the best among the grain cereals.

( 210 )
Charaka Samhita — Gyaan Kosha

[This passage from the Charaka Samhita enumerates medicinal substances classified according to their therapeutic actions. The text lists plants and substances grouped by their primary therapeutic categories:]

Among those that allay thirst — among those named for alleviating disorders of milk production, for promoting wholesome secretions, for acting as astringents, for pacifying bile mixed with blood — among those that increase kapha and pitta, among the agents that promote secretion of mother's milk, among those that check diarrhea: barley promotes formation of feces; jambava (rose apple) promotes the movement of vata; shashkulya promotes kapha and pitta; kulttha (horse gram) promotes acidity and pitta; masha (black gram) promotes kapha and pitta. Madanaphala is useful for emesis, asthapana and anuvAsana enemas. Trivrita is a gentle laxative. Chaturangula is a mild purgative. Shrutakshira acts as a sharp purgative. Priyangu is useful as a nasal medication (shirovirechana). Vidanga destroys worms. Shirisha is antidote to poison. Khadira is beneficial in skin diseases. Rasna alleviates vata. Amalaka promotes longevity. Haritaki (chebulic myrobalan) is the best among conducive substances (pathya). Erandamula (root of castor) is an aphrodisiac and alleviates vata. Pippali root stimulates digestion, promotes appetite, and alleviates abdominal distension. Chitraka root stimulates digestion and alleviates rectal swelling. Pushkara root relieves hiccough, dyspnea, cough, and pain in the flanks. Musta is an astringent, digestive stimulant, and promotes digestion.

[Right column:] Udichya is refreshing, digestive, and promotes evacuation. Kadamba is astringent, digestive stimulant, and promoter of digestion. Ananta is astringent, digestive, and alleviates blood and pitta. Amrita (guduchi) is astringent, alleviates vata, stimulates digestion, and relieves obstruction of kapha and blood. Bilva is astringent, stimulates digestion, and alleviates vata and kapha. Thus the group of vishadigana acts as digestive stimulant, astringent, and remover of all doshas. Utpala, kumuda, and their allies pacify blood disorders and pitta. Duralabha removes excess pitta and kapha. Gandhapriyangu pacifies excessive pitta and hemorrhage. Kutaja bark is astringent for kapha, pitta, and blood, and removes their excess. Kashmarya fruit is an astringent for blood and pacifies pitta. Prishniparni is astringent, alleviates vata, stimulates digestion, and is an aphrodisiac. Vidarigandhaa is an aphrodisiac and alleviates all doshas. Bala is an astringent, strengthening, and alleviates vata. Gokshura alleviates suppression of urine and vata. Hingu (asafoetida) juice is an excising agent, digestive stimulant, purgative, carminative, and alleviates vata and kapha. Amlavetasa is a purgative, digestive stimulant, carminative, and alleviates vata and kapha. Yavashuka promotes wholesome digestion.

[This passage is from the Charaka Samhita, enumerating causes and their effects on health and disease, in the form of a continuous enumeration. The following is a rendering of the content:]

Practices that destroy morbid conditions — excessive use of ghee is harmful to the digestive system; the use of meat juices alleviates the disorders caused by ghee excess; the use of ghee and milk serves as a rejuvenating therapy; the combined use of ghee and kuka promotes virility; oil gargles strengthen the teeth and stimulate appetite; the use of sandal and udumbara removes burning sensations; cooling plasters and applications relieve burning of the skin; treatments with kushtha herb alleviate vata disorders; dhuka promotes vision, virility, hair growth, clarity of throat and complexion, strength, healing, and supports vital breath as the sustainer of life; water alleviates stiffness, cold, and trembling; water treated with mud clods relieves excessive thirst; eating in proper measure according one's digestive capacity prevents accumulation of undigested matter; eating at the proper time maintains digestive fire; performing activities suited to one's constitution maintains health; restraining natural urges is unhealthy; eating a heavy meal is difficult to digest.

Eating one meal a day promotes easy digestion; excessive sexual indulgence with women causes wasting; suppression of seminal discharge causes impotence; celibacy promotes longevity; fasting diminishes lifespan; eating in moderation causes emaciation; eating when food has not yet digested corrupts the digestive tract; eating at irregular times disturbs the digestive fire; eating foods of mutually contradictory potency causes reprehensible diseases; proper diet is the remedy; all improper conduct is the cause of disease; sexual intercourse during menstruation brings misfortune; celibacy is life-promoting; mental depression destroys virility; undertaking tasks beyond one's strength obstructs the channels; despondency increases disease; knowledge removes fatigue; joy nourishes; grief causes wasting; contentment promotes nourishment; excessive sleep causes drowsiness; consuming all flavors together strengthens; consuming only one flavor causes weakness; the fetus becomes an obstacle to improper evacuation; indigestion is to be addressed in the tender ones; for the elderly and pregnant women, strong medications, exercise, and similarly strenuous activities are to be avoided; a cheerful mind supports the retention of the fetus.
