[Charaka Samhita]

[The left column contains a verse enumerating difficult conditions for treatment:] Those who are one-eyed, those afflicted with painful conditions difficult to treat, those with irregular fevers difficult to cure, those suffering from diseases like cough, chronic diseases, and the group of diseases including rajayakshma (tuberculosis), those with prameha (urinary disorders), those treated with leeches and surgical instruments, those treated with enemas, regions of the Himalayas where medicinal herbs grow, desert regions known for their health, regions where the ruler's orders are not followed, the failings of patients, the ignorance of physicians regarding treatment, the shortcomings of those who are greedy, the characteristics of those who cause trouble, signs of distress and affliction, knowledge of the qualities needed by a physician, knowledge of medicinal substances as described in the treatise, the proper application of therapeutic procedures, knowledge of timing and its uses, the eight actions — these are the sources of doubt; inability to act, fear of [false accusations], the wisdom to engage in debate, knowledge [gained] from teachers through study of the scriptures, Ayurveda as the means to immortality, the good counsel of the wise, the connected discourse that must be practiced, the compilation of all that is prescribed — all of these constitute happiness. [Verse 33]

Since there is no essential difference in meaning, food is of one kind; but because it is of plant origin or animal origin, it is of two kinds. According to whether it is more beneficial or more harmful, it is used in four ways — as a drink (pana), as a meal (ashana), as something to be eaten (bhakshya), or as something to be licked (lehya). Its taste is of six kinds, and by the distinctions of the six rasas (tastes) it has twenty qualities: heavy, light, cold, hot, unctuous, dry, slow, sharp, unstable — and also: sharp, soft, hard, clear, slimy, smooth, rough, subtle, gross, dense, liquid, and penetrating. From these distinctions, the variations of substances and their combinations are innumerable in their abundance. The particular parts of those substances that are most useful, and the conception of their predominance, arise from the individual constitution (prakriti) of persons. A proper account is now given of foods that are most beneficial and most harmful: Among the shuka grains (bearded cereals), lohitashali (the red variety of sathi rice) is supremely excellent as a wholesome food. Among the shami grains (legumes), [mudga — green gram is best]. Among waters, rainwater (from clouds) is best. Among salts, saindhava (rock salt) is best. Among vegetables, the vegetable of jivanti is best. Among the meats of deer, the meat of the ena (black buck) is best. Among birds, the meat of the lava (quail) is best. Among burrowing animals, the godha (monitor lizard) is best. Among fish, the rohita is best. Among ghees, cow's ghee is best. Among milks, cow's milk is best. Among plant-based oils, sesame oil is best. Among the fats of boars, [boar fat is noted]. Among the fats of marshy-land animals (anupa mruga), chulluka fat is best. Among the fats of fish, the fat of the hamsa (swan/goose) is best. Among the fats of aquatic birds, the fat of the kukkuta (domestic fowl) is best. Among the fats of vishkira birds (ground-scratching birds), [their respective fats are noted]. Among the medas (marrow/fat) from bones, the fat of the goat (aja) is best. Among roots (kanda), shringavera (ginger/adrak) is best. Among fruits —

translation:
( 214 )
In the Charaka Samhita

Among the root substances that are digestive-stimulating and digestive: Motha; among those that are astringent, digestive-stimulating, and anti-diarrheal: Udichya (Vala); among the astringent digestive-stimulants: Katvanga (Sonapaatha); among those that pacify hemorrhagic disorders: Giloh (Guduchi) or Peepal; among those that are astringent, digestive-stimulant, and relieve cough, bleeding, and constipation: Amrita (Guduchi); among those that are astringent, digestive-stimulant, and pacify vata and kapha: Bilva; among those that are digestive, astringent, and eliminate all doshas: Ativisha (Atis); among the astringents that pacify blood and pitta: Utpala (blue lotus), Kumuda, and Padma; among those that dry up pitta and kapha: Duralabha (Javasa); among those that pacify extreme pitta combined with bleeding: Gandhapriyangu; among the astringents that dry up kapha, pitta, and blood: Kutaki bark; among the astringents that pacify blood disorders: Kaimaryaphala; among the astringent, vata-pacifying, digestive-stimulant, and aphrodisiac substances: Prishniparni (Pithvan); among aphrodisiacs that eliminate all doshas: Vidarikhanda; among the binding vata-removers: Bala; among those that relieve urinary difficulty and vata: Gokharu; among the cutting, digestive-stimulating, and carminative substances for vata and kapha: Hing (asafoetida); among the purgative, digestive-stimulating, and carminative substances for vata and kapha: Amalvet; among the digestive, hemorrhoid-relieving substances: Yavgruk; for pacifying grahani disorders, hemorrhoids, and ghrita-related conditions: the practice of buttermilk (takra); among the remedies for grahani disorders: the flesh of flesh-eating animals; among rejuvenating substances: regular use of ghee and milk; among the aphrodisiacs and relievers of udavarta: practice with sattu prepared in ghee; among those that strengthen teeth and improve taste: the use of oil for gargling.

For gargling practices: Chandana (sandalwood) for burning sensation relief and application; for cooling and removal of heat in poultices: Rayasana and Agaru; for skin-burning, sweating disorders, eye applications: Khas (Usira); among those useful for vata-pacifying massage and footwear: Kuta; beneficial for eyes, hair, throat, and complexion; among those to be avoided and those that promote healing: Mahua; among the chief causes of prana (life force): Vayu (air); for pacifying ama, stiffness, cold, pain, and spasms: Agni (fire); among the stanching substances; for pacifying extreme thirst: water purified by heating with soil or clods of earth.

Among the causes of disease: eating too much; for those with strong digestive fire: eating according to the strength of digestion; in conduct and behavior: living according to one's constitution; among health-promoting practices: eating at the proper time; among the causes of ill health: suppression of natural urges; among the qualities of food: satisfaction; among the producers of mental well-being: wine (in appropriate measure); among the destroyers of intellect, fortitude, and memory: the abuse of wine; among causes of difficult digestion: heavy eating; among the producers of comfortable digestion: eating one meal at a time; among the gateways to grief: association with women (in inappropriate contexts); among the causes of impotency: suppression of the semen's natural urge; among the causes of inauspicious conditions: eating food in another's house; among the causes of shortened lifespan: fasting; among moderate eaters: eating the right measured amount; among the faults of the housewife: indigestion and overeating; among the causes of irregular digestive fire: irregular eating; among the causes of condemned diseases: intake of substances with mutually incompatible potencies.

भोजन, पथ्योंमें शान्ति, संपूर्ण अपथ्योंमें आयास, ( श्रम ) व्याधिके मुखोंमें मिथ्यायोग, लक्ष्मीके नाशाकारकोंमें रजस्वलाका गमन, आयुष्यके कर्ताओंमें ब्रह्मचर्य, वृष्योंमें संकल्प, अवृष्योंमें दौर्मनस्य प्राणके उपरोधियोंमें अयोग्य बलसे प्रारंभ, रोगवर्द्धकोंमें विषाद, श्रमके हारकोंमें स्नान, प्रीतिके कारणोंमें हर्ष, शोषके कर्ताओंमें शोक पुष्टिके कारणोंमें निवृति, तन्द्राके कारणोंमें अति स्वप्न, बलके कारणोंमें सर्व रसोंका अभ्यास, दुर्बलताके कारणोंमें एक रसका अभ्यास, अनाहायोंमें गर्भ शल्य, उद्धार करने योग्योंमें अजीर्ण, मृदु औषध करने योग्योंमें बालक, वापन करने योग्योंमें वृद्ध, तीक्ष्ण औषध व्यायाम, इनके वर्जन कर्ताओंमें गर्भिणी, गर्भके धारकोंमें सौमनस्य, कठिनतासे चिकित्साके योग्योंमें सन्निपात, विषम चिकित्साके योग्योंमें आम, रोगोंमें ज्वर, दीर्घ रोगोंमें कुष्ठ, रोगके समूहोंमें राजयक्ष्मा, अनुषंगके रोगोंमें प्रमेह अनुशक्तोंमें जलके जीवतन्त्रोंमें बस्ति, औषधिकी भूमियोंमें हिमाचल, आरोग्य देशोंमें मरुस्थल; अहित देशोंमें अधिक जलका देश, आतुरके गुणोंमें आज्ञाका करना, चिकित्साके अंगोंमें वैद्य, वर्जनके योग्योंमें नास्तिक, क्लेशके कर्ताओंमें चपलता, अनिष्टोंमें आज्ञाका न करना, वान्तके लक्षणोंमें अनिर्वेद, वैद्यके गुणोंमें योग, औषधियोंमें विज्ञान,

साधनोंमें शास्त्रसहित तर्क कालज्ञानके प्रयोजनोंमें संप्रतिपति, व्यवसाय कालके अवलंघनके हेतुओंमें अनुयोग, निस्संशयके कारणोंमें धृष्टकर्मता, भयके कारकोंमें असमर्थता। बुद्धिके वर्द्धकोंमें बुद्धिमानोंके साथ संभाषण, शास्त्रकी प्राप्तिके हेतुओंमें आचार्य, अमृतोंमें आयुर्वेद, अनुष्ठान करने योग्योंमें सद्वचन संपूर्ण अहितोंमें असंबद्ध वचनका संग्रह, सुखोंमें सबका सन्यास इति ॥ ३३ ॥

भवन्तिचात्र ।
अध्यानांशतमुदिष्टंयद्विपञ्चाशदुत्तरम् । अलमेतद्विकाराणांविधातायोपदिश्यते ॥ ३४ ॥

इसमें ये श्लोकहैं कि ये १५२ एकसौ बावन, अध्य ( मुख्य ) वर्णन किये हैं विकारोंके विघातके लिये ये समर्थ कहेहैं ॥ ३४ ॥

समानकारणायेऽथिस्तेषांश्रेष्ठस्य लक्षणम् । ज्यायरत्वंकार्यकारित्वेऽवरत्वंचाप्युदाहृतम् ॥ ३५ ।

और समान कारण जो अर्थहैं उनमें श्रेष्ठका लक्षण उपदेश किया कार्यके कर्ताओंमें अत्यंत श्रेष्ठता और अश्रेष्ठता कही ॥ ३५ ॥

वातपित्तकफेऽयश्चयत्प्रशमनेहितम् । प्राधान्यतश्चिनिदिष्टं द्वयाधिहरमुत्तमम् ॥ ३६ ॥

Sutrasthana (Chapter on Fundamental Principles) (215)

Among foods, wholesome ones bring peace; among all unwholesome ones, exertion is foremost; among the causes that open the doors to disease, wrong use of things is primary; among destroyers of prosperity, sexual intercourse with a menstruating woman; among the promoters of long life, celibacy; among the aphrodisiacs, mental resolve; among the causes of sexual debility, mental distress; among the obstructions to vital breath, beginning exertion with inadequate strength; among the aggravators of disease, depression; among the removers of fatigue, bathing; among the causes of happiness, joy; among the causes of emaciation, grief; among the causes of nourishment, withdrawal from activity; among the causes of drowsiness, excessive sleep; among the causes of strength, the practice of all tastes; among the causes of weakness, the practice of a single taste; among conditions causing non-digestion, fetal obstruction; among what is worthy of gentle medicine, children; among those suited for purifying therapy, the elderly; among those who should avoid strenuous exercise, pregnant women; among the supporters of the fetus, a cheerful mind; among conditions requiring difficult treatment, sannipata (triple-dosha imbalance); among conditions requiring irregular treatment, ama (undigested matter); among diseases, fever; among chronic diseases, leprosy; among groups of diseases, rajayakshma (consumption); among persistent diseases, prameha (urinary disorders); among life-sustaining procedures in water, basti (enema); among medicinal lands, the Himalayas; among healthful regions, the desert; among harmful regions, lands with excess water; among the qualities of a patient, obedience to instruction; among the components of treatment, the physician; among those to be excluded, atheists; among causes of suffering, fickleness; among undesirable things, disobedience; among the signs of one who has vomited, absence of despondency; among the qualities of a physician, practical skill; among medicines, knowledge;

Among the means of treatment, reasoning supported by scripture; among the purposes of knowledge of time, proper comprehension; among the reasons for transgressing the time of action, questioning; among the causes of certainty, the capacity to act boldly; among the causes of fear, incapacity. Among the enhancers of intellect, conversation with the learned; among the means of obtaining knowledge of scripture, a teacher; among the nectars, Ayurveda; among things worthy of practice, right speech; among all harmful things, the accumulation of incoherent talk; among pleasures, the renunciation of all. Thus ends verse 33.

And here the following verses occur:
What has been described here numbers one hundred and fifty-two in total. These are stated to be sufficient and capable of counteracting diseases, as taught by the teacher. (34)

Among things having the same cause, the characteristic of the best has been described. The highest excellence lies in the capacity to accomplish the work, while inferiority is characterized by the opposite. (35)

That which is beneficial in pacifying vata, pitta, and kapha, and which has been principally prescribed — what subdues two doshas simultaneously is considered the best. (36)

( २१६ )

वात, पित, कफ इनकी शान्तिमें जो हितहै और जो व्याधिके हारकोमें उत्तम है वहभी प्रधानतासे वर्णन किया ३६

एतच्छम्यनिपुणंचिकित्सांसंप्रयोजयेत् । एवंकुर्वन्सदावैद्योधर्मकामौसमश्नुते ॥ ३७ ॥

इन सबको निपुणतासे जानकर चिकित्साके प्रयोगको करै इस प्रकार करता हुआ वैद्य सदैव धर्म कामको भोगतहै ॥ ३७ ॥

पथ्यंयथानपेतंयद्यच्चोक्तंमनसःप्रियम् । यच्चाप्रियमपथ्यञ्चनियतं तच्चलक्षयेत् ॥ ३८ ॥

जो मार्गके अनुसार है और जो मन को प्रिय कहहै वह पथ्य और जो नियमसे अप्रियहै वह अपथ्यहै उसको न देखै ॥ ३८ ॥

मात्राकालिकयाभूमिदेहदोषगुणान्तरम् । प्राप्यतच्छिदश्यन्तेतोभावास्तथातथा ॥ ३९ ॥

मात्रा, काल, किया, भूमि, देह, दोष और गुणान्तर इनमें जिस तिसको प्राप्त होकर तिस तिस प्रकारके भाव देखतेहैं ३९

तस्मात्स्वभावोनिदिष्टैस्तथामात्रादिराश्रयः । तदपेक्ष्योभयंकर्मप्रयोज्यंसिद्धिमिच्छता ॥ ४० ॥

तिससे स्वभाव और मात्रा आदिका आश्रय वर्णन कियाहै इन दोनोंकी अपेक्षासे सिद्धिका अभिलाषी वैद्य चिकित्साको करै ॥ ४० ॥

तदात्रेयस्यभगवतोवचनमनुनिशम्युनरिपभगवन्तमात्रेयमग्निवेश उवाच । यथोद्देशमभिनिर्दिष्टः केवलोऽयमर्थोभगवताश्रुतस्त्वस्माभिः । आसवद्रव्याणामिदानींलक्षणमनितसंक्षेपेणोपदिश्यमानंश्रुश्रूषामहेइतितमुवाचभगवानात्रेयः । धान्यफलसारपुष्पकाण्डपत्रचोभवन्त्यासवयोनयः अग्निवेश! संग्रहेणाष्टौशर्करानवमास्तासुद्रव्यसंयोगकरणतोऽपिरे संख्येयासुयथापथ्यतमानासवामानांचतुरशीतिंनिबोधसुरासौवीरतुषोदकमैरेयमेदकधान्याम्लषड्धान्यावासवाः । मृद्वीकाखजूरकाश्मर्यधन्वनराजादनतृणशूल्यपरूषाभयामलकमृगलिण्डकाजाम्बबकिपित्थ-बकुल-बदरककेन्धुपीलुपियालपनसन्यग्रोधाश्वत्थपुक्षक पीतनोदुम्बराजमोदश्रृङ्गाटकशंखिनीतिफलासवाःषड्विंशतिः । विदारिगन्धाश्वगन्धाऋष्णगन्धाशतावरीश्यामात्रिवृद्न्तीद्र्वन्ती
translation:
(Page 216 — Charaka Samhita)

Vata, Pitta, and Kapha — what is beneficial for their pacification and what is foremost among the remedies for diseases has also been described chiefly. (verse 36)

The physician who applies this knowledge of treatment with full skill and expertise, and acts accordingly, ever attains both dharma (righteousness) and the enjoyment of desires (kama). (37)

That which accords with the proper path and is pleasing to the mind is pathya (wholesome); that which by rule is unpleasant is apathya (unwholesome). One should observe this distinction. (38)

On the basis of quantity (matra), time (kala), action (kriya), place (bhumi), body (deha), and the distinctions of doshas and qualities — when these factors are severally encountered, the various effects manifest accordingly. (39)

Therefore, both the inherent nature of substances and the factors beginning with quantity have been described as the basis. The physician who desires success should apply treatment with attention to both of these. (40)

Thereupon Agnivesha, having heard the words of the Blessed Atreya, addressed the Blessed Atreya again: "What has been described by you in brief is understood by us. Now please instruct us concisely on the characteristics of asava (fermented preparations) so that we may listen."

The Blessed Atreya then spoke: "O Agnivesha! Grains, fruits, essences, flowers, stems, and leaves are the sources of asava. In summary, know that there are eighty-four types of asava — sura, sauviraka, tushodaka, maireya, medaka, dhanyamla, and the six grain-based vasavas. Among these are those derived from mrdvika (grapes), kharjura (dates), kashmari, dhavana, rajadana, trnasulya, parusa, amalaka, mrgalindaka, jambu, kapittha, bakula, badara, kakandhu, pilu, piyala, panasa, nyagrodha, ashvattha, plaksha, pitana, udumbara, ajamoda, shringataka, shankhini — these are twenty-six fruit-based asavas. Then come those from vidarigandha, ashvagandha, krishnagandha, shatavari, shyama, trivrt, danti, dravanti —

( २१७ )

बिल्वोरुमुकिचत्रमूलैरेकादशमूलासवाः । शालिप्रियकाश्वकर्णचन्दनस्यन्दनखदिरकदरसतपर्णिजुनासनारिमेदतिन्दुकिकिणिहीशमीशुक्तिशिंशपाशिरीषवञ्जुलधन्वनमधूकसारासवाविंशतिः। पञ्चोत्पलनिलनकुमुद-सौगन्धिकपुण्डरीकशतपत्रमधूक-प्रियङ्गुधातकीपुष्पैदेशमाःपुष्पासवाः । इक्षुकाण्डेक्षुदक्षुबालिकापुण्डूकचतुर्थाःकाण्डासवाः। पटोलतादौपत्रासवैद्वौभवतः । तिञ्चकलोधैरलवालुककर्मुकचतुर्थास्तवगासवांभवन्ति । शर्करासवएक एव । इत्येषामासवानामासुतत्वादासवसंज्ञाएवमेषामासवानां चतुरशीतिः परस्परेणासंस्पृष्टा नामासवद्रव्याणामुपनिर्दिष्टाः । द्रव्यसंयोगविभागस्तवेषांबहुविकल्पसंस्कारश्वयथास्वयोनिसंस्कारसंस्कताश्वासवाःस्वंकर्मकुर्वन्तिसंयोगसंस्कारदेशकालमात्रादयश्वभावास्तेषांतेषामासवानांतेते समुपदिश्यन्तेतत्तत्कार्यमिभसमीक्ष्यति ॥ ४१ ॥

इस आत्रेयके वचनको सुनकर फिर भी अग्निवेश भगवान् आत्रेयको बोले- कि यह अर्थ भगवानने केवल उद्देश के अनुसार वर्णन किया, अब हम आसवद्रव्योंके अत्यन्त विस्तारसे, लक्षणको आपके उपदेशद्वारा सुना चाहतेहैं; उस अग्निवेशके प्रति भगवान् आत्रेय बोले, कि धान्य, फल, सार,पुष्प,काण्ड, पत्र, त्वचा ये आसवकी योनि हैं, हे अग्निवेश, संग्रहसे ये आठ और नवभी शर्करा उनमें होतीहैं, उनमें द्रव्यके संयोग करनेसे संख्याके अयोग्य जिस प्रकार अत्यन्त पथ्य आसवोंकी चौरासी ८४ संख्या है उसको तुम,सुनो सुरा,सौवीर, तुषोदक, मैरेय, मेदक, धान्य, अम्ल षष्ठ धान्यके आसव हैं. मुनक्का, खजूर, काश्मर्य, ( केशर ) धन्वन, राजादन, तृण, शूल्य, ( मांस ) परुष, हरड़, आमले, मृगलिण्डिका, जामुन, कैत, बकुल, वेर, कर्कन्धु, पीलु प्रियाल, पनस, वट, पीपल, पिलखन, कपीतन, गूलर, अजमोद, सिंघाडा, शंखिनीका फल, इनके २६ छब्बीस, आसव हैं और विदारगंधा, अश्वगंधा, कृष्णगंधा, शतावर, श्यामा, त्रिवृत, दन्ती, द्रवन्ती, बिल्व, उरुक, चित्रक ये ग्यारह मूलासब हैं; शाल, प्रियक अश्वकर्ण चंदन, स्यन्दन, खदिर, कन्दर, सतपर्ण, अर्जुन, असन, अरिमेध, (खैर) तिन्दुक, किणही, (ओंगा) शमी, शुक्ति, शिंशपा, शिरस,बंजुल,धन्वन,मधुक ये बीस सारा-

Sutrasthana (Chapter on General Principles)
(217)

The eleven-root asava (fermented preparation) is made from bilva, urumuka, and chitraka roots. The twenty-ingredient sara-asava includes shali, priyaka, ashvakarna, chandana, syandana, khadira, kadara, sataparna, arjuna, asana, arimetha, tinduka, kinahi, shami, shukti, shimshapa, shirisha, vanjula, dhvanvana, and madhuka. The flower-asavas are made from the five lotuses — blue lotus, white lotus, kumuda, saugandhika, pundarika — together with shatapatra, madhuka, and priyangu. The four cane-asavas are from ikshukanda, ikshuda, ikshubhalika, and punduka. Two asavas come from patola and leaf preparations. The four tilvaka asavas include lodhra, lavalu, karmuka, and tilvaga. The sharkara (sugar) asava is a single one. Because all of these are prepared by fermentation, they are all called "asava." These eighty-four asavas, not mixing with one another, have been enumerated by name among the asava substances. The combinations, separations, processing methods, purification procedures, and the various preparations of these asavas — their properties of combination, processing, place, time, quantity and natural qualities — are each set forth so that the appropriate effect of each may be considered. (41)

Hearing the words of Atreya, Agnivesha again spoke to the revered Atreya, saying: "The Lord has described this matter only in outline; we now wish to hear in full detail, through your teaching, the characteristics of the asava substances." To Agnivesha, the revered Atreya replied: Grain, fruit, essence (sara), flower, stem (kanda), leaf, and bark — these are the sources (yoni) of asava. O Agnivesha, in brief, these eight, and also nine types of sugar, are found within them. Through the combination of substances with these, in the manner that yields the most wholesome preparations, the number eighty-four is obtained — hear it now. Sura, sauvira, tushodaka, maireya, medaka, and the grain-based sour preparation are the six grain asavas. Munakka (raisins), dates, kashmari (keshar), dhanvana, rajadana, trina, shulya (meat-based), parusa, harada, amla, mriga-lindika, jamun, kait, bakula, ber, karkandhu, pilu, priyal, panasa, vata, pippala, pilakhan, kapitana, gular, ajamoda, singhada, and the fruit of shankhini — these twenty-six are asavas. Furthermore, vidara-gandha, ashvagandha, krishna-gandha, shatavara, shyama, trivrit, danti, dravanti, bilva, uruka, and chitraka — these eleven are the mula-asavas (root-based). Shala, priyaka, ashvakarna, chandana, syandana, khadira, kandara, sataparna, arjuna, asana, arimetha, (khaira), tinduka, kinahi, (onga), shami, shukti, shimshapa, shirasa, vanjula, dhanvana, madhuka — these twenty sara-

सबहैं; पद्म, उत्पल, नलिन, कुमुद, सौगंधिक, पुंडरीक, शतपत्र, मधूक, प्रियंगु, धाईके पुष्प ये दश पुष्पोंके आसव, इक्षुकांड, इक्षु, इक्षुवालिका, पोंडा ये काण्ड केआसवहैं; पटोल ताड ये दो पत्रासवहैं; तिठ्ठक, लोध, एल, बालुक, क्रमुक ये चार त्वचाके आसव होतेहैं. शर्कराका आसव एकहीहै इन आसवोंको इन औषधियोंमें होनेसे आसव संज्ञाहै इस प्रकार ये आसव चौरासी हैं, वे परस्पर विना मिले आसव द्रव्योंके दिखायेहैं इनका द्रव्य संयोग विभागतो अनेक विकल्पसे युक्तहै और संस्कारभी बहु विकल्प और यथायोनि संस्कारसे संस्कृत आसव अपने कर्मको करतेहैं. संयोग, संस्कार, देश, मात्राकाल आदि स्वभाव उन आसवोंके जो २ हैं वे २ तिस २ कार्यकी देखकर भली प्रकार उपदेश किये जातेहैं ॥ ४१ ॥

भवंतिचात्र ।

मनःशरीराग्निबलप्रदानामर्वम शोकारुचिनाशनानाम् । संहर्षणानांभवरासवानामशीतिरुकाच तुरुत्तरैषा ॥ ४२ ॥

इसमें यह श्लोक हैं कि मन, शरीर, अग्नि इनके बल दाताओंकी अस्वप्र शोक अरुचिके नाशकोंकी संहर्षणोंकी और प्रवर आसवोंकी यह चौरासी कही ४२

शरीरयोगप्रकृतौमतानितत्त्वेन

चाहारविनिश्चयोयः । उवाच ज्ञःपुरुषादिकेऽस्मन्मुनिस्तथाग्याणिवरासवांश्चेति ॥ ४३ ॥

इतिअन्नपानचतुष्केयज्ञःपुरुषीयोऽध्यायःसमाप्तः ।

शरीर योगकी प्रकृतिमें जो संमतहै और तत्वसे जो आहारका विनिश्चयहै मुख्य द्रव्य और उत्तम २ आसव ये सब मुनिने यज्ञः पुरुषादिक इस अध्यायमें वर्णन कियेहैं इति ॥ ४३ ॥

अत्र पानचतुष्के यज्ञः पुरुषाध्यायःसमाप्तः ॥ २५ ॥

षड्विंशोऽध्यायः ।

अथातोआत्रेयभद्रकाप्यीयमध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः ।
इति ह स्माह भगवानात्रेयः।

इसके अनंतर आत्रेय भद्रका पीय अध्यायका वर्णन करतेहैं यह भगवान् आत्रेय कहतेहैं कि ॥

आत्रेयोभद्रकाप्यश्शाकुन्तेयस्तथैवच । पूर्णाक्ष्यश्चैवमौद्गल्यो हिरण्याक्षश्च कौशिकः ॥ १ ॥

आत्रेय भद्रकाप्य और शाकुंतेय पूर्णाक्ष मौद्गल्य हिरण्याक्ष कौशिक ॥ १ ॥

यःकुमारशिरानामभरद्वाजःसचानघः । श्रीमान्वाग्योविदश्चैवराजामितमतांवरः ॥ २ ॥

( 218 )
From the Charaka Samhita.

Among them all: Padma, Utpala, Nalina, Kumuda, Saugandhika, Pundarika, Shatapatra, Madhuka, Priyangu, and the flowers of the Dhai plant — these are the ten flower-based asavas (fermented medicinal preparations). Ikshu-kanda, Ikshu, Ikshuvallika, and Ponda — these are the stem-based asavas. Patola and Tada — these are the two leaf-based asavas. Titthhaka, Lodha, Ela, Valuka, and Kramuka — these are the four bark-based asavas. The asava of Sharkara (sugar) is only one. These preparations are called asavas because they are produced within these medicinal substances. Thus these asavas are eighty-four in number. They are shown as asava substances without being mixed with one another. The combination and separation of their constituent substances admits of many variations, and the processing also has many variations; asavas prepared according to their proper method perform their respective functions. The nature of each of these asavas — their combination, processing, region, dose, and timing — are properly instructed after examining what each one is suited for. ॥ 41 ॥

And here are the verses:

These eighty-four asavas, which strengthen the mind, body, and digestive fire, which destroy grief and loss of appetite, which bring joy, and which are the most excellent among fermented preparations — this enumeration of eighty and four more has been given. ॥ 42 ॥

In this verse it is stated: those that give strength to the mind, body, and digestive fire; those that destroy grief and aversion to food; those that bring exhilaration — these eighty-four finest asavas have been enumerated. ॥ 42 ॥

Regarding the determination of food in accord with the true nature of bodily constitution,

The wise sage Yajnya spoke thus in the chapter on Purushadika about the excellent asavas: ॥ 43 ॥

Here in the group of four chapters on food and drink, the chapter called Yajnya-Purushiya is concluded.

Here, in the set of four chapters on beverages, the Yajnya-Purushiya chapter is concluded. ॥ 25 ॥

The Twenty-Sixth Chapter.

Now we shall explain the chapter known as Atreyabhadrakapyiya.
Thus has the venerable Atreya declared.

Following this, the chapter called Atreyabhadrakapyiya is being described. The venerable Atreya speaks thus:

Atreya, Bhadrakapya, Shakunteya, and likewise Purnaaksha, Maudgalya, Hiranyaaksha, and Kaushika. ॥ 1 ॥

Atreya, Bhadrakapya, and Shakunteya, Purnaaksha, Maudgalya, Hiranyaaksha, Kaushika. ॥ 1 ॥

He who is known as Kumarashira Bharadvaja, the sinless one, the illustrious one, learned in speech, and Rajamitamata, the foremost among them. ॥ 2 ॥

सूत्रस्थानम् १।
( २१२ )

और जिसका कुमार शिरानामहै वह पापोंसे रहित भरद्वाज और बुद्धिमानोंमें श्रेष्ठ और श्रीमान् वायोविद राजा ॥२॥
निमिश्वराजावैदेहोबडिशश्चमहामतिः। काङ्कायनश्चवाह्लीकोवाह्लीकिभिषजांवरः ॥ ३ ॥
राजा निमि, वैदेह और महामति बडिश और कांकायन और भिषजोंमें श्रेष्ठ बाल्हीक ॥ ३ ॥
एतेश्रुतवयोवृद्धाजिताात्मानोमहर्षयः । वनेचैवरथरेम्यसमीयुविजिहीर्षवः ॥ ४ ॥
शास्त्र और अवस्थामें वृद्ध ये सब महर्षि संदेहके दूर करनेके अर्थें रमणीक चैत्ररथवनमें आते भये ॥ ४ ॥
तेषांतत्रोपविष्टानामियमर्थवती कथा । बभूवार्थविदांसम्यक्रसाहारविनिश्चये ॥ ५ ॥
वहां बैठे हुये उनके मध्यमें यह अर्थवाली कथा अर्थके ज्ञाताओंमें हुई कि भलीप्रकार रस और आहारका विनिश्चय क्याहै कि ॥ ५ ॥
एकएवरसइत्युवाचभद्रकाप्योयं पञ्चानामिन्द्रियार्थानामन्यतमं जिह्वावैषयिकंभावमाचक्षतेकुशलाः । सपुनरुदकादनन्यइति ६
एकही रसहै यह भद्रकाप्यने कहा जो पांचों इंद्रियोंके विषयोंमें कोईसे

जिह्वाका विषय भाव कुशल कहतेहैं और वह जलसे अन्य नहीं है ॥ ६ ॥
द्वौरसावितिशाकुन्तेयोब्राह्मणश्छेदनीयश्चोपशमनीयश्चेति ॥ ७॥
दो रसहैं यह शाकुंतेय ब्राह्मण कहते भये कि छेदनी और उपशमनीय ॥७॥
त्रयोरसाइतिपूर्णाक्षःमौद्र्ल्यश्छेदनीयोपशमनीयौसाधारणाश्च
तीन रसहैं यह पूर्णाक्षमौद्रल्यने कहा कि छेदनीय, उपशमनीय और साधारण ॥ ८ ॥
चत्वारोरसाइतिहिरण्याक्षःकौशिकःस्वादुहितश्चस्वादुरिहतश्च अरस्वादुरिहतश्चारस्वादुहितश्चेति ९
चार रसहैं यह हिरण्याक्ष कौशिकने कहा कि स्वादु अहित स्वादुहित अस्वादुअहित अस्वादुहित ॥ ९ ॥
पञ्चरसाइतिकुमारशिराभरद्वाजोभौमोदकाग्नेयवायवीयान्तरिक्षाः१०
पांच रसहैं यह कुमारशिरा भरद्वाजने कहा कि भूमि, जल, अग्नि, वायु आकाश इन पांचोंसे उत्पन्न ॥ १० ॥
षड्साइतिवाय्योविवदोराजर्षिःगुरुलघुशीतोष्णस्निग्धरूक्षाः ११
छः रसहैं यह वायोविवदराजर्षिने कहा किगुरु, लघु, शीत, उष्ण, स्निग्ध, रूक्ष ॥ ११ ॥

Sutra-sthana, Chapter 1
(Page 212)

And he whose name is Kumara-shira — that one is Bharadvaja, free from sins, foremost among the wise, and the illustrious king Vayovid. (2)

King Nimi, Videha, Badisha of great intellect, Kankayena, and Bahlika — the foremost of physicians. (3)

These great sages, advanced in learning and in age, who had conquered their souls, came together in the delightful Chaitraratha forest, wishing to resolve their doubts. (4)

While they were seated there, a meaningful discussion arose among those knowers of truth, namely: what is the proper determination regarding rasa (taste/essence) and food? (5)

"There is only one rasa," said Bhadrakapya — meaning that which the wise call the object of the tongue among the five sense-objects, and that is none other than water. (6)

"There are two rasas," said the brahmin Shakunteya — namely, that which cuts (chedaniya) and that which pacifies (upshamaniya). (7)

"There are three rasas," said Purnaksha Maudgalya — namely, that which cuts, that which pacifies, and that which is common (sadharna). (8)

"There are four rasas," said Hiranyaksha Kaushika — namely, palatable and harmful, palatable and beneficial, unpalatable and harmful, unpalatable and beneficial. (9)

"There are five rasas," said Kumara-shira Bharadvaja — namely, those arising from the five elements: earth, water, fire, air, and space. (10)

"There are six rasas," said the royal sage Vayovivada — namely, heavy, light, cold, hot, unctuous, and dry. (11)

( २२० )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।

सप्तरसाइतिनिमवैदेहोमधुराम्ललवणकटुकितककषायक्षाराः १ २
सात रसहैं यह वैदेह निमिने कहः कि मधुर, अम्ल, लवण, कटु, कषाय, तित्त, क्षार ये प्रकटहैं ॥ १२ ॥

अष्टौरसाइतिबडिशधामार्गवोमधुराम्ललवणकटुतित्तककषायक्षाराव्यक्ताः ॥ १३ ॥
आठ रसहैं यह बडिशधामार्गव कहते हैं कि मधुर, अम्ल, लवण, कटु, तित्त, कषाय, क्षार ॥ १३ ॥

अपरिसंख्येयारसाइतिकाङ्कायनोबाह्लीकिमेषगाश्रयगुणकर्मसंस्कारविशेषाणामपरिमेयत्वात् १४ ॥
असंख्य रसहैं यह कांकायन बाह्लीक कहते भये क्योंकि वैद्य आश्रय गुण कर्म संस्कार ये विशेष अपरिमितहैं १४

षडेवरसाइत्युवाचभगवानात्रेयः पुनर्वसुः मधुराम्ललवणकटुतित्तककषायाः । तेषांषण्णांरसानांयोनिरुदकम् । छेदनोपशमनेद्वैकमणी । तयोर्मिश्रीभावात्साधारणत्वंस्वाद्स्वादुताभिकः । द्वौ हिताहितौप्रभावौ । पञ्चमहामूतविकारास्त्वाश्रयाः ॥ १५ ॥
छःहीरसहैं यह भगवान् अत्रेय, पुनर्वसु कहते भये कि मधुर, अम्ल,

लवण, कटु, तित्त, कषाय इन छःओंकी योनिजलहैं छेदन, उपशमन दो कर्म हैं, उनके मिलानेसे साधारणताहै और स्वादु, अस्वादुता, भक्ति, हित, अहित, नामके दो प्रभाव, पांच महाभूतोंके विकारतो आश्रयहैं ॥ १५ ॥

प्रकृतिविकृतिविचारदेशकालवशास्तेषुआश्रयेषुद्रव्यसंज्ञकेषुगुणागुरुलघुशीतोष्णस्निग्धरूक्षाधाः १६ ॥
जो प्रकृति, विकृति, विचार, देश, काल इनके वशहैं उन द्रव्यसंज्ञक आश्रयोंमें गुरु, लघु, शीत, उष्ण, स्निग्ध, रूक्ष आदि गुणहैं ॥ १६ ॥

क्षरणात्क्षारोनासौरसोद्रव्यंतदनेकरससमुत्पन्नमनेकरसंकटुकलवणभूयिष्ठमनेकेन्द्रियार्थसमन्वितंकरणाभिनिर्वृत्तम् ॥ १७ ॥
क्षरणसे क्षार होताहै, वह रस नहीं है, वह द्रव्य अनेक रसोंसे उत्पन्न, अनेक रस कटु, लवण की अधिकतासे अनेक प्रकारका अनेक इन्द्रिय और अर्थसे युक्त करणसे निर्वृत ( पैदा ) होताहै १७

अव्यक्तीभावस्तुखटुरसानांमरूतावनुरसेअनुरससमन्वितेवाद्रव्येऔर रसोंका अव्यक्त होना तो प्रकृत अनुरस वा अनुरससे समन्वितद्रव्योंमेंहै १८

अपरिसंख्येयत्वंपुनरेतेषामाश्रयादीनांभावानांविशेषाणांचाश्रायतेन

From the Charaka Samhita

[Verse 12] Vaideh states that the rasas (tastes) are seven: sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, astringent, and alkaline. These seven tastes are thus enumerated. ॥12॥

[Verse 13] Badisha and Dhāmārgava declare the rasas to be eight: sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, astringent, alkaline, and one additional (indistinct/unmanifest). ॥13॥

[Verse 14] Kānkāyana and Bāhlīka hold that the rasas are innumerable, because the special qualities of the substrates, properties, actions, and transformative processes that serve as their basis are themselves without limit. ॥14॥

[Verse 15] Bhagavān Ātreya Punarvasu declares: the rasas are six only — sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, and astringent. Water is the source of all six. Cutting and pacifying are the two actions. Their mixture produces a common quality, perceived as pleasant or unpleasant taste. There are two effects: beneficial and harmful. The five great elements (mahābhūtas) and their modifications are the substrates. ॥15॥

[Verse 16] In those substrates known as dravyas, governed by natural constitution, modification, thought, place, and time, the qualities heavy, light, cold, hot, unctuous, and dry are present. ॥16॥

[Verse 17] Kṣāra (alkali) arises from the process of flowing/dissolution (kṣaraṇa); it is not itself a rasa. It is a substance arising from many rasas, possessing many tastes, predominantly pungent and salty, connected with multiple sense objects, and produced by a specific process. ॥17॥

[Verse 18] The non-manifestation of other tastes occurs in a substance where the natural (prākṛta) anurasa (secondary taste) or a substance combined with anurasa is present. ॥18॥

( 221 )

[Verse 19:] Therefore otherness is established. [Commentary:] The enumeration of these bases such as the substratum is not fixed; it does not take hold of the specifics of substances, and from that it does not become something different. [19]

[Sanskrit verse:] Because of the predominance of mutual combination among these, the qualities and natures become innumerable. Therefore, the wise do not prescribe the actions of combined tastes. [20]

[Commentary:] Because of the great degree of their mutual combination, their cessation (arising) is not fixed; due to the distinctions among qualities and natures, substances become innumerable. Therefore the wise do not teach the actions of combined tastes. [20]

Keeping that very reason in mind, we shall explain separately the characteristics of the six tastes unmixed with one another. Then, further on, we shall say something about the divisions of substances. All substances arise from the five elements; in this sense they are conscious and non-conscious. Their qualities are sound and so forth, and from heaviness onward up to fluidity — the five actions beginning with emesis have been stated. [21]

[Verse 21 commentary:] Substances are described, beginning with the teacher, up to fluidity — five types of action beginning with emesis are stated. [21]

[Verse 22:] Among these, those substances in which the qualities of heaviness, roughness, hardness, slowness, stability, clarity, density, grossness, and smell predominate are the earthly (prithviya) ones; they are the causes of growth, compactness, heaviness, and stability. [22]

[Commentary:] Among these, heaviness, roughness, hardness, slowness, stability, clarity, density, grossness, smell — those substances in which these qualities predominate are earthly substances; they are the causes of growth, compactness, heaviness, and stability. [22]

[Verse 23:] Those substances in which the qualities of fluidity, oiliness, coldness, slowness, softness, and sliminess predominate are the watery (apya) ones; they are the causes of moistening, lubrication, binding, flowing, and pleasure. [23]

[Commentary:] Those in which fluidity, oiliness, coldness, slowness, softness, and sliminess predominate as their qualities are watery (aqueous). They are the causes of moistening, lubrication, binding, flowing, and pleasure. [23]

[Verse 24:] Those substances in which the qualities of heat, sharpness, fineness, lightness, dryness, clarity, and form predominate are the fiery (agneya) ones; they are the causes of burning, digestion, luster, illumination, and color. [24]

[Commentary:] Those in which heat, sharpness, fineness, lightness, dryness, clarity, and form predominate as their qualities are fiery. They are the causes of burning, digestion, luster, illumination, and color. [24]

( २२२ )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

क्षयग्लानिविचारवैषयलाघवकराणि ॥ २५ ॥

और लघु, शीत, खर, विषद, सूक्ष्म, स्पर्श ये गुण जिनमें अधिकहैं वे वायवीयहैं; वे रूक्षता, ग्लानि, विचार, वैषय, लाघव, इनको करतेहैं ॥ २५ ॥

मृदु लघु सूक्ष्म श्लक्षणशब्दगुणबहुलान्याकाशात्मकानितानिमार्दवसौषिपंयलाघवकराणि ॥ २६ ॥

और मृदु लघु सूक्ष्म श्लक्षण, शब्द, ये गुण जिनमें, अधिकहैं वे आकाशात्मक हैं वे मार्दव, सौषिर्य लाघवके कारकहैं २६

अनेनोपदेशेननानानौषधिभूतंजगतिकिञ्चिद्द्रव्यमुपलभ्यतेतांयुक्तिमर्थश्वतंतमभिप्रेत्यनचगुणप्रभावादेवकार्युकाणिभवन्ति ॥ २७ ॥

इस उपदेश से नाना औषध रूपसे जगत्में किञ्चित् द्रव्य मिलताहै, उस युक्ति और तिस २ अर्थके अभिप्रायसे कुछ गुणके प्रभावसेही कायकारी नहीं होते ॥ २७ ॥

द्रव्याणिहिद्रव्यप्रभावाद्गुणप्रभावाच्चतिस्मस्तिस्मन्कालेतत्तदिधष्ठानमासाद्यतांतांञ्युक्तिंयत्कुर्वन्तिततकर्मयेनकुर्वन्तितद्वीर्यं, यत्रकुर्वन्तितदधिकरणंयदाकुर्वन्तिसकालो यथाकुर्वन्तिसउपायोयत्साधयन्तिततफलम् ॥ २८ ॥

क्योंकि द्रव्य द्रव्यके प्रभावसे गुणके प्रभावसे द्रव्यगुणके प्रभावसे, तिस तिसकालमें तिस तिस अधिष्ठान और तिस तिस युक्तिको प्राप्त होकर, जिसको करतेहैं वह कर्महै जिससे करतेहैं–वह वीर्य जिसमें करते हैं वह अधिकरण जब करतेहैं वह काल जैसे करतेहैं वह उपाय, जिसको, करतेहैं वह फल, होताहै ॥ २८ ॥

भेदश्चैषांत्रिषष्टिविधिविकल्पोद्रव्यदेशकालप्रभावात्तदुपदेक्ष्यामः ॥ २९ ॥

और इनका भेद द्रव्य, देश, कालके प्रभावसे ६३ तिरसठ प्रकारके विकल्पका जोहैं उसका उपदेश करतेहैं कि ॥ २९ ॥

स्वादुरम्लादिभिर्योगंशेषैरम्लाद्यःपृथक् । यानिपञ्चदशैतानिञ्च्याणिहिरसानितु ॥ ३० ॥

स्वादुका अम्ल आदिके संग योग, पृथक् २ अम्ल आदिका शेष रसोंके संग योग ये पंद्रह द्रव्य जो द्विरस होतेहैं ॥ ३० ॥

पृथगम्लादियुक्तस्ययोगःशेषैःपृथगभवेत् । मधुरस्यतथाम्लस्यलवणस्यकटोस्तथा ॥ ३१ ॥

पृथक् २ अम्ल आदिसे युक्तका जो शेष रसोंके संग पृथक् २ योग होताहै, मधुरका, अम्लका, लवणका और कटुका ॥ ३१ ॥

translation:
( 222 )
From the Charaka Samhita

[Verse 25] These qualities — light, cold, rough, clear, subtle, and tangible — when predominant, belong to the air element; they produce emaciation, languor, distraction, sensory dispersion, and lightness. (25)

[Verse 26] The qualities soft, light, subtle, smooth, and sound — when predominant, belong to the ether element; they produce softness, porosity, and lightness. (26)

[Verse 27] By this teaching, there is no substance found anywhere in the world that is not a medicine. Keeping in mind that purpose and its particular intent, it is not by the power of qualities alone that actions are accomplished. (27)

[Verse 28] For substances, through the power of the substance itself, through the power of qualities, and through the power of substance-quality together — arriving at their respective seats at their respective times and obtaining their respective methods — whatever action they perform is called karma (action); that by which they perform it is their potency (virya); that in which they perform it is the locus (adhikarana); when they perform it is the time (kala); how they perform it is the means (upaya); and what they accomplish is the result (phala). (28)

[Verse 29] The distinctions and sixty-three varieties of these, arising from the influence of substance, place, and time — we shall teach those now. (29)

[Verse 30] The combination of sweet with sour and the rest, and separately the combinations of sour and so on with the remaining tastes — these fifteen are the dual-taste combinations of the six tastes. (30)

[Verse 31] The separate combinations of each, starting with sour, joined with the remaining tastes — thus for sweet, for sour, for saline, and for pungent — each yields its own separate combinations. (31)

( २२३ )

त्रिरसानियथासंख्यंद्रव्याण्युक्ता
निर्विंशितिः । वक्ष्यन्तेतुचतुष्के
णद्रव्याणिदशपञ्च ॥ ३२ ॥

ये यथा संख्य बीस २० द्रव्य, त्रिरस कहेहैं; अब चतुष्क रसके पंद्रह द्रव्योंको कहतेहैं ॥ ३२ ॥

स्वाद्वम्लौसिहतौयोगंलवणांयैः
पृथग्गतौ । योगशेषैःपृथकुयातः
चतुष्करससंख्यया ॥ ३३ ॥

किं मिले हुए स्वादु, अम्ल, लवण आदिके संग पृथक् २ योगको प्राप्त होकर शेषोंके संग पृथक् योगको प्राप्त होकर संख्यासे चाररस होतेहैं ॥ ३३ ॥

सिहतौस्वादुलवणौतद्वत्कड्वादि
भिःपृथक् । युक्तौशेषैःपृथग्योगं
यातःस्वादूषणौयथा ॥ ३४ ॥

तिसीप्रकार मिलेहुए स्वादु और लवण कटु आदिसे शेषोंके संग पृथक् योगोंको प्राप्त होकर और तिसी प्रकार मिले हुए स्वादु और कषणभी शेषोंके संयोगसे चार प्रकारके होतेहैं ॥ ३४ ॥

कड्वाघैरम्ललवणौसंयुक्तौसिहतौ
पृथक् । यातःशेषैःपृथग्योगशेषै
रम्लकटूतथा ॥ ३५ ॥

कटु आदिसे संयुक्त अम्ल और लवण दोनों पृथक् २ रसोंसे सहित होकर शेषोंके संग पृथक् २ योगको प्राप्तहोकर और तिसीप्रकार शेषोंके संग अम्ल कटु चार २ होतेहैं ॥ ३५ ॥

युज्यतेतुकषायेणसितिकौलवणो
षणौ । षट्तुपञ्चरसान्याहुरेकैक
स्यापवर्जनात् ॥ ३६ ॥

कषायके योगसे तिक्तसहित लवण कषण चार २ कहेहैं छःरसोंमें एक एक रसके अपवर्जनसे कोई आचार्य पांच रसोंकी कहतेहैं ॥ ३६ ॥

षट्चैवैकरसानिन्युरेकंषड्रसमेव
तु । इतित्रिषष्टिद्रैव्याणांनिनिर्दिष्टा
रससंख्यया ॥ ३७ ॥

षट् एकरसके और एक षड्रसका इसप्रकार सातरस कोई कहतेहैं यह रसोंकी संख्यासे ६३ तिरसठ द्रव्य कहे ३७

त्रिषष्टिःस्यात्वसंख्येयारसानुरस
कल्पनात् । रसास्तरतमाभ्यां
तांसंख्यामिभपतन्तिहि ॥ ३८ ॥

रस और अन्यरसकी कल्पनासे ये तिरसठ असंख्य होतेहैं तारतम्यसे अभ्यास किये रस संख्याको प्राप्त होतेहैं ॥ ३८॥

संयोगाःसतपञ्चाशत्कल्पनातुत्रिष
ष्टिधा । रसानांतरयोग्यत्वाक्ल
िपतारसिचिन्तकैः ॥ ३९ ॥

इनके संयोग ५७ सतावनहैं और कल्पनातो उनमें रसोंकी योग्यतासे रसके चिन्तकोंने ६३ तिरसठ प्रकारकी कीहै ३९॥

किच्चदेकोरसःकल्प्यःसंयुक्ताश्चर
साःकिंचित् । दोषौषधादीन्सञ्चि
न्त्यिभिषजासिद्धिमिच्छता ४०॥

translation:
Page 223 — Sthana (a section of the Charaka Samhita), continuing the enumeration of substances classified by taste (rasa).

Verse 32:
The twenty substances distributed according to the three-taste classification have been stated. Now the fifteen substances belonging to the four-taste group will be described.

Commentary 32: The twenty substances arranged by their respective tastes have been named. Now the fifteen substances of the four-taste group are described.

Verse 33:
Sweet and sour, taken together, combine with the group including salt and so forth, each separately; then combining with the remaining tastes separately, the count of four-taste combinations is arrived at.

Commentary 33: Sweet, sour, and salt, meeting in combination and then uniting separately with the remaining tastes, yield four types of combinations in count.

Verse 34:
Sweet and salt, similarly combining separately with pungent and so on, and then combining with the remaining tastes, just as sweet and pungent do — so the four types arise.

Commentary 34: In this manner, sweet and salt joined with pungent and the rest, combining separately with the others, and similarly sweet and astringent joining with the rest, produce four types each.

Verse 35:
Sour and salt, combined with pungent and the rest, each separately, combine with the remaining tastes; similarly sour and pungent yield four combinations each.

Commentary 35: Sour and salt, joined with pungent and others, meeting separately with the remaining tastes — and in the same manner sour and pungent with the others — produce four each.

Verse 36:
Astringent combines with bitter along with salt and pungent, giving four each. Some teachers say that removing one taste at a time from the six gives five-taste combinations.

Commentary 36: With astringent joining bitter together with salt and pungent, four each are counted. Some teachers describe five-taste combinations by removing one of the six tastes at a time.

Verse 37:
Some teachers have proposed six single-taste substances and one six-taste substance, making seven in this way. The count of substances thus arrives at sixty-three according to taste classification.

Commentary 37: Six single-taste substances and one substance with all six tastes — thus some say seven. By this reckoning, sixty-three substances are enumerated.

Verse 38:
The sixty-three may indeed become innumerable through the various hypothetical taste-combinations. But by applying the principle of gradation (more or less intensity), the count returns to a manageable number.

Commentary 38: Through the combination of one taste with others the sixty-three become innumerable; but by gradations and systematic study, the count of tastes is brought under comprehension.

Verse 39:
The combinations number fifty-seven; but by reckoning the possible taste-fitness, thinkers on taste have set the number at sixty-three.

Commentary 39: Their combinations are fifty-seven, but with consideration of the suitability of tastes, scholars of taste-theory have established the count as sixty-three.

Verse 40:
Sometimes a single taste should be conceived alone, and sometimes tastes in combination — the physician who desires success should reflect on the doshas, medicinal substances, and all related factors accordingly.

सिद्धिका अभिलाषी वैद्य कहीं एक
रसकी कई संयुक्त रसोंकी दोष और
औषध आदिके विचारसे कल्पना करै॥०

द्रव्याणिद्विरसादीनिसंयुक्तांश्वर
सान्बुधः । रसानेकैकशश्चैवक
ल्पयन्तिगदान्प्रति ॥ ४१ ॥

बुद्धिमान मनुष्य द्विरस आदि द्रव्योंकी
और संयुक्त रसोंकी और एक २ रसोंकी
रोगके भेदसे कल्पना करतेंहैं ॥ ४१ ॥

यःस्याद्रसिवकल्पज्ञःस्याच्चदोष
विकल्पवित् । नसमुहेद्विकाराणां

जो वैद्य रसके विकल्पको और दोषके
विकल्पको जानताहै वह विकारोंके हेतु
लिंग और उपशान्तियोंमें मोहको प्राप्त

व्यक्तःशुक्तस्यचादौंचरसौद्रव्य
स्यलक्ष्यते । विपर्य्ययेणानुरसो
रसोनास्तिहिसप्तमः ॥ ४३ ॥

और प्रथम प्रकटतासे भुक्त द्रव्यमें
द्रव्यका रस दीखताहै और विपर्ययसे
अनुरस होताहै सप्तम रसकोई नहींहै॥४३

परापरत्वेयुक्तिश्चसंख्यासंयोगएव
च । विभागश्चपृथक्क्षपरिमाण
मथापिच ॥ ४४ ॥

परत्व,अपरत्व, युक्ति, संख्या, संयोग,
विभाग, पृथक्क और परिमाण॥ ४४ ॥

संस्कारोऽभ्यासइत्येतेगुणाज्ञेयाः

संस्कार अभ्यास ये पर आदि गुण

चिकित्साके लक्षणोंसे उनका वर्णन

देशकालवयोमानपाकवीर्य्यरसा

देश, काल, अवस्थामान, पाक,

संख्यास्याद्गिणतंयोगःसहसंयोग
उच्यते । द्रव्याणांद्वन्द्वसर्वैककं

गणितकी संख्या, सह संयोगको
योग कहतेंहैं वह द्रव्योंके द्वन्द्व, सर्व और
एकके कमैसे उत्पन्नहै और नित्यहै॥४७॥

विभागस्तुविभक्तिस्तुवियोगोभा
गशोग्रहः । पृथक्त्वंस्यादसंयो

विभक्तिको विभाग और भाग के

translation:
(Page 224 — from the Charaka Samhita)

A physician who aspires to success should, through careful consideration of a single rasa (taste/substance), of the faults of combined rasas, and of medicines, form a proper conception of treatment.

Verse 41:
One should understand substances having two or more rasas combined, and also each rasa individually, and form therapeutic plans according to the type of disease. A wise person conceives of dravyas (substances) with two or more rasas, of combined rasas, and of individual rasas, classifying them according to the nature of the disease. (41)

Verse 42:
One who knows the variations of rasa and the variations of the doshas will never be confused regarding the causes, signs, and alleviation of diseases. (42)

Verse 43:
In a substance that has been consumed, the primary rasa of the dravya is apparent first; by way of secondary sequence the anu-rasa (secondary taste) appears; there is no seventh rasa. (43)

Verse 44:
Superiority (paratva), inferiority (aparatva), yukti (reasoning/appropriateness), sankhya (number), samyoga (combination), vibhaga (division), prithaktva (separateness), and parimana (quantity/measure) — these are the eight qualities to be understood. (44)

Verse 45:
Samskara (refinement/processing) and abhyasa (practice/repetition) — these, along with para (superiority) and the other qualities mentioned, are to be known as gunas. These are the means to therapeutic success, and their characteristics will be described in the context of treatment. (45)

Verse 46:
In matters of desa (place/region), kala (time), vaya (age), mana (measure), paka (digestion/cooking), virya (potency), rasa (taste), and so forth — that which properly applies the principle of superior and inferior relationship (parāparatva-yojana) is called yukti (appropriate reasoning). (46)

Verse 47:
Number (sankhya) arises from counting. What is called samyoga (combination) is the joining together of dravyas — occurring as pairs (dvandva), as all together, or one by one — and is eternal. (47)

Verse 48:
Vibhakti (division/separation) is called vibhaga; the taking of a portion is called viyoga (disjunction); the state of non-combination is called prithaktva (separateness); and manifoldness of character is called vailakshanya (distinctness/difference). (48)

Parimana (measure/quantity) is that by which things are measured; samskara (processing/refinement) is the operation [that transforms a substance — text continues on next page].

सूत्रस्थानम् ।
( २२५ )

मतम् । भावाभ्यसनमभ्यासः
शीलनंसततक्रिया ॥ ४९ ॥

और मानको परिमाण और करणको
संस्कार कहते हैं, भावोंके अभ्यासको
और निरंतरक्रियाको शीलन कहते
हैं ॥ ४९ ॥

इतिस्वलक्षणैरुक्तागुणाःसर्वेपरा
दयः । चिकित्सायैरविदितैर्नैय
थावत्प्रवर्त्तते ॥ ५० ॥

ये संपूर्णपरआदि गुण अपने २
लक्षणोंसे कहे जिनके जाने बिना यथार्थ
चिकित्सा प्रवृत्त नहीं होती ॥ ५० ॥

गुणागुणाश्रयानोकास्तस्माद्रस
गुणान्विभषक् । विद्याद्रव्यगुणा
न्कर्तुरिभभायाःपृथग्विधाः ॥ ५१ ॥

गुण, गुणोंके आश्रय नहीं कहे हैं.
तिससे वैद्य रसके गुणोंको द्रव्यके गुण
जानै, क्योंकि कतिके अभिप्राय भिन्न
भिन्न प्रकारके होते हैं ॥ ५१ ॥

अतश्प्रकृतिबुद्ध्देशकालान्त
राणिच । तन्त्रकर्तुरिभभायानु
पायांश्चार्थमादिशेत् ॥ ५२ ॥

इससे प्रकृति, देश, कालान्तरोंको
जानकर और उनमें कतिके अभिप्राय
और उपायोंको जानकर चिकित्साको
कहै ॥ ५२ ॥

परश्चातःभवक्ष्यन्तेरसानांषड्विभ

कयः। षट्पञ्चभूतप्रभवाःसंख्या
ताश्चयथारसाः ॥ ५३ ॥

इससे परे रसोंके छः विभागाको
कहते हैं; जैसे छः रस पांच भूतोंसे उत्पन्न
कहे हैं–इति ॥ ५३ ॥

सौम्याःखल्वापोऽन्तरिक्षप्रभवाः
प्रकृतिशीतालघ्वश्चअव्यक्त
साश्वतास्तवन्तरिक्षादुभश्यमाना
भष्टाश्वपञ्चमहाभूतविकारगुणस
मन्विताजङ्गमस्थावराणांमृतानां
मूर्तिरिभभीणयन्ततासुमूर्तिषु
इङिरमूच्छिन्तरसाः ॥ ५४ ॥

अन्तरिक्षसे उत्पन्न जल सौम्य हैं
प्रकृतिसे शीतल, लघु और अव्यक्त
रस हैं वे अन्तरिक्षसे पड़नेके समय और
पड़कर पांच महाभूतोंके गुणोंसे युक्तहो-
कर जंगम, स्थावर भूतोंकी मूर्तियोंको
उत्पन्न करते हैं जिन मूर्तियोंमें छःओंरस
प्रतिबिंबित होते हैं ॥ ५४ ॥

तेषांषण्णांरसानांसोमगुणातिरेका

दम्लःसलिलाग्निभूयिष्ठत्वाद्वणो

translation:
Sutra-sthana (Section on Fundamental Principles)
(Page 225)

Opinion: The repeated practice of mental states is called abhyasa (practice); the continuous and constant performance of an action is called shilana (habituation). ॥ 49 ॥

And the measurement of a standard and the refinement of an instrument are called samskara; the repeated practice of mental states and the continuous performance of action are called shilana. ॥ 49 ॥

Thus all the gunas (qualities), beginning with para (superior), have been described by their own defining characteristics. Without knowing them, proper medical treatment cannot proceed. ॥ 50 ॥

Since gunas are not themselves the substrate of gunas, the physician should understand the gunas of a rasa (taste/essence) as the gunas of the substance; for different authorities hold different views on the matter. ॥ 51 ॥

Therefore, having understood the prakriti (constitution), desha (place), and the intervals of time, and knowing the intentions and the remedies of the treatise's author, one should prescribe treatment. ॥ 52 ॥

Now hereafter will be described the six divisions of the rasas (tastes):

The six tastes, originating from the five great elements, are counted and named accordingly. ॥ 53 ॥

The waters that arise from the atmosphere are indeed of a soma (lunar/cooling) nature; by natural constitution they are cool, light, and of subtle, imperceptible taste. As they fall from the atmosphere and upon falling, becoming endowed with the qualities of the five great elements, they generate the forms of mobile and immobile beings; in those forms the six tastes are reflected and manifest. ॥ 54 ॥

Among those six tastes: sweet taste arises from the predominance of the soma (lunar) quality; sour arises from the predominance of earth and fire; salt arises from the predominance of water and fire; pungent arises from the predominance of air and fire; bitter arises from the predominance of air and ether; astringent arises from the predominance of air and earth. Thus the sixfold nature of these tastes is produced. ॥ 55 ॥

text:
( २२६ )

उन छः ओंरसोंके मध्यमें चंद्रमाके गुणकी अधिकतासे मधुर रस होता है, पृथ्वी और अग्निकी अधिकतासे अम्ल, जलकी अधिकतासे लवण, वायु और अग्निकी अधिकतासे कटु, वायु और आकाशकी अधिकतासे तिक्त, पवनके कषायकी अधिकतासे कषाय, रस उत्पन्न होता है ऐसे उन रसोंका षट्त्व (६भेद) उत्पन्न हुए ॥ ५५ ॥

न्यूनातिरेकिविशेषान्महाभूतानामिवजङ्गमस्थावराणांनानावर्णकृतिविशेषाःषड्ऋतुकत्वाञ्चकालस्यउत्पन्नोमहाभूतानांन्यूनातिरेकिविशेषः ॥ ५६ ॥

न्यूनता और अधिकताके विशेषसे जैसे जंगम, स्थावर महा भूतोंको नाना वर्ण और आकार विशेष होतेंहैं और छः ऋतुरूप कालसेभी महाभूतोंका न्यून और अधिक विशेष उत्पन्न होताहै ५६

तत्राग्निमारुतात्मकारसाःप्रायेणोर्ध्वभाजोलाघवात्पुवकत्वाञ्चवायोरूर्ध्वज्वलनत्वाञ्चवह्नेःसिलिलपृथिव्यात्मकास्तुप्रायेणाधोभाजःपृथिव्यागुरुत्वाञ्चिघ्नगत्वाचोदकस्यव्यामिश्रात्मकास्तुपुनरुभयतोभागभाजः ॥ ५७ ॥

उनमें अग्निमारुतात्मक (रूप) जो रसहैं, वे प्रायः ऊपरके भागी होतेंहैं,

क्योंकि वायु लघु और चलनकर्मीहै और अग्निका ज्वलन ऊपरकोहै, जल और पृथिवी आत्मकतो प्रायः अधोभागी होतेंहैं क्योंकि पृथिवी गुरुहै और जल, निम्नस्थलगामीहै और जो रस व्यामिश्र (मिले) रसात्मकहैं वे उभयभाजीहैं ॥ ५७ ॥

तेषांषण्णांरसानामेकैकस्ययथाद्रव्यगुणकर्माण्यनुव्याख्यास्यामः।तत्रमधुरोरसःशरीरसात्म्याद्रसरुधिरमांसमेदोऽस्थिमज्जौजःशुकाभिवर्द्धनआयुष्यःषडिन्द्रियप्रसादनोबलवर्णकरःपित्तविषमारुतघ्नस्तृष्णाप्रशमनस्तव्च्यःकेश्यःकण्ठ्यःप्रीणनोजीवनस्तर्पणःक्लेहनःस्थैर्यकरःक्षीणक्षतसन्धानरोघ्णांमुखकण्ठौष्ठतालुप्रह्लादनोदाहमूर्च्छाप्रशमनःषट्पदिपिपीलिकानामिष्टतमःस्निग्धःशीतोगुरुश्च५८

उन छः रसोंमें एक२ के द्रव्य गुणके अनुसार कर्मोंका वर्णन करतेंहैं उनमें मधुर, रस शरीरका सात्म्य होनेसे रस, रुधिर, मांस, मेदा, अस्थि मज्जा और शुक्र इनका वर्द्धक आयुका दाता छः इंद्रियोंका प्रसादक वर्ण, बलकारी पित्त, विष और मारुतका नाशक, तृष्णाका प्रशमन, त्वचा, केश, कंठ इनका हितकारी प्रीणन, जीवन,
translation:
( 226 )

Among those six tastes, sweet taste arises from the predominance of the qualities of the Moon; sour from the predominance of Earth and Fire; salt from the predominance of Water; pungent from the predominance of Wind and Fire; bitter from the predominance of Wind and Space; and astringent from the predominance of Wind's astringency. In this way the six-fold division of tastes is produced. ॥55॥

Just as variations in excess and deficiency of the great elements produce diverse colors and forms among moving and stationary beings, so too through the six seasons — which constitute time — variations of excess and deficiency among the great elements arise. ॥56॥

Those tastes that are composed predominantly of Fire and Wind tend to move upward, because Wind is light and mobile, and Fire flames upward. Those composed of Water and Earth tend to move downward, because Earth is heavy and Water flows to lower ground. Those tastes that are mixed in nature partake of both directions. ॥57॥

We shall now describe, one by one, the substances, qualities, and actions of each of those six tastes. Among them, sweet taste — being agreeable to the body's constitution — promotes and increases the seven bodily constituents: plasma, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, and semen. It is life-prolonging, pleasing to the six sense organs, enhances complexion and strength, destroys excess bile, poison, and wind, allays thirst, is beneficial to skin, hair, and throat, nourishes, sustains life, satisfies, moistens, gives stability, heals the wasted and the wounded, is pleasing to the mouth, throat, lips, and palate, pacifies burning and fainting, and is most agreeable to bees and ants. It is unctuous, cool, and heavy. ॥58॥

( २२७ )

translation:
( 227 )

[Verse 58]
[Madhura rasa — sweet taste — is] nourishing, unctuous, stabilizing, a healer of the wasted and wounded; it is supremely pleasing to the nose, mouth, lips, throat, and palate; it is unctuous, cool, and heavy. ॥ 58 ॥

[Verse 59 — Sanskrit]
That same rasa, even though endowed with all these qualities, when used to excess for a single purpose, gives rise to obesity, softness, laziness, excessive sleep, heaviness, loss of appetite, weakness of digestive fire, excessive growth of the tissues of the mouth, throat, and flesh, cough, catarrh, cold fever, distension, sweetness of the mouth, belching, loss of consciousness and voice, goiter of the neck, cervical swellings, swelling of the scrotum, swelling of the throat, coating of the bladder and anal passage, eye diseases, non-suppuration, and other such disorders born of kapha. ॥ 59 ॥

[Commentary in Hindi]
That rasa, even though endowed with such qualities, when used for only one purpose in excess, produces the following kapha-disorders: obesity, softness, laziness, excessive sleep, heaviness, loss of desire for food, weakness of digestive fire, extreme growth of the tissues of the mouth, throat, and flesh, cough, catarrh, sluggishness, cold fever, distension, sweetness of the mouth, belching, loss of consciousness and voice, goiter of the neck, elephantiasis, swelling of the throat, distension of the bladder, and coating of the anus, eye diseases, non-suppuration — all such disorders are produced by the aforementioned rasa. ॥ 59 ॥

[Verse 60 — Sanskrit]
Amla rasa (sour taste) stimulates appetite in food; kindles the digestive fire; nourishes the body; awakens the mind; strengthens the sense organs; increases strength; normalizes the downward movement of vata; nourishes the heart; stimulates salivation in the mouth; draws down what has been eaten; generates moisture; and is pleasing, light, hot, and unctuous. ॥ 60 ॥

[Commentary in Hindi]
Sour taste stimulates appetite in food; it kindles the digestive fire, nourishes the body, enlivens the mind, strengthens the sense organs, increases strength, normalizes the movement of vata, nourishes the heart, stimulates salivation in the mouth, draws down food that has been consumed, produces moisture; it is light, hot, and unctuous. ॥ 60 ॥

[Verse 61 — Sanskrit]
That same rasa, even endowed with all these qualities, when used excessively for a single purpose, causes the teeth to tingle and ache, makes the eyelids close, causes the body hair to stand on end, liquefies kapha, aggravates pitta, corrupts the blood, burns the flesh, makes the body flaccid, and causes swelling in those who are emaciated, wounded, or weak. Moreover, it aggravates wounds caused by cuts, blows, bites, falls, crushing, pounding, and the three types of injuries; and because of its burning nature, it scorches the throat, chest, and heart. ॥ 61 ॥

text:
( २२८ )

वह उन गुणोंका एकभी अत्यंत उपयोग किया हुआ दांतोंको आनन्द और तृत्त करताहै,नेत्रोंका संमीलन, लोमोंका संभीज करताहै, कफका विलापन, (गलाना) पित्तका वर्द्धन करताहै,रक्तको दूषित करताहै, मांसकादाह, कायाको शिथिल, क्षीण, कृश, दुर्बलोंके शोथकी वृद्धिको करताहै और क्षत, अभिहत, दष्ट, भग्र, शूल, च्युत, अवमृदित, परिसर्पित, मर्दित, छिन्न, विद्ध, उत्पिष्ट आदिको पचाताहै और अग्निके स्वभावसे कण्ठ उर हृदयको दग्ध करताहै ॥ ६१ ॥

लवणोरसःपाचनःकुेदनोदीपन
ऋयावनश्छेदनोभेदनस्तीक्षणःस
रोविकासयधःसंसयवकाशकरो
वातहरःस्तम्भबन्धसंघातिवधम
नःसर्वेरसप्रत्यनिकभूतआस्यंविश्रावयति, कफंविष्यन्दयति, मागँश्छोथयति,सर्वशरीरावयवान्यृदुकरोति, रोचयत्याहारमाहारयोगीचात्यर्थंगुरुःस्निग्धउष्णश्च

लवणरस पाचन, कुेदन, दीपन, च्यावन, छेदन, भेदन और तीक्ष्ण,सर, विकाशि, अधःसंसी, अवकाशकारक, वातहारी, स्तंभ, बंध, संघात इनका नाशक, सब रसोंका विरोधी यह आस्यका स्रावण, कफका विष्यंदन,

मागोंका शोधन, सब शरीरोंके अवयवोंका मृदुकरण, आहारका रोचन करताहै, आहारका योगी, अत्यंत गुरु नही, स्निग्ध, उष्णहै ॥ ६२ ॥

सएवंगुणोऽप्येकएवात्यर्थमुपयुज्यमानः पित्तंकोपयति, रक्तंवर्द्धयति, तर्षयति, मूच्छंयति, ताप यति, दाहयति,कृष्णाितमांसानि, प्रगालयतिकुष्ठानि,विषंवर्द्धयति, शोफान्स्फोटयति,दन्ताञ्छयावित पुंस्त्वमुपहन्ति,इन्द्रियाण्युपरुणद्धि, वलीपलितखालित्यमापादयतिच,लोहितपित्चाम्लपित्तवीसर्पवातरक्तविचर्चिकेन्द्रलुतप्रभृतीन्विकारानुपजनयति॥ ६३॥

एवं गुणका एकभी लवणरस, अत्यंत उपयोग, किया हुआ–पित्तको कुपित करताहै, रक्तको बढाताहै, तृषाकारकहै मूच्छा, ताप, दाह इनको करताहै, मांसोंको सुखाताहै, कुष्ठोंको गालताहै, विषकी वृद्धि करताहै,शोफोंको फोड़ताहै, दांतोंको काले करताहै, पुंस्त्वका नाश करताहै, इन्द्रियोंको रोकताहै, बली (पालित्य)और खालित्य,अर्थात्–त्वचाका गिराना और गंजकरना करताहै, इनको और लोहितपित्त, अम्लपित्त, वीसर्प, वातलोहित, विचर्चिका, इन्द्रलुत आदि विकारोंको उत्पन्न करताहै ॥ ६३॥
translation:
( 228 )

When any one of those qualities is used in excess, it gives pleasure and satisfaction to the teeth, causes the eyes to close, makes the body hair stand, melts and dissolves kapha, increases pitta, contaminates the blood, causes burning of the flesh, makes the body lax, emaciated, thin; increases swelling in the weak; and it digests and heals wounds, injuries, bites, fractures, colic, displacements, bruises, spreading lesions, crushings, cuts, piercings, and pressures — yet by the nature of fire it burns the throat, chest, and heart. (Verse 61)

The saline taste is digestive, stimulating, appetite-kindling, relaxing, cutting, splitting, sharp, promoting flow, dilating, creating space, wind-dispelling, destroying stiffness, binding and compaction; it is antagonistic to all other tastes; it causes secretion in the mouth, liquefies kapha, purifies the channels, softens all the parts of the body, promotes relish for food; it is compatible with food, not excessively heavy, unctuous and warm.

The saline taste is digestive, stimulating, appetizing, loosening, cutting, splitting, sharp, promoting flow, dilating, downward-moving, space-creating, wind-dispelling, and a destroyer of stiffness, binding and compaction; it is antagonistic to all tastes; it causes salivation, liquefies kapha,

purifies the channels, softens all the body parts, promotes relish for food; it is compatible with food, not excessively heavy, unctuous and warm. (Verse 62)

Even these same qualities, when the saline taste alone is used in extreme excess, aggravate pitta, increase the blood, cause thirst, fainting, fever, and burning; they dry up the flesh, melt away skin diseases (kushtha), increase poison, rupture swellings, blacken the teeth, destroy virility, block the sense organs, cause wrinkling, greying, and baldness — that is, falling and loss of hair — and produce diseases such as hemorrhagic pitta disorders, acid pitta, spreading skin eruptions, vata-blood disorders, eczema, ringworm (indraluptha), and other such conditions. (Verse 63)

translation:
(Page 229 — Charaka Samhita, continuing a discussion of the six tastes and their properties)

[Verse 64 — Properties of Pungent (Katu) Taste:]

The pungent taste purifies the mouth; kindles the digestive fire; dries up ingested food; sharpens the sense of smell; purges the eyes; stimulates and clarifies the sense organs; destroys sluggishness, swelling, accumulation, urticarial eruptions, discharges, oiliness, perspiration, moisture, and waste products; stimulates appetite; destroys itching, ulcers, and worms; cuts through muscular accumulations; breaks up clots of blood; opens the channels; and pacifies phlegm. It is light, hot, and dry. (64)

[Prose commentary in Hindi:]
The pungent taste purifies the mouth; kindles the digestive fire; dries ingested food; stimulates the sense of smell; purges the eyes; stimulates the sense organs; destroys sluggishness, swelling, accumulation, skin eruptions, discharges, oiliness, sweat, moisture, and waste; stimulates appetite for food; destroys itching, ulcers, and worms; cuts through flesh and clots of blood; opens the channels; pacifies phlegm. It is light, hot, and dry. (64)

[Verse 65 — Excess use of a single taste:]

Even a taste that has all these good qualities, if used exclusively and to excess, through the effect of its digestion-transformation (vipaka) destroys virility; and through the effect of its inherent quality and potency causes delusion, lassitude, exhaustion, wasting, fainting, numbness, darkness, and dizziness; burns the throat; generates heat in the body; diminishes strength; produces thirst; and through an excess of wind and fire causes distress, intoxication, trembling, pricking pain, and splitting sensations — thereby producing disorders of wind (vata) in the feet, arms, sides, back, and other parts of the body. (65)

[Hindi prose commentary:]
Even a single taste, when used excessively, through the effect of its vipaka destroys virility; through the effect of its rasa and virya causes delusion, lassitude, exhaustion, wasting, fainting, numbness, darkness, and dizziness; burns the throat; generates heat in the body; diminishes strength; produces thirst; and through excess of wind and fire causes confusion, intoxication, distress, trembling, pricking, and splitting — thereby producing disorders of vata in the feet, arms, sides, back, and other places. (65)

[Verse 66 — Properties of Bitter (Tikta) Taste:]

The bitter taste, though itself not palatable, removes distaste for food; destroys poison and worms; relieves fainting, burning, itching, skin diseases, and thirst; firms up the skin and flesh; is fever-reducing; kindles the digestive fire; promotes digestion; purifies breast milk; is scraping (lekhana) in action; and absorbs and dries up moisture, fat, muscle-fat, marrow, lymph, pus, sweat, urine, feces, bile, and phlegm. It is dry, cold, and light. (66)

translation:
( 230 )
In the Charaka Samhita
Digitized By Sidhanta Sangitri Gyaan Kosha

The bitter taste is itself something that diminishes relish; it destroys loss of appetite, poison, and worms; it pacifies fainting, burning sensation, itching, skin diseases, and thirst; it stabilizes the skin and muscle tissue; it is fever-reducing, kindler of digestive fire, digestive, and a purifier of breast milk; it is also a scraping agent, and it dries up moisture, fat, adipose tissue, marrow, lymph, pus, sweat, urine, feces, bile, and phlegm; and it is dry, cold, and light in quality. (66)

This same taste, even when it is a single rasa but used in excess, due to its dry, rough, and clear nature, causes extreme drying of rasa (plasma), blood, muscle, fat, bone, marrow, and semen; it brings about roughness of the channels; it diminishes strength; it causes emaciation and confusion; it dries up the face; and it produces other vata disorders. (67)

The astringent taste is pacifying, binding, consolidating, compressing, healing, drying, and stambhana (arresting); it pacifies phlegm and blood-bile disorders; it produces dryness in the body; it is dry, cool, and heavy in quality. (68)

This same taste, even when it is a single rasa but used excessively, causes drying of the mouth, distress to the heart, bloating of the abdomen, suppression of speech, obstruction of the channels, darkening of complexion, destruction of virility, premature aging, retention of gas, urine, and feces; it causes emaciation, depression, thirst, and stiffness; and due to its rough, clear, and dry nature, it produces vata disorders such as hemiplegia, convulsions, opisthotonus, and other such conditions. (69)

translation:
Mantrasthana (Chapter on Formulations)
(Page 231)

These six tastes, when each is used separately in proper measure, are beneficial to the body and to one's wellbeing in the world. When used improperly or in excess, they become harmful. Therefore, a learned physician should employ them only in proper measure and for the purpose of benefit. (70)

And on this topic there are the following verses:

A substance whose potency (virya) is cooling and whose taste and post-digestive effect (vipaka) are both sweet — among those, the sour and the hot, and whatever is hot and pungent — these are their respective qualities. (71)

A summary of the qualities of all these tastes is to be set forth through the teaching on tastes, and those whose qualities are opposite to their potency are to be explained through their post-digestive transformation. (72)

Just as milk, just as ghee, just as chanaka (chickpea) and chitraka (leadwort) — so also all others of this kind are to be described by the physician in terms of their taste. (73)

Some substances that are sweet may be slightly heating and astringent as well as bitter — for example, the great five-root group (brihat panchamula), and the flesh of aquatic animals. (74)

Saindhava (rock salt), although a salt, is not heating; amalaka (Indian gooseberry), though sour, is similarly not heating; and agarwood, guduchi, and the bitter group — these bitter substances are said to be heating. (75)

Some sour substances are astringent and binding, while others that are sour are aperient and separating — for example, kapittha (wood apple) is binding, while amalaka (gooseberry) is aperient. Pippali (long pepper) and nagara (dry ginger) are aphrodisiac, while pungent substances are said to be non-aphrodisiac. (76)

है और अम्ल मध्यहै और लवण अन्त्य
है ये दोनोंरस स्नेहमें कहतेहैं ॥ ७९ ॥

मध्यःकषावराःशैत्यात्कषायस्वा
दुतिक्तकाः । तिक्तात्कषायोम
धुरःशीताच्छीततरःपरः । स्वादु
गुरुत्वादिधकःकषायाल्लवणोऽ
वरः ॥ ८० ॥

शीततासे मध्यम और कर्षणमें अवर,
कषाय, स्वादु, तिक्तक होतेहैं तिक्तसे
कषाय मधुरहै और शीतसे अतिशीत
श्रेष्ठ है कषायसे गुरु होनेसे स्वादु अधिक
है और लवण अवरहै ॥ ८० ॥

अम्लात्कटुस्ततस्तिक्तोलघुत्वादु
त्तमोमतः । केचिछ्घूनामवरिम
च्छंतिलवणंरसम् ॥ ८१ ॥

अम्लसे कटु और उससे तिक्त लघु
होनेसे उत्तम मानहै कोई तो लघुरसोंमें
लवण रसको अवर मानते हैं ॥ ८१ ॥

गौरवेलाघवेचैवसोऽवरस्तूभयोर
पि । परश्चातोविपाकानांलक्षणं
सम्प्रवक्ष्यते ॥ ८२ ॥

और वह गौरव और लाघवमें
दोनों अवरहैं, इससे आगे विपाककेलक्ष-
णोंको कहतेहैं ॥ ८२ ॥

कटुतिक्तकषायाणांविपाकःश्रा
यशःकटुः । अम्लोऽम्लंपच्यते
स्वादुमधुरंलवणस्तथा ॥ ८३ ॥

कटु, तिक्त, कषाय इनका विपाक
प्रायः कटु होताहै, अम्ल का पाक
अम्ल, स्वादु और लवणका मधुर
होताहै ॥ ८३ ॥

मधुरोलवणाम्लौचस्निग्धभावाच
योरसाः । वातमूत्रपुरीषाणांमा
योमोक्षेसुखामताः ॥ ८४ ॥

translation:
( 232 )

[Verse 77]
Therefore, in the teaching of tastes, one should not prescribe all substances indiscriminately. Kashaya (astringent) is constipating and cooling — haritaki (chebulic myrobalan) being otherwise understood. Thus, in teaching about tastes, one should not prescribe all substances [uniformly]. (77)

[Verse 78]
Even when two substances are seen to have the same taste, their properties may differ due to other qualities in the substance. Because of dryness (rookshata), among the astringent and dry substances, kashaya is the best, and katu (pungent) is middling. (78)

[Verse 79]
Among hot substances, tikta (bitter) is the lowest, while lavana (salt) surpasses due to its heat-producing quality; amla (sour) is middling and katu (pungent) comes last. Among unctuous (snigdha) substances, madhura (sweet) is the best, amla is middling, and lavana is last. These two tastes are said to promote unctuousness (sneha). (79)

[Verse 80]
Due to their cooling nature, kashaya, madhura, and tikta are middling and inferior in terms of astringency. Compared to tikta, kashaya is more cooling, and madhura is even cooler than kashaya. Madhura exceeds kashaya because of its heaviness, while lavana is inferior. (80)

[Verse 81]
After amla, katu, and then tikta are considered superior due to lightness. Some, however, hold lavana to be the lowest among the light tastes. (81)

[Verse 82]
And lavana is inferior in both heaviness and lightness. After this, the characteristics of vipaka (post-digestive transformation) will now be explained. (82)

[Verse 83]
The vipaka of pungent (katu), bitter (tikta), and astringent (kashaya) tastes is generally pungent. The vipaka of sour (amla) is sour, while the vipaka of sweet (madhura) and salty (lavana) is sweet. (83)

[Verse 84]
Sweet, salty, and sour tastes, by virtue of their unctuous quality, facilitate the easy elimination of vata, urine, and feces — this is considered beneficial. (84)

मधुर और लवण, अम्ल ये तीनों
रस स्निग्धस्वभावहैं और प्रायः वात,
मूत्र और मल इनके मोक्षमें सुखके
दाता कहेहैं ॥ ८४ ॥

कटुतिक्तकषायास्तुरूक्षभावाञ्च
योरसाः । दुःखाविमोक्षेदश्यन्ते
वातविण्मूत्रेतसाम् ॥ ८५ ॥

कटु, तिक्त, कषाय, येतीनों रस
रूक्ष स्वभावहैं और वात, मल, मूत्र,
वीर्य इनके मोक्षमें, दुःख दातारैं ॥८५॥

शुकहाबद्धिविण्मूत्रोविपाकोवात
लःकटुः । मधुरःसृष्टिविण्मूत्रोविपाकेकफशुक्लः ॥ ८६ ॥

कटुरस शुक्रका नाशक, मल,
मूत्रका बन्धक, विपाकमें वातलहै. मधु-
रस मलमूत्रका सृष्टा, विपाकमें कफ
शुक्रका वर्धकहैं ॥ ८६ ॥

पित्तरुत्सृष्टिविण्मूत्रःपाकेऽम्लःशु
क्कनाशनः । तेषांगुरुःस्यान्मधुरः
कटुकाम्लावतोऽन्यथा ॥ ८७ ॥

अम्लरस पित्तकारी, मलमूत्रका,
सृष्टा और पाकमें शुकनाशकहै; इन
सबके मध्यमें मधुररस गुरुहै और
कटुक और अम्ल इससे अन्यथा
( लघु ) है ॥ ८७ ॥

विपाकलक्षणस्यालपमध्यभूयरत्व
मेवच । द्रव्याणांगुणवैशेष्यात्
तत्रोपलक्षयेत् ॥ ८८ ॥

विपाकके लक्षणका अल्प, मध्य
और अधिकताको द्रव्यके गुणोंकी विशे
षतासे तहां तहां देखैं ॥ ८८ ॥

तीक्ष्णरूक्षंमृदुस्निग्धंलघुष्णगुरु
शीतलम् । वीर्यमष्टिविधंकेचित्केचिद्विविधमास्थिताः ॥ ८९ ॥

और तीक्ष, रूक्ष, मृदु, स्निग्ध, लघु,
उष्ण, गुरु, शीतल यह आठ प्रकारका
वीर्य कोई कहतेहैं और कोई शीत उष्ण
के भेदसे दो प्रकारका कहतेहैं ॥ ८९ ॥

शीतोष्णमितिवीर्यन्तुक्रियतेये
नयाक्रिया। नावीर्यंकुरुतेकिंचित्सर्वावीर्यकृताक्रिया ॥ ९० ॥

जिससे जो क्रिया किया जाय वह
वीर्य होताहै वीर्यके बिना बीज कुछ नहीं
करसकता सब क्रिया वीर्यकी की हुई
होतीहै ॥ ९० ॥

रसोनिपातेद्रव्याणांविपाकःकर्मनिष्ठयां । वीर्येयावदधीवासाञ्चिपाताचोपलभ्यते ॥ ९१ ॥

द्रव्योंके निपातमें रस और कर्मंमें
टिककर विपाक जबतक अधिवास और
निपातसे वीर्यको प्राप्त होतेहैं ॥ ९१ ॥

रसवीर्यविपाकानांसामान्येन
स्यलक्ष्यते । विशेषःकर्मणाञ्चैव
प्रभावस्तस्यचरमृतः ॥ ९२ ॥

रस, वीर्य, विपाक इनमें जिसकी
सामान्यता दीखे और कर्मोंका विशेष
जो दीखताहै वह उसका प्रभाव कहाहैं।

translation:
Digitized By Siddhamatra Gyaan Kosha ( 233 )

Sweet, salty, and sour — these three tastes are unctuous (snigdha) in nature, and they are said to be promoters of ease in the elimination of wind, urine, and feces. || 84 ||

The tastes pungent, bitter, and astringent are dry (ruksha) in nature; they cause difficulty in the elimination of wind, feces, urine, and semen. || 85 ||

Pungent, bitter, and astringent — these three tastes are dry in nature and cause difficulty in the elimination of wind, feces, urine, and semen. || 85 ||

The pungent taste, in its vipaka (post-digestive effect), is vata-producing, suppresses feces and urine, and destroys semen. The sweet taste promotes the flow of feces and urine in its vipaka, and increases kapha and semen. || 86 ||

The pungent taste destroys semen, suppresses feces and urine, and in vipaka increases vata. The sweet taste promotes feces and urine, and in vipaka increases kapha and semen. || 86 ||

The sour taste, in its vipaka, is pitta-producing, promotes feces and urine, and destroys semen. Among all of these, sweet taste is heavy (guru), while pungent and sour are otherwise (light, laghu). || 87 ||

The sour taste promotes pitta, promotes feces and urine, and in digestion destroys semen. Among all of these, the sweet taste is heavy, while pungent and sour are otherwise (light). || 87 ||

The characteristic of vipaka — whether mild, medium, or pronounced — should be understood in each case according to the particular qualities of the substance. || 88 ||

The special qualities of vipaka — whether lesser, middling, or greater — are to be recognized in each place according to the particular qualities of the substances. || 88 ||

Sharp, dry, soft, unctuous, light, hot, heavy, and cold — some declare potency (virya) to be of these eight kinds; others hold it to be of two kinds, namely cold and hot. || 89 ||

And sharp, dry, soft, unctuous, light, hot, heavy, and cold — these eight kinds of potency some authorities enumerate, while others describe only two kinds: cold and hot. || 89 ||

That by which an action is accomplished is called potency (virya). Without potency nothing can be done; every action is brought about by potency. || 90 ||

That by which an action is performed is virya. Without virya, nothing can be accomplished; all actions are the result of virya. || 90 ||

At the moment of contact of substances with the body, rasa (taste) operates; vipaka (post-digestive effect) operates at the conclusion of digestion; and virya (potency) is perceived throughout, from the moment of contact to digestion. || 91 ||

In substances, when taste, potency, and post-digestive effect are similar in general, their specific difference in action is explained by prabhava (inherent special potency). || 92 ||

Taste, potency, and post-digestive effect — where their general similarity is seen, and where a particular difference in action is observed, that is called the prabhava of that substance.

translation:
(Page 234 — Charaka Samhita)

Verse 93: Chitraka (Plumbago) is pungent in taste (rasa), pungent after digestion (vipaka), and hot in potency (virya). In the same way, it is by the specific power (prabhava) of Danti (Baliospermum montanum) and Jamal-gota root that they cause purgation in humans. (93)

Verse 94: That a poison is called "poison-destroying" — the reason for this lies in prabhava alone. Similarly, that it causes upward or downward movement — that too is the effect of prabhava. (94)

Verse 95: The various twofold actions of gems worn on the body are also produced by their prabhava. Therefore, prabhava is considered beyond ordinary reasoning and not to be analyzed by mere logic. (95)

Verse 96: A substance performs its action sometimes by rasa (taste), sometimes by virya (potency), sometimes by guna (quality), sometimes by vipaka (post-digestive transformation), and sometimes by prabhava (specific power). (96)

Verse 97: Virya overcomes rasa and vipaka, and prabhava overcomes all three of these. The natural strength of a substance lies in the balance of its rasa and other qualities. (97)

Verse 98: Thus vipaka, virya, and prabhava have all been properly described. (98)

Verse 99: Next, the knowledge of the six rasas (tastes) will be described. The sweet taste is recognized by the sensations of unctuousness, nourishment, pleasure, and softness experienced in the mouth. (99)

Verse 100: The sweet taste seems to coat and pervade the mouth. The sour taste is recognized by the setting of the teeth on edge, increased salivation in the mouth, sweating, heightened sensitivity of the mouth, and a burning sensation in the mouth and throat when the sour substance is consumed. (100)

[Text continues:] It dissolves, moistens, flows, and produces lightness...

तेहैं ॥ १०५ ॥

तमुवाचभगवानात्रेयः । देहधा
तुमत्यनीकभूतानिद्रव्याणिदेहधा
तुविरोधमापायन्तेपरस्परविरुद्धा
निकानिचित्संयोगात्संस्काराद्प
राणिदेशकालमात्रादिभिश्थापरा
णितथाभ्वभावादपराणि १०६ ॥

उसके प्रति भगवान् आत्रेय बोले
कि देह धातुके प्रत्यनीक विपरीत जो
द्रव्य हैं वह देह और धातुके विरोधको
प्राप्त करते हैं और कोई संयोगसे परस्पर
विरुद्ध हैं कोई संस्कारसे कोई देश काल
मात्रा आदिसे और तैसेही कोई स्वभावसे
विरोधी होजाते हैं ॥ १०६ ॥

translation:
Page 235

[Verse 101]
That which quickly dissolves in the mouth, which is of the nature of fire (agneya) and saline, and which causes salivation and a sense of lightness in the mouth — know that to be the Lavana (salty) rasa (taste). || 101 ||

[Commentary 101]
That which, melting in the mouth, quickly produces discharge, lightness, and salivation — by this sign of dissolution in the mouth, know it to be the salty taste. || 101 ||

[Verse 102]
That which acutely stimulates and pains the sense organs on contact, which burns the mouth and causes discharge from the nose and eyes — that is called Katu (pungent). || 102 ||

[Commentary 102]
That which causes pain in the tongue, produces a piercing sensation on contact, burns the mouth, and causes discharge from the nose and eyes — that is called the pungent taste. || 102 ||

[Verse 103]
That which on contact destroys the sense of taste and is itself not pleasant, but which causes clarity, dryness, and a certain refreshing effect in the mouth — that is called Tikta (bitter). || 103 ||

[Commentary 103]
That which on contact destroys the sense of taste, is not itself pleasant, and causes clarity (vaishadya), dryness, and a feeling of refreshment in the mouth — that is called the bitter taste. || 103 ||

[Verse 104]
That which produces clarity, numbness, and heaviness in the tongue, which seems to bind the throat, and which is particularly astringent and causes coughing — that is called Kashaya (astringent). || 104 ||

[Commentary 104]
That taste which produces clarity, numbness, and heaviness in the tongue, as though binding the throat, and which is especially productive of coughing — that taste is called the astringent taste. || 104 ||

[Verse 105 context]
After Bhagavan Atreya had spoken thus, Agnivesha said: O Bhagavan! What you have spoken regarding substances and actions, in accord with true meaning, has been heard. But I wish to hear from you a detailed teaching on the characteristics of antagonistic (viruddha) dietary combinations, even if only in summary. || 105 ||

[Commentary 105]
As Bhagavan Atreya spoke thus, Agnivesha said: O Lord! Your words concerning the subject of substances and actions, rich in true meaning, have been heard. But I wish to hear from you, in detail, the teaching already given regarding the characteristics of antagonistic dietary factors. || 105 ||

[Verse 106]
Then Bhagavan Atreya replied: Substances that are opposed to the bodily tissues (dhatus) bring about opposition to those tissues. Some are mutually opposed by combination (samyoga), some by processing (samskara), some by place (desha), time (kala), quantity (matra), and so forth; and others by their very inherent nature become antagonistic. || 106 ||

[Commentary 106]
Bhagavan Atreya said: Those substances which are contrary to the bodily tissues lead to opposition against the body and the tissues. Some are mutually antagonistic by combination, some by preparation, some by place, time, or quantity, and likewise some become antagonistic by their inherent nature. || 106 ||
