( २३६ )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।
Digitized By Siddhanta Gangotri Gyaan Kosha

पयुज्यन्तेतेषामेकदेशंवैरोधिकम
धिकरुत्योपदेक्ष्यामः ॥ १०७ ॥
उनमें जो भोजनके विषय अधिकतर
उपयोगी हैं उनका जो विरोधी एक देश
उसके अधिकारसे उपदेश करतेहैं १०७॥

नमत्स्यान्पयसासहाभ्यवहरेदुभ
यंह्येतन्मधुरंमधुरविपाकान्महाभि
ष्यन्दिशीतोष्णत्वाद्विरुद्धवीर्यं
विरुद्धवीर्यंत्वाच्छोणितप्रदूषणा
यमहाभिष्यन्दित्वात्मार्गोपरोधा
यच ॥ १०८ ॥
दूधके संग मत्स्योंको भक्षण न
करें क्योंकि ये दोनों मधुर मधुर हैं
विपाकसे शीतोष्ण महाअभिष्यन्दी
हैं विरुद्धवीर्य होनेसे विरुद्धवीर्य हैं
शोणितको दूषित करनेके लिये महाभिष्य
न्दी होनेसे मार्गोंके उपरोधकारी हैं १०८

तदनन्तरमात्रेयवचनमनुनिशम्य
भद्रकाप्योऽग्निवेशमुवाच। सर्वा
नेवमत्स्यान्पयसासहाभ्यवहरेत्
अन्यत्रैकस्माचिलिचिमात् । स
पुनःशकलीसर्वतोलोहितराजिः
रोहितप्रकारःश्रायोभूमौचरितत
श्वेतपयसासहाभ्यवहरेन्निःसंशयं
शोणितजानांविबन्धजानांवाव्या
धीनामन्यतमंअथवामरणंप्रामुया
दिति ॥ १०९ ॥

उसके अनन्तर आत्रेयकी अनुमतिसे
भद्रकाप्य अग्निवेशको बोले, कि-एक
चिलिचिम मत्स्यको छोड़कर संपूर्ण
मत्स्योंको दूधके संग भोजन करें, क्यों-
कि वह शाकलि और सर्वतः लोहित
राजि (पंक्ति) और लोहितप्रकार-
रको शाकलि कहते हैं और वह प्रायः
भूमिमें विचरताहै यदि उसको दुधके
संग भक्षण करें तो शोणितसे उत्पन्न वा
विबन्धसेउत्पन्न व्याधियोंके मध्यमें कोईसी
व्याधिको अवश्य प्राप्त होताहै ॥ १०९॥

नेतिभगवानात्रेयः । सर्विनेवम
त्स्यान्पयसाभ्यवहरेद्विशेषतस्तु
चिलिचिमंसहिमहाभिष्यन्दितम
त्वात्स्थूललक्षणतरानेतान्व्या
धीनुपजनयत्यामिवषमुदीरयति
च ॥ ११० ॥

यह बात नहीं यह भगवान् आत्रेय
कहतेहैं, कि-सबही मत्स्योंको दूधके
संग न खाय और चिलिचिमको विशे-
षकर भक्षण न करें, क्योंकि वह अत्यन्त
महाभिष्यन्दी होनेसे स्थूललक्षणवाली
इन व्याधियोंको पैदा करताहै और
अत्यन्त आमविषको बढाताहै ॥११०॥

ग्राम्यानूपौदकपिशितानिमथुति
लगुडपयोमाषमूलकबिसैर्विरूढ
धान्यैश्वनैकधाअथात् । तन्मूल

translation:
( 236 )
From the Charaka Samhita

We will now teach a portion of the incompatible uses of those items. || 107 ||
Among the dietary items most commonly used, we instruct regarding those that are incompatible in even one respect. 107.

One should not eat fish together with milk, for both are sweet in taste and sweet in post-digestive effect; being great producers of excess bodily secretions, cold-hot in potency, and of mutually incompatible potencies — this incompatibility of potency leads to the corruption of blood and, due to producing excessive secretion, to the obstruction of the bodily channels. || 108 ||
One should not eat fish with milk because both are sweet and sweet in post-digestive effect; they are great producers of excess secretion; being of incompatible potency they corrupt the blood, and being great promoters of excess secretion they obstruct the bodily channels. 108.

Then, having listened to the words of Atreya, Bhadrakapya spoke to Agnivesha: One may consume all fish together with milk, except for one — the chilichima fish. That fish has red lines all over its body, is of the rohita type, and generally moves on the ground; if it is eaten with milk, one will certainly contract some disease — either one arising from blood disorders or one arising from obstruction. || 109 ||

"Not so," said the Venerable Atreya. All fish should not be consumed with milk, and in particular the chilichima fish, because it is an extraordinarily great producer of excess secretion and thereby gives rise to these diseases in their most pronounced form, and greatly increases raw toxins in the body. || 110 ||

text:
मत्रस्थानम् ।
Digitized By Siddanta Gangiri Gyaan Kosha
( २३७ )

लघूकतामैनिमण्यमथवामरणमाभोति ॥ ११९ ॥

ग्राम्य और अनूप जलके मांसको मधु, तिल, गुड, दुग्ध, उड्द, मूलक, विष इनके संग और स्वयं उत्पन्न अन्नोंके संग मिलाकर, न खाय उसका मूल यहहै, कि बाधिरता, अन्धता, वेपथु,(कंप) जड़ता, वाणीकी मूकता,मैनिमण्य,अथवा,मरणको प्राप्त होताहै ११९

नपौष्करंरोहिणीकंवाशाकंनकपोतान्सार्षपतैलभृष्टान्मधुपयोभ्यांसहाभ्यवहरेत् । तन्मूलंहिशोणिताभिष्यन्दधमनीणितचयापस्मारशंखकगलगण्डरोहिणीकानामन्यतमंप्रामोत्यथवामरणमिति ॥ ११२ ॥

पौष्कर वा रोहिणीके शाकको वा कपोतोंको सरसोंके तैलमें भुनकर मधु वा दुग्धके संग भक्षण न करै, उसका मूल यहहै, कि शोणितका अभिष्यन्द, धमनिका नाश, अपस्मार, शंखक, गल-गण्ड, रोहिणीक, इनमेंसे कोईसी व्याधिको वा मरणको प्राप्त होताहै ॥ ११२॥

नमूलकलशुनकृष्णगन्धार्जेकसुमुखसुरसादीनिभक्षयित्वापयःसेव्यंकुष्ठाबाधभयात् ॥ ११३॥

और मूली,लहसन,कृष्णगन्धा,अर्जेक, सुमुख, सुरसा आदिको भक्षण करिके, दूधको कुष्ठ होनेके भयसे न पीवे॥११३

नवास्तुशाकंनिलकुचंपकंमधुपयोभ्यांसहोपयोज्यम् । एतद्विमरणायाथवाबलवर्णतेजोवीर्य्योपरोधायालघुव्याधयेषाण्ड्यायच ११४

वथुएके शाकको पके हुए लिकुचको मधु और दूधके संग भक्षण न करै क्योंकि यह मरणके लिये अथवा बल वर्ण, वीर्य, तेज इनके उपरोधके लिये महाव्याधि और षंडताके लिये होता है ॥ ११४ ॥

तदेविलकुचपकंनमाषसूपगुडसपिंभिःसहोपयोज्यंवैरोधकत्वात्॥

और उसी पके हुए लिकुचको उड़दकी दाल गुड, घीके संग न खाय क्योंकि वे परस्पर विरोधी हैं ॥११५॥

तथाश्रातकमातुलुङ्गलिकुचकरमर्दमोचदन्तशठबदरकोशाश्रमव्याम्बवकपित्थतिन्तड़ीकपारावताक्षोटपनसनालिकेरदाडिमामलकान्येवम्प्काराणिचान्यानि सर्वेचाम्लंद्रव्यमद्रवंचपयसासहविरुद्धम् ॥ ११६ ॥

तिसी प्रकार आघातक, मातुलुंग, लिकुच, करमंद, मोचदन्त, शठबदर, कोशाघ्रभव्य, जाम्बव, कैत, तिन्तिनीक, पारावत, अकरोट, पनस, नालिकेर, दाडिम, आमले ये और इस प्रकारके
translation:
Chapter on Regulations (237)

[Verse 119]
Mixing the meat of domestic and marshy animals with honey, sesame, jaggery, milk, black gram, radish, and poison, or eating them together with spontaneously grown grains, should be avoided. The consequences of such consumption are: deafness, blindness, trembling (palsy), rigidity of the body, muteness of speech, debility of the senses, or even death. [119]

[Verse 112]
One should not eat the vegetables of Poushkara or Rohini, or pigeons, after frying them in mustard oil, together with honey or milk. The root cause of this prohibition is that such combinations lead to hemorrhage, destruction of blood vessels, epilepsy, temporal headache, goiter, diphtheria (rohini), or any one of these diseases, or death. [112]

[Verse 113]
After eating radish, garlic, krishnagandha, arjaka, sumukha, surasa and similar substances, one should not drink milk, out of fear of causing leprosy (kushtha). [113]

[Verse 114]
The fresh vegetable called vastushaka, the fruit lichee (likucha), and champaka should not be used together with honey and milk. The reason is that this combination either leads to death, or obstructs strength, complexion, vitality, and virility, or causes major disease, or leads to impotence. [114]

[Verse 115]
Similarly, the ripe lichee (likucha) should not be eaten together with black gram soup, jaggery, and ghee, because they are mutually incompatible (viruddha). [115]

[Verse 116]
Similarly, aghata, matulunga, likucha, karamarda, mochadanta, shathbadara, koshaghrabhavya, jambava, kapittha, tintidika, paravata, akrota, panasa, nalikera, dadima, amalaka — these and all such sour substances, as well as all sour substances that are not liquid, are incompatible when consumed with milk. [116]

And in the same manner, aghata, matulunga, likucha, karamanda, mochadanta, shathbadara, koshaghrabhavya, jambava, kaita, tintiniaka, paravata, akrota, panasa, nalikera, dadima, amalaka — these and other such substances...

( २३८ )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।
Digitized By Siddhanta &Gangotri Gyaan Kosha

अन्यपदार्थ और सब प्रकारका द्रव,
अद्रव, अम्ल, दुग्धके संग विरुद्धैं १ १ ६.
कंगुवरकमकुष्ठककुलत्थमाषनि
प्पावाःपयसासहिविरुद्धाःपञ्चोत्
तिकाशाकंशार्करोमरेयोमधुचस
होपयुक्तंविरुद्धंवातञ्चातिकोपय
ति ॥ १ १ ७ ॥
कंगु, वरकम्, कुष्ठक, कुलथी, उड्द,
निष्पाव ये दूधके संग विरुद्ध हैं, पञ्चो-
त्तिरिकाका शाक शर्कराका मैरेय और
मधु-ये संग भोजन किये हुए विरुद्ध हैं
और वातके अत्यन्त कोपकारी हैं १ १ ७॥

हारिद्रकःसर्षपतैलभृष्टोविरुद्धिप
तञ्चातिकोपयति पायसोमन्था
नुपानोविरुद्धः । उपोदिकातिल
कलकिसद्धाहेतुरतीसारस्य १ १ ८

सरसोंके तेलमें भुनी हलदी विरुद्ध
पित्तको कुपित अतीव करती है, मंथके
अनुपानसे पायस विरुद्ध है और पोईके
शाक तिलके कलकमें सिद्ध हुए अतिसारके
हेतु होते हैं ॥ १ १ ८ ॥

बलाकावारुण्याकुल्माषैरपिपि
विरुद्धा । सैवशूकरवसापिरभृष्टास
योव्यापादयति ॥ १ १ ९ ॥
वारुणी और कुल्माषोंके संग, बला-
काभी विरुद्धहै और वही शूकरकी
वसामें भुनी हुई शीघ्रही मरण करती
है ॥ १ १ ९ ॥

मायूरमांसमेरण्डसीसकासक्तमेर
ण्डाग्निभृष्टंसयोव्यापादयति १ २ ०
मयूरका मांस एरण्डके सीसकमें
मिलकर और एरण्डकी अग्निमें पककर
शीघ्र मरण करता है ॥ १२० ॥

तदेवभस्मपांसुपिरद्धवस्तंसक्षौद्रं
मरणाय ॥ १२१ ॥
और वही भस्म और पांशुसे अष्ट
( भुना ) हुआ सहत सहित मरणके
लिये होताहै ॥ १२१ ॥

हारीतकमांसंहारिद्राग्निभृष्टंसयो
व्यापादयति । मत्स्यतैलनिस्ता
डनिसिद्धाःपिप्पल्यस्तथाकाकमा
चीमधुचमरणाय ॥ १ २२ ॥
मत्स्यके तैलमें पकाई पीपल और
काकमाची और मधु मरणके लिये
होतीहै ॥ १ २२ ॥

मधुचोष्णमुष्णार्तस्यचमधुमर
णाय ॥ १ २ ३ ॥
उष्ण मधु और उष्णके रोगीको
मधु मरणके लिये होतेहैं ॥ १२३ ॥

मधुसिपिंषीतुल्येमधुवारिचान्तरि
क्षंसमतुलंतमधुपुष्करबीजंमधुपीत्वो
ष्णोदकंभछातकौष्णोदकम् १ २ ४
और तुल्य घृत और मधु और
आकाशका जल ये तुल्यहों और मधु,
पुष्करबीज, मधुपीकर उष्णोदक, भछा-
तक और उष्णोदक ॥ १२४ ॥

translation:
( 238 )
From the Charaka Samhita

[Continuing the enumeration of incompatible substances:]

Other substances, and all types of liquid, non-liquid, sour — these are incompatible with milk. (116)

Kangu, varaka, kushthaka, kulattha, udda, and nishpava — these are incompatible with milk. The vegetable of panchottirika, sugar with maireya liquor, and honey — these taken together are incompatible and extremely aggravating to vata. (117)

Turmeric fried in mustard oil is incompatible and greatly aggravates pitta. Payasa (milk-pudding) is incompatible when taken with mantha as an after-drink. Poi vegetable cooked in sesame paste causes diarrhea. (118)

Balaka is also incompatible with varunee and kulmasha. That same balaka, when fried in pig's fat, causes death quickly. (119)

Peacock flesh mixed with castor-oil residue (lead/sesame pressed in castor) and cooked over a castor-wood fire causes death quickly. (120)

That same preparation, when mixed with ash and dust, along with honey, becomes lethal. (121)

Haritaka (chebulic myrobalan) flesh roasted over turmeric fire causes death. Pippali (long pepper) cooked in fish oil along with kakamachi and honey is lethal. (122)

Hot honey, and honey given to one suffering from heat conditions, is lethal. (123)

Equal quantities of ghee and honey are fatal; rainwater equal in measure to honey; honey followed by drinking hot water; bhallataka (marking nut) with hot water. (124)

SUTRA-STHANA
(Chapter 239)

[Verse 125]
Taka (a preparation), siddha (cooked preparations), kampipitaka, paryushita (stale food), kachamachi, angara (charcoal-cooked), shulya (roasted meat), and bhasa (a bird) — these are declared as incompatible (viruddha) foods as specified by the preceding questions.

Commentary 125: In the context of matta (fermented), siddha (cooked), kampipitaka, and stale food; kachamachi, meat roasted on charcoal, and the bhasa bird — these are incompatible substances as shown in response to the question.

[Verse 126]
Now follow the verses on this topic:
Whatever food, having become vitiated, fails to expel the doshas from the body, and whatever group of foods does not remove them — all of that is only harmful.

Commentary 126: These verses state that any substance which, becoming impure, does not eliminate vitiated doshas from the body, but rather retains them — all such substances are merely harmful.

[Verse 127]
Also, with regard to region, time, digestive fire, suitability and unsuitability, wind and other factors, preparation, potency, constitution, and sequence of use —

Commentary 127: Whatever is determined by region, time, digestive fire, what is suitable or unsuitable, wind (vata) and other humors, method of preparation, potency, state of the bowel, and sequence —

[Verse 128]
Whatever is incompatible through avoidance, treatment, processing, and combination — that which is contrary to the proper method of the editor (sampadaka) does not produce benefit.

Commentary 128: What is incompatible through avoidance and treatment, through processing and combination — whatever is contrary to the proper procedural rules is not beneficial.

[Verse 129]
What is regionally incompatible: in arid (dhanva) regions, dry and sharp substances; in marshy (anupa) regions, unctuous and cold medicinal substances — whatever is prescribed contrary to these is incompatible.

Commentary 129: What is incompatible with regard to region: in arid (dhanva) land, dry and sharp substances, and in marshy (anupa) land, unctuous and cold medicines — their use is incompatible.

[Verse 130]
What is temporally incompatible: consuming cold and dry substances in the cold season, and consuming pungent and hot substances in the hot season — this is incompatible with respect to time.

Commentary 130: Consuming cold and dry substances, and in the cold and hot seasons consuming pungent and hot substances — this is incompatible with the season.

[Verse 131]
What is incompatible with respect to digestive fire: whatever is not in accordance with the fire — whether among the four or twenty-five types — is incompatible. Honey and ghee taken in equal measure are incompatible by reason of dose.

Commentary 131: Whatever does not correspond to the nature of one of the four types of digestive fire is incompatible with that fire. Honey and ghee taken in equal measured quantities are mutually incompatible.

[Verse 132]
For a person accustomed to pungent and hot things, consuming sweet and cold substances — that is suitability-incompatibility (satmya-viruddha); and what is incompatible through fire and other factors —

अग्नि आदिसे विरुद्ध सात्म्य विरुद्ध कहाताहै ॥ १३२ ॥

यासमानगुणाभ्यासविरुद्धान्नौषध किया। संस्कारतोविरुद्धन्तयद्रोज्यंविषवद्रजेत् ॥ १३३ ॥

समान गुण और अभ्यासके विरुद्ध जो अन्त और औषधकी किया वह और जो भोजनके अनंतर विषकी समान होजाय वह संस्कारविरुद्ध कहाताहै १३३

ऐरण्डसीसकासकंशिखिमांसंत थैविहि । विरुद्धंवीर्य्यतोज्ञेयंवीर्य्यतःशीतलात्मकम् ॥ १३४ ॥

और एरण्डके शीसक (तेलमें) मिलाहुआ मयूरका मांसभी तिसीप्रकार संस्कार विरुद्ध होताहै और वीर्यसे शीतल रूप पदार्थको ॥ १३४ ॥

तत्संयोज्योष्णवीर्य्येणद्रव्येणस हसेव्यते । क्रूरकोठस्यचात्यल्पं मंदवीर्य्यमभेदनम् ॥ १३५ ॥

उष्ण वीर्य द्रव्यके संग मिलाकर जो सेवन किया जाय वह वीर्यमें मन्द वीर्यसे विरुद्ध जानना और क्रूर कोष्ठ मनुष्यको अत्यंत अल्पवीर्यमें मन्द और अभेदक ॥ १३५ ॥

मृदुकोठस्यगुरुचभेदनीयंतथाव हु । एतत्कोठिविरुद्धन्तुविरुद्धं स्यादवस्थया ॥ १३६ ॥

औषध और मृदुकोठको गुरु भेदक औषध का जो सेवन वह कोठको विरुद्ध होताहै ॥ १३६ ॥

श्रमव्यपायव्यायामसक्तस्यानिलकोपनम् । निद्रालसस्यालसस्य भोजनंश्लेष्मकोपनम् ॥ १३७ ॥

श्रम, व्यवाय, व्यायाम इनमें आसक्त मनुष्यको वातकोपन औषधिका निद्राके अलसको और अलस मनुष्यको श्लेष्म, कोपन औषधिका जो भक्षण वह अवस्थासे विरुद्ध होताहै ॥ १३७ ॥

यच्चानुत्सृज्यविण्मूत्रंभुंकेयश्चानुभुक्षितः । तच्चकर्मिविरुद्धंस्यायचातिक्षुद्दशानुगः ॥ १३८ ॥

और जो मलमूत्र, किये बिना भोजन करताहै और जो क्षुधाके बिना खाताहै जो अत्यंत क्षुधाके वश होकर खाताहै वह कर्म विरुद्ध होताहै ॥ १३८ ॥

परहार्षविरुद्धन्तुवराहादीन्निषेव्य यत् । सेवेतोष्णंघृतादींश्चपीत्वा शीतंनिषेवते ॥ १३९ ॥

वराह आदिको भक्षण करिके उष्णका सेवन करै और घृत आदिको पीकर शीतका सेवन करै, वह आहारके विरुद्ध होताहै ॥ १३९ ॥

विरुद्धंपाकतश्चापिदुष्टदुदारुसाधितम् । अपक्तण्डुलात्यर्थपक दग्धंचयद्भवेत् ॥ १४० ॥

translation:
( 240 )
From the Charaka Samhita

[132] That which is contrary to fire and to one's habitual practice is called Satmya-viruddha (incompatibility with one's constitution).

[133] Food and medicine that are contrary to one's habitual qualities, or that become like poison after eating — such is called Samskara-viruddha (incompatibility through preparation). The food or medicine that after consumption becomes equivalent to poison is known as contrary through processing.

[134] The flesh of a peacock mixed with castor-oil (sesame oil) is likewise contrary through preparation, and substances that are cold in potency —

[135] — when combined with a substance hot in potency and consumed together, know that to be incompatible in terms of potency. For a person of hard bowel constitution, a very mild-potency substance that does not cause purgation is also incompatible.

[136] For a person of soft bowel constitution, a heavy purgative medicine is likewise incompatible with the bowel. This is known as Kotha-viruddha (bowel incompatibility). Such incompatibility may also arise due to the state or condition of the person — this is called Avastha-viruddha (state incompatibility).

[137] For a person engaged in exertion, sexual activity, or exercise, consuming a vata-aggravating substance is incompatible. For a lethargic or sleepy person, consuming a kapha-aggravating substance is incompatible with their state.

[138] One who eats without first evacuating stool and urine, or one who eats without hunger, or one who eats when overpowered by extreme hunger — all such acts are Karma-viruddha (incompatibility of action).

[139] That which is contrary to Parihara (avoidance rules) is when one consumes boar's meat and the like, and then takes hot things; or after drinking ghee and similar substances, takes cold things — such eating is contrary to dietary rules.

[140] Incompatibility arising from improper cooking — food cooked in a spoiled or rotten vessel, food with raw rice, overcooked or burnt food — whatever results from such improper cooking is likewise incompatible.

And that which is cooked in a spoiled or corrupt manner in wood-fire, or uncooked rice, or over-cooked or burnt food — all such food becomes incompatible by virtue of processing. (140)

Incompatibility by combination is, for example, sour substances combined with milk. That which is not pleasing to the mind is called cardiac incompatibility (hrid-viruddha). (141)

And sour combined with milk is a combinational incompatibility; whatever is not pleasing to the mind is called cardiac incompatibility. (141)

That which has not properly developed its taste, or that which has lost its taste, or that in which the taste has been destroyed — this is called quality-incompatibility (sampad-viruddha). (142)

And that which has not produced its taste, or that which has become tasteless, or that whose essence has been destroyed — that is quality-incompatibility. (142)

That food which is eaten by a person who is distressed or agitated should be known as method-incompatibility (vidhi-viruddha); and food of the kind described above, when consumed in such a manner, becomes incompatible. (143)

And the one who eats while agitated — that is to be understood as method-incompatibility; and in this way, eating the above-mentioned foods becomes incompatible. (143)

However, incompatibility may prove harmless in those who have habituated to it (satmya), or when consumed in small quantities, or in those with a very sharp digestive fire, in youth, in those strengthened by oil-therapies and exercise, or in those who are robust. (144)

And for those accustomed to it, or when taken in small quantity, or in one with sharp digestion, in a young person, in one strong through oleation and exercise — even incompatible food may not cause harm.

The results of incompatible food include: impotence, blindness, erysipelas, abdominal dropsy, eruptions/blisters, madness, fistula-in-ano, fainting, intoxication, bloating, throat-obstruction, pallor (anemia), and food-poisoning. (145)

Impotence, blindness, erysipelas, dropsy, blisters, madness, fistula-in-ano, fainting, intoxication, bloating, throat-constriction, anemia, food-toxicity. (145)

Incompatible food is declared by the teachers to be the cause of: leucoderma, leprosy/skin diseases, diseases of the intestinal tract, wasting, bilious fever, chronic rhinitis — and also defects in progeny, and even death. (146)

Leucoderma, skin diseases, intestinal disorders, wasting, bilious conditions, fever, rhinitis — for all these diseases, and for defects in progeny, and for death, incompatible food is declared by the teachers to be the cause. (146)

The remedies for these conditions — arising from incompatible substances — and for other disorders caused by such incompatibilities, are as follows: emesis (vomiting), purgation, use of antagonistic substances for pacification, and likewise special preparatory procedures for the body using specific substances beforehand. (147)

For these and other disorders arising from incompatibility, the therapeutic measures are: emesis, purgation, and the use of substances that counteract them for pacification, as well as prior bodily conditioning with specific substances...

नराकसंहितायाम्

विरोधी द्रव्योंका शान्तिके लिये उपयोग
और वैसेही द्रव्योंसे पहिले शरीरका
संस्कार ॥ १४७ ॥

भवतिचात्र ।
विरुद्धाशनजान्रोगान्प्रतिहन्ति
विरेचनम् । वमनंशमनञ्चैवपूर्वं
वाहितसेवनम् ॥ १४८ ॥

इसमें ये श्लोकेहैं विरुद्ध भोजनसे
पैदाहुए रोगोंकी विरेचन, वमन, और
शमन वा पहिलेही हितका सेवन नष्ट
करताहै ॥ १४८ ॥

तत्रश्लोकाः ।
मतिरासीन्महर्षीणांयायारसिव
निश्चये । द्रव्याणिगुणकर्मभ्यां
द्रव्यसंख्यारसाश्रयाः ॥ १४९ ॥

उसमें ये श्लोकेहैं कि रसके निश्च-
यमें महर्षियोंकी जो मति हुई, द्रव्य,
गुण, और कर्मसे द्रव्योंकी संख्या रसके
आश्रय ॥ १४९ ॥

कारणंरससंख्याचरसानुरसलक्ष
णम् । परादीनांगुणानाञ्चलक्षणा
निपृथक्पृथक् ॥ १५० ॥

कारण, रसोंकी संख्या, रस, और
अनुरसका लक्षणपर आदि गुणोंके पृथक्
२ लक्षण ॥ १५० ॥

पञ्चात्मकानांषट्त्वञ्चरसानांयेन
हेतुना । ऊर्ध्वानुलोमभाजश्चयदु
णातिशयाद्रसाः ॥ १५१ ॥

पांच प्रकारके रस जिस प्रकार छः
प्रकारके होतेहैं जैसे गुणोंकी अधिक-
तासे रस– ऊर्ध्व, अनु लोमके भागी
होतेहैं ॥ १५१ ॥

षण्णांरसानांषट्चैवसुविभक्काव
भक्तयः। उद्देशश्चापिवद्धथद्रव्या
णांगुणकर्मिण ॥ १५२ ॥

और छःओं रसोंकी भली प्रकार,
छः प्रकारके विभाग, गुण,कर्ममें द्रव्यों
कांउद्देश और अपिवद्ध ॥ १५२ ॥

प्रवरावरसमध्यत्वंरसानांगौरवादि
षु । पाकप्रभावयोर्लिङ्गंवीर्यसं
ख्याविनिश्चयः ॥ १५३ ॥

और गौरव आदिमें रसोंका प्रवर
अवर मध्य पाक और प्रभावका लिंग,
वीर्यकी संख्याका निश्चय ॥ १५३ ॥

षण्णामास्वाद्यमानानांरसानांयत्
स्वलक्षणम्। यच्चिरुध्यतेयस्मा
येनयत्कारिचैवयत् ॥ १५४ ॥

और भक्षण किये हुए रसोंका जो
स्वलक्षण जिससे जिसके संगजो विरुद्धहै
और जो जिस रोगको करताहै १५४॥

वैरोधिकनिमित्तानांव्याधीनामौ
षधञ्चयत्। आत्रेयभद्रकाप्यीये
तत्सर्वमवदन्मुनिः ॥ १५५ ॥

इत्यत्रपानचतुष्केआत्रेयभद्रकाप्यीयोनाम
षड्विंशोऽध्यायःसमाप्तः ॥ २६ ॥

translation:
( 242 )
In the Charaka Samhita

The use of antagonistic substances for pacification, and prior purification of the body with similar substances. || 147 ||

And here it is stated:
Purgation destroys diseases arising from incompatible food; likewise emesis, pacification, and prior use of wholesome substances eliminate them. || 148 ||

In this, these verses state: diseases arising from incompatible food are destroyed by purgation, emesis, and pacification, or by prior use of beneficial substances. || 148 ||

There the verses are:
The opinion of the great sages regarding the determination of tastes — substances are based on their qualities and actions, and the enumeration of substances rests on taste. || 149 ||

In this, the verses state: in the determination of taste, the opinion of the great sages was that the number of substances, based on their qualities and actions, depends on taste. || 149 ||

The cause, the enumeration of tastes, the taste itself, the characteristics of secondary taste, and the separate characteristics of qualities beginning with the primary ones. || 150 ||

The cause, the number of tastes, taste, and the characteristics of secondary taste, and the separate characteristics of qualities beginning with the primary. || 150 ||

The reason why the five-elemental tastes become six in number — because by preponderance of qualities the tastes become partakers of upward or downward direction. || 151 ||

The five-elemental tastes become six in number in the manner that through the preponderance of qualities, the tastes become inclined toward upward or downward directions. || 151 ||

The six well-classified subdivisions of the six tastes, and the description of the qualities and actions of substances. || 152 ||

The proper sixfold classification of all six tastes, the description of qualities and actions of substances, and their enumeration. || 152 ||

The superior, inferior, and middling nature of tastes with respect to heaviness and so forth; the indicator of digestion and potency; and the determination of the count of potencies. || 153 ||

The superior, inferior, and middle grades of tastes regarding heaviness and similar properties; the indicator of digestion and potency; the determination of the count of potencies. || 153 ||

The characteristic properties of the six tastes when experienced; what is incompatible with what; what is opposed to whom; and what each one causes. || 154 ||

The characteristic properties of the six tastes when consumed; which is incompatible with which; what disease each causes. || 154 ||

The medicines for the diseases arising from incompatible combinations — all of this the sage expounded in the Atreya-Bhadrakapya dialogue. || 155 ||

Here ends the twenty-sixth chapter, named the Atreya-Bhadrakapya chapter, in the group of four chapters on drinking. || 26 ||

और विरोधके, निमित्तसेपैदा हुई व्याधियोंकी जो औषधहै, इस संपूर्णका आत्रेय भद्रकाप्यय अध्यायमें मुनिने वर्णन किया ॥ १५५ ॥

इत्यन्नपानचतुष्के आत्रेयमद्रकाप्पीयोऽध्यायः ॥ २६ ॥

सप्तविंशोऽध्यायः ।
अथातोऽन्नपानविधिमध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः ।
इतिह्स्माहभगवानात्रेयः ।
इसके अनंतर अन्नपान विधि अध्यायका वर्णन करते हैं यह भगवान् आत्रेय कहते हैं

इष्टवर्णगन्धरसस्पर्शविधिविहित मन्नपानंप्राणिनांप्राणसंज्ञकानां प्राणमाचक्षतेकुशलाः । प्रत्यक्ष फलदर्शनाचिदन्धनाह्यन्तराग्नेः स्थितिस्तदेवसत्वमूर्जयति । तच्छरीरधातुव्यूहबलवर्णेंन्द्रिय प्रसादकरंयथोक्तमुपसेव्यमानंवि परीतमिहतायसम्पद्यते ॥ १ ॥

इष वर्णके गंधरस स्पर्श और विधिसे किया अन्नपान प्राणसंज्ञाके प्राणियोंका कुशलोंने प्राण कहाहै; प्रत्यक्ष फल देखनेसे अन्तराग्निकी स्थितिका वही इन्धन है वह सत्वको बढ़ाता है वही शरीरकी धातुओंके व्यूह, वर्ण, बल, इंद्रिय, इनको यथार्थ सेवन किया हुआ

प्रसन्न करताहै; और विपरीत सेवनसे अहितकारी होताहै ॥ १ ॥

तस्माच्छिताहिताबोधनार्थमच्न पानविधिमखिलेनोपदेक्ष्यामोऽग्निवेश ॥ २ ॥

तिससे, हे अग्निवेश, हित, अहितके ज्ञानके लिये संपूर्ण अन्नपान विधिका उपदेश करते हैं ॥ २ ॥

तत्स्वभावादुदकंक्लेदयति, लवणं विष्यन्दयति, क्षारःपाचयति,मधुसन्दधाति, सर्पिःस्नेहयति, क्षीरं जीवयति,मांसंवृंहयति, रसःश्रीणयति, सुराजंरीकरोति, शीधुअवधमयति, द्राक्षारसोदीपयति, फाणितंमाचिनोति, दधिशोफंजनयति, पिण्याकशावंगलपयति, प्रभूतान्तर्मलोमांससूपः, दृष्टिशुकणःक्षारः, प्रायःपित्तलमम्ल मन्यत्रमधुनःपुराणाचशालिखवंगोधूमात्, प्रायःसर्वितकंवातलमवृष्यञ्चान्यत्रवेत्राग्रपटोलात्, प्रायःकटुकंवातलमवृष्यञ्चान्यत्र पिप्पलीविश्वभेषजात् ॥ ३ ॥

The medicines for diseases arising from incompatible substances and their causes — all of this has been described by the sage in the chapter of Atreya Bhadrakapya. || 155 ||

Thus ends the chapter on Atreyabhadrakapyiya in the Quadruplet on Food and Drink. || 26 ||

Twenty-Seventh Chapter.
Now we shall explain the chapter on the Rules of Food and Drink.
Thus spoke the Venerable Atreya.
After this, in the chapter on the Rules of Food and Drink, the Venerable Atreya says:

Food and drink of desirable color, smell, taste, and touch, prepared according to proper method — the wise call this the very life-force of living beings who are designated as having life-breath. The direct evidence is this: the continuance of the inner fire depends on it as on fuel; it sustains one's vitality. When taken as prescribed, it brings clarity to the body's tissues, complexion, strength, and sense organs; when taken otherwise, it proves harmful. || 1 ||

Food and drink of proper color, smell, taste, and touch, prepared in the right manner — the wise have called this the very life of living beings. As is seen directly, it is the fuel that sustains the inner digestive fire; it increases vitality; it is what brings satisfaction to the body's tissues, complexion, strength, and sense organs when used properly; and when used contrarily, it becomes harmful. || 1 ||

Therefore, O Agnivesha, in order to impart knowledge of what is beneficial and what is harmful, we shall explain the entire method of food and drink. || 2 ||

O Agnivesha, in order that you may know what is beneficial and what is harmful, we now teach the complete rules of food and drink. || 2 ||

By its own nature, water moistens; salt liquefies; alkali digests; honey binds; ghee lubricates; milk nourishes life; meat broth builds tissue; the essence of flesh refreshes; sura (fermented liquor) loosens; shidhu (fermented drink) intoxicates; grape juice stimulates appetite; phanita (raw sugar syrup) accumulates; curd causes swelling; oil-cake cleanses; meat soup in large quantity increases internal waste tissue; the supernatant alkaline wash is good for the eyes; most sour things increase pitta, except old honey, aged shali rice, and wheat; most astringent things increase vata and are not aphrodisiac, except patola and vetra shoots; most pungent things increase vata and are not aphrodisiac, except pippali and dry ginger. || 3 ||

In that food and drink, water by its nature promotes moistening; salt promotes fluidity; alkali promotes digestion; honey promotes binding; ghee...

( २४४ )

स्निग्ध करताहै, दूध, जीवनकारीहै, मांस वृद्धिकारीहै; रस प्रसन्न करताहै, सुरा जर्जर करतीहै; शीधु, अवधमन करतीहै; द्राक्षारस, दीपनकारी है, फाणित आचयन (संचय) करताहै; दधि शोफको पैदा करताहै पिण्याकका शाक गुानिकारीहै; उड्डकी दाल प्रभूत (अधिक) अंत-मेलहै; क्षार, दृष्टि और शुक्रका नाशकहै और, प्रायः अम्लरस, मधु, और पुराने, शालि, जौ और, गेहूंको छोड़कर पित्तकारीहै, और प्रायः संपूर्ण, तिक्त, बेंतका अग्र, और पटोलको छोड़कर, वातल और अवृष्य (वीर्य नाशक) हैं और, प्रायः कटुकरस, पीपल, और सोंठको छोड़कर, वातल और अवृष्यहैं ॥ ३ ॥

परमतोवर्गसंग्रहेणाहारद्रव्याण्य नुव्याख्यास्यामः ॥ ४ ॥

इससे आगे वर्गके संग्रहसे द्रव्योंका व्याख्यान करतेहैं ॥ ४ ॥

शूकधान्यशमीधान्यमांसशाक फलाशयान् । वर्गान्हिरतमचा म्बुगोरसेक्षुविकारिकान् ॥ ५ ॥

शूकधान्य, शमीधान्य, मांस, शाक, फल, और हिरत, मद्य, अम्बु, गोरस, इक्षुके विकार ॥ ५ ॥

दशदौचपरौवर्गौकताञाहारयो गिनाम् । रसवीर्यविपाकैश्च भावैश्चोपदेक्ष्यते ॥ ६ ॥

इन दश वर्गोंको और कृतान्न और आहार योग इन दो अन्य वर्गोंको रसवीर्य विपाकोंसे और प्रभावसे उपदेश करते हैं ॥ ६ ॥

अथ शूकधान्यवर्गः ।

रक्तशालिर्महाशालिःकलमःशकु नाहृतः । चूर्णकोदीर्घशूकश्गौ रःपाण्डुकलांगुलौ ॥ ७ ॥

रक्तशालि, महाशालि, कलम शकुनाहृत तृणक, दीर्घशूक, गौर, पाण्डुक लांगल ॥ ७ ॥

सुगन्धिकालोहवालाःशालिवा र्यःप्रमोदकाः । पतङ्गास्तपनीयाश्चयेचान्येशालयःशुभाः॥ ८ ॥

सुगंधिक लोहवाल शालिव प्रमोदक पतंग और तपनीय और जो अन्य उत्तम शालिहैं ॥ ८ ॥

शीतारसेविपाकेचमधुराःस्वल्प मारुताः । बद्धाल्पवर्चसःस्निग्धा बृंहणाःशुकमूत्रलाः ॥ ९ ॥

वे शीतल-रस और विपाकमें मधुर और अल्पमारुत और मलके अल्पबंधक स्निग्ध, बृंहण शुक्ल, मूत्रल, हैं॥९ ॥

रक्तशालिर्वरस्तेषांतृष्णाग्निभ्रिम लापहः । महांस्तस्यानुकलमस्त स्याप्यनुततःपरे ॥ १० ॥

उन सबमें रक्तशालि श्रेष्ठ है तृष्णा और तीनों मलोंका नाशकहै और उससे
translation:
(244)

It is unctuous; milk is life-giving; meat promotes flesh; it clarifies the rasa (essence of food); wine causes deterioration; shidhu (fermented drink) causes suppression; grape juice is digestive; phanita (molasses concentrate) accumulates (in the body); curd produces swelling; the vegetable of oilcake-residue is beneficial for the voice; urad dal in excess causes internal mixing; alkali destroys vision and semen; and generally, sour-tasting foods, honey, and old rice, barley, and wheat excepted, cause pitta; and generally, all bitter things, the tip of cane, and pointed gourd excepted, are vata-producing and virility-destroying; and generally, except for pungent taste, pippali, and dry ginger, they are vata-producing and virility-destroying. (3)

Now we shall explain the food substances in detail, group by group. (4)

The groups are: shuka-dhanya (husked grains), shami-dhanya (legumes), meats, vegetables, fruits, greens (harita), beverages (madya), water (ambu), milk products (gorasa), and preparations of sugarcane. (5)

These ten groups, along with prepared foods and dietary combinations — two further groups — will be taught according to their rasa (taste), virya (potency), vipaka (post-digestive effect), and prabhava (special properties). (6)

Now begins the chapter on shuka-dhanya (husked grains):

Rakta-shali, maha-shali, kalama, shakunahrita, trinaka, dirgha-shuka, gaura, panduka, and langala — (7)

Sugandika, lohavala, shalivara, pramodaka, patanga, tapaniya, and whatever other excellent varieties of shali there are — (8)

They are cool in taste and in post-digestive effect, sweet, slightly wind-producing, binding of stool in small measure, unctuous, nourishing, and diuretic. (9)

Among all of them, rakta-shali is the best — it removes thirst, corrects the digestive fire, and cures the three types of waste disorders. Next in quality is maha-shali, and after that comes kalama, and after that the rest in succession. (10)

( २४५ )

नीचे महाशालि उससे नीचे कलम
औरभी उससे नीचे अन्यशालि होतेहैं १०

मधुरश्वाम्लपाकश्वव्रीहिःपित्तक
रोगुरुः । बहुमूत्रपुरीषोष्मात्रिदो
षत्वेवपाटलः ॥ १४ ॥

मधुर और अम्लपाक जो व्रीहिहै वह
पित्तकारक और गुरुहै और पाटल बहु
मूत्र मल, कारीहै ऊष्ण और त्रिदोषको
करताहै ॥ १४ ॥

सकोरदूषःश्यामाकःकषायमधुरो
लघुः । वातलःकफपित्तघ्नःशीत
संग्राहिशोषणः ॥ १५ ॥

कोरदूषक और श्यामक ये, कसैले
मधुर लघु वातल कफ पित्तके नाशक
शीतल संग्राही शोषण, होतेहैं ॥ १५॥

हस्तिश्यामाकनीवारतोयपणींग
वेषुकाः । पशातिकाम्भःश्यामा
कलोहित्याणुमियङ्गवः॥ १६॥

और हस्त श्यामाक नीवार तोय-
पणीं गवेषुक पशातिका जल श्यामक
लोहित्या अणुप्रियंगु ॥ १६ ॥

मुकुन्दझिण्टिगर्मूटीचरुकावरका
स्तथा । शिविरोत्कटजूर्णाह्नः
श्यामकसदशागुणैः ॥ १७ ॥

मुकुंद झिंटी गर्मूटी चरुक और आव-
रक शिविर उत्कट जूर्णा ये सब गुणोंमें
श्यामाकके सदशहैं ॥ १७ ॥

रूक्षःशीतोगुरुःस्वादुःबहुवातश
कृवः । स्थैर्यकृत्सकषायस्तु
बल्यःश्लेष्मविकारनुत्॥ १८॥

जो रूक्ष शीतल गुरु स्वाद जिसका
मल बहुत वातल हो वह यव होताहै;और
स्थिरताका कर्ता कषाय सहित बल्य
कफके विकारका नाशक जो है ॥ १८॥

translation:

Sutrasthana
( 245 )

Below Mahashaali comes Kalam, and below that comes Anyashaali. (10)

Yavaka, Hayana, Panshuvapya, Naishdhaka and others — these grains imitate the qualities and defects of the Shali rices. (11)

Among them, Shashtika is cold, unctuous, heavy, sweet, and destroys the three doshas; being stable in nature, it is the best; it is of fair and dark complexion. (12)

Following it in quality are Varaka, Uddaalaka, China-Shalaka, Ujjvala, Dadura, Gandhana, Kurvinda — all these Shali varieties are far inferior to Shashtika in qualities. (13)

Vrihi, which is sweet and sour in post-digestive effect, is heavy and aggravates Pitta; and Patala, being very productive of urine and stool, is warm and causes all three doshas. (14)

Koradushaka and Shyamaka — these are astringent-sweet, light, aggravating Vata, destructive of Kapha and Pitta, cooling, binding, and drying. (15)

Hasti-Shyamaka, Nivara, Toyapani, Gaveshtuka, Pashatika, Jala-Shyamaka, Lohitya, and Anu-Priyanghu — (16)

Mukunda, Jhinti, Garmuti, Charuka, Avaraka, Shivira, Utkata, and Jurna — all these are equal in qualities to Shyamaka. (17)

That grain which is rough, cold, heavy, and sweet, and which produces much wind and stool — that is Yava (barley). It promotes firmness of body, is slightly astringent, gives strength, and destroys disorders of Kapha. (18)

Rough, with astringency as a secondary taste, sweet, Kapha-destroying... [text continues on next page]

( २४६ )
चरकसंहिताम्
Digitized By Siddhanta Sangiri Layam Kosha

तहा । मेद:किमिविषघ्नबल्यो
वेणुयवोमत: ॥ १९ ॥
और वेणुयव रूक्ष कषायके समान रस
मधुर,और कफ पित्त नाशक, मेदा किमि
विषका नाशक बलकारक होताहै ॥ १९॥

सन्धानरुद्धात्रोगोधूम:स्वादु
शीतल: । जीवनोबृंहणोवृष्य:स्नि

संधान ( मल ) काकारी वातहर

दाता बृंहण वृष्य स्निग्ध स्थिरताका

नान्दीमुखीमधूलीचमधुरिस्निग्ध
शीतले । इत्ययंशूकधान्यानां

और नांदीमुखी मधूली ये दोनों

translation:
( 246 )
Charaka Samhita

Thus: it destroys fat, worms, and poison, and is strengthening — such is Venuyava (bamboo barley). ॥ 19 ॥
Venuyava is dry, of taste similar to astringent, sweet, and destroys kapha and pitta, destroys fat, worms, and poison, and is strengthening. ॥ 19 ॥

Wheat, which is preservative (binding of tissues), alleviates diseases of vata, is sweet and cooling; it is life-sustaining, nourishing, aphrodisiac, unctuous, promotes stability, and is heavy. ॥ 20 ॥
Wheat, which binds and removes vata, is sweet and cooling; it is life-giving, nourishing, aphrodisiac, unctuous, promotes steadiness, and is also heavy. ॥ 20 ॥

Nandimukhi and Madhuli — both are sweet, unctuous, and cooling. Thus the first group of the Shuka (awned) grains is concluded. ॥ 21 ॥
Nandimukhi and Madhuli — both are sweet, unctuous, and cool. With these, the first group of shuka grains (grains bearing awns) is completed. ॥ 21 ॥

Thus ends the Shuka-Dhanya-Varga (group of awned grains).
Now begins the Shami-Dhanya-Varga (group of leguminous grains).

Mudga (green gram) is astringent-sweet, dry, cool, pungent in digestion (vipaka), light, clear, and destroys kapha and pitta — it is considered the best among soups (dals). ॥ 22 ॥
Green gram is astringent, sweet, dry; pungent after digestion, light, clear, and is the finest destroyer of kapha and pitta among all dals. ॥ 22 ॥

Rajamasha (a variety of bean) is dry, astringent, aggravates vata, destroys kapha and pitta, causes constipation (vishthambha), and is non-aphrodisiac — so it is described. ॥ 23 ॥
Rajamasha (ravaash) is dry, astringent, aggravates vata, destroys kapha and pitta, is constipating, and is non-aphrodisiac. ॥ 23 ॥

Masha (black gram / urad) is highly aphrodisiac, alleviates vata, is unctuous, warm, sweet, heavy, strengthening, increases feces, and quickly promotes virility. ॥ 24 ॥
Black gram (urad) is greatly aphrodisiac, removes vata, is unctuous, warm, sweet, heavy, strengthening, increases stool, and quickly bestows virility. ॥ 24 ॥

Kulttha (horse gram) is warm, astringent, sour in digestion, destroys kapha, semen disorders, and vata; it is binding, and is beneficial in cough, hiccup, asthma, and hemorrhoids. ॥ 25 ॥
Horse gram is warm, astringent, sour after digestion, destroys kapha, semen, and vata; it is beneficial in cough, hiccup, asthma, and piles. ॥ 25 ॥

Makushthaka (moth bean) is sweet, sweet even after digestion, binding, dry, and cooling — it is praised especially in rakta-pitta (bleeding disorders) and fever. ॥ 26 ॥
Moth bean (motha) is sweet, sweet even after digestion, binding, dry, and cooling; it is excellent in blood-pitta disorders, fever, and similar conditions. ॥ 26 ॥

पूजस्थानमयू।

चणकाश्वमसूराश्वखण्डिकाःसह
रेणवः । लघवःशीतमधुराःसक

चणक और मसूर खंडिका और रेणु
ये सब लघु, शीतल, मधुर, कषाय,
विरूक्षण होतेहैं ॥ २७॥

पित्तश्लेष्मणिशस्यन्तेसूपेष्वाले
पनेषुच। तेषांमसूरःसंग्राहीकशा

और पित्त, छेष्ममें सूप और आले-

स्निग्धोष्णमधुरस्तीक्षःकषायः

और तिल, स्निग्ध उष्ण, मधुर, तीक्ष्ण
कषाय, कटु होताहै त्वचा केशाको हित
बल्य, वातनाशक, कफ, पित्तकारी,
होताहै ॥ २९ ॥

गुर्व्योऽथमधुराःशीताबलघ्नारूक्ष

और संपूर्ण शिम्बिजाति, गुरु, मधुर,
शीतल, बलनाशक, रूक्षणात्मक लेह
सहित बलवानोंको भोगने योग्य और

वातनुत् । अवल्गुजःसैडगजोनि
ष्पावावातपित्तलाः ॥ ३१ ॥
और आढकी (अरहर) कफ, पित्तकी
नाशक वातल कफ बात नाशक होतीहै
और अवल्गुज सैडगज निष्पाव ये वात
पित्तल हैं ॥ ३१ ॥

काकाण्डोलात्मगुप्तानांमाषवत्फ
लमादिशेत् । द्वितीयोऽयंशमी
धान्यवर्गःश्रोक्तोमहर्षिणा ३२
और काकाण्डोल आत्मगुप्त इनका
फल माषके समान कहै यह दूसरा शमी
( फछी ) धान्योंका वर्ग महर्षिने कहा
है ॥ ३२ ॥ इतिशमीधान्यवर्गः ॥
इतिशमीधान्यवर्गः ।
अथमांसवर्गः ।

गोखराश्वतरोष्ट्राश्वद्वीपिसिंहर्षं

भ्रुमार्जारमूषिकाः ॥ ३३ ॥
गौ, खर, अश्वतर, ऊंट, द्वीपि, सिंह,

लोपाक, जंबुक, श्येन, वांताद चाष

translation:
(Page 247 — from the section on grains and the beginning of the section on meats)

Verse 27:
Chanaka (chickpea), horse-gram (masura), khandika, and renu — all of these are light, cool, sweet, astringent, and drying in quality. (27)

Commentary: Chanaka, masur, khandika, and renu are all light, cooling, sweet, astringent, and drying. (27)

Verse 28:
These are recommended in cases of excess pitta and phlegm (kapha), whether used as soups or as external applications (lepa). Among them, masur (red lentil) is especially astringent, kapha-reducing, and the most productive of vata. (28)

Commentary: In conditions of excess pitta and kapha, these are excellent as soups and as poultices. Among them, masur is astringent, extremely vata-aggravating. (28)

Verse 29:
Sesame (tila) is unctuous, hot, sweet, sharp, astringent, and pungent. It is beneficial to the skin and hair, strength-promoting, vata-destroying, and increases kapha and pitta. (29)

Commentary: Sesame is unctuous, hot, sweet, sharp, astringent, and pungent. It benefits the skin and hair, promotes strength, destroys vata, and increases kapha and pitta. (29)

Verse 30:
The various kinds of pod-vegetables (shimbi jati) are heavy, sweet, cool, strength-reducing, and drying in nature. With added preparations they are fit for consumption by the strong, and they come in many varieties. (30)

Commentary: All pod-vegetables are heavy, sweet, cooling, strength-reducing, and drying; with preparations they are suitable for the strong, and they are of many kinds. (30)

Verse 31:
Adhaki (pigeon pea/arhar) destroys kapha and pitta but increases vata. Avalguja, saidgaja, and nishpava increase vata and pitta. (31)

Commentary: Adhaki (arhar) destroys kapha and pitta but increases vata. Avalguja, saidgaja, and nishpava increase vata and pitta. (31)

Verse 32:
The fruits of kakandola and atmagupta should be considered equivalent to masha (black gram). This is the second group of shami-grains (pod-grains), as described by the great sage. (32)

Commentary: Kakandola and atmagupta — their fruits are comparable to masha. This is the second group of shami (pod) grains as declared by the great sage. Here ends the section on shami-grains.

Now begins the section on meats (Mansa Varga):

Verse 33:
Cow, donkey, mule, camel, leopard, lion, bear, monkey, wolf, tiger, hyena, dog, cat, mouse — (33)

Commentary: Cow, donkey, mule, camel, leopard, lion, bear, monkey, wolf, tiger, hyena, badger, cat, mouse. (33)

Verse 34:
Lopaka (fox), jackal, hawk, crow, vantada, chasha (blue jay), shashni, madhubha, bhasa (vulture-like bird), vulture (gridhra), owl (uluka), kulingaka — (34)

Commentary: Lopaka, jackal, hawk, vantada, crow, shashna, madhubha, bhas, vulture, owl, kulinga. (34)

text:
( २४८ )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।
Digitized By Slddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

धूमीकाकुररश्वेतिप्रसहामृगपक्षिणः । श्वेतःश्यामश्चित्रपृष्ठःकालकःकाकुलीमृगः ॥ ३५ ॥

धूमीक कुरर ये मृग और पक्षी प्रसह कहातेहैं श्वेत और श्याम, चित्रपृष्ठ, कालक, काकुलीमृग, ॥ ३५ ॥

कुचीकाचिछ्डकोमेकोगोधाशङ्कगण्डकौ । कदलीनकुलःश्विादितिभूमिशयाःस्मृताः ॥ ३६ ॥

कुचिका चिछ्डड भेक गोधा शछ्लक, गंडक कदली नकुल श्वाविद् ( सेह ) ये भूमिशय कहेहैं ॥ ३६ ॥

स्मरश्चमरःखङ्गोमहिषोगवयोगजः । न्यङ्कुर्वराहश्चानूपामृगाःसर्वेरुरुस्तथा ॥ ३७ ॥

स्मर, चमर, खङ्ग, महिष, गवय, गज, न्यंकु, वराह, संपूर्ण मृग और रुरु ये अनूप कहातेहैं ॥ ३७ ॥

कूर्मःकर्कटकोमत्स्यःशिशुमारतिमिङ्गिलः । शुक्तिशंखोद्रकुम्भीरउलुकीमकरादयः ॥ ३८ ॥

कूर्म, कर्कटक, मत्स्य, शिशुमार, तिमिंगल शुक्तिशंख, उद्रकुंभीर, उलूपी मकर, आदि ॥ ३८ ॥

इतिवारिशयाःप्रोक्तावक्ष्यन्तेवारिचारिणः । हंसःकौञ्चोबलाकाचबकःकारण्डवःप्लुवः ॥ ३९ ॥

ये वारिशय, कहेहैं अंबजल, चारियोंको कहतेहैं हंस कौंच बलाका बक, कारंडव, प्लुव ॥ ३९ ॥

शरारीपुष्कराह्वश्केशरीमानतुण्डकः । मृणालकण्ठोमद्गुश्कादम्बःकाकतुण्डकः ॥ ४० ॥

शरारी पुष्कराह्व केशरी मानतुंडक मृणालकंठ मद्गु कादंब काकतुंडक ४०

उत्कोशःपुण्डरीकाक्षोमेघरावोऽम्बुकुकुटी । आरानन्दीमुखीवाटीसुमुखाःसहचारिणः ॥ ४१ ॥

उत्कोश पुंडरीकाक्ष, मेघराव, अंबुकुकुटी आरानंदी मुखीबाटी सुमुखः ये सहचारी हैं ॥ ४१ ॥

रोहिणीकामकालीचसारसोरक्तशीर्षकः । चक्रवाकास्तथान्येचरगाःसन्त्यम्बुचारिणः ॥ ४२ ॥

रोहिणी कामकाली, सारस, रक्तशीर्षक, चक्रवाक और, तैसेही अन्यभी पक्षी जलचारी होतेहैं ॥ ४२ ॥

पृषतःशरभोवामःश्वदंष्ट्रामृगमातृकाः । शशोरणौकुरङ्गश्वगोकर्णःकोट्टकारकः ॥ ४३ ॥

और पृषत शरभ वाम, श्वदंष्ट्री, मृगमातृका शश उरण कुरंग गोकर्ण कोट्टकारक ॥ ४३ ॥

In the Charaka Samhita

[Verse 35]
The Prasaha class of animals and birds includes: Dhumika, Kurara, Shveta (white), Shyama (dark), Chitraprishtha (spotted-backed), Kalaka, and Kakulimriga. — 35

[Commentary 35]
Dhumika and Kurara — these animals and birds are called Prasaha (predatory/bold). White and dark, spotted-backed, Kalaka, Kakulimriga. — 35

[Verse 36]
Kuchika, Chhad, Bheka (frog), Godha (monitor lizard), Shankha (conch-creature), Gandaka, Kadali (banana-rat), Nakula (mongoose), and Shvavid (porcupine) — these are remembered as Bhumishaya (ground-dwelling/burrowing creatures). — 36

[Commentary 36]
Kuchika, Chhad, Bheka, Godha, Shhlaka, Gandaka, Kadali, Nakula, Shvavid (porcupine) — these are called Bhumishaya. — 36

[Verse 37]
Smara, Chamara (yak), Khanga (rhinoceros), Mahisha (buffalo), Gavaya (gayal), Gaja (elephant), Nyankhu, Varaha (boar), and Ruru (a type of deer) — all these are called Anupa (marsh-dwelling) animals. — 37

[Commentary 37]
Smara, Chamara, Khanga, Mahisha, Gavaya, Gaja, Nyanku, Varaha — all these animals and Ruru are called Anupa. — 37

[Verse 38]
Kurma (tortoise), Karkataka (crab), Matsya (fish), Shishumara (dolphin/Gangetic porpoise), Timingila (whale), Shukti (oyster), Shankha (conch), Udra (otter), Kumbhira (crocodile), Uluki (a water creature), Makara (a large aquatic creature), and others. — 38

[Commentary 38]
Tortoise, crab, fish, Shishumara, Timingila, oyster-conch, Udra, Kumbhira, Uluki, Makara, etc. — 38

[Verse 39]
Thus the Varishaya (water-dwelling creatures) have been described; now the Varichari (water-roaming birds) will be told: Hamsa (goose/swan), Krauncha (curlew/crane), Balaka (egret), Baka (heron), Karandava (a waterbird), and Pluva (a waterbird). — 39

[Commentary 39]
These are the Varishaya. Now the Varichari are named: Hamsa, Krauncha, Balaka, Baka, Karandava, Pluva. — 39

[Verse 40]
Sharari, Pushkarahva, Keshari, Manatundaka, Mrinala-kantha (lotus-throated), Madgu, Kadamba (a waterbird), and Kakatundaka. — 40

[Commentary 40]
Sharari, Pushkarahva, Keshari, Manatundaka, Mrinalakantha, Madgu, Kadamba, Kakatundaka — 40

[Verse 41]
Utkrosha, Pundarikaksha, Megharava, Ambukukuti, Aranandi, Mukhivati, and Sumukha — these are the companion (Sahachari) birds. — 41

[Commentary 41]
Utkrosha, Pundarikaksha, Megharava, Ambukukuti, Aranandi, Mukhivati, Sumukha — these are the Sahachari. — 41

[Verse 42]
Rohini, Kamakali, Sarasa (crane), Raktashirsha (red-headed bird), Chakravaka (ruddy shelduck), and other birds of similar kind — these too are water-roaming (Ambuchari) birds. — 42

[Commentary 42]
Rohini, Kamakali, Sarasa, Raktashirsha, Chakravaka, and similarly other birds are also water-roaming. — 42

[Verse 43]
Prishata (spotted deer), Sharabha (a mythical eight-legged beast), Vama, Shvadamshtra-mriga, Mrigamatrika, Shasha (hare), Urana (ram/sheep), Kuranga (antelope), Gokarna, and Kottakaraka. — 43

[Commentary 43]
And Prishata, Sharabha, Vama, Shvadanshti, Mrigamatrika, Shasha, Urana, Kuranga, Gokarna, Kottakaraka. — 43

मत्रस्थानम् ।
( २४९ )
Digitized By Sidhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

लपुच्छकः । ऋष्यश्तरपोतश्च
विज्ञेयाजाङ्गलामृगाः ॥ ४४ ॥
चारुष्क, हारिण, एण, शंबर काल,
पुच्छक, ऋष्य तरपोत, ये सब जंगलके
मृग जानने ॥ ४४ ॥

लावोवर्तीरकश्चैववार्तीकःसकपिञ्जलः । चकोरश्चोपचक्रश्च कुक्कु
टोरक्कवर्तकः ॥ ४५ ॥
और लाव वतीरक वार्तीक कपिंजल,
चकोर उपचक्र कुक्कुट, रक्तवर्तका॥४५॥

लावाद्याविष्किरास्त्वेतेवक्ष्यन्ते
वर्तकाद्यः । वर्तकोवर्तिकाचैव
बर्हिणीतितिरिकुकुटौ ॥ ४६ ॥
ये लाव आदि विष्किर कहातेहैं अबव-
तक आदिको कहतेहैं, वतक वितिका
बर्हिं तितिरि कुक्कुट ॥ ४६ ॥

कङ्कःसारपदेन्द्राभगोनर्देगिरिवर्त
काः । क्रकरोऽवकरश्चैववराहश्चे
तिविष्किराः ॥ ४७ ॥
कंक शारपद इंद्राभ गोनर्द गिरिवर्त्त
कक अवकर वराह ये भी विष्किर कहा-
तेहैं ॥ ४७ ॥

शतपत्रोभृङ्गराजःकोयष्टीजीव
जीवकः । कैरातःकोकिलोऽत्यू
होगोपापुत्रःप्रियात्मजः ॥ ४८॥
और शतपत्र भृंगिराज कोयष्टी जीव
जीवक कैरात, कोकिल, अत्यूह, गोपापुत्र
प्रियात्मज ॥ ४८ ॥

लड्डालट्टूपकोवभुर्वटहाडिण्डिमा
नकः । जटीदुन्दुभिवाकावलोह
पृष्ठकुलिङ्गकाः ॥ ४९ ॥
लड्ढ लट्टूषक, बञ्ज बटहा डिंडिमा-
नक जटी दुंदुभि वाकाव लोहपृष्ठ कुलिं-
गक ॥ ४९ ॥

कपोतशुकसारङ्गाश्चिरिटीकंकुय
ष्टिकाः । सारिकाकलविङ्कश्चच
टकोऽङ्गारचूडकः ॥ ५० ॥
कपोत शुक, सारंग, चिरटी कंकुयिष्टक
सारिका कलविंक चटक अंगारचूडक ५०

पारावतःपाण्डिवकइत्युकाःअतु
दाद्विजाः । प्रसह्यभक्षयन्तीति
प्रसहास्तेनसंज्ञिताः ॥ ५१ ॥
पारावत, पांडिवक, ये पक्षी अतुद
कहातेहैं जो प्रसह्य अर्थात् बलात्कारसे
भक्षण करतेहैं इससे प्रसह कहातेहैं ५१

भूशयाबिलवासितवादानूपापूसं
श्रयात् । जलेनिवासाञ्जलजाज
लचर्याञ्जलेचराः । स्थलजाजा
ङ्गलाःमोकामृगाजाङ्गलचारि
णः ॥ ५२ ॥
बिलमें बसनेसे भूशय और अनूपके
संश्रयसे अनूप जलमें निवाससे जलज
और जलमें विचरनेसे जलचर होतेहैं
और स्थलमें पैदा हुए जो जंगलमें
विचरें वे जांगल कहेहैं ॥ ५२ ॥

SUTRA-STHANA (Chapter on Fundamentals)
(Page 249)

[Verse 44]
Lapuchchhaka and Rishyashtara's young — these are to be known as the jungle (jangala) animals. Charushka, Harina, Ena, Shambara, Kala, Puchchhaka, and Rishya-tarpota — all these are to be known as the deer of the jungle. (44)

[Verse 45]
Lava, Vartiraka, Vartika, Kapinjala, Chakora, Upachakra, Kukkuta, and Raktavartaka — these are the birds of this group. (45)

[Verse 46]
Those beginning with Lava are called Vishkira (ground-scratching) birds; those beginning with Vartaka are called by that name. Vartaka, Vartika, Barhini (peacock), Tittiri (partridge), and Kukkuta (rooster) — these are the Vishkira birds. (46)

[Verse 47]
Kanka, Sharapada, Indrabhagona, Girde, Girivarttaka, Krakara, Avakara, and Varaha — these also are known as Vishkira birds. (47)

[Verse 48]
Shatapatra, Bhringa-raja, Koyashti, Jivajivaka, Kairata, Kokila (cuckoo), Atyuha, Gopaputa, and Priyatmaja — these are other birds of this group. (48)

[Verse 49]
Laddala, Lattupaka, Bhurva, Taha, Dindima, Naka, Jati, Dundubhi, Vakava, Lohaprishtha, and Kulinga — these are yet other birds in this classification. (49)

[Verse 50]
Kapota (pigeon), Shuka (parrot), Saranga, Chiriti, Kankuyashtika, Sarika (myna), Kalavinka, Chataka (sparrow), and Angarachudaka — these are further birds of this group. (50)

[Verse 51]
Paravata (dove) and Pandivaka — these birds are called Atuda. Those that eat by force (prasahya) are known as Prasaha. This is how they get their name. (51)

[Verse 52]
Animals that live in burrows are called Bhushaya; those that dwell in marshy (anupa) regions are called Anupa; those that reside in water are called Jalaja (water-born); those that move about in water are called Jalachara (water-movers). Those that are born on land and roam in the jungle are called Jangala (forest-dwelling). (52)

विकीर्य्यिविष्किराश्चेतिप्रतुयप्रतु
दाःस्मृताः । योनिरष्टिवधात्वेषां
मांसानांपरिकीर्त्तिताः ॥ ५३ ॥
और विकीर्य ( खोदकर ) भक्षण
करनेसे विष्किर और चोंचसे तोद (तोड)
कर खानेसे मतुद कहेहैं यह आठ प्रका-
रकी मांसोंकी योनि कही ॥ ५३ ॥

प्रसहाभूशयानूपवारिजावारिचा
रिणः । गुरूष्णस्निग्धमधुराबलो
पचयवर्द्धनाः ॥ ५४ ॥
प्रसह भूशय अनूप वारिज जलचारी
ये सब गुरु, उष्ण, स्निग्ध, मधुरहैं; और
बलवृद्धिको करतेहैं ॥ ५४ ॥

वृष्याःपरंवातहराःकफपित्ताभि
वर्द्धिनः । हिताभ्यायामिनित्यानां
नरादीनामयश्वये ॥ ५५ ॥
अधिक वृष्यहैं वातहरहैं और कफ
पित्तके अत्यंत वर्द्धकहैं जो नित्य व्याया
म करतेहैं उनको और जो दीताग्निहैं
उनको हित हैं ॥ ५५ ॥

प्रसहानांविशेषणमांसमांसाशिनां
भिषक् । जीर्णाशोग्रहणीदोष
शोषात्तानांप्रयोजयेत् ॥ ५६ ॥
प्रसहोंके मांसको वैद्य मांस भक्षकको
और जीणे अऩे ग्रहणी दोष शोषसे
आर्तोंको दे ॥ ५६ ॥

लावाथोविष्किरोवर्गःप्रतुदाजाञ्
लामृगाः । लघवःशीतमधुराःस

कषायाहितानृणाम् ॥ ५७ ॥
लाव आदि जो विष्किर पक्षियोंको
वर्ग है मतुद जो जंगलके मृगहैं ये लघु
शितल, मधुर, कषायहैं; और मनुष्योंको
हितहैं ॥ ५७ ॥

पित्तोत्तरेवातमध्येसन्निपातेकफा
नुगे।विष्कराव्वर्त्तकायारतुपसहा
ल्पान्तरागुणेः ॥ ५८ ॥
पित्त जिसमें अधिक हो वात मध्यम
हो कफका अनुयायी जो सन्निपात उसमें
विष्किर वर्तका आदि गुणोंमें प्रसहसे
कुछही अल्पहैं ॥ ५८ ॥

नातिशीतगुरुस्निग्धंमांसमाजमदो
षलम् । शरीरधातुसामान्यादन
भिष्यन्दिबृंहणम् ॥ ५९ ॥
और अजाका मांस अति शीत नहींहै;
गुरु स्निग्ध दोषोंका अजनक शरीर धातु-
ओंके सामान्यसे अभि[illegible]दी नहींहै; और
बृंहणहै ॥ ५९ ॥

मांसंमधुरशीतत्वाद्गुरुबृंहणमाविक
म् । योनावजाविकेमिश्रगोच
रत्वादिनिश्चिते ॥ ६० ॥
भेडका मांस मधुर शीतल होनेसे
गुरु और बृंहणहै; अजा, और अवि
( भेड ) मिले हुये गोचर होनेसे अनि-
श्चित होतेहैं ॥ ६० ॥

translation:
( 250 )

[Verse 53]
Those that scatter (vikeerya — scratch and dig) are called Vishkira, and those that peck (strike with beak) are called Pratuda — these are described as the eight categories of meats based on their source. Thus the eight types of meat-sources have been described. (53)

[Verse 54]
The meats of Prasaha (predatory animals), Bhushaya (burrowing animals), Anupa (marshy-land animals), Varija (water-born creatures), and Varichari (aquatic wanderers) — all of these are heavy, hot, unctuous, and sweet in taste, and they increase strength and build bodily tissue. (54)

[Verse 55]
They are strongly aphrodisiac, reduce Vata, and greatly increase Kapha and Pitta. They are beneficial for those who exercise regularly and for those with strong digestive fire. (55)

[Verse 56]
The physician should particularly prescribe the meat of Prasaha animals to those who eat meat, and to those suffering from weak digestion, disorders of the duodenum (grahani), and wasting (consumption). (56)

[Verse 57]
The class of birds such as the Lava (quail) that are Vishkira, and the forest animals that are Pratuda — these are light, cooling, sweet, and astringent, and are beneficial to human beings. (57)

[Verse 58]
In a condition where Pitta is predominant, Vata is moderate, and Kapha is associated — that is, in Sannipata — the Vishkira birds such as the Vartaka (quail) etc. are slightly less in qualities compared to the Prasaha meats. (58)

[Verse 59]
The meat of the goat (aja) is not excessively cold, heavy, or unctuous; it does not aggravate the bodily doshas; it is similar in quality to the body's own tissues; it is not excessively moistening; and it is nourishing (brimhana). (59)

[Verse 60]
The meat of the sheep (avika) is sweet and cool, hence heavy and nourishing. Since goats and sheep often graze together in mixed pastures, their meat qualities are not always clearly distinct. (60)

गुणैःपृथक् । केषाञ्चिद्गुणवैशे
ष्यादिशेषउपदेक्ष्यते ॥ ६१ ॥

प्रथम सामान्यसे उपदेश किये
मांसोंका अपने २ गुणोंसे पृथक् २ और
किन्हीं२ केगुणोंकी विशेषतासे विशेष ६१

दर्शनश्रोत्रमेधाग्निवयोवर्णस्वरायु
षाम् । बर्हींहिततमोबल्योवात
घ्नोमांससुकलः ॥ ६२ ॥

दर्शन श्रोत्र बुद्धि अग्नि वायु वर्ण
स्वरकी अवस्था इनके लिये उपदेश करते
हैं, बर्हीं अत्यंताहित और बलका दाता
वात नाशक, मांस और शुक्र वर्द्धक
होताहै ॥ ६२ ॥

गुरुष्णिग्धमधुराःस्वरवर्णबल
प्रदाः । बृंहणाःशुकलाश्चोक्काहं
साःमारुतनाशनाः ॥ ६३ ॥

और हंस गुरु स्निग्ध मधुर स्वरवर्ण
बल इनके दाता, बृंहण ( पोषक ) शुक्र
वर्द्धक उत्तम स्वरके नाशक होतेहैं॥ ६३॥

स्निग्धाश्चोष्णाश्चवृष्याश्चबृंहणाः
स्वरबोधनाः । बल्याःपरंवातह
राःस्वेदनाश्चरणायुधाः ॥ ६४ ॥

और चरणायुध ( मुरगे ) स्निग्ध
उष्ण वृष्य बृंहण स्वरके बोधक, बलके
दाता अत्यंत वातहर और स्वेदकारी
होतेहैं ॥ ६४ ॥

गुरूष्णमधुरोनातिधन्वानूपनिषेव
णात् । तितिरिःसऋयेच्छीघ्रं

त्रिन्दोषाननिलोल्वणात् ॥ ६५॥
और गुरु उष्ण मधुर जो तितिरिहै
वह अधिकतासे जलके समीपके धान्योंके
सेवनसे शीघ्रही, वातहै अधिक जिनमें
ऐसे तीन दोषोंको पैदा करताहै ॥ ६५॥

पित्तश्लेष्मविकारेषुसरक्तेषुकिम
ऴाः । मन्दवातेषुशस्यन्तेशै
त्यमाधुर्येलाघवात् ॥ ६६ ॥

शीतल मधुर लघु होनेसे कपिंजल
रुधिर सहित पित्त क्लेष्मके विकारोंमें
और मंद वातोंमें श्रेष्ठ होतेहैं ॥ ६६ ॥

लावाःकषायमधुराःलघवोऽग्निविव
र्द्धनाः । सन्निपातप्रशमनाःकटु
काश्चिपाकतः । कषायमधुराः
शीतारक्तपित्तनिबर्हणाः ॥ ६७॥

और लाव, कषाय मधुर लघु अग्नि
वर्द्धन सन्निपातके प्रशमन और विपा-
कमें कटु होतेहैं और कषाय में मधुर
शीतल रक्तपित्तके नाशक ॥ ६७ ॥

विपाकेमधुराश्चैवकपोताग्रहवा
सिनः । तेभ्योलघुतराःकिञ्चित्
कपोतावनवासिनः ॥ ६८ ॥

और विपाकमें मधुर गृहवासी कपोत
होतेहैं और उनसे कुछ लघु वनके वासी
कपोत होतेहैं ॥ ६८ ॥

शीताःसंग्राहिणश्चैवस्वल्पयूषाश्च
तेमताः । शुकमांसकषायाम्लंवि
पाकेरूक्षशीतलम् ॥ ६९ ॥

translation:
(251)

Qualities are described separately. For some, their special qualities will be taught further. (61)

First, the meats were described generally by their individual qualities, and some are distinguished by the special qualities of certain others. (61)

The meat of the peacock (barhi) is beneficial for vision, hearing, intellect, digestive fire, vitality, complexion, voice, and longevity. It is extremely beneficial, strengthens the body, destroys vata, builds flesh and semen. (62)

The meat of the swan (hamsa) is heavy, unctuous, and sweet; it bestows voice, complexion, and strength; it is nourishing, increases semen, and destroys excess vata. (63)

The rooster (charanayudha) is unctuous, hot, aphrodisiac, and nourishing; it stimulates the voice, gives strength, greatly destroys vata, and induces perspiration. (64)

The partridge (tittiri), which is heavy, hot, and sweet — when consumed in excess along with grains grown near water — quickly produces an aggravation of all three doshas, especially vata. (65)

The kapinjala (gray partridge), being cool, sweet, and light, is excellent for disorders of pitta and kapha associated with blood, and for conditions of mild vata. (66)

The lava (quail) is astringent-sweet, light, kindles the digestive fire, pacifies sannipata (simultaneous aggravation of all three doshas), is pungent in its post-digestive effect, and in its astringent-sweet and cooling nature, destroys rakta-pitta (bleeding disorders). (67)

The domesticated pigeon is sweet in post-digestive effect; the forest-dwelling pigeon is somewhat lighter than the domesticated one. (68)

They are considered cooling and binding, and their soup is meager. The meat of the parrot (shuka) is astringent and sour, and in post-digestive effect it is dry and cool. (69)

text:
( २५२ )

और वे शीतल संग्राही अल्पयूषवान्
मानेहैं और शुकका मांस कसैला अम्ल
पाकमें रूक्ष शीतल होताहै ॥ ६९ ॥

शोषकासक्षयिहतंसंग्राहिलघुदी
पनम् । कषायविशदोरूक्षःशीतः
पाकेकटुर्लघुः ॥ ७० ॥

और शोक कास क्षय इनमें हित
संग्राही लघु दीपन लघु होताहै और
कषायमें विशद रूक्ष शीतल पाकमें कटु
लघु ॥ ७० ॥

शशःस्वादुःप्रशस्तश्वसन्निपातेऽ
निलावरे । चटकामधुराःस्निग्धा
बलशुकिववर्धनाः ॥ ७१ ॥

स्वादु और वातहै अल्प जिसमें ऐसा
सन्निपातमें श्रेष्ठ, शश होताहै, और
चटका ( चिड़ा ) मधुर स्निग्ध और बल
शुक्रके विवर्धन होतेहैं ॥ ७१ ॥

सन्निपातप्रशमनाःशमनामारुत
स्यच । मधुराःकटुकाःपाकेत्रि
दोषशमनाःशिवाः ॥ ७२ ॥

और शिव ( गीदड़ ) सन्निपातके
प्रशमन और मारुतके और त्रिदोषके
शमन मधुर और पाकमें कटु होतेहैं ७२

लघवोबद्धविण्मूत्राःशीताश्चैणाः
प्रकीर्तिताः । गोधाविपाकेमधु
राः कषायकटुकारसे ॥ ७३ ॥

और एण ( मृग ) लघु मल मूत्र
के बंधक, शीतल कहे हैं, और गोधा,
पाकमें मधुर, रसमें कषाय कटु ॥ ७३॥

वातपित्तप्रशमनीबृंहणीबलवर्धि
नी । शल्कोमधुराम्लस्तुविपा
केकटुकःस्मृतः । वातपित्तकफ
ग्रश्वकासश्वासहरस्तथा॥ ७४ ॥

और वात पित्तनाशक, बृंहण और
बल वर्धक होतीहै, और शल्यक (सेह)
मधुर अम्ल, पाकमें कटु कहा है, और
वातपित्त कफका नाशक और कासश्वास
का हारक होता है ॥ ७४ ॥

शैवलाहारभोजितवात्स्वभस्यच
विवर्जनात् ॥ ७५ ॥

और शैवल आहारका भोजी और
स्वप्नका त्यागी होनेसे ॥ ७५ ॥

रोहितोदीपनीयश्वलघुपाकोमहा
बलः । गुरूष्णःमुराबल्याबृंह
णाःपवनापहाः ॥ ७६ ॥

रोहितमृग, दीपन, पाकमें लघु, महा-
बली होताहै और गुरु उष्ण मधुर बलके
दाता बृंहण वातनाशक ॥ ७६ ॥

मत्स्याःस्निग्धाश्वृष्याश्वबहुदो
षाःप्रकीर्तिताः । स्नेहनंबृंहणंवृ
प्यंश्रमघ्नमनिलापहम् ॥ ७७ ॥

मत्स्य स्निग्ध, वृष्य, बहुत दोषवाले
कहे हैं और इनका स्नेह युक्त मांस
बृंहण वृष्य श्रमको हरनेवाला वातका
नाशक कहा है ॥ ७७ ॥
translation:
( 252 )

And those [birds] are cooling, astringent, of little broth-essence; the meat of the parrot is sour, pungent in digestion, rough and cooling. ॥ 69 ॥

[Verse 70]: Beneficial in consumption, cough, and wasting diseases; astringent [in quality]; it is an astringent, clear, rough, and cooling substance; its post-digestive effect (vipaka) is pungent, and it is light.

And [this meat] is beneficial in grief, cough, and wasting conditions; it is astringent, acts as a retainer (sangrahi), is light, and promotes digestion; it is clear, rough, and cooling in quality, and pungent and light in its post-digestive effect. ॥ 70 ॥

[Verse 71]: The hare is sweet in taste, excellent in cases of vata-dominant tridosha disorders; sparrows are sweet, unctuous, and promote strength and semen.

The hare is sweet and [beneficial] where vata is slightly predominant in a tridoshic condition — it is the best [choice]; the sparrow (chida) is sweet, unctuous, and promotes strength and semen. ॥ 71 ॥

[Verse 72]: [The jackal] pacifies tridosha, calms vata, is sweet and pungent in taste, pacifies the three doshas — it is auspicious.

And shiva (the jackal) pacifies tridoshic disorders, calms vata and all three doshas, is sweet in taste and pungent in its post-digestive effect. ॥ 72 ॥

[Verse 73]: The antelope (ena) is light, causes binding of stool and urine, and is cooling — so it is described. The monitor lizard (godha) is sweet in its post-digestive effect, astringent and pungent in primary taste.

And the antelope (deer) is light, a binder of stool and urine, and is described as cooling; and the monitor lizard is sweet in post-digestive effect, and astringent-pungent in taste. ॥ 73 ॥

[Verse 74]: [It] pacifies vata and pitta, is nourishing and strengthening. The porcupine (shalyaka) is remembered as sweet-sour in taste and pungent in post-digestion. It destroys vata, pitta, kapha, cough, and breathlessness.

And [it] destroys vata and pitta, nourishes, and increases strength; the porcupine (seha) is sweet-sour in taste and pungent in post-digestive effect; it destroys vata, pitta, and kapha, and removes cough and dyspnea. ॥ 74 ॥

[Verse 75]: [This is achieved] by feeding on aquatic vegetation (shaivala) as food and by abandoning sleep during the day.

And [this animal is beneficial] by virtue of feeding on aquatic plants and by abstaining from daytime sleep. ॥ 75 ॥

[Verse 76]: The rohita deer is digestive-stimulating, light in digestion, and very powerful. [Other animals described here are] heavy, hot, strengthening, nourishing, and destroy vata.

The rohita deer promotes digestion, is light in post-digestive effect, and is extremely powerful; and [the others] are heavy, hot, sweet, donors of strength, nourishing, and destroyers of vata. ॥ 76 ॥

[Verse 77]: Fish are unctuous, aphrodisiac, and said to have many doshic faults. Their oily flesh is nourishing, aphrodisiac, relieves fatigue, and destroys vata.

Fish are unctuous, aphrodisiac, and considered to have many doshic faults; their oily flesh is nourishing, aphrodisiac, relieves exhaustion, and is a destroyer of vata — so it is said. ॥ 77 ॥

text:
( २५३ )
Digitized By Siddanta Gangiri Gyaan Kosha

बल्योवातहरोवृष्यश्चशुष्योबलव
र्द्धनः । मेधास्मृतिकरःपथ्यःशो
षघ्नःकूर्मउच्यते । वराहिपिशतं
बल्यंरोचनंस्वेदनंगुरु ॥ ७८ ॥
और कूर्म बलकारी वातहारी वीर्य
वर्द्धक नेत्रोंको हित बलवर्द्धन, मेधा
स्मृतिकारक पथ्य और शोषनाशक
कहाहै और वराहका मांस, बलदायी
रोचन, स्वेदन गुरु होताहै ॥ ७८ ॥

गव्यंकेवलवातेषुपीनसेविषमज्व
रे । शुष्ककासश्रमात्यिग्मांसक्ष
यिहतऋयत् ॥ ७९ ॥
गौकामांस, केवल वातमें पीनस
और विषमज्वरमें और शुष्ककास श्रम
अत्यंत अग्निमांसका क्षय, इनमें हित
है ॥ ७९ ॥

स्निग्धोष्णमधुरंवृष्यंमाहिषंगुरुत
पणम् । दार्ढ्यवृहत्त्वमुत्साहंव
मञ्जनयत्यपि ॥ ८० ॥
भैंसका मांस स्निग्ध उष्ण मधुर
वृष्य गुरु तृितका करता है और
दृढता बृंहण उत्साह और शयन इनको
भी पैदा करताहै ॥ ८० ॥

धार्तराष्ट्रचकोराणांदक्षाणांशिखि
नामपि । चटकानाऋयानिस्युर
ण्डानिचिहतानिच ॥ ८१ ॥
धातेराष्ट्र (सपेद चरण हंस) चकोर
दक्ष (मुरगा) मयूर चटक इनके अंड
और हित कारी जो अन्य अंडहैं॥ ८१॥

रेतःक्षीणेषुकासेषुह्रद्रोगेषुक्षतेषु
च । मधुराण्यवपाकीनिसतोबल
कराणिच ॥ ८२ ॥
वे सब वीर्यक्षीण कास हृद्रोग क्षतमें
हित होतेहैं मधुरहैं शीघ्रपाकहैं और
तत्काल बलकारीहैं ॥ ८२ ॥

शरीरबृंहणेनान्यत्दार्ढ्यंमांसाद्धि
शिष्यते । इतिवर्गस्तृतीयोऽयं
मांसानांपरिकीर्तितः ॥ ८३ ॥
इति मांसवर्गः ।
शरीरकी वृद्धि करनेमें मांससे अन्य
कोई दृढ नहींहै, यह तीसरा वर्ग मांसोंका
वर्णन किया ॥ ८३ ॥इति मांसवर्गः॥

अथ शाकवर्गः ।

पाठातुषाशठीशाकंवास्तुकंसुनि
षण्णकम् ।विद्याद्दृशाहितंदोषघ्नं
भिन्नवर्चस्तुवास्तुकम् ॥ ८४ ॥
पाठा तुषा शठी वास्तुक सुनिषण्णक
ये शाक शाही त्रिदोषके नाशकहैं
मल भेदक तो वास्तु (बथुआ)
होताहै ॥ ८४ ॥

त्रिदोषशमनीवृष्याकाकमाचीर
सायनी । नात्युष्णशीतवीर्यां
च भेदनीकुठनाशिनी ॥ ८५ ॥
और काकमाची (काय फललता)
त्रिदोष नाशक वृष्य रसायन अति उष्ण
और शीतलवीर्य नहीं; भेदक कुठ
शमनी होतीहै ॥ ८५ ॥

translation:
( 253 )

Verse 78:
The tortoise (kurma) is said to be strengthening, wind-pacifying, aphrodisiac, dry yet strength-building, intellect- and memory-promoting, wholesome, and curative of wasting diseases. The flesh of the boar is strength-giving, appetite-stimulating, promotes sweating, and is heavy.
— 78 —

Verse 79:
The flesh of the cow is beneficial only in disorders of wind (vata), nasal catarrh, and irregular fevers, as well as in dry cough, fatigue, and severe wasting of muscle tissue.
— 79 —

Verse 80:
Buffalo meat is unctuous, hot, sweet, aphrodisiac, and heavy; it produces firmness, bulk of body, vigor, and also promotes sleep.
— 80 —

Verse 81:
The eggs of the bar-headed goose (dhartarashttra), the chakora partridge, the domestic fowl (daksha), the peacock, the sparrow, and other birds that are beneficial — all are wholesome.
— 81 —

Verse 82:
These eggs are beneficial in conditions of semen-depletion, cough, heart disease, and injuries; they are sweet, quickly digested, and immediately strength-giving.
— 82 —

Verse 83:
Nothing is as effective as meat for building up the body and producing firmness. This is the third chapter, describing the group of meats.
— Thus ends the Chapter on Meats (Mamsavarga). —

Now begins the Chapter on Vegetables (Shakavarga):

Verse 84:
Patha, tusha, shathi, vastuka (bathua/goosefoot), and sunishannaka — know these vegetables to be beneficial to the eyes, destroyers of the three doshas; and vastuka in particular causes loosening of the stool.
— 84 —

Verse 85:
Kakamachi (the nightshade plant) pacifies the three doshas, is aphrodisiac, and acts as a rasayana (rejuvenator); its potency is neither excessively hot nor cold; it is a purgative and cures skin diseases (kushtha).
— 85 —

text:
( २५२ )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

राजक्षवकशाकन्तुत्रिदोषशमनं
लघु । ग्राहिहस्तंविशेषेणग्रहण्य
शोविकारिणाम् ॥ ८६ ॥
राजक्षवक ( राई ) का शाक तो
त्रिदोषका शमन लघु ग्राही और विशेष-
कर ग्रहणी अशके रोगियोंको उत्तमहै८६

कालशाकन्तुकटुकेदीपनंगरशो
फिजत् । लघूष्णंवातलंरूक्षंक
रालंशाकमुच्यते ॥ ८७ ॥
कालका शाक तो कटु दीपन गलके
शोफका नाशकहै, और करालका शाक
लघु उष्ण वातल रूक्ष कहाहै ॥ ८७ ॥

दीपनीचोष्णवीर्याचंग्राहिणीक
फमारुते । प्रशस्यतेऽम्लचाङ्गेरी
ग्रहण्यशोहिताचसा ॥ ८८ ॥
और अम्लचांगेरी, दीपन वीर्यमें
उष्ण ग्राही कफ वातमें श्रेष्ठ और ग्रहणी
और अर्शमें हितहै ॥ ८८ ॥

मधुरामधुरापाकेभेदनीश्लेष्मवर्द्धि
नी । वृष्याऽस्निग्धाचशीताचमद
श्रीचाप्युपोदका ॥ ८९ ॥
और उपोदकी ( पोई ) मदघ्नी जो हैं,
वे मधुर, पाकमें मधुर भेदक कफ वर्द्धक
वृष्य, स्निग्ध और शीतलहैं ॥ ८९ ॥

रूक्षोमदविषघ्नश्मप्रशस्तोरक्कपि
त्तिनाम् । मधुरोमधुरःपाकेशीत
लस्तंडुलीयकः ॥ ९० ॥

और तंडुलीयकका शाक रूक्ष, मद
और विष नाशक, रक्तपित्तयोंको हित
मधुर, पाकमें मधुर और शीतल होताहै९०

मण्डूकपर्णीवेत्राग्रंकुचेलावनित
क्ककम् । कर्कोटकावल्गुजकौप

शकुलादनी ॥ ९१ ॥

वृषपुष्पाणिशाङ्गिंष्ठाकेवूकंसकिट

वार्ताकंतिलपर्णिका । कुलकंक
र्कशिनिम्बंशाकंपर्पटकञ्चयत् ९२
वृषकेपुष्प, शाङ्गेषा केवुक किटिछक

translation:
( 252 )
From the Charaka Samhita

Rajaksavaka (mustard greens) pacifies all three doshas, is light, and is particularly astringent; it is especially recommended for those suffering from disorders of the grahani (small intestine/digestive tract). || 86 ||

The greens of Kala (a dark leafy vegetable) are pungent and digestive-stimulating, and destroy swelling of the throat; the greens of Karala are said to be light, hot in potency, wind-aggravating, and rough. || 87 ||

Amlachangeri (sorrel/Oxalis) is digestive-stimulating, hot in potency, astringent, and excellent for kapha and vata; it is beneficial in disorders of the grahani and in hemorrhoids. || 88 ||

Upodaki (poi/Basella) is sweet in taste and sweet after digestion, laxative, kapha-increasing, aphrodisiac, not oily, cooling, and destroys intoxication. || 89 ||

Tanduliyaka (amaranth greens) is rough, destroys intoxication and poison, is recommended for those with rakta-pitta (bleeding disorders), is sweet, sweet after digestion, and cooling. || 90 ||

Mandukparni (brahmi/Centella), the tip of the cane (vetragra), Kuchela, Vanatittaka, Karkotaka, Valgujaka, Patola, and Shakuladani. || 91 ||

The flowers of Vrisha (Adhatoda), Shangishtha, Kevuka, Kitichhaka, Nadi-kalaya, Gobhi (cabbage), Baingan (eggplant), Tilaparnika, Kulaka, Karkasha-nimba, and Parpataka — all these greens. || 92 ||

All of these are kapha and pitta-reducing, bitter, cooling, and become pungent after digestion. All the snupa-group vegetables, as well as Phanjika, Chichhli, and Katumbuka. || 93 ||

All varieties of yam (aluka) along with their leaves, Kutinjara, the flowers of Shana and Shalmali, Karbuda, and Suvarchala. || 94 ||

text:
सूत्रस्थानम् ।
( २५५ )
Digitized By Sādhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

निष्पावःकोविदारश्वपतुरश्वाखुपर्णिका । कुमारजीवोलोद्राकपालङ्कचामारिषस्तथा ॥ ९५ ॥

निष्पाव कोविदार पतुर आखुपर्णिका कुमारजीव लट्वाक पालंकी और मारिष ॥ ९५ ॥

कलम्बोनालिकास्मर्युःकुसुम्भवृकधूमकौ । लक्ष्मणश्वपुच्छाडोनलिनीकाकुवेरकः ॥ ९६ ॥

कलंब नालिका स्मर्यु कुसुंभ वृकधूम, लक्ष्मण, श्रपुच्छाड नलिनीका कुबेरक ॥ ९६ ॥

लोणिकायवशाकश्चकूष्माण्डकमवल्गुजः । यातुकःशालकल्याणीत्रिपर्णीपीलुपर्णिका ॥ ९७ ॥

लोणिका, यवशाक, कुष्माण्डक अवल्गुज यातुक शालकल्याणी त्रिपर्णी पीलुपर्णी ॥ ९७ ॥

शाकंगुरुचरूक्षश्चपायोविष्ठम्यजीर्यति । मधुरंशीतवीर्यञ्चपुरीषस्यचभेदनम् ॥ ९८ ॥

ये शाक गुरु रूक्ष और विष्टम्भ करके जीर्ण होते हैं, और मधुर हैं शीतल वीर्य हैं, मल भेदकहैं ॥ ९८ ॥

स्विन्नंनिष्पीडितरसंस्नेहाढ्यंतत्रशस्यते । शणस्यकोविदारस्यकबुदारस्यशाल्मलेः ॥ ९९ ॥

और स्वेदन किये इनका निष्पीडित रस स्नेह युक्त होनेसे श्रेष्ठ कहा है, और शणकोविदार कबुदार, संभल ॥ ९९ ॥

पुष्पग्राहिम्पशस्त्वरक्किपितेविशेषतः । न्यग्रोधोदुम्बराश्वत्थपुक्षपआदिपल्लवाः ॥ १०० ॥

इनके पुष्प ग्राही और विशेष कर रक्त पित्तमें श्रेष्ठ होताहै, वट गूलर पीपल पिलखन पद्म आदिके पत्ते ॥ १०० ॥

कषायाःस्तम्भनाःशीताहिताःपित्तातिसारिणाम् । वायुवत्सादनीह्न्यात्कफगण्डीरिचत्रकौ १०१

कषाय स्तंभन शीतल, और पित्तके अतिसारियोंको हित होते हैं, और वत्सादिनी वायुको कंडीरियेचित्रक, कफकी नाश करतेहैं ॥ १०१ ॥

श्रेयसीबिल्वपर्णीचिबिल्वपत्रन्तुवातनुत् । भाण्डीशतावरीशाकंबलाजीवन्तजञ्चयत् ॥ १०२ ॥

और उत्तम बिल्वपर्णी, और बिल्वपत्र ये वातको नष्ट करते हैं, और भांडी शतावरकाशाक बलाजीवन्ती ॥ १०२ ॥

पर्वण्याःपर्वपुष्प्याश्चवातपित्तहरंस्मृतम् । लघुभिन्नशकितिचंकलाङ्गुलक्युरुवुकयोः ॥ १०३ ॥

पर्वणी पर्वपुष्पी इनका शाक वातहर कहाहै लांगुलकी उरुबुक इनका शाक लघु तिक्त और मल भेदक होताहै १०३

Verse 95:
Nishpava (flat bean), Kovidara, Shvapatura, Ashvakarni (horse-ear plant), Kumarajiva, Lodhra, Kapalanka, Chamarisha — these are the plants listed here.

Commentary: Nishpava, Kovidara, Patura, Ashvaparnnika, Kumarajiva, Latvaka, Palankee, and Marisha. (95)

Verse 96:
Kalamba, Nalika, Smaryu, Kusumbha, Vrikadhooma, Lakshmana, Ashvapuchchhada, Nalinee, and Kuberaka. (96)

Verse 97:
Lonika, Yavashaka, Kushmanda, Avalguja, Yatuka, Shalakalyani, Triparnee, and Piluparnee. (97)

Verse 98:
These leafy vegetables are heavy, dry, and cause constipation; they are slowly digested. They are sweet in taste, cold in potency, and act as purgatives for the stool. (98)

Verse 99:
The juice extracted after steaming these is recommended, as it becomes enriched with unctuous qualities. This applies to Shana, Kovidara, Kabudara, and Shalmali. (99)

Verse 100:
Their flowers are astringent, and are especially excellent in conditions of blood-pitta (hemorrhagic disorders). The leaves of Vata (banyan), Gular (cluster fig), Peepal, Pilkhan, Padma (lotus), and similar trees are recommended. (100)

Verse 101:
These are astringent, styptic, and cooling, and are beneficial for those suffering from pitta-type diarrhea. Vatsadani subdues Vayu (wind); Kandirichitrak destroys Kapha (phlegm). (101)

Verse 102:
The excellent Bilva-parnee and Bilva leaves destroy Vata (wind disorders). The vegetables of Bhandi, Shatavari, Bala, and Jivanti are also to be used. (102)

Verse 103:
The vegetables of Parvani and Parvapushpi are known to relieve both Vata and Pitta. The vegetables of Langulaki and Urubu are light, bitter, and act as purgatives for the stool. (103)

( २५६ )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।
Digitized By Siodhanta eSangoit Gyaan Kosha

तिलवेतसशाकञ्चशाकंमञ्चांगुल
स्यवा । वातलंकटुतिक्काम्लमधो
मार्गप्रवर्तकम् ॥ १०४ ॥
और तिलवेतस और पंचांगुलका
शाक वातल कटु तिक्त अम्ल है और
अधोमार्गका प्रवर्तकहै ॥ १०४ ॥

रूक्षाम्लमुष्णंकौसुम्भंकफघ्निपित्त
वर्द्धनम् । त्रपुसैर्वारुकंस्वादुगुरु
विष्टम्भशीतलम् ॥ १०५ ॥
कुसुंभका शाक रूक्ष अम्ल उष्ण है
कफनाशक और पित्त वर्द्धक है, त्रपुस
एवंवारुकका शाक स्वादु गुरु विष्टंभि
शीतल है ॥ १०५ ॥

मुखप्रियञ्चरूक्षञ्चमूत्रलंत्रपुसंत्व
ति।एर्वारुकञ्चसंपकंदाहतृष्णाकु
माार्चिनुत् । वचोंभेदीन्यलावूिन
रूक्षशीतगुरूणिच ॥ १०६ ॥
और त्रपुसका तो मुखमें प्रिय रूक्ष अति
मूत्रल होताहै,और अलाबू (मीठीतूंबी)
मलकीभेदक रूक्ष शीतल गुरु होतीहै १०६

चिभिंठ्येर्वारुकेतदद्वञ्चोंभेदिहते
तुते । कूष्माण्डमुकंसक्षारंमधुरा
म्लंतथालघु ॥ १०७ ॥
और चिभिंट एवंवारुक (ककड़ीके
भेद)येदो और पका हुआ एर्वारुक दाह तृ
ष्णाघ्नानि इनको नष्ट करताहै तिसी प्रकार
मलभेदनमें हितकारी होते हैं और कु-
ष्मांड क्षार मधुर अम्ल लघु कहाहै १०७

षष्ठमूत्रपुरीषञ्चसर्वदोषनिवर्हण
म् । केलूटञ्चकदम्बञ्चनदीमाष
कमेन्दुकम् ॥ १०८ ॥
और मूत्र पुरीषका उत्पादक, सर्व
दोषनाशक होताहै और केलूट, कदंब,
नदीमाषक, ऐन्दुक, इनको ॥ १०८ ॥

विषदंगुरुशीतंचसमिभिष्यन्दिचो
च्यते ॥ १०९ ॥
विषद, गुरु शीतल, भली प्रकार
अभिष्यन्दी कहते हैं ॥ १०९ ॥

उत्पलानिकषायाणिपित्तरक्तहरा
णिच । तथातालप्रलम्बञ्चउरः
क्षतरुजापहम् । खर्जूरंतालशस्य
ञ्चरक्तपित्तक्षयापहम् ॥ ११० ॥
उत्पल, कसेले पित्तरक्तनाशक
होते हैं तैसेही तालमलंब, उरःक्षतकी
पीडाका नाशक है खजूर और तालशस्य
ये रक्तपित्त क्षय इनका नाशक हैं ११०

भरूटंबिसशालूककौञ्चादनकशेरु
कम् । शृङ्गाटकंकलोडञ्चगुरु
विष्टम्भशीतलम् । कुमुदोत्पल
नालास्तुसपुष्पाःसफलाःस्मृताः १११

भरूट, बिस, शालूक, कौंचादन
कसेरु, सिंघाड़ा, कलोड्य, ये गुरु, वि-
ष्टम्भी, और शीतल, होतेहैं, और कुमुद
उत्पलके, नाल, पुष्प और फल सहित
ये ॥ १११ ॥

translation:
( 256 )
From the Charaka Samhita

Verse 104:
The vegetables of tila-vetasa (a type of sesame plant) and panchamgula are vata-aggravating, pungent, bitter, and sour in taste, and they promote downward movement (of bodily substances). || 104 ||

Verse 105:
The vegetable of kusumbha (safflower) is dry, sour, and hot in quality; it suppresses kapha and increases pitta. The vegetables of trapusa (cucumber) and varuka are tasty, heavy, constipating, and cooling. || 105 ||

Verse 106:
Trapusa is pleasing to the mouth, dry, and strongly diuretic. Alabu (sweet gourd) is a bowel-opener, dry, cooling, and heavy. || 106 ||

Verse 107:
Chibibhinta and varuka (both varieties of cucumber) — these two, along with ripe varuka, destroy burning sensation and thirst, and are beneficial in clearing the bowels. Kushmanda (ash gourd) is said to be alkaline, sweet, sour, and light. || 107 ||

Verse 108:
It promotes urine and stool, and destroys all doshas. Keluta, kadamba, nadimasaka, and enduka — || 108 ||

Verse 109:
— are said to be clean (vishada), heavy, cooling, and highly productive of secretions (abhishyandi). || 109 ||

Verse 110:
The utpala (blue lotus) and similar flowers are astringent and remove excess pitta and blood. Similarly, talapralamba removes the pain of chest injuries. Dates (kharjura) and the fruit of the palm tree remove hemorrhagic disorders and wasting disease. || 110 ||

Verse 111:
Bharuta, bisa (lotus stem), shaluka (lotus root), kaunchadan, kaseru (water chestnut), singhara (water caltrop), kalodya — all these are heavy, constipating, and cooling. The stem, flower, and fruit of kumuda and utpala (water lilies and lotuses) are all considered beneficial. || 111 ||

text:
Digitized By Shreegiri Gyaan Kosha ( २५७ )

शीताःस्वादुकषायास्तुकफमारु
तकोपनाः । कषायमीषद्विष्टिंभि
र्कपित्तहरंस्मृतम् ॥ ११२ ॥
शीतल, स्वादु, कषाय, होते हैं;
और, कफ, वातको कुपित, करते हैं;
इनका, कषाय, किंचित् विष्टंभी, और
रक्त, पित्त, नाशक, कहाहै ॥ ११२ ॥
पौष्करन्तुभवेद्बीजंमधुरंरसपाक
योः । बल्यःशीतोगुरुःस्निग्धस्त
पणोवृंहणात्मकः ॥ ११३ ॥
और पुष्करका बीज, रस, और
पाकमें मधुर होता है, और, बल्य,
शीतल, गुरु, स्निग्ध, तपंण वृद्धिका-
रक ॥ ११३ ॥
वातपित्तहरःस्वादुर्वृष्योमुञात
कःस्मृतः । जीवनोवृंहणोवृष्यः
कंक्यःशस्तोरसायने ॥ ११४ ॥
वात पित्तनाशक, स्वादु, और अत्यंत
वृष्य मुंजातक होता है, और जीवन
वृंहण वृष्य, कण्ठको हित, और रसायनमें
श्रेष्ठ होता है ॥ ११४ ॥
विदारीकन्दोबल्यश्चमूत्रलःस्वादु
शीतलः । अम्लीकायाःस्मृतः
कन्दोग्रहण्यशोहितोलघुः॥ ११५ ॥
विदारीकन्द, बल्य, मूत्रल, स्वादु,
और शीतल होताहै; अम्लिकाका कन्द,
ग्रहणी और अर्शमें हित और, लघु
कहाहै ॥ ११५ ॥

नात्युष्णःकफवातघ्नोग्राहीशस्तो
मदात्यये । त्रिदोषंबद्धिविण्मूत्रं
सार्षपंशाकमुच्यते ॥ ११६ ॥
और अत्यन्त उष्ण नहीं, कफ, वात
नाशक, ग्राह्य, और मदात्ययमें श्रेष्ठ
सरसोंका शाक कहाहै ॥ ११६ ॥
तद्वत्पिण्डालुकंविद्यात्कन्दत्वा
च्चमुखप्रियम् । सर्पच्छत्रकवर्ज्या
स्तुबहुचोन्यच्छत्रजातयः ११७
और त्रिदोष और मलमूत्रका बन्धक
कहाहै, तिसी प्रकार पिंडालुककों कन्द
होनेसे मुखमें प्रिय जानै और सर्पछ-
त्रकको छोडकर बहुतसी अन्य छत्रकी
जाति ॥ ११७ ॥
शीताःपीनसकर्यंश्चमधुरागुर्व्येव
च । चतुर्थःशाकवर्गेऽयंपत्रक
न्दफलाश्रयः ॥ ११८ ॥
इतिशाकवर्गः ।
शीतल पीनसकारक मधुर और
गुर्वीं ( भारी ) कही हैं पत्र, कन्द, फल-
के आश्रयसे चौथा यह शाक वर्गहै ११८
इति–शाकवर्गः
अथफलवर्गः ।
