translation:
(278)
From the Charaka Samhita

That which is oil, by virtue of the transformation arising from combination, is said to destroy all diseases. (279)

By the use of oil, the chiefs of the demons in ancient times became free from old age, free from disorder, free from fatigue, and attained extraordinary strength. (280)

Castor oil is sweet, heavy, and increases kapha; it is supreme in removing vata, blood disorders, abdominal tumors, heart disease, and chronic fever. (281)

Mustard oil is pungent and hot; it vitiates blood and pitta, and removes kapha, semen disorders, vata, itching, and skin eruptions (kotha). (282)

Piyala (chironji) oil is sweet, heavy, and increases kapha; those who wish benefit regard it as suitable in the combination of vata and pitta, due to its lack of excessive heat. (283)

Linseed (atasi) oil is sweet and sour, but pungent in post-digestive effect (vipaka); it is hot in potency, beneficial for vata, and aggravates blood and pitta. (284)

Safflower (kusumbha) oil is hot, pungent in vipaka, heavy, and causes burning sensation; it is especially provocative of all diseases. (285)

And other oils that come from fruits — those that are used near food — should be described according to their respective qualities and actions. (286)

Marrow (majja) and fat (vasa) are sweet, nourishing, aphrodisiac, and strength-giving; whether cooling or heating, vasa and majja should be prescribed according to the constitution of the individual. (287)

It is nourishing, stimulates digestion, aphrodisiac, hot, removes vata and kapha, sweet in post-digestive effect, appetizing, and a universal medicine. (288)

मंत्रस्थानम् ।
Digitized By Siddhaata eGangoth Gyaan Kosha
( २७९ )

और विषभेषज ( सुंठी ) स्नेहसेयुक्त दीपन, वृष्य, उष्ण, वात, कफ, नाशक, पाकमें मधुर, हृद्य और रोचक होतीहै२८८

श्लेष्मलामधुराचाद्रिगुर्वीस्निग्धा चिपिप्पली । साशुष्काकफवात घ्नीकटुकावृष्यसम्मता ॥ २८९ ॥

और हरी पीपल, छेष्मल, मधुर, गरिष्ठ और स्निग्ध, आद्रे होती है, और शुष्क पीपल, कफ, वात, नाशक, कटु, उष्ण, और वृष्य औषधियोंमें सम्मत होती है ॥ २८९ ॥

नात्यर्थमुष्णंमिरचमवृष्यंलघुरोचनम् । छेदित्वाच्छोषणत्वाच दीपनंकफवातजित् ॥ २९० ॥

और मिर्च, अत्यन्त, उष्ण नहीं वृष्य नहीं लघु और रोचक और छेदक और शोषक, होनेसे दीपन होतीहैं कफ और वातको जीततीहैं ॥ २९० ॥

वातश्लेष्मिवबन्धघ्नंकटुकंदीपनं लघु ॥ हिंगुश्रुलपशमनंनिवयात् पाचनरोचनम् ॥ २९१ ॥

और हींग वात, कफ, विबन्धका नाशक कटु, उष्ण, दीपन, लघु, शूलका शमन पाचन और रोचन होताहै२९१॥

रोचनंदीपनंहृद्यंचक्षुष्यमिवदाहि च ॥ त्रिदोषघ्नंसमधुरंसैन्धवंलव णोत्तमम् ॥ २९२ ॥

लवणोंमें उत्तम सैन्धव, रोचन, दीपन

हृद्य, चक्षुको हित अविदाही त्रिदोष नाशक और मधुर होताहै ॥ २९२ ॥

सौक्ष्म्यादौष्ण्याच्छवुत्वाचसौगन्ध्याचरुचिप्रदम् ॥ सौवर्चलं विबन्धघ्नंहृद्यमुद्रारशोधिंच २९३

और सौवर्चल,( काला नोन ) सूक्ष्म, उष्ण, लघु सुगन्ध होनेसे रुचिको करता है विबन्धका नाशक हृद्य उद्रारका शोधक है ॥ २९३ ॥

तैक्ष्ण्यादौष्ण्याद्वयवायित्वादीपनंशूलनाशनम् ॥ ऊर्ध्वाधश्च वातानामानुलोम्यकरंविडम् २९४

और बायिविडंग, तीक्ष्ण उष्ण व्यवायी होनेसे दीपन है और शूलका नाशक होताहै और ऊपर नीचेकी वायुका अनुलोम, करताहै ॥ २९४ ॥

सतिक्ककटुसक्षारंतीक्ष्णमुत्क्षेदिचोद्रिदम् ॥ नकाललवणेगन्धःसौवर्चलगुणाश्चते ॥ २९५॥

और क्षार, ( खारी लवण ) तिक्त, कटु उत्केदी, तीक्ष्ण, ऊर्ध्वभेदी जो होताहै उस काला लवणमें, कुछ भेद नहीं, जो, सौवर्चलके गुणहैं वेही उसके होतेहैं२९५

सामुद्रकंसमधुरंसतिक्तंकटुपांशुजम् ॥ रोचनंलवणंसर्वंपाकिकं स्यिनिलापहम् ॥ २९६ ॥

समुद्रका लवण, मधुर, तिक्त, कटु पांसुओंसे उत्पन्न होताहै, सब प्रकारका

( २८० )

लवण, रोचन, पाचक, रेचक, वात,
नाशक, होताहै ॥ २९६ ॥

हृत्पाण्डुग्रहणीदोषप्लीहानाहगल
ग्रहान् । कासंकफजमशॉसिया
वश्कोव्यपोहित ॥ २९७ ॥

याव ( जौ ) का शूक, हृदय, पाण्डु,
ग्रहिणी, इनके दोषोंको प्लीहा, आनाह
और गलग्रहको, कफके कासको और
अर्शको, नष्ट करताहै ॥ २९७ ॥

तीक्ष्णोष्णोलघुरूक्षश्च्केदीपाकी
विदारणः । दहनोदीपनश्छेत्तास
बेःक्षारोऽग्निसन्निभः ॥ २९८ ॥

और सब प्रकारका क्षार, तीक्ष्ण,
उष्ण, लघु, रूक्ष, केदी और पाचक,
विदारण, दाहक, दीपन, छेदक, अग्निके
समान होताहै ॥ २९८ ॥

कारव्यःकुंजिकाजाजीकवरीधा
न्यतुम्बुरुः । रोचनंदीपनंवातक
फदौर्गन्ध्यनाशनम् ॥ २९९ ॥

और कारव्य, कुंजिका, अजाजी,
कवरी,धान्य तुम्बुरु, ये,रोचन,दीपन वात
कफ और दुगंधिके नाशक होतेंहैं २९९

आहारयोगिनांभकिनश्चयोनतु
विद्यते । समामोद्दादशश्चायंवर्ग
आहारयोगिनाम् ॥ ३०० ॥

इत्याहारयोगवर्गः।

और आहारके योगी जो पदार्थहैं,

उनके भेदोंका निश्चय नहींहैं किइतनेंहैं।
आहारके योगियोंका यह द्वादशवांवर्ग
समाप्त हुआ ॥ ३०० ॥

इत्याहारयोगवर्गः ।

शूकधान्यंशमीधान्यंसमातीतंप्र
शस्यते । पुराणंप्रायशोरूक्षंप्राये
णाभिनवंगुरु ॥ ३०१ ॥

शूकधान्य और शमीधान्य, यह
गतवर्षका होय तो श्रेष्ठ होताहै और वह
प्रायः पुराना रूक्ष, होताहैं और नया
अन्नप्रायः गुरु होताहैं ॥ ३०१ ॥

यद्यदागच्छतिक्षिप्रंतत्तञ्जवुतरं
स्मृतम् ॥ ३०२ ॥

ज्यों ज्यों शीघ्र पक आता है, त्यों
त्यों अत्यन्त लघु कहाहैं ॥ ३०२ ॥

निस्तुषंयुक्तिभृष्टंतुसूप्यंलघुविप
च्यते ॥ ३०३ ॥

तुषसे रहित युक्तिसे भुना हुआ,
दालके हित और पाकमें लघु होतेंहैं ३०३

मृतंकेशातिमेध्यश्चवृद्धंबालंविषै
हतम् । अगोचरमृतंव्याडमृदितं
मांसमुत्सृजेत् ॥ ३०४ ॥

मृत, और कृश, अत्यन्तअपवित्र,
वृद्ध, बाल, विषोंसे हत, परोक्षमें मृत,
व्याड ( हिंसक ) का मारा हुवा, इतने
मांसोंको त्याग दे ॥ ३०५ ॥

अतोऽन्यथाहितंमांसंवृहणंबलव
र्द्धनम् ॥ श्रीणनःसर्वभूतानांह्यो
translation:
( 280 )

[Salt, appetizer, digestive, laxative, and destroyer of wind — verse 296.]

The chaff of yava (barley) removes afflictions of the heart, anemia, disorders of the digestive tract, diseases of the spleen, bloating, and throat obstruction; it also removes cough arising from kapha and hemorrhoids. (297)

[Alkali substances are] sharp, hot, light, rough, cutting, and digestive in action; they are tearing, burning, kindling, cutting — resembling fire itself. (298)

Karavya (caraway), kunjika (black cumin), ajaji (cumin), kavari, dhaniya (coriander), and tumburu — these are appetizing, digestive, and destroyers of wind, kapha, and foul odor. (299)

As for the substances that combine with food, their varieties cannot be precisely numbered. This twelfth group of food-combining substances is hereby concluded. (300)

Thus ends the chapter on food-combining groups.

Shuka-dhanya (awned grains) and shami-dhanya (leguminous grains), when of the previous year's harvest, are considered excellent. Old grain is generally rough and dry, while new grain is generally heavy. (301)

Whatever grain ripens quickly is known to be correspondingly light. (302)

Grain that is husked, skillfully roasted, and prepared as soup becomes light and easy to digest. (303)

Meat that is from an animal that died on its own, or that is very thin, extremely impure, aged, young, poisoned, killed out of sight, killed by a predator, or that has been crushed — all such meat should be abandoned. (305)

Meat other than these is beneficial, nourishing, and strengthening. It is pleasing to all living beings...

text:
Digitized By Siddhanta Sangrahi Gyaan Kosha
(२८१)

मांसरसःपरम् ॥ ३०५ ॥

इनसे अन्य प्रकारका जो मांस है, वह हित, छंदण, और बलवर्धक होताहै सब भूतोंको तृति करनेवाला, और परम हृद्य, मांसरस होताहै ॥ ३०५ ॥

शुष्यतांव्याधिघ्युक्तानांकृशानां क्षीणरेतसाम् ॥ बलवर्णिथिनाञ्चै वरसंविधायथामृतम् ॥ ३०६ ॥

सूखते हुए, और जो व्याधिसे छूटे हैं, कृश जो क्षीणवीर्य हैं, और जो बल, रूपके अभिलाषी हैं, उनके लिये यह रस अमृतकी समानहै ॥ ३०६ ॥

सर्वरोगप्रशमनंयथास्वंविहितं रसम् ॥ विद्यात्स्वर्य्येबलकरंच योबुद्धीन्द्रियायुषाम् ॥ ३०७॥

और यथायोग्य बनाया हुआ रस, सब रोगोंको शान्त करताहै; और उस रसको स्वरका हितकारी, अवस्था बुद्धि, इन्द्रिय और जीवन, इनका बलकारी जानना ॥ ३०७ ॥

व्यायामिनित्याःस्त्रीनित्यामधिनित्याश्चयेनराः ॥ नित्यंमांसरसाहारानातुराःस्युर्नदुर्बलाः ३०८॥

जो, व्यायाम, स्त्रीका भोग, मद्यपान, नित्य करते हैं और नित्यमांसके रसका, आहार करते हैं, वे न आतुर होते हैं, और न दुर्बल होते हैं ॥ ३०८ ॥

किमिवातातपहतंशुष्कंजीर्णम नार्चवम् ॥ शाकंनिःस्नेहसिद्धञ्च वर्ज्येयञ्चापिरश्रुतम् ॥ ३०९ ॥

और, कृमि, वात, आतप, इनसे हता हुआ, शुष्क, जीर्ण, और अन्य ऋतुका, और जो स्नेहमें सिद्ध न हुआ हो वह, और जो परिश्रुत (रसेदार) नहो, ऐसे शाककों, वर्जे दे ॥ ३०९ ॥

पुराणमामंसंकिलष्टंकिमिव्याल हिमातपैः ॥ अदेशाकालजंकिञ्चित्यस्यातफलमसाधुतव् ॥ ३१०

पुराना, आम (कच्चा) और कृमि, व्याल, और आतप, इनसे, युक्त और देश, कालमें, अनुत्पन्न, और छिन्न, जो फल वह असाधु होता है ॥ ३१० ॥

हरितानांयथाशाकंनिर्देशंसाधनाहते ॥ ३११ ॥

हरित फलोंका साधनके बिना शाकके आनुसार निर्देशहै अर्थात् गुणहै ॥ ३११

मद्याम्बुगोरसादीनांस्वेस्वेवर्गेविनिश्चयः ॥ ३१२ ॥

मद्य, जल, गोरस, आदिकोंका, अपने २ वर्गेंमें निश्चय है ॥ ३१२ ॥

यदाहारगुणैःपानंविपरीतंतदिंष्यते । अन्नानुपानंधातूनांदृढ्यञ्च विरोधिच ॥ ३१३ ॥

जो पान, आहारके गुणोंसे हो वह विपरीत होताहै धातुओंका गुण अपनेके अनुसार वह देखहै जो विरोधी नहो ३१३

translation:
Page 281

Meat broth is supreme. (305)

Meat other than the kinds previously described is beneficial, pleasing, and strength-promoting; it satisfies all living beings and is supremely agreeable to the heart — such is meat broth. (305)

For those who are wasting away, afflicted by disease, who are emaciated, whose vital essence is depleted, and for those who desire strength and good complexion — this broth is like nectar. (306)

That broth prepared in the proper manner according to each condition should be understood to subdue all diseases; it is also beneficial for the voice, and promotes the strength of the intellect, the senses, and the life-force. (307)

Those men who regularly exercise, regularly enjoy the company of women, and regularly drink wine, and who daily take meat broth as their nourishment — they neither become afflicted with illness nor do they become weak. (308)

Vegetables that have been damaged by insects, wind, or sunlight; that are dry and stale; that belong to a different season; that have not been cooked with fats; and that are not well-strained (not juicy) — such vegetables should be avoided. (309)

Old and unripe fruits, those affected by insects, reptiles, cold, or heat; those grown out of their proper region or season; and those that are improperly cut — such fruits are unwholesome. (310)

For fresh greens, the same guidelines as those described for cooked vegetables apply in terms of preparation and properties. (311)

The classification of wine, water, milk products, and similar substances is determined within their respective categories. (312)

When a drink is contrary to the qualities of the food taken, it becomes harmful. The drink taken after food should be such that it does not oppose the strengthening of the bodily tissues and does not act adversely against them. (313)

Digitized सुश्रुतसंहिताप्राप्त Gyaan Kosha

आसवानांसमुद्दिष्टाअशीतिश्चतुरुत्तराः ॥ ३१४ ॥
और चौरासी आसव पीछे वर्णन कर चुके हैं ॥ ३१४ ॥

जलंपेयमपेयञ्चपरीक्ष्यानुपिबेद्धितम् ॥ ३१५ ॥
पीनेयोग्य और अयोग्य भेदसे जल दो प्रकारका होताहै; उसकी परीक्षा करिके हित जलका पान करे ॥ ३१५ ॥

स्निग्धोष्णंमारुतेशस्तंपित्तेमधुरशीतलम् । कफेऽनुपानंरूक्षोष्णं क्षयेमांसरसःपरम् ॥ ३१६ ॥
वातमें, स्निग्धोष्ण, जल, श्रेष्ठ होताहै पित्तमें मधुर, शीतल, कफमें, रूक्षोष्ण, अनुपान होताहै क्षयमें मांसरस, श्रेष्ठ होताहै ॥ ३१६ ॥

उपवासाध्वभारस्त्रीमारुतातपकर्मिभिः । क्लान्तानामनुपानार्थं यःपथ्यंयथामृतम् ॥ ३१७ ॥
उपवास, मार्ग, भार, स्त्री, पवन, आतप, कर्म; इनसे जो क्लान्तहैं उनके अनुपानके लिये दूध अमृतके समान पथ्यहै ॥ ३१७ ॥

सुराऽकशानांपुष्टच्यर्थमनुपानंप्रशस्यते । काश्र्याथर्थंस्थूलदेहानामनुशस्तंमधूदकदम् ॥ ३१८ ॥
मदिराके पानसे कृशोंकी पुष्टिके लिये दुग्धका अनुपान श्रेष्ठहै और अति

स्थूलोंकी कृशताके लिये मधुयुक्त जल श्रेष्ठहै ॥ ३१८ ॥

अल्पाग्निनामिन्द्राणांतन्द्राशोकभयक्लमैः । मद्यमांसोचितानाञ्च मद्यमेवानुशस्यते ॥ ३१९ ॥
मन्दाग्नि, निद्रासे रहित, तन्द्रा, शोक, भय, ग्लानि, इनसे युक्तोंको और मद्य मांसके अभ्यासियोंको मदिराका अनुपान नहीं श्रेष्ठहै ॥ ३१९ ॥

अथानुपानकर्मप्रवक्ष्यामि । अनुपानंतर्पयतिप्रीणयतिऊर्जयितिपच्यांतिमभिनिर्वर्तयतिभुक्तमवसादयतिअन्नसङ्घातंभिनत्तिमादर्वमापादयतिक्लेदयतिजरयितिमुखपरिणामितामाशुव्यवाययिताञ्चाहारस्योपजनयतिति ॥ ३२० ॥
इसके अनन्तर अनुपान कर्मको कहतेहैं, अनुपान तृप्त करता है प्रीणन ऊर्जन,को करताहै, और पूर्णताको सिद्ध करताहै, भोजनका परिपाक करता है, अन्न आदिके समूहको भेदन करता है, मृदुताको उत्पन्न करता है, क्लेदन, और अन्नकी, जीर्णता, करता है, मुखके परिणामको और शीघ्र, व्यवायपनेको और आहारकी इच्छाको पैदा करता है ॥ ३२० ॥

तत्रश्लोकाः ।
अनुपानंहितंयुक्तंतर्पयत्याशुमान

Verse 314: Eighty-four types of asavas (fermented medicinal preparations) have been described above. (314)

Verse 315: Water should be examined to determine whether it is fit for drinking or not, and only wholesome water should be consumed. (315)

Verse 316: For disorders of vata, warm unctuous water is best as an anupana (post-drink/chaser); for pitta, sweet and cool liquid; for kapha, dry and warm liquid; and for consumption (kshaya), meat broth is best. (316)

Verse 317: For those fatigued by fasting, long travel, carrying heavy loads, sexual activity, exposure to wind, heat, or exertion, milk as an anupana is like nectar and is most beneficial. (317)

Verse 318: For those who are emaciated due to drinking wine, milk as an anupana is recommended for nourishment; and for those who are excessively obese, water mixed with honey is best as an anupana for reducing corpulence. (318)

Verse 319: For those with weak digestive fire, those suffering from drowsiness, grief, fear, and fatigue, and for those habituated to wine and meat, wine itself is recommended as an anupana. (319)

Verse 320: Now the functions of anupana are described: anupana satisfies, nourishes, and energizes; it promotes digestion; it breaks up and disperses the mass of food consumed; it softens; it moistens and helps in digestion of food; it quickly brings about the transformation in the mouth, promotes distribution of nutrients throughout the body, and stimulates the appetite. (320)

text:
Digitized By Siddanta Vaangbhri Gyaan Kosha (२६३)

वग्रु। सुखंपचितचाहारमायुषेच
बलायच ॥ ३२१ ॥
उसमें ये श्लोकहैं, कि हित और
युक्त अनुपान, मनुष्यको शीघ्र, वृत्त
करता है, सुखसे आहारको पचाताहै
और बलकारी होताहै ॥ ३२१ ॥

नोढ्र्वांङ्गमारुताविष्टानिहकाश्वा
सकासिनः । नगीतभाषाध्ययन
प्रसक्तानोरासिक्षताः ॥ ३२२ ॥
जिनके, ऊर्ध्वअंगमें, वात न हो
और जिनको हिक्का, श्वास और कासहो,
और जो गीत, भाषण, अध्ययनमें प्रसक्त
हों जिनकी छातीमें क्षत (घाव) हो॥३२२

पिबेयुरुदकंभुक्तातञ्चिकण्ठोरासि
स्थितम् । स्नेहमाहारजंहत्वाभूयो
दोषायकल्पते ॥ ३२३ ॥
इतने मनुष्य भोजन करके अन्तमें
जलको न पीवैं, क्योंकि वह जल कण्ठ,
और छातीमें, टिककर, आहारसे उत्पन्न
हुए स्नेहको नष्ट करके फिरभी दोषोंको
करताहै ॥ ३२३ ॥

अनुपानैकदेशोऽयमुक्तःप्रायोपयो
गिकः। द्रव्यन्तुनिहिन्देर्दृशक्यं
कत्स्नेन्ननामिभः ॥ ३२४ ॥
यह अनुमानका एकदेश, वह कहा
जो प्रायः उपयोगी है, और संपूर्ण द्रव्य
नाम ले लेकर, दिखानेकी शक्य नहीं
है ॥ ३२४ ॥

यथानामौषधंकिञ्चिद्देशजानांव
चोयथा ॥ द्रव्यंततत्थावाच्य
मनुक्तिमहतद्रवेत् ॥ ३२५ ॥
जैसे, नानाप्रकारकी औषध और
अनेक देशोंमें उत्पन्न मनुष्योंका वचन
जैसे अनेक प्रकारकहै, तिसी प्रकार
वह २ द्रव्यभी कहना, जो यहां नहीं
कहाहै ॥ ३२५ ॥

चराःशरीरावयवाःस्वभावोधात
वःक्रिया ।। लिङ्गंप्रमाणंसंस्का
रोमात्राचासिम्नत्परीक्ष्यते३२६॥
चर शरीरके अवयव, स्वभाव, धातु,
क्रिया, लिंग, प्रमाण, संस्कार, मात्रा,
इनकी यहां परीक्षा कीजातीहै अर्थात्
वर्णन करतेहैं ॥ ३२६ ॥

चरोड्नुपजलाकाशधन्वाथोभ
क्ष्यसंविधौ ।। जलजानूपजाश्चैव
जलानूपचराश्चये ॥ ३२७ ॥
अनूपजल, आकाश, धन्वदेश,
आदिमें जो भक्षयकी विधिहै उसे चर
कहतेहैं जलमें और अनूपदेशमें जो
उत्पन्नहैं और जल अनूप देशमें विचरते
जीवहैं ॥ ३२७ ॥

गुरुभक्ष्याशयेसत्त्वाःसर्वेतेगुरवः
स्मृताः ।। लघुभक्ष्यास्तुलघवो
धन्वजाधन्वचारिणः ॥ ३२८ ॥
और जिनका भक्ष्य, गुरु है वे सब
गुरु कहेहैं और जो लघु, भक्ष्य हैं वे

translation:
Digitized By Siddanta Vaangbhri Gyaan Kosha (263)

[Verse 321]
An anupana (after-drink) that is wholesome, beneficial, and suited to one's constitution aids digestion comfortably, quickly restores the body, and promotes strength. [321]

[Verse 322]
Those who do not have upward-moving wind disorders, or who suffer from hiccup, labored breathing, or cough, and those engaged in singing, speaking, or study, and those who have a wound (injury) in the chest — [322]

[Verse 323]
Such persons should not drink water after eating, for water that settles in the throat and chest will destroy the unctuous essence produced from food and will again give rise to disorders. [323]

[Verse 324]
What has been described here is only a partial account of anupana, given as a practical guide for general use. It is not possible to enumerate every substance by name in its entirety. [324]

[Verse 325]
Just as medicines named after the regions where they originate are many and varied, and the speech of people born in different lands varies, similarly, substances not mentioned here should be understood by analogy. [325]

[Verse 326]
In the context of the mobile (chara) beings, the limbs of the body, their natural constitution, the dhatus (tissues), their actions, characteristics, measure, refinement, and quantity — all of these are examined here, that is, they are being described. [326]

[Verse 327]
Regarding the dietary rules for creatures of marshy water, sky, arid land, and so forth — those born in water, those born in marshy regions, and those that wander in watery and marshy areas are called chara (mobile). [327]

[Verse 328]
All creatures whose food is heavy are themselves reckoned as heavy. Those that eat light food — the creatures of the arid land and those roaming dry regions — are considered light.

text:
( २८४ )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha

और धन्वदेशमें उत्पन्न और वहां विचरनेवाले जीव लघु होतेहैं ॥ ३२८॥
शरीरावयवाःसक्थिशिरःस्कन्धाद्यस्तथा॥सक्थिमांसादुरुस्कन्धस्ततःकोङ्स्ततःशिरः३२९
शरीरके अवयव जो सक्थि, शिर, स्कन्ध, आदिहैं वेभी गुरुहैं मांससे सक्थि गुरुहैं सक्थिसे स्कन्ध, स्कन्धसे कोङ, कोङसे शिर गुरुहैं ॥ ३२९ ॥
वृषणौचर्मसेदृश्शरोणीवृककीयरुहुदम् ।। मांसादुरुतरंविद्याथास्वंमध्यमस्थिंच ॥ ३३० ॥
और वृषण, चर्म, लिंग, श्रोणि, वृक्क यकृत, हृदा, इनको यथायोग्य मांससे अत्यन्त गुरु जानै और मध्यम अस्थिभी, गुरु हैं ॥ ३३० ॥
स्वभावाल्लघवोमुद्गास्तथालावकपिअला: । स्वभावाद्गुरवोमाषावराहमहिषास्तथा ॥ ३३१ ॥
मूंग, स्वभावसे लघुहैं तैसेही लाव और कपिंजल, लघु होतेहैं उड्द स्वभावसे गुरुहैं तैसेही वराह महिष गुरुहैं ३३१
धातूनांशोणितायानांगुरुंविद्याय थोत्तरम्।अलसेभ्योविशिष्यन्ते प्राणिनोयेबहुक्रियाः ॥ ३३२ ॥
रुधिर आदिजो धातुहैं उनकोभी यथोत्तर गुरुजानै जो मनुष्य बहुत कर्मोंको करतेहैं वे आलसियोंसे अच्छे होतेहैं ॥ ३३२ ॥

गौरवेलिङ्गसामान्येपुंसांस्त्रीणाञ्च लाघवम् । महाप्रमाणागुरवःस्व जातौलघवोऽन्यथा ॥ ३३३ ॥
गौरव और लिंग सामान्यमें गुरुष और स्त्रियोंकी लाघवहैं, अपनी जातिमें जो महाप्रमाणहैं वे गुरु और अल्प प्रमाणके लघु होतेहैं ॥ ३३३ ॥
गुरूणांलाघवंविद्यात्संस्काराच्च विपर्ययम् । व्रीहेलाजायथाच स्युःसक्तूनांसिद्धपिण्डकाः ३३४
गुरु पदायोंकोभी संस्कारसे लाघव और विपरीत भाव हो जाताहै जैसे व्रीहिसे लाजा और सत्तूओंसे सिद्ध पिंड गुरु होतेहैं ॥ ३३४ ॥
अल्पादानेगुरूणाञ्चलघूनांचातिसेवने । मात्राकारणमुदिष्टंद्रव्याणांगुरुलाघवे ॥ ३३५ ॥
गुरु पदार्थोंके अल्प आदानमें और लघु पदार्थोंके अत्यंत सेवनमें और द्रव्योंके गौरव लाघवमें मात्राही कारण कहाहै ॥ ३३५ ॥
गुरूणामल्पमादेयंलघूनांतृप्तिरिष्यते । मात्रामपेक्षतेद्रव्यंमात्राचाग्निमपेक्षते ॥ ३३६ ॥
गुरु पदार्थोंमेंसे अल्प भक्षण करना और लघु पदार्थोंसे तृप्ति इष्टहैं मात्राको द्रव्यकी अपेक्षाहै और अग्निकीभी अपेक्षाहै ॥ १३६ ॥

translation:
( 284 )
From the Charaka Samhita

Creatures born in and roaming the Dhanva (desert) region are light (laghu) in quality. (328)

The limbs of the body — thighs, head, shoulders and so forth — are as follows: the flesh of the thighs is heavier than flesh in general; heavier than the thighs is the shoulder; heavier than the shoulder is the hip-joint; and heavier than the hip-joint is the head. (329)

The testes, skin, penis, pelvis, kidneys, liver, and heart — know these to be exceedingly heavy compared to ordinary flesh. The bones are of medium heaviness. (330)

By nature, mung beans, lava birds, and kapinjala birds are light. By nature, urad (black gram), boar meat, and buffalo meat are heavy. (331)

Among the bodily constituents beginning with blood, each successive one is heavier than the one before. Those living beings who are active in many deeds are superior to those who are lazy. (332)

In the general category of gender, maleness carries heaviness and femaleness carries lightness. Within their own species, those that are of larger measure are heavier, and those of smaller measure are lighter. (333)

Even heavy substances can acquire lightness through processing, and the reverse can also occur. For example, from paddy rice come parched grains (laja), which are light, while from grain flour come cooked dumplings (siddha-pindaka), which are heavy. (334)

In the case of heavy substances, taking them in small quantity, and in the case of light substances, consuming them in excess — in both cases, the quantity (matra) is declared to be the determining factor in heaviness and lightness of substances. (335)

Of heavy substances, only a small amount should be taken; of light substances, satisfaction (full intake) is desired. The substance depends upon the measure (matra), and the measure in turn depends upon the digestive fire (agni). (336)

text:
सूत्रस्थानम् । ( २८५ )

बलमारोग्यमायुःप्राणाश्चाग्नौप्र
तिष्ठाः । अनुपानेन्धनैश्चाग्नि
दीप्यतेशाम्यतेऽन्यथा ॥ ३३७॥

बल आरोग्य अवस्था प्राण ये सब
अग्निमें स्थितहैं; अनुपान और इंधनसे
अग्नि दीत होतीहै और अन्यथा शांत
होतीहै ॥ ३३७ ॥

गुरुलाघवचिन्त्येयंप्रायेणाल्पब
लान्रित । मन्दकर्मिननारोग्या
न्सुकुमारान्सुखोचिताञ्च। ३३८।

गुरु लाघवकी यह चिंता प्रायः अल्प-
बल मनुष्योंके प्रतिहै और उनकेभी
लियेहै जो मंदकर्मी हैं अनारोग्यहैं
सुकुमारहैं और सुखके भोगीहैं ॥ ३३८॥

दीप्ताग्नयःखराहाराःकर्मनित्या
महोदराः । येनराःप्रतितांश्चि
न्त्यनावश्यंगुरुलाघवम् ॥ ३३९॥

और जो नर दीप्ताग्नि कठोरभोजी
नित्यकर्मी और महोदरहैं उनके गति
लाघवकी चिंता आवश्यक नहींहै ३३९॥

हिताभिर्जुहुयाञ्चित्यमन्तराग्निस
माहितः । अनुपानसमिद्भिर्नामा
त्राकालौविचारयन् ॥ ३४० ॥

हितकारी मात्राओंसे सावधान होकर
जठराग्निमें प्रतिदिन अनुपानकी समिधोंसे
होमकरे और मनुष्य मात्रा कालको
विचारता रहे ॥ ३४० ॥

आहिताग्नेःसदापथ्यान्यन्तराग्नौ
जुहोतियः । दिवसेदिवसेब्रह्मजप
त्यथददातिच । नरनिःश्रेयसेयु
क्तसात्म्यञ्चपानभोजने ॥ ३४१ ॥

जो नर आहिताग्नि होकर अंतराग्निमें
सदा पथ्यका होम करताहै प्रतिदिन
गायत्रीको जपताहै और दान देताहै,
जो मनुष्य सदैव श्रेयमें युक्त है और
पान भोजनसे अपने सात्म्यका ज्ञाता
है ॥ ३४१ ॥

भजन्तेनामयाःकेचिद्राविनोऽप्य
न्तरादते । षट्त्रिंशच्चसहस्राणि
रात्रीणांहितभोजनः ॥ ३४२ ॥

उसको विघ्नके विना जो कोई भावी-
भी रोग हैं वेभी नहीं भजते हैं; छतीस
सहस्र रात्रिपर्यंत जो हित भोजन
करताहै ॥ ३४२ ॥

जीवत्यनातुरोजन्तुर्जितात्मास
म्मतःसतामिति । तत्र श्लोकाः।
अनुपानगुणाःसाम्यावर्गैद्वादश
निश्चिताः । सगुणान्यञ्चपानानि
गुरुलाघवसंग्रहः ॥ ३४३ ॥

सज्जनोंका संमत वह नर आत्माका
जय करके निरोग जीवताहै; —इति—
इसमें ये श्लोक हैं कि—

मुख्यता संहित अनुपानके गुणके
द्वादशवर्गे निश्चितहैं और गुणों सहित
अन्नपान गुरु और लाघवका संग्रह ३४३
translation:
Sutrasthana (Chapter on Fundamental Principles), Page 285

Verse 337:
Strength, health, lifespan, and vital breath — all are established in the digestive fire. By the fuel of anupana (liquid taken with or after medicine/food), the fire is kindled; otherwise it is subdued.

Commentary 337:
Strength, health, the state of life, and vital breath — all these rest in the digestive fire. Through anupana and fuel, the fire is made bright; otherwise it becomes quiescent.

Verse 338:
The question of heaviness and lightness is to be considered principally for those of little strength — and for those who are slow in their activities, who are not healthy, who are delicate, and who are accustomed to comfort.

Commentary 338:
This consideration of heaviness and lightness applies chiefly to people of little strength, and also to those who are inactive, who lack good health, who are delicate, and who are devoted to comfort.

Verse 339:
Those persons who have a keen digestive fire, who eat coarse food, who are always engaged in work, and who have large abdomens — for them, the consideration of heaviness and lightness is not necessary.

Commentary 339:
Those men who have a strong digestive fire, who eat hard food, who are always active, and who have large abdomens — for them, concern about heaviness and lightness is not necessary.

Verse 340:
With a composed mind, one should offer into the digestive fire — as if performing a sacrifice — the proper quantities of anupana as fuel, always mindful of the right measure and the right time.

Commentary 340:
Carefully observing the beneficial measures, one should daily offer into the digestive fire the fuel of anupana as in a sacrifice, and one should always reflect upon the proper measure and the proper time.

Verse 341:
One who, like a keeper of the sacred fire, always offers wholesome things into the inner fire; who recites the Gayatri mantra daily and gives in charity; who is ever devoted to what is truly good; and who knows his own wholesome diet and drink —

Commentary 341:
That person who, maintaining the inner fire, always offers wholesome things into it, who daily recites the Gayatri and gives donations, who is always devoted to what is truly beneficial, and who knows what is congenial for him in food and drink —

Verse 342:
— such a person is not approached by any disease, even those that may be imminent. One who eats wholesome food for thirty-six thousand nights remains free of disease.

Commentary 342:
Without any obstacle, even diseases that are about to come do not afflict him; one who eats wholesome food for thirty-six thousand nights remains unafflicted.

Verse 343:
A person who has conquered himself, who is approved by the good, lives free of disease — thus it is said. On this subject, the verses state: The qualities of anupana are established as twelve categories in the compendium; together with the qualities of various drinks, this is the summary of heaviness and lightness.

Commentary 343:
That person who, having conquered his own self, is esteemed by good people, lives healthy — thus the conclusion. On this, the verses declare: The principal qualities of anupana are fixed in twelve categories, and together with the qualities of food and drink, this is the collection on heaviness and lightness. (Verse 343)

text:
( २८६ )

Digitized By वर्कसंहितायाम् yan Kosha

अनुपानविधावुक्तंतत्परीक्ष्यंविशेषतः । प्राणाःप्राणभृतामन्नम् अन्लोकोऽभिधावति ॥ ३४४ ॥

जो अनुपानकी विधिमें कहाहै वह विशेषकर परीक्षा करने योग्यहै; अन्न प्राण धारियोंका प्राण है जगत्, अन्नके सन्मुख दौड़ताहै ॥ ३४४ ॥

वर्णप्रसादःसौस्वर्यंजीवितंप्रितिभासुखम् ।। तुष्टिःपुष्टिर्बलंमेधा सर्वमन्नेप्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ ३४५ ॥

वर्ण प्रसाद सुंदरस्वर जीवन बुद्धि सुख तुष्टि पुष्टि बल मेधा ये सब अन्नमें प्रतिष्ठितहैं ॥ ३४५ ॥

लौकिकंकर्ममेयद्वृत्तौस्वर्गेतौयचैवेदिकम् ।। कर्मोपवर्गेयचोक्तं तच्चाप्यन्नेप्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ ३४६ ॥

इत्यन्नपानचतुष्केऽन्नपानविधिरध्यायः ।

और जो जीविकाके लिये लौकिक कर्म हैं और जो स्वर्गकी गतिमें वैदिक कर्म हैं और जो कर्म मोक्षके लिये कहाहै वहभी अन्नमेंही प्रतिष्ठितहैं ॥ ३४६ ॥
इति अन्नपानचतुष्के अन्नपानविधिः अध्यायः॥२७ ॥

अष्टाविंशोऽध्यायः ।
अथातोविविधाशितपीतीयमध्यायं व्याख्यास्याम: ।
इति हस्माहभगवानात्रेयः ।
इसके अनंतर विविधा शितपीतीय अध्यायका वर्णन करतेहैं;
ऐसे भगवान् आत्रेयने कहा है–

विविधमशितपीतलीढखादितंजन्तोहितमन्नमग्निसन्धुक्षितवलेनयथास्वेनोष्मणासम्यिग्वपच्यमानंकालवदनवस्थितसर्वधातुपाकमनुपहतसर्वधातूष्ममारुतश्रोतःकेवलंशरीरमुपचयबलवर्णसुखायुषायोजयतीतिशरीरधातूनूर्जयन्धातवोिहधात्वाहाराःभ्रक्तिमनुवर्त्तन्ते ॥ १ ॥

कि अनेक प्रकारका जो अशित पीत लीढ खादितरूप जंतुका हितकारी अन्नहै वह अग्निके संधुक्षण (जलना) के बलसे जैसे २ अपनी ऊष्मासे पकता हुआ कालके समान अनवस्थित (चंचल) जो संपूर्ण धातु उनके पाककों अनुपहत (वर्तमान) संपूर्ण धातुओंकी ऊष्मा वात श्रोतरूप जो केवल शरीरहै उसकी वृद्धि बलवर्ण सुख अवस्थासे युक्त करताहै उससे शरीरकी धातुओंको बढाताहै फिर धातुहैंआहारिजनका ऐसी धातुप्रकृतिके अनुसार वर्ततीहैं ॥ १ ॥

तत्राहारप्रसादाख्योरसःकिट्टञ्च मलाख्यमभिनिर्वर्त्तेतेकिट्टात्मूत्रस्वेदपुरीषवातपित्तश्लेष्माणःकर्णिक्षनासिकास्यलोमकूपप्रजनमलकेशश्मशुलोमनखाद्यश्चावयवाः ॥ २ ॥
translation:
( 286 )

[Chapter on the Rules of Anupana — Concluding verses, and Beginning of Chapter 28]

Verse 344:
What has been stated in the rules concerning anupana (the liquid taken after food or medicine) should be examined with particular care. Food is the very life-breath of all living beings; the whole world runs toward food.

Verse 345:
Luster of complexion, pleasantness of voice, longevity, contentment, happiness, satisfaction, nourishment, strength, and intelligence — all of these are established in food.

Verse 346:
Whatever worldly action is undertaken for one's livelihood, whatever Vedic rite is performed to attain heaven, and whatever action is prescribed for liberation — all of that too is grounded in food.
Thus ends the chapter on the Rules of Food and Drink, the twenty-seventh chapter of the Annapana Chatushka.

CHAPTER TWENTY-EIGHT
We shall now expound the chapter called "Vividhashita-Pitiya" (On the Various Things Eaten, Drunk, Licked, and Chewed).
Thus spoke the revered Atreya.

Verse 1:
Food of various kinds — eaten, drunk, licked, or chewed — that is beneficial to a living being, when acted upon by the power of digestive fire, is properly cooked by its own heat in due course. It sustains all the tissues whose power of digestion remains unimpaired; through the channels of wind and bodily passages, it brings about increase in the body's tissues, strength, complexion, happiness, and longevity. In this way the tissues nourish themselves, and the nutrient essences of food serve as the sustenance for each tissue in accordance with their own nature.

Verse 2:
From that food two things are produced: the refined essence called rasa (nutritive fluid), and the waste product called kitta (residue). From the kitta arise: urine, sweat, feces, wind, bile, phlegm, and the secretions of the ears, nose, mouth, hair follicles, and reproductive organs — as well as hair of the head, beard, body hair, nails, and the like.

In it, the food substance called Prasada (the nutritive portion) produces a waste product called Rasamala (the impurity of rasa), and from the waste products arise urine, sweat, feces, vata, pitta, and kapha; and also the ears, eyes, nose, mouth, hair follicles, reproductive organs, excreta, head-hair, beard, body hair, nails, and other bodily parts are produced. (2)

The nutritive portion of food nourishes rasa, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, semen, and ojas; the substances of the five sense organs, the ligaments and connective tissues of the body, and all other bodily parts — all of these, whether called dhatus (tissues), malas (waste products), or prasadas (refined essences), nourish one another and maintain themselves in their proper measure. (3)

Just as age and the body maintain themselves, similarly rasa and mala, remaining in their proper measure and sustaining equilibrium of the dhatus they reside in, ensure that when the prasada-dhatus are either depleted or in excess, rasa — through the root cause of diet, whether in terms of increase or decrease — restores equilibrium of the dhatus and thereby promotes health. (4)

Likewise this applies to the waste products (kita) of the malas as well. Those malas that exceed their proper measure, when treated with qualities alternating between cold and hot, are seen to restore equilibrium of the bodily dhatus. (5)

The channels (srotas), whose mouths serve as the pathways of those dhatus known as mala and prasada, fill each respective dhatu in its proper portion; the body is sustained by what is eaten, drunk, licked, and chewed. And from what is eaten, drunk, licked, and chewed, diseases in this body also arise. (6)

translation:
( 288 )
Charaka Samhita

[Verse 6] These channels, each in its proper share, appropriately nourish the bodily tissues. In this way, the body arises from what is eaten, drunk, licked, and chewed — and it is from these same four modes of intake that diseases in the body also arise.

[Verse 7] The specific qualities of beneficial and harmful intake produce, respectively, the specific characteristics of good and bad in this body.

[Verse 8] When the revered Atreya had spoken thus, Agnivesha said to him: "Lord, we see that even people who consume food designated as wholesome fall ill, and likewise those who consume food designated as unwholesome sometimes appear free of disease. Seeing this, how can we know that the specific use of wholesome and unwholesome substances truly produces the specific forms of good and ill?"

[Verse 9] Then the revered Lord Atreya replied to him: "O Agnivesha, for those who consume unwholesome food, diseases are indeed produced. And it is not merely that by consuming wholesome food alone one becomes completely free from all fear of disease. For there exist other causes of disease apart from unwholesome diet. These are: untimely conduct, failure of the intellect (prajnaparadha), the natural effects of time, and the qualities of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, as well as unsuitability. These causes of disease afflict even the person who consumes proper food in the right manner. That is why even those who follow wholesome diet are seen to be ill. For those who consume unwholesome diet, however, not all faulty practices necessarily produce the same degree of dosa; nor do all dosas have equal strength; nor are all bodies equally capable of withstanding disease. Indeed, that which is unwholesome becomes more intensely harmful through the combination of place, time, potency, and excessive use. And that same dosa, when compounded with incompatible treatment, deep-seated, originating from the seats of life-force, striking at vital points, may become most severe and rapidly manifesting."

Then the revered Atreya spoke to Agnivesha: "O Agnivesha! Those who make proper use of wholesome food do not suffer disease on account of that wholesome food, yet the fear of all diseases is not completely overcome merely by the use of wholesome food alone. This is because other disease-causing factors exist independently of diet — namely, time and its adverse turns, errors of intellect, natural transformation, sound, touch, form, taste, and smell. These, being unwholesome in their nature, and working through the improper use of the sense-objects, connect a person to misfortune. Thus even those who use wholesome food may be seen afflicted with disease, while those who use unwholesome food do not immediately suffer harm from every cause. Nor do all unwholesome things cause equal harm, nor are all faults of equal strength, nor are all bodies equally capable of bearing disease. That same unwholesome substance, when combined with the wrong place, time, association, potency, and quantity, becomes exceedingly unwholesome. And those same aggravated doshas, when opposing the proper line of treatment in deeply lodged conditions, become destructive to the vital seats (marmas) long established in the abodes of the life-force — extremely distressing and very swift in effect." (9)

Bodies that are excessively obese or excessively emaciated, that are devoid of well-established flesh and blood, that are weak, and that are maintained on unwholesome food —

— such bodies subsist on little food, have little vitality, and are unable to bear disease. (10)

On the contrary, bodies of the opposite constitution are able to bear disease. And from unwholesome diet, aggravated doshas, and particular bodily constitutions, diseases arise that may be mild or severe, of rapid onset or chronic in nature. (11)

It is for this very reason that vata, pitta, and kapha, when aggravated in their specific seats, give rise to specific diseases. O Agnivesha! We shall now properly describe those diseases that arise in the respective seats of these aggravated doshas, whichever diseases arise in whichever location. (12)

जारोगावक्ष्यन्तेरक्तदोषजाः।१४।

पांडुता स्रोतोंका अवरोध,क्षीबता, साद,
कृशांगता,अग्निकानाश और समयके विना
वली और पलित ( सपेदकेश ) ये रोग
रसके दोषसे होतेहैं अब रक्तकें दोषसे
उत्पन्नोंको कहतेहैं ॥ १४ ॥

कुष्ठवीसर्पिपडकारक्तिपित्तमसूद्र
रः । गुदमेठास्यपाकश्फूीहागु
ल्मोऽथिवद्रधी ॥ १५ ॥

कुष्ठ, वीसर्पं, पिडका, रक्तिपित्त,
असृक्दर, ( रुधिरका मदर ) गुदा, लिंग,
मुख, इनका पाक, प्लीहा,गुल्म, विद्रधी १५

नीलिकाकामलाव्यङ्गिपिपुवस्ति
ठकालकाः । दद्रुश्चर्म्मदलंश्वित्रः
पामाकोठास्रमण्डलम् । रक्तप्रदो
षाजायन्तेश्रृणुमांसप्रदोषजान्।१६।

नीलिका कामला, व्यंगता, पिप्रुव,
तिलकालक, दद्रुँ चर्मेदल श्वित्र, पामा
कोठास्र मंडल ये रोग रक्तके दोषसे
उत्पन्न होतेहैं अब मांसके दोषसे उत्प-
न्नोंको सुनो ॥ १६ ॥

अधिमांसाबुंदंकीलगलशालूक
शुण्डकाः।।पूतिमांसालजीगण्ड
गण्डमालोपिजिह्विकाः ॥ १७ ॥

अधिमांस, अर्बुद, कील,गल, शालूक,
शुंडिका, पूतिमांस, अलजी, गंड, गंड-
माला, उपजिह्विका ॥ १७ ॥

विद्यान्मांसाशयान्मेदःसंश्रयांस्तु
प्रवक्ष्यते ।। निदानानिप्रमेहाणां
पूर्वरूपाणियानिच ॥ १८ ॥

ये मांसके दोषसे उत्पन्न जानना
मेदासे उत्पन्न रोगोंको कहेंगे प्रमेहोंके
निदान और पूर्वँ रूपोंको कहेंगे ॥१८॥

अध्यस्थिदन्तदन्तास्थिभेदःशू
लंविवर्णता ॥ केशलोमनखश्म
श्रुदोषाश्चास्थिप्रकोपजाः।।१९।।

वे अस्थियोंमें, दन्तोंमें, दन्त, अस्थि
का भेद, शूल, विवर्णता, केश, लोम,
नख, श्मश्रु, इनके, दोष, अस्थिके
कोपसे उत्पन्न होतेहैं ॥ १९ ॥

रुक्पर्वणांभ्रमोमूच्छोदर्शनंतम
सोमताः ॥ अरुषांस्थूलमूलानां
पर्वजानाञ्चदर्शनम् ॥ २० ॥

translation:
( 290 )
Charaka Samhita

In each of the various locations where various diseases arise, we describe them accurately:

Verse 13:
Lack of faith (in food and medicine), loss of taste, foul breath, loss of the sense of taste, nausea, heaviness, drowsiness, bodily aching, and feverish stupor — these are the symptoms.

Commentary 13:
That is: lack of faith, loss of appetite, foulness of the mouth, loss of consciousness of taste, nausea, heaviness, drowsiness, bodily aching, and feverish stupor.

Verse 14:
Pallor, obstruction of the channels, weakness, exhaustion, thinness of the limbs, loss of digestive fire, and the untimely appearance of wrinkles and grey hair — these diseases arise from vitiation of rasa (plasma/nutrient fluid). Now we describe those arising from vitiation of blood.

Commentary 14:
Pallor, obstruction of the channels, weakness, exhaustion, thinness of limbs, loss of digestive fire, and the untimely appearance of wrinkles and white hair — these diseases arise from vitiation of rasa. Now we shall describe those arising from vitiation of blood.

Verse 15:
Skin diseases (kushtha), spreading skin eruptions (visarpa), pustules (pidaka), hemorrhagic disorders (raktapitta), bleeding from the rectum, diseases of the rectum, penis and mouth (their suppuration), diseases of the spleen, abdominal tumors (gulma), and abscesses (vidradhi).

Commentary 15:
Kushtha, visarpa, pidaka, raktapitta, hemorrhage (bleeding disorder), diseases of the rectum, penis, and mouth and their suppuration, spleen disorders, gulma, and vidradhi — (these are from blood vitiation).

Verse 16:
Nilika (blue-black patches), jaundice (kamala), vyanga (facial discoloration), pipru (a type of skin blemish), tilakalaka, dadru (ringworm), charmadala, shvitra (leucoderma), pama, kotha, and circular blood-patches — these arise from vitiation of blood. Now listen to those arising from vitiation of flesh (mamsa).

Commentary 16:
Nilika, kamala (jaundice), vyanga, pipru, tilakalaka, dadru, charmadala, shvitra, pama, kotha, and blood-circles — these diseases arise from vitiation of blood. Now hear those arising from vitiation of flesh.

Verse 17:
Adhimamsa (excess flesh growth), arbuda (tumor), kila (hard growth), gala (throat disease), shaluka, shundika, putimamsa (putrid flesh), alaji (an eye/lid disease), ganda (cheek swelling), gandamala (scrofula), and upajihvika (growth beneath the tongue).

Commentary 17:
Adhimamsa, arbuda, kila, gala, shaluka, shundika, putimamsa, alaji, ganda, gandamala, upajihvika — these are the diseases from flesh vitiation.

Verse 18:
These should be understood as arising from the flesh. Now we shall describe those arising from vitiation of meda (fat tissue), as well as the causative factors and premonitory symptoms of prameha (urinary disorders).

Commentary 18:
Those should be known as arising from vitiation of flesh. We shall next describe diseases arising from fat, and then the causes and early signs of prameha.

Verse 19:
Pain in the bones and teeth, fractures of teeth and bones, pain (shula), discoloration, and disorders of the hair, body hair, nails, and beard — all these arise from aggravation of the bones (asthi).

Commentary 19:
In the bones and teeth: fracture of teeth and bone, pain, discoloration, disorders of hair, body hair, nails, and beard — these arise from aggravation of the bones.

Verse 20:
Pain in the joints, giddiness, fainting, visual disturbances, stupor, appearance of sores with thick roots, and swelling of the joints — (these arise from vitiation of the joint structures).

सूत्रस्थानम्
( २९१ )

पर्वोंमें पीडा, भ्रम, मूच्छां अंधकारका दर्शन होताहै और अरुष ( मर्म ) स्थूल मूल दीखै और पर्वजोंका दर्शन ॥२०॥

मज्जाप्रदोषाच्छुक्रस्यदोषात्क्लैब्यमहर्षणम् ।। रोगिणंक्लीबमल्पायुंविरूपंबाअजायते ।। २१ ।।

ये मज्जाके दोषसे क्लीबता हर्षका अभाव होताहै और रोगी नपुंसक अल्पायु वा विरूप बालक पैदा होताहै ॥२१॥

नवासआयतेगर्भःपतितिप्रस्रवत्यपि ।। शुक्निंदुष्टसापत्यंसदारंबाधतेनरम् ।। २२ ।।

अथवा गर्भ नहीं रहता पतित होजाताहै प्रसव होताहै दुष्ट शुक्र संतान और स्त्री सहित मनुष्यको बाधा करता है ॥२२॥

इन्द्रियाणिसमाश्रित्यप्रकुप्यन्तयदामलाः । उपतापोपघाताभ्यांयोजयन्तींन्द्रियाणिते ।। २३ ।।

इंद्रियोंमें टिककर जब मल कुपित होतेहैं तब उपताप और उपघातसे युक्त इंद्रियोंको करतेहैं ।। २३ ।।

स्नायोशिराकण्डरयोर्दुष्टाःक्रिश्यन्तिमानवम् । स्तम्भसङ्कोचस्फोभिर्गन्थस्फुरणसूतिभिः ।। २४ ।।

और स्नायु, शिरा, कांड इनमें दूषित मल मनुष्यको ये क्लेश देतेहैं कि स्तंभ संकोच खल्ली ग्रंथि स्फुरण सुति ये होतेहैं ।। २४ ।।

मलानाश्रित्यकुपिताभेददोषप्रदूषणम् । दोषामलानांकुर्वन्तिस ङ्गोत्सर्गावतीवच ।। २५ ।।

मलोंमें स्थित होकर जब कुपित होतेहैं तब भेद दोषोंका प्रदूषण मलोंमें दोष करतेहैं और अत्यंत संग उत्सर्ग होतेहैं ।। २५ ।।

विविधादिशितात्पीतादिहिताळ्ढीढखादिताव् । भवन्त्येतेमनुष्याणांविकारायउदाहृताः ।। २६ ।।

अनेक प्रकारके अहित पीतसे और अहित ठीठ खादितसे ये विकार होतेहैं जो कहेहैं ।। २६ ।।

तेषामिच्छन्नुत्पत्तिंसेवेतमतिमान्सदा । हितान्येवाशितांदीनिनस्युस्तज्जास्तथामयाः ।। २७ ।।

उनकी अनुत्पत्तिकी इच्छा करता हुआ बुद्धिमान् मनुष्य सदैव हितही अशित आदिकी सेवा करे तिससे उनसे उत्पन्न रोग नहीं होते ।। २७ ।।

रसजानांविकाराणांसर्वेलंघनमौषधम् । विधिशोणितकेऽध्यायेरक्तजानांभिषजितम् ।। २८ ।।

रसमें उत्पन्न विकारोंकी संपूर्ण औषध लंघनहैं और विधशोणितक अध्यायमें रक्तमें उत्पन्न रोगोंकी चिकित्सा कहीहै२८

मांसजानान्तुसंशुद्धिःशस्त्रशाराझिकर्म्मच । अष्ठौनिन्दितसंख्या

translation:
(Page 291 of Sutrasthana — Charaka Samhita)

[Verse 20:] In the joints there is pain, confusion, fainting, and the experience of darkness; the roots of the joints appear thick and swollen, and there is a sensation of the joints being crushed.

[Verse 21:] From a defect of marrow (majja), the semen (shukra) becomes vitiated, resulting in impotence and lack of sexual pleasure. The patient becomes impotent, short-lived, or gives rise to a malformed child.

[Verse 22:] Or the fetus does not stay and is aborted, or there is a premature delivery; the defective semen troubles the man along with his wife and offspring.

[Verse 23:] When the waste products (malas), having taken up residence in the sense organs, become aggravated, they afflict those organs with irritation (upatapa) and injury (upaghata).

[Verse 24:] When the waste products are vitiated in the tendons (snayu), veins (shira), and ligaments (kandara), they afflict the person with stiffness, contraction, cramping, nodules, trembling, and numbness.

[Verse 25:] When the doshas, dwelling in the malas, become aggravated, they cause vitiation through separation (bheda) of the doshas and malas, and produce extreme retention or excessive discharge.

[Verse 26:] From the intake of various unwholesome foods — what is eaten, drunk, or consumed in an improper manner — the disorders of human beings arise as described here.

[Verse 27:] A wise person who wishes to prevent these disorders should always consume only wholesome food and drink; by doing so, the diseases arising from those causes will not occur.

[Verse 28:] For all disorders arising from rasa (the primary tissue fluid), fasting (langhana) is the complete remedy. For disorders arising from blood (rakta), the treatment is described in the chapter on Vidhishonitaka.

For disorders of flesh (mamsa-ja), purification and surgical procedures are the remedy. [The text continues on the next page regarding the eight censurable conditions...]

text:
( २९२ )
चरकसंहितायाम्

तेमेदोजानांचिकित्सतम् ॥ २९ ॥
और मांसमें उत्पन्नोंकी संशुद्धि शस्त्र
और क्षार अग्निकर्म है और अष्टौनिंदित
संख्यात अध्यायमें मेदामें उत्पन्नोंकी
चिकित्सा कहीहै ॥ २९ ॥

अस्थ्याश्रयाणांव्याधीनांपञ्चक
र्मोणिभेषजम् । बस्तयःक्षीरस
र्पींषितक्कोपिहितानिच ॥ ३० ॥
अस्थिमें आश्रित व्याधियोंकी औषध
पंचकर्म औषधहैं बस्ति और वे दूध घी
जो तिक्तसे उपहित हों ॥ ३० ॥

मज्जाशुक्रसमुत्थानामौषधंस्वादुति
क्तकम् । अञ्चंव्यवायव्यायामौ
शुद्धिःकालेचमात्रया ॥ ३१ ॥
मज्जा और शुक्रमें उत्पन्नोंकी औषध
स्वादु और तिक्तहैं अञ्च और व्यवाय
व्यायामसे और समयपर मात्रासे शुद्धि
होतीहै ॥ ३१ ॥

शान्तिरिन्द्रियजानान्तुचिरमर्मी
येप्रवक्ष्यते ॥ ३२ ॥
और इंद्रियोंमें उत्पन्न रोगोंकी शांति
चिरममर्मीय अध्यायमें कहेंगे ॥ ३२ ॥

स्नाय्वादिजानांप्रशमोवक्ष्यतेवात
रोगिके । नवेगान्धारणेऽध्याये
चिकित्सासंग्रहःकृतः ॥ ३३ ॥
स्नायु आदिमें उत्पन्नोंकी शांति वात
रोगिक अध्यायमें कहेंगे और नवेगा-
न्धारण अध्यायमें मलमें उत्पन्न विका-
रोंकी चिकित्साका संग्रह कियाहै ॥ ३३ ॥

मलजानांविकाराणांसिद्धिःयोका
किञ्चित्किञ्चत् ॥ ३४ ॥
और मलसे उत्पन्न जो विकारहैं
तिनकी कहीं २ सिद्धिभी कहीहै ॥ ३४ ॥

व्यायामादुष्मणस्तैक्ष्याच्चितस्या
नवधारणात् । कोष्ठाञ्छाखाम
लायान्तिद्रुतवान्मारुतस्यच ३५
व्यायामसे उष्मासे तीक्ष्णतासे और
हितके अनिश्रयसे और मारुतके द्रुत
(वेग) से कोष्ठमेंसे शाखाके मल चले
जातेहैं ॥ ३५ ॥

तत्रस्थाश्चिवलम्बन्तेकदाचिच्चा
समीरिताः । नादेशकालेकुप्यन्त
भूयोहेतुमतीक्षणः ॥ ३६ ॥
और कदाचित् वायुके प्रेरित नहीं
किये वहांही टिके हुये विलंबको प्राप्त
होते हैं और फिरभी हेतुकी प्रतीक्षा
करते हुये देश कालके बिना कुपित
नहीं होते ॥ ३६ ॥

वृद्ध्याभिष्यन्दनातपाकात्स्रोतो
मुखविशोधनात् । शाखांसुका
मलाःकोष्ठंयान्तिवायोश्चनिग्रहा
त् ॥ ३७ ॥
वृद्धि अभिष्यंद पाक स्रोतोंके मुख-
की शुद्धि इनसे मल शाखाओंको छोड़-
कर कोष्ठमें वायुके निग्रहसे आजाते
हैं ॥ ३७ ॥

translation:
( 292 )
From the Charaka Samhita

[Verse 29] — The treatment of those disorders arising in fat (medas) has been described. The purification of those arising in muscle (mamsa) is by surgical instruments and by alkali-cautery (kshara-karma). The treatment of those arising in fat has been described in the chapter on the eight censurable (body-types). ॥ 29 ॥

[Verse 30] — For diseases seated in bone (asthi), the five purificatory procedures (panchakarma) are the medicine, along with enemas (basti) and preparations of milk and ghee that are combined with bitter substances. ॥ 30 ॥

[Verse 31] — For disorders arising in marrow (majja) and semen (shukra), sweet and bitter medicines are prescribed. Purification is achieved through mild physical movement, sexual activity, and exercise, taken at the proper time and in the proper measure. ॥ 31 ॥

[Verse 32] — The treatment of diseases arising in the sense organs will be described at length in the chapter on the vital points (marman). ॥ 32 ॥

[Verse 33] — The pacification of disorders arising in tendons and ligaments (snayu) etc. will be described in the chapter on vata-diseases, and in the chapter on the non-suppression of natural urges, a compilation of treatments for disorders arising in the waste products (mala) has been made. ॥ 33 ॥

[Verse 34] — For the various disorders arising from waste products (mala), some cures have been mentioned here and there. ॥ 34 ॥

[Verse 35] — Through exercise, through heat, through sharp (digestive) intensity, through not retaining what should flow, and through the swift movement of the vital air (vayu), the waste products move quickly from the alimentary tract (koshtha) into the peripheral channels (shakha). ॥ 35 ॥

[Verse 36] — Sometimes, when not driven out by vayu, the waste products remain lodged there and undergo a delay; and even then, awaiting the right cause, they do not become aggravated without the appropriate place and time. ॥ 36 ॥

[Verse 37] — Through increase (vriddhi), through liquefaction (abhishyanda), through digestion (paka), and through the cleansing of the mouths of the channels, and also through the restraint of vayu — the waste products leave the peripheral channels and return to the alimentary tract (koshtha). ॥ 37 ॥

[The text continues] — Regarding those disorders that have not yet arisen, preventing their arising, and regarding those that have already arisen... [page ends here]

text:
Digitized By Siddha Gyan Kosha ( २९३ )

वृत्ये । रोगाणांयोविधिदृष्टःसुखार्थीतंसमाचरेत् ॥ ३८ ॥

अजात रोगोंकी निवृत्तिमें जो विधि शास्त्रमें देखी है सुखार्थी मनुष्य उसका आश्रय ले ( करै )॥ ३८ ॥

सुखार्थाःसर्वभूतानांमताःसर्वाःप्रवृत्तयः । ज्ञानाज्ञानविशेषानुमार्गामार्गप्रवृत्तयः ॥ ३९ ॥

संपूर्ण भूतोंकी सब प्रवृत्ति सुखके अर्थहैं, ज्ञान और अज्ञानके विशेषसे मार्ग और अमार्गमें प्रवृत्ति होतीहैं ॥ ३९ ॥

हितमेवानुरुध्यन्तेप्रसमीक्ष्यपरीक्षकाः । रजोमोहावृतात्मानःप्रियमेवतुलौकिकाः ॥ ४० ॥

परीक्षक मनुष्य विचार कर हितकाही अनुरोध करते हैं और रजोगुण और मोहसे आच्छादित है आत्मा जिनका ऐसे लौकिक, प्रियकाही अनुरोध करतेहैं ॥ ४० ॥

श्रुतंबुद्धिःस्मृतिदाक्ष्यंधृतिहितनिषेवणम् । वाक्मशुद्धिःशमोधैर्यंमाश्रयन्तिपरीक्षकम् ॥ ४१ ॥

और परीक्षक मनुष्योंमें श्रुत (शास्त्र) बुद्धि स्मृति दढता धृति हितका सेवन वाणीकी उत्तम शुद्धि शांति धीरता ये वास करतेहैं ॥ ४१ ॥

लौकिकंनाश्रयन्येतेगुणामोहतम

श्रितम् । तन्मूलाबहुलाश्चैवरोगाशारीरमानसाः ॥ ४२ ॥

और गुण मोह तमसे युक्त लौकिक मनुष्योंमें ये पूर्वोक्त आशय ही लेते शरीर और मनके बहुतसे रोगोंका मूलभी वहीहैं ॥ ४२ ॥

प्रज्ञापराधाच्चयहितानार्थीन्पञ्च निषेवते । सन्धारयितवेगांश्चसेवतेसाहसानिच ॥ ४३ ॥

मज्ञा ( बुद्धि ) के अपराधसे पांच अहित अर्थोंका सेवन मनुष्य करताहै, वेगोंका धारण करताहै साहसोंका सेवन करताहै ॥ ४३ ॥

तदात्वसुखसंज्ञेषुभावष्वज्ञोऽनुरज्यते । रज्यतेनतुविज्ञातातिविज्ञानेहमलीकुते ॥ ४४ ॥

और तत्काल सुख नामके पदार्थोंमें मूर्ख मनुष्य प्रीति करताहै और निर्मल विज्ञानके होनेसे ज्ञाता मनुष्य उनमें प्रीतिको नहीं करता ॥ ४४ ॥

नरोगान्नाप्यविज्ञानादाहारसुपयोजयेत् । परीक्ष्यहितमश्नीयादेहोह्याहारसम्भवः ॥ ४५ ॥

और रागसे वा अविज्ञानसे आहारका उपयोग ( भक्षण ) न करै, परीक्षा करके हित भोजन करै क्योंकि देह आहारसे उत्पन्नहै ॥ ४५ ॥

आहारस्यविभावस्थौविशेषाहेतुसं

Verse 38:
One who desires happiness should follow the method, as seen in scripture, for preventing diseases that have not yet arisen. (38)

Verse 39:
All the activities of all beings are for the purpose of happiness. The difference between knowledge and ignorance determines whether one proceeds on the right path or the wrong path. (39)

Verse 40:
Those who are examiners (physicians) carefully consider what is truly beneficial and act accordingly. But those whose souls are veiled by rajas (passion) and moha (delusion) seek only what is pleasant. (40)

Verse 41:
In true examiners (physicians) dwell these qualities: learning (from scripture), intellect, memory, skill, steadfastness, practice of what is beneficial, purity of speech, calm, and courage. (41)

Verse 42:
Those worldly people who do not take shelter of these qualities, being overwhelmed by delusion and tamas (darkness), hold on to those earlier-mentioned tendencies — and these are the very root of the many physical and mental diseases. (42)

Verse 43:
Due to transgression of intelligence (prajnaparadha), a person pursues five unwholesome objects, suppresses natural urges, and engages in rash actions. (43)

Verse 44:
The ignorant person becomes attached to objects that give only momentary pleasure, while one who possesses clear wisdom does not become attached to them. (44)

Verse 45:
One should not use food out of passion or ignorance. One should eat only what is beneficial after proper examination, because the body is produced from food. (45)

text:
( २९४ )
चरकसंहितायाम्

ञ्काः । शुभाशुभसमुत्पन्नौतान्प
रीक्ष्योपयोजयेत् ॥ ४६ ॥
आहारकी उत्पत्तिमें जो हेतु संञ्क
आठ विशेषहैं शुभ अशुभकी उत्पत्तिमें
उनकी परीक्षा करके उपयोग करै॥४६॥

परिहार्य्याण्यपथ्यानिसदापिरहर
ञ्रः ।भवत्यनृणतांप्राप्तःसाधूना
मिहपण्डितः ॥ ४७ ॥
और अपथ्योंको त्यागदे अपथ्योंको
सदैव त्यागता हुआ मनुष्य अनृणी
होकर साधुओंका पंडित होताहै ॥४७॥

यत्तुरोगसमुत्थानमशक्यमिह
केनचित् । परिहर्तुंनतत्प्राप्य
शोचितव्यंमनीषिणा ॥ ४८ ॥
और जो रोगकी उत्पति किसी प्रकार
निवृत्ति करनेको अशक्यहै उसको प्राप्त
होकर बुद्धिमान् मनुष्य शोच न करै ४८॥

तत्र श्लोकाः ।
उसमें ये श्लोकहैं कि—
आहारप्रभवोयस्तुरोगाश्चाहारस
म्भवाः । हिताहितविशेषाश्चिव
शेषःसुखदुःखयोः ॥ ४९ ॥
आहारसे उत्पन्न जंतुहैं रोगभी आहा-
रसे उत्पन्नहैं, हित अहितके विशेष, सुख
दुःखके विशेष ॥ ४९ ॥

सहत्वेचासहत्वेचदुःखानांदेहस
त्त्वयोः । विशेषोरोगसंघाश्वधा
तुजायेगृथक्पृथक् ॥ ५० ॥

दुःखोंके सहने, देह और सत्वका
विशेष, रोगोंके संघ जो पृथक् २ धातु-
ओंमें होतेहैं ॥ ५० ॥

तेषाञ्चैवप्रशमनंकोशञ्छाखाउ
पेत्यच ।दोषायथाप्रकुप्यन्तिशा
खाभ्यःकोठमेत्यच ॥ ५१ ॥
और उनकी शांति कोठमेंसे शाखामें
अकार और शाखाओंसे कोठमें आकर
दोष जैसे कुपित होते हैं ॥ ५१ ॥

प्राज्ञासयोर्विशेषश्चस्वस्थातुरिह
तञ्चयत् । विविधाशितपीतीये
तत्सर्वंसम्प्रकाशितम् ॥ ५२ ॥
इति अग्निवेशकृतेतन्त्रेचरकप्रतिसंस्कृतेसूत्र
स्थानेअन्नपानचतुष्केविविधाशितपीती
योनामअष्टाविंशोऽध्यायःसमाप्तः ।

प्राञ्च और अञ्चका विशेष स्वस्थ
और आतुरका जो हितहै वह सब विवि-
धाशितपीतीय अध्यायमें भली प्रकार
प्रकाशित किया ॥ ५२ ॥
इत्यन्नपानचतुष्केविविधाशितपीतीयोऽध्यायःसमाप्तः २८
समाप्तं अन्नपानचतुष्कम् ।

एकोनत्रिंशोऽध्यायः ।
अथातोदशप्राणायतनीयमध्यायं
व्याख्यास्यामः ।
इतिहस्माहभगवानात्रेयः ।
इसके अनंतर दश प्राणायतनीय
अध्यायका व्याख्यान करते हैं ॥
ऐसे भगवान् आत्रेयने कहा है—
translation:
( 294 )
Charaka Samhita

[Verse 46:] Those [factors] — both auspicious and inauspicious — that arise [in food] should be examined and then utilized.
The eight special factors that are the causes at the origin of food — one should examine which are auspicious and which are inauspicious, and then make use of them. (46)

[Verse 47:] One should always avoid unwholesome foods; by constantly abandoning unwholesome things, a person becomes free from debt [obligation] and is considered a wise man among the virtuous.
And one who forsakes unwholesome things, constantly abandoning them, becomes free of obligation and is counted as a learned man among the virtuous. (47)

[Verse 48:] But when a disease that has arisen cannot in any way be removed by anyone, the wise person should not grieve upon encountering it.
And when the arising of a disease is beyond anyone's power to cure, a person of wisdom should not grieve upon being afflicted by it. (48)

Verses on this subject — the following verses relate to this topic:

[Verse 49:] Those living beings that are produced from food — diseases too are produced from food; the distinctions between wholesome and unwholesome, and the distinctions between pleasure and pain.
Creatures arise from food; diseases too arise from food; the distinctions of what is beneficial and what is harmful, the distinctions of pleasure and pain. (49)

[Verse 50:] The differences in bearing and not bearing sorrows in body and mind, the groups of diseases arising separately in the various bodily constituents (dhatus).
The capacity or incapacity to endure sorrows — the distinctions of body and mind — and the groups of diseases that arise separately in each of the dhatus. (50)

[Verse 51:] Their pacification occurs when [doshas] move from the core (koshtha) to the branches (shakha), and doshas become aggravated when they move from the branches back to the koshtha.
And the pacification of those [diseases]: the doshas move from the koshtha to the shakhas, and from the shakhas they return to the koshtha — this is how the doshas become aggravated. (51)

[Verse 52:] The distinctions between the wise and the unwise, the healthy and the sick — all of this has been fully illuminated in the chapter on the various foods and drinks.
What is beneficial for the healthy and the ailing — all of that has been clearly set forth in the chapter on Vividhashitapitiya. (52)

Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter, titled Vividhashitapitiya, in the Annapana-chatushka of the treatise composed by Agnivesha and revised by Charaka, in the Sutrasthana.
The Annapana-chatushka is hereby concluded.

Twenty-Ninth Chapter.
We shall now explain the chapter on the Ten Seats of the Life Principle (Dashapranaayataniya).
Thus has the revered Atreya spoken.
Next, the explanation of the chapter on the Ten Seats of the Life Principle is given. So has the blessed Atreya said —

Digitized By Siddhanta Granthi Gyaan Kosha
सूत्रस्थानम्
( २९५ )

दशैवायतनान्याहुःप्राणायेषुप्र
तिष्ठाः ॥ शंखोमर्मत्रयंकण्ठो
रक्तशुक्रौजसीगुदम् ॥ १ ॥

जिनमें प्राण प्रतिष्ठित हैं वे दशही
आयतन कहे हैं कि शंख तीनमर्म कंठ
रक्त शुक्र ओज गुदा ॥ १ ॥

तानीन्द्रियाणिविज्ञानंचेतनाहेतु
मामयम् ॥ जानीतेयःसविद्वान्
वैप्राणाभिसरउच्यतेइति ॥ २ ॥

उनको और इंद्रियोंको विज्ञान चेतना
हेतु रोगको जो जानताहै वह विद्वान्
प्राणाभिसर कहाताहै ॥ २ ॥ इति-

द्विविधास्तुखलुभिषजोभवन्ति
अग्निवेश ! प्राणानामेकेऽभिसरा
हन्तारोरोगाणां,रोगाणामेकेऽभि
सराहन्तारःप्राणानामिति ॥ ३ ॥

हेअग्निवेश दो! प्रकारके भिषज होते
हैं एक तो प्राणोंके अभिसर और रोगोंके
हंता और एक रोगोंके अभिसर और
प्राणियोंके हंता होते हैं ॥ ३ ॥

एवंवादिनंभगवन्तमात्रेयमभिवे
शउवाचभगवन् ! तेकथमस्माभि
र्वेदितव्याभवेयुरिति ॥ ४ ॥

इस प्रकार कहते हुये भगवान आत्रेय
को अग्निवेश वोले कि हे भगवन्! उनको
हम किस प्रकार जान सकतेहैं ॥ ४ ॥

भगवानुवाचयइमेकुलीनाःपर्य्य
वदातश्रुताःपरिदृष्टकर्माणोदक्षाः
शुचयोजितहस्ताजितात्मानःस
र्वोपकरणवन्तःसर्वेन्द्रियोपपन्नाः
प्रकृतिज्ञाःप्रतिपत्तिज्ञास्तेप्राणि
नामभिसराहन्तारोरोगाणांतथा
विधाहिकेवलशरीरज्ञानेशरीरा
भिनिवृत्तिज्ञानेप्रकृतिविकारज्ञा
नेचिनःसंशयाःसुखसाध्यकच्छ्र
साध्ययाप्यप्रत्याख्येयानाश्चरो
गाणांसमुत्थानपूर्वरूपलिङ्गवेद
नोपशयविशेषविज्ञानेव्यपगतस
न्देहाःत्रिविधस्यायुर्वेदसूत्रस्यस
संग्रहव्याकरणस्यसत्रिविधौषध
ग्रामस्यप्रवक्तारः ॥ ५ ॥

भगवान् बोले कि, जो इन वैद्योंमें
कुलीनहैं जिनका श्रुतभी शुद्धहै कर्मों
के दृष्टहैं चतुर, शुद्ध, हस्त जिनका
जितहै आत्मा जितहैं संपूर्ण सामग्रीसे
युक्तहैं संपूर्ण इंद्रियों सहित हैं, प्रकृतिके
ज्ञाता प्रतिपत्ति ( सिद्धि ) कोभी जानते
हों ऐसे वैद्य प्राणियोंके अभिसर (रक्षक)
और रोगोंके हंता होतेहैं क्योंकि उस
प्रकारके वैद्य केवल शरीरके ज्ञानमें
शरीरकी अभि निवृत्ति ( आनंद ) के
ज्ञानमें प्रकृतिके विकार ज्ञानमें संदेह
रहित होतेहैं और सुखसे साध्य कष्ट

Sutra Sthana
(Page 295)

Verse 1:
These ten are called the vital seats in which the life-breaths are established: the temples (shankhau), the three vital points (marmatraya), the throat, blood, semen, ojas, and the rectum. (1)

Commentary on 1: Those in which the life-breath is established are called the ten seats — the temples, the three vital points, the throat, blood, semen, ojas, and the rectum. (1)

Verse 2:
One who knows those sense organs, consciousness, the causes of disease, and vital awareness is called a learned physician — a "Pranabhisara." (2)

Commentary on 2: One who knows those sense organs, consciousness, the cause of disease, and the vital force — such a person is called a learned Pranabhisara. (2)

Verse 3:
O Agnivesha! Physicians are of two kinds: some are protectors of the life-breath and destroyers of disease, while others become allies of disease and destroyers of life. (3)

Commentary on 3: O Agnivesha! Physicians are of two kinds — some protect life and destroy disease, and others support disease and destroy living beings. (3)

Verse 4:
When the Lord Atreya spoke thus, Agnivesha said to him: "O Lord! How may we distinguish between the two?" (4)

Commentary on 4: As Bhagavan Atreya spoke in this way, Agnivesha said: "O Lord, how can we recognize them?" (4)

Verse 5:
The Lord replied: Those physicians who are of good lineage, of pure learning, who have observed and practiced well, who are skilled, clean, with controlled hands and a disciplined mind, fully equipped with all instruments and instruments, endowed with all sense faculties, who know the natural constitution (prakriti) of patients and also know the proper therapeutic response — such physicians are protectors of living beings and destroyers of disease. For those physicians who have no doubt in the knowledge of the body alone, in the knowledge of the body's natural states, and in the knowledge of the natural derangements (vikara), and who know the origins, premonitory symptoms, signs, sensations, and specific diagnostic features of diseases that are easily curable, difficult to cure, manageable, or incurable — such physicians are free from doubt and are expounders of the threefold Ayurvedic scripture with its summary, elaboration, and the threefold classification of medicinal substances. (5)

Commentary on 5: The Lord said: Among physicians, those who are of noble lineage, whose learning is pure, skilled in observed practice, clean, with controlled hands and a controlled mind, fully equipped, with all sense faculties intact, knowing the patient's natural constitution and also knowing the means of attainment (siddhi) — such physicians are the protectors (abhisara) of living beings and the destroyers of disease. For such physicians have no doubt in the knowledge of the body alone, in the knowledge of the body's states and pleasures, or in the knowledge of the body's natural disorders; and they clearly know which diseases are easily curable, difficult to cure...

text:
( २९६ )

साध्य याप्य प्रत्याख्यान ( नहीं ) करने योग्य जो रोगैहैं उनका उठना पूर्वरूप लिंग वेदना ( पीडा ) उपशय इनके विशेष ज्ञानमें संदेह रहित होतेहैं; तीन प्रकारका जो आयुर्वेदका सूत्रहै संग्रह व्याकरण सहित उसके और तीन प्रकारके औषधोंके समूहके वक्ता होतेहैं॥५॥

पञ्चत्रिंशत्श्वमूलफलानांचतुणां महास्नेहानांपञ्चानांलवणानामष्टानाञ्चसूत्राणामष्टानाञ्चमूत्राणाम् षटानाञ्चक्षीराणांक्षीरतक्रवृक्षाणाञ्चषण्णांशिरोविरेचनादेशपञ्चकर्मांशयस्योषधगणस्याष्टाविंशतेश्वयवागूनांद्वाविंशतश्वचूर्णप्रदेहानां षण्णांविरेचनशतानांपञ्चानाञ्चकषायशतानामितिस्वस्थवृत्तौचभोजनपाननियमस्थानचङ्क्रमणशय्यासन-मात्रा-द्रव्याञ्जनधूमनावनाभ्यञ्जन-परिमार्जनवेगविधारणा विधारण-व्यायामसात्म्येन्द्रियपरीक्षोपक्रमसद्वृत्तकुशलाः ॥ ६ ॥

और पैंतीस मूल फलोंके चार महान् स्नेहोंके पांचलवणोंके आठ सूत्रोंके आठ मूत्रोंके आठ दूधोंके और क्षीर त्वचाके वृक्षोंके छः शिरके विरेचनोंके और पंच कर्मका आश्रय जो औषध गण उसके अठाईस यवागुओंके वाईस चूर्णप्रदे-

होंके छः सौविरेचनोंके पांचसौ कषायोंके और स्वस्थ अवस्थामें भोजन पान नियम स्थिति चंक्रमण ( गमन ) शय्या आसन मात्रा द्रव्य अंजन धूम नावन स्नेवना अभ्यंजन परिमार्जन वेगका विधारण, अविधारण व्यायाम सात्म्य इंद्रियोंकी परीक्षा उपक्रम सद्वृत्त इनमें कुशल होतेहैं ॥ ६ ॥

चतुष्पादोपगृहीतेचभेषजेषोडशकलेसाविनिश्चयेसत्रिपञ्र्यषणेस वातकलाकलज्ञानेव्यपगतसन्देहाः ॥ चतुर्विधस्यचक्षेहस्यचतुर्विंशत्यपनयनस्यउपकल्पनीयोकचतुःषष्टिपर्यन्तस्यव्यवस्थापयितारोबहुविधविधान-युक्तानाञ्चक्षेहस्वेयवम्यविरेचयौषभोपचाराणांकुशलाः । शिरोरोगादेशदोषांशिवकल्पजस्यव्याधिसंग्रहस्यसंक्षयिपडकिव्रधेःत्रयाणाञ्चशोफानांबहुविधशोफानुबन्धानामष्टाचत्वारिंशत्श्वरोगाधिकारिणांचत्वारिंशदधिकस्यच नानात्मजस्यव्याधिशतस्य । तथाविगर्हितातिस्थूलातिकृशानांसहेतुलक्षणोपक्रमाणांस्वभस्यच हिताहितस्यास्वभातिस्वभस्यच सहेतूपक्रमस्यषण्णाञ्चलंघनादी
translation:
(Page 296)

Those diseases which are to be classed as curable, palliable, or incurable — the physician is free of doubt in the special knowledge of their prodromal signs, symptoms, pain, and therapeutic indications. He is a speaker on the threefold compendium of Ayurveda — including its grammatical exposition — and on the threefold groups of medicines. (verse 5)

Of thirty-five root-fruits, of the four great unctuous substances, of the five salts, of the eight aphorisms, of the eight urines, of the eight milks, of the milk-bark trees, of the six head-purging measures, of the five procedures related to the digestive tract, of the twenty-eight groups of medicinal substances, of the twenty-two gruels, of the twenty-two powder-pastes, of the six hundred purgative preparations, of the five hundred decoctions — and in the healthy state: the rules for eating and drinking, posture, walking, bed, seat, dosage, medicinal collyrium, medicated smoke, nasal therapy, anointing, cleansing, the suppression and non-suppression of natural urges, exercise, acclimatization, examination of the senses, therapeutic procedures, and right conduct — in all these they are skilled. (verse 6)

And of thirty-five root-fruits, four great unctuous substances, five salts, eight aphorisms, eight urines, eight milks, milk-bark trees, six head-purges, and the five therapeutic procedures — of the medicinal group based on these, twenty-eight gruels, twenty-two powder-pastes —

Of the six hundred purgatives, five hundred decoctions, and in the healthy state: rules of diet and drink, posture, walking, lying down, sitting, dosage, medicinal substances, collyrium, smoke, nasal therapy, anointing, cleansing, suppression and non-suppression of urges, exercise, acclimatization, examination of the senses, therapeutic procedures, and right conduct — in all these they are proficient. (verse 6)

Regarding the four-limbed [physician-patient-medicine-attendant] framework, in the sixteen divisions of medicine, in determining the three types of conditions with certainty, in understanding the states of imbalance and balance of wind — free from doubt. They are able to organize the fourfold unctuous therapy up to twenty-four eliminative procedures, along with their sixty-four preparatory measures, along with the many varied regulations; and they are skilled in unctuous, sudation, and emetic-purgative pharmaceutical treatments. In diseases of the head, in local disorders, in conditions arising from the body's own constitution, in the compendium of diseases, in wasting, in six types of abscesses, in the many forms of edema, in forty-eight disease categories, in over forty varieties of multi-causational diseases, in hundreds of conditions of varied origin — likewise in those who are censured, the excessively obese, and the excessively emaciated — with their causes, signs, and treatments, of what is beneficial and harmful in diet, of wholesome and unwholesome food with their rationale, and of the six types of fasting measures beginning with langhana —

translation:
(Page 217)

[Sanskrit verse — sutra 7:]
They are expert in: the names of the therapeutic procedures (upakramas) such as nourishing (santarpana) and depleting (apatarpana) treatments; the nature of diseases and their alleviation; diseases arising from blood; the causes and forms of intoxication (mada), fainting (murcha), and loss of consciousness (sannyasa); and the appropriate medicines for these. They are also expert in: determining the proper dietary regimen; the foods most beneficial according to one's constitution; the principal compendium of dietary articles; the eighty-four types of fermented preparations (asavas); the determination of the properties of substances — their primary tastes (rasa) and secondary tastes (anurasa); the twelve groups of food and drink along with their qualities and effects, including the various types of anupana (vehicle); the collection of foods; dietary movements; and harmful [foods].

[Hindi commentary begins:]

The physician of four-fold character — that which is medicine — has sixteen aspects. One who is free from doubt in determining these, in the three-fold inquiry (tripayeshana), and in the knowledge of the gradations of vata, is considered expert.

Such a physician is expert in the twenty-four preparations of the four types of sneha (oleation substances) up to the sixty-four arrangements described in the Upakalpaniya section. They are skilled in the various methods of sneha (oleation), sveda (fomentation), vamana (emesis), and virechana (purgation), and in their medicinal application. They are knowledgeable about diseases of the head and others arising from the combinations of doshic fractions; the classification of those diseases; the three aspects of kshaya (depletion), pindaka (nodule), and vidradhi (abscess); the many types of edema (shopha) and their associated conditions; the forty-eight diseases and their authorities; the forty-four and more types of soumya (cold/phlegmatic) disorders arising in various ways, along with their three-fold causation, signs, and therapeutic procedures. They know the regimens for the censured — the extremely obese and the extremely emaciated — along with causes, beneficial and harmful sleep, excessive sleep, and the six procedures beginning with langhana (fasting). They are expert in the nature and alleviation of diseases arising from santarpana (over-nourishment) and apatarpana (under-nourishment), in diseases arising from blood along with their causative medicines, and in the knowledge of mada (intoxication), murcha (fainting), and sannyasa (unconsciousness). They are expert in determining the correct dietary regimen, in the principal collection of foods and behaviors most beneficial to one's constitution, in the eighty-four asavas (fermented preparations), in determining the properties of substances with reference to their primary and secondary tastes, along with their incompatibilities, the twelve groups of food and drink, the qualities and effects of food and drink along with their anupana (vehicles), the various types of anupana qualities, the collection of foods, the movement of food in the body, and harmful [foods].

translation:
( 298 )

[Left column:]
Of the special uses of the auspicious and inauspicious; of the specifics relating to the dhatus (bodily tissues), diseases, and collections of medicines; of the dasha-prana (ten vital forces) and their seats; and of what will be called the ten great fundamental topics in the thirtieth chapter ahead — in which are contained the complete teachings of the treatise, its characteristics, the knowledge of grasping and retaining [knowledge], its application, action, function, time, agent, and instrument — in all of these they are skilled. || 7 ||

Those who are skilled in memory, intellect, the principles of the shastras, logical reasoning, and knowledge; who through harmony with the qualities of character and disposition of the self, and through cultivating universal friendliness of mind toward all beings — like a mother, father, brother, and kinsman — are thus equipped: O Agnivesha, they are the protectors of life and the destroyers of disease. || 8 ||

And those who, through memory, intellect, the teachings of the shastras, reasoning, knowledge — the qualities of the character of the self — without contradiction, having cultivated universal friendliness of mind toward all beings, like a mother, father, brother, and kinsman, are skilled and equipped: O Agnivesha, those physicians are the guardians of life and the destroyers of diseases. || 8 ||

Those who are the opposite of these are the ones who advance diseases and destroy the lives of beings. Physicians concealed under false appearances, who are thorns to the world, who adopt the outward form and share the practices of [true physicians] by royal favor, wander about the kingdoms. To them this special knowledge

[Right column:]
— out of greed for gain, when they hear of someone's illness they rush to his side; and in his hearing they extol their own medical qualities; and the [false] physician then performs the treatment for him. They repeatedly aggravate the patient's faults, and through flattery, excitement, and attendance they seek to win over the patient's friends and relatives to themselves; they display their own activities as worthy of praise, and look in on the patient repeatedly morning and evening. Being unable to conceal their own ignorance through cleverness, and unable to remove the disease, they point to the patient himself as incapable and non-cooperative; and having privately deliberated, they shift to another approach, using their own country or region as a pretext. Before ordinary people they describe their skill as though it were incompetence, and slander the steadfastness of the truly wise. But when an assembly of learned men is at hand, they avoid it from afar, as travelers on a road avoid a great forest out of fear. || 9 ||

Those who are the opposite of these [true physicians] become the destroyers of beings and the allies of disease. Endowed with deceit (kapat), they are thorns, pretenders who share the outward appearance of the good, wandering through kingdoms by the favor of kings. To them this special knowledge [is not truly accessible].

प्रति कर्म ( विरुद्ध ) करताहै उसके
दोषोंको वारंवार कहते हैं और आतुरके
मित्रोंको प्रहर्षण उपजाप ( भेद ) सेवा-
ओं अपना करनेकी इच्छा करते हैं
और अपनी अल्प इच्छाको प्रकट करते
हैं और जार कर कर्मको वारंवार देखतेहैं
और चतुरतासे अपने अज्ञानके छिपाने-
की कामनासे व्याधिके दूर करनेमें
असमर्थ हुये रोगीकोही सामग्रीहीन अप-
चारी अनात्मा बताते हैं और अंतको
प्राप्त देखकर अन्यका आश्रय लेते हैं
अपने देशको अन्य देश करके और
प्राकृत जनोंके समूहमें अपनी कुशल-
ताको अकुशलके समान वर्णन करते हैं
अधीरके समान धीरताको धीरोंमें कहते
हैं; विद्वान् जनोंके सन्निपात ( समूह )
को देखकर अत्यंत भयसे इस प्रकार
दूरसे त्यागते हैं जैसे वनको मार्गके
गामी शीघ्र त्याग देते हैं ॥ ९ ॥

यश्चैषांकश्चित्सूत्रावयवउपयुक्त
तंप्रकृतेप्रकृतान्तरेवासततमुदा
हरन्तिनचानुयोगमिच्छन्तिअनु
योगंवामृत्योरिवचानुयोगादुदि
जन्ते । नचैषामाचार्यःशिष्यो

वासब्रह्मचारीवैवादिकोवाकिश्चि-
त्ज्ञायते इति ॥ १० ॥

और जो कोई सूत्रका अंग इनको
उपयुक्त ( आता ) होताहै उस अप्रकृत-
को वा अन्य प्रकरणमें निरंतर पढते हैं
अनुयोग और अनुपयोगकी इच्छा
नहीं करते मृत्युके समान अनुयोगसे
कँपते हैं; और इनका कोई आचार्य
शिष्य सहाध्यायी वा विवादी नहीं जाना
जाताहै ॥ १० ॥ इति–

भिषक्छद्मप्रविश्यैवव्याधितांस्त
केयन्तिये । वसंतिमवसंश्रित्यच
नेशाकुन्तिकोद्विजान् । श्रुतदष्ट
कियाकालमात्रास्थानबहिष्कृ
ताः । वर्जनीयाहितेमृत्योश्चर
न्त्यनुचराभुवि ॥ ११ ॥

इसमें ये श्लोकहैं कि वैद्यके छलमें
प्रवेश करके जो रोगियोंको ऐसे तर्कना
करते हैं, जैसे वसंतमें जाकर वनमें पक्षी
घाती पक्षियोंको तर्कना करताहै और
श्रुत दष्ट क्रियाकाल मात्रा इनके ज्ञानसे
रहित होते हैं; ऐसे जो मृत्युके अनुचर
भूमिमें विचरते हैं वे वैद्य त्यागके
योग्य हैं ॥ ११ ॥

वृत्तिहेतोर्भिषग्मानपूर्णान्मूर्षिवि
शारदान् । वर्जयेदातुरोविद्वाञ्च
सपिस्तेपितमारुताः ॥ १२

जीविकाके हेतु जो भिषक्के मानसे

translation:
Digitized By Siddhanta eGangotri Gyaan Kosha
Sutrasthana, Chapter 1
(Page 299)

Those who are very much like physicians only in outward appearance wander about driven by greed for gain in various fields; upon hearing of someone's illness they rush about in all directions, and loudly proclaim the virtues of their own medical skill. They repeatedly enumerate the faults of a physician who does the opposite of what they do, and seek to win over the patient's friends through flattery, persuasion, and insinuation, expressing a show of modest desire while repeatedly inspecting the case with cunning. Wishing to conceal their own ignorance and being incapable of curing the disease, they declare the patient himself to be at fault — lacking proper materials, having behaved wrongly, or being of base nature. When they see that the end is near, they seek refuge with others; they describe their own land as foreign territory, and among ordinary folk they boast of their skill just as a skilled person might, while among the steadfast they speak of steadfastness as though they were themselves steadfast. When they see a gathering of learned men, they flee far away in great fear, just as a traveler swiftly abandons the forest road. ॥ 9 ॥

And if any portion of a sutra happens to suit any of these people, they recite it repeatedly — whether in its proper context or in some other context — but they neither desire inquiry nor welcome it; they tremble at questioning just as at death. And for such persons, no teacher, student, fellow-student, or disputant is known to exist. ॥ 10 ॥ Thus —

Those who enter by the disguise of a physician and torment the afflicted — just as a fowler who settles in a grove in spring to lure birds — excluded from knowledge of what has been heard, of proper action, of the right time and measure, and wandering over the earth as servants of death, such physicians are to be abandoned. ॥ 11 ॥

A learned patient should avoid physicians who are filled with arrogance, motivated only by livelihood, and who are ignorant and boastful — like the venom of a serpent mingled with clarified butter blown by the wind. ॥ 12

Those physicians whose mind is filled with pride of profession and who practice medicine only for the sake of livelihood —

text:
( ३०० )
चरकसंहितायाम् ।

पूर्ण मूर्खं विशारदैहैं उनको बुद्धिमान् रोगी वर्जेंदे क्योंकि वे पीई है पवन जिन्होंने ऐसे सर्प होतैहैं ॥ १२ ॥

येतुशास्त्रविदोदक्षाःशुचयःकर्मकोविदाः । जितहस्ताजितात्मानःतेभ्योनित्यकृतंनमः ॥ १३ ॥

और जो शास्त्रके ज्ञाता चतुर शुद्ध कर्ममें कोविद (ज्ञानी) हैं और जित हस्त और जितात्मा हैं उनको नित्य नमस्कार करैं ॥ १३ ॥ इति—

तत्र श्लोकः ।

दशप्राणायतनिकेश्लोकस्थानार्थसंग्रहः। द्विविधाभिषजश्चोक्काः प्राणस्यायतनानिच ॥ १४ ॥

इति दशप्राणायतनीयोनामोनान्विंशोऽध्यायः समाप्तः ।

उसमें यह श्लोकहै कि दशप्राणायतनिक अध्यायमें श्लोकोंके स्थानमें अर्थसंग्रहहै दो प्रकारके वैद्य और प्राणके आयतन कहेहैं ॥ १४ ॥

इति दश प्राणायतनीयोऽध्यायः समाप्तः ॥२९॥

त्रिंशत्मोऽध्यायः ।
अथातोऽर्थेदशमूलीयमध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः ।
इति ह्स्माह भगवानात्रेयः ।

इसके अनन्तर अर्थेमें दशमूलीय अध्यायका वर्णन करते हैं ॥
यह भगवान् आत्रेय कहते हैं—

अर्थेदशमहामूलाःसमासकामहाफलाः । महचार्थश्वहृदयंपप्यैंयैरुच्यतेबुधैः ॥ १ ॥

अर्थमें दश महामूल महाफलके हैं और महान् अर्थको हृदयके पर्याय शब्दोंसे बुद्धिमान् मनुष्य वर्णन करतेहैं १

षडङ्गमङ्गविज्ञानिमिन्द्रियाण्यर्थेपञ्चकमू । आत्माचसगुणश्चेतः चिन्त्यञ्चहृदिसंस्थितम् ॥ २ ॥

अंगके विज्ञानके छः अंगहैं इंद्रिय अर्थ पंचक आत्मा और सगुण चेत और चिंतनके योग्य ये हृदयमें स्थित हैं ॥ २ ॥

प्रतिष्ठार्थंहिभावानामेषांहृदयमिष्यते । गोपानसीनामागारकाणिकेवार्थिचन्तकैः ॥ ३ ॥

भावोंकी प्रतिष्ठाके लिये इनकाही हृदय नाम ऐसे कहाहै जैसे गोपानसी-योंका स्थान आगारकी कणिका (चौक) अर्थके चिंतकोंने कही है ॥ ३ ॥

तस्योपघातान्मूञ्छोंयंमेदान्मरणमृञ्छति । यञ्चितस्पर्शिविज्ञानंधारितत्तत्रसंश्थितम् ॥ ४ ॥

उसके उपघातसे मूञ्छा होतीहै और जिसके भेदनसे यह मरणको प्राप्त होता है, और जो स्पर्शका विज्ञानहै वहभी धारणकारी हृदयमें आश्रित है॥ ४ ॥

तत्परस्यौजसःस्थानंतत्रचैतन्य
